<details><summary>Version-map notes</summary>

The iOS 27 design is a refinement of Liquid Glass (user opacity slider, sharper icons). Neither the HIG change logs nor WebKit gates show colour, type or control changes for 27, so 26 and 27 are one generation. Apple publishes no iOS lifecycle policy: support status here comes only from the release rows on the security page. One correction: the WebFetch summary gave iOS 26.5.1 as 16 Jun 2026; the raw page says 01 Jun 2026, and the raw page was used. Secondary only (third-party WWDC 2026 coverage, e.g. macmyths.com, feedbagel.com) agrees that iOS 27 keeps Liquid Glass. It is not cited. Working files are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tibi-Rust-native-theme/a0421ea2-02c5-43d6-8b7a-682d83a2e8e4/scratchpad/m2-src/ios-map/ (sec.html, hig/*.json incl. color-20250607.json, webkit/*.mm). Not checked: individual facts rows. Not mapped: WebKit tags to specific iOS point releases (no primary source).

</details>

**Claim:** `defaults.muted_color` (): the cell says #8e8e93; flat iOS 18: rgba(60,60,67,0.6); on white #8a8a8e; Liquid Glass iOS 26: rgba(60,60,67,0.6); on white #8a8a8e.

### Researcher notes

Each researcher's own notes, verbatim: coverage, method caveats and errors found outside the *differs* rows (wrong citations on ✅ rows, unpinned links). Step 7 corrects the citation errors (S4) as part of the row fixes.

<details><summary>preset</summary>

TARGET VERSION: ios.toml names no version, so cell_version is "none" for every row. Its palette is the flat-generation (iOS 13-18) one. accent, danger and warning, light and dark, equal the HIG values captured on 2025-06-07 and WebKit's platform/ios-18 baselines exactly. The light border/separator #c6c6c8 is exactly separatorColor rgba(60,60,67,0.29) composited on white, which is the iOS 18 alpha; iOS 26 lowered it to 0.12. Fonts and Dynamic Type sizes did not change between 18 and 26. Against iOS 26 the preset is stale for: blue (#0088ff/#0091ff), red (#ff383c/#ff4245), orange (#ff8d28/#ff9230), separator, the switch geometry (WebKit) and the progress-bar thickness (WebKit). No source separates iOS 27 from 26: the HIG colour and typography change logs end at 2025-12-16, and WebKit's platform/ios baseline was committed as the iOS 26 baseline. No iOS 27 value is claimed.
COUNTS: 330 keys checked: 51 same, 54 differs, 225 unverifiable. Line 3 (name) skipped. No line range is left uncovered.
METHOD CAVEATS: (1) Values tagged (WebKit) come from WebKit's own iOS rendering of HTML form controls, the platform-facts '(WebKit)' source tag. UIKit may differ, so every such row sets probe_could_settle. (2) The 44 pt min_height comes from the HIG's control and hit-target size, not from a drawn outer box. (3) The text_scale roles were mapped as in the macOS column (.caption1/.headline/.title1/.largeTitle); the notes on lines 69 and 74 give the alternatives (Subhead, Title 2).
STEP 1 MAP, CORRECTIONS AND ADDITIONS: (a) There is a better iOS 18 source than mapping WebKit tags to iOS releases: WebKit main carries LayoutTests/platform/ios-18 baselines, which hold UIKit's iOS 18 dynamic-colour values, next to platform/ios, which holds iOS 26. (b) The iOS 26 dark values missing from Step 1 are Red 255,66,69 and Orange 255,146,48 (HIG plus WebKit). (c) HIG layout.json (updated 2026-09-09) no longer holds iOS margin or spacing numbers, so it did not settle any layout key.
ALREADY ON todo.md: disabled_opacity 0.3 together with disabled colours (todo.md:688-697); iOS sizes unsourced (todo.md:2317-2322). This review adds a HIG source for the 44 min_height, a UIKit source for container_margin 8, and the UIStackView spacing 0.0 default for widget_gap. NOT on todo.md (new): the palette is iOS 13-18, not iOS 26 (Step 1 said so too); muted is systemGray rather than secondaryLabel; the text_scale line heights are size x 1.2 rather than the HIG leading; section_heading 15/700 matches no iOS style; dark input background #1c1c1e is not systemBackground; dark border #38383a matches no source.
LEGEND for the unverifiable notes:
U1 UIKit has no shadow-colour API; the HIG gives no value.
U2 No iOS API or HIG value for text on a status or accent fill.
U3 No published RGB. WebKit leaves selection to UIKit (platformActiveSelectionBackgroundColor = transparent, https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/de320ba3ff90229f983988d42d4b0f83315459da/Source/WebCore/rendering/ios/RenderThemeIOS.mm#L1005-L1008).
U4 The HIG lists Link (UIColor.link) without an RGB; WebKit has no baseline for it.
U5 No iOS API. Already on todo.md:688-697. For reference, WebKit iOS dims disabled inputs by opacity 0.4 (https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/31adf9d1605fad1fb548e86d36384161a2a060b4/Source/WebCore/css/html.css#L962-L964).
U6 No iOS API or HIG value for focus-ring geometry.
U7 No iOS global corner radius. WebKit's iOS non-capsule controls use 5 (https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/de320ba3ff90229f983988d42d4b0f83315459da/Source/WebCore/rendering/ios/RenderThemeIOS.mm#L259; https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/31adf9d1605fad1fb548e86d36384161a2a060b4/Source/WebCore/css/html.css#L465). Buttons 45 pt or taller get 0.175 x their smaller side; smaller buttons are capsules.
U8 No iOS global line width. WebKit iOS text fields use 1 px at the pre-refresh tag (https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/31adf9d1605fad1fb548e86d36384161a2a060b4/Source/WebCore/css/html.css#L466) and 0.5 in the iOS 26 painter (https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/de320ba3ff90229f983988d42d4b0f83315459da/Source/WebCore/rendering/cocoa/RenderThemeCocoa.mm#L2915).
U9 No iOS API or HIG statement.
U10 UIFont.monospacedSystemFont's doc names no family; the HIG lists SF Mono only as an SF variant.
U11 monospacedSystemFont takes the size and weight as arguments; there is no default.
U12 SF Symbols scales are relative to text; there is no point-size constant.
U13 The HIG gives a 44x44 default control size, not a 64 minimum width. On todo.md:2317-2322.
U14 No HIG or UIKit value; imagePadding has no documented default.
U15 Touch controls have no hover state; iPadOS has pointer hover, but no hover colour is published.
U16 No published pressed-state colours; WebKit keeps systemBlue text on :active.
U17 WebKit uses opaque-secondary-fill-disabled (secondarySystemFill at 0.75, made opaque, RenderThemeIOS.mm:1148), which has no RGB baseline.
U18 No published colour for a focused text-field border.
U19 No published value; WebKit dims a disabled input by opacity 0.4 instead.
U20 iOS has no checkbox. HIG Toggles (toggles.json, read 2026-10-11) says macOS supports the checkbox style. WebKit draws HTML checkboxes on iOS at 16x16 (https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/31adf9d1605fad1fb548e86d36384161a2a060b4/Source/WebCore/css/html.css#L1008-L1013).
U21 iPadOS has tooltips (UIToolTipInteraction, iOS 15+), but no colours or width are published.
U22 UIScrollView indicators have no published sizes or colours.
U23 UISlider has no tick marks. WebKit draws datalist ticks of 1x3 (old RenderThemeIOS.mm:796-800), and the refreshed painter uses track/4 = 1 (RenderThemeCocoa.mm:3880).
U24 No published disabled slider colours.
U25 UIProgressView has no published minimum width.
U26 UITabBar and HIG Tab bars give no iOS height or item width; tab-bars.json's 68 pt is tvOS. On todo.md:2317-2322.
U27 No published selected-tab colours.
U28 UIMenu spacing and highlight colours are not published.
U29 iOS tables do not alternate row colours.
U30 Same as U15. Table selection is tableCellDefaultSelectionTintColor (209,209,214 / 58,58,60, WebKit baselines L150-154), which is not hover.
U31 No published value.
U32 The iPadOS sidebar background is not published. systemGroupedBackground is #f2f2f7 / #000000 (baselines L54-58).
U33 The popover fill is not published. Dark #1c1c1e equals systemBackground at the elevated level (baseline L10; uiuserinterfacelevel/elevated.json, read 2026-10-11). Light #ffffff is the same at both levels.
U34 No iOS splitter API.
U35 No published colours. WebKit's refreshed switch uses disabled opacity 0.5 (RenderThemeCocoa.mm:415).
U36 The track corner fraction comes from Apple's internal SDK; open-source WebKit sets 0 (RenderThemeCocoa.mm:108-110).
U37 UIAlertController's size is not published. On todo.md:2317-2322.
U38 No stated default; HIG Accessibility only suggests an underline in addition to colour.
U39 No published link-state colours; hover is not a touch state.
U40 UIActivityIndicatorView styles have no published sizes.
U41 Pop-up and pull-down buttons have no published value.
U42 UISegmentedControl metrics and selected-segment colours are not published.
U43 HIG Disclosure controls gives no iOS metrics or colours.
U44 iOS windows have no inactive title bar colours.
U45 UIStackView.spacing defaults to 0.0 (uistackview/spacing.json, read 2026-10-11), which platform-facts treats as (none) in the Windows column; no 8 pt gap is published. On todo.md:2317-2322.
U46 The systemMinimumLayoutMargins doc gives 20 only as an example. On todo.md:2317-2322.
U47 No published value. On todo.md:2317-2322.

## M2d — Material 3 and Material 3 Expressive

**Status:** Steps 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 done 2026-10-11, beside M1 (D7), in the `m2-research` worktree; Step 3 awaits the maintainer; Step 7 not started. One Workflow ran all five parts (41 Opus agents at high effort, 5.41M subagent tokens, 36.5 min). Triage values: *fix* (Step 7), *Step 8* / *Step 13* (the part's build steps, already decided), *maintainer (Step 3 probe)*, *maintainer (version gap)*, *M4* (reader code), *defer* (an existing docs/todo.md entry), *drop*.

**D6's premise does not hold at a stable release, so Step 1's pick is the maintainer's.** The latest stable Compose Material 3
is **1.4.0** (2025-09-24, androidx `5113b82a`); in it `MaterialExpressiveTheme`, `expressiveLightColorScheme` and
`MotionScheme.expressive()` are `internal` and the Expressive components were removed (1.4.0-beta01). They are public only
from **1.5.0-beta01** (2026-10-07, `19991f2c`, not stable; `LoadingIndicator` and `MaterialShapes` still
`@ExperimentalMaterial3ExpressiveApi`). The facts' `1e67768` pin matches 1.5.0-beta01 (tokens and API identical). For
`material-3` the choice barely matters (1.4.0 and 1.5.0-beta01 token values differ only in Checkbox, List, Typography
plumbing and seven new list/menu/chip token files). The token database has no single version: each generated `*Tokens.kt`
file names its own (v0_210, v0_11_0, 14_1_0, …). Every v0_192 colour hex in the column is confirmed and the Compose colour
roles are identical, except Expressive's four light `on-*-container` roles at tone 30. Expressive changes nothing else
through the theme (no component reads `LocalUsingExpressiveTheme`): its look comes from the new opt-in components. All 50
*differs* rows are CONFIRMED: they are what Step 13 re-bases (slider 16 track and 4 x 44 handle, progress
`secondary-container` and round caps, checkbox drawn 20, outlined button `outline-variant`, menu and list paddings, dialog
without shadow or height bounds, spinner 40, select 280, `bodyLarge` 16/24 as the ambient text style).

**Inherited values.** Many values the preset does not set come from rules in inheritance-rules.toml:

- tab.active_background and tab.bar_background come from background_color (:212, :214).
- dialog.border.shadow_enabled comes from defaults.border.shadow_enabled (:94).

**Rows that differ today (Step 2, not yet verified).** Each of the 50 rows is mapped to the preset keys that depend on it, light and dark separately, each as a depends-on-differs-row finding. Rows already contradicted by their own facts cell are also flagged as mismatches:
- 1116: the preset's border.opacity 0.12, against an enabled outline that the cell says is opaque.
- 1133: icon_sizes.small 16, where the cell says no token.
- 1277-1283: scrollbar values the cell lists as (none). Three are stated by the preset (groove_width 12, min_thumb_length 30, overlay_mode false) and two are inherited (track_color, thumb_color). thumb_width 4 is also uncited, but it happens to equal Compose 1.5.

Six rows have no dependent preset key, because the preset does not set the field and no inheritance rule fills it: 1340 and 1341 (sidebar corner radius and shadow), 1391 (list.border.padding_vertical), 1554 (combo_box.arrow_area_width), and 1305 and 1313 only partly (the tab indicator shape and the progress bar's shape are not modelled).

**Other blocking findings.** These values have no source in the facts:
- Status colours: warning, success and info, with their text colours. Row 1082 says M3 has no warning role; rows 1084 and 1086 say none for success and info.
- link_color (row 1054 says none).
- mono_font Roboto Mono 14/400 (rows 1036-1038 say none).
- icon_sizes.large 32 (row 1134 says none).
- checkbox.label_gap 8 (row 1213 says app-defined).
- progress_bar.min_width 100 (row 1304 says app-defined).
- spinner.min_diameter 16 (row 1534 says none).
- scrollbar.thumb_hover_color and thumb_active_color (row 1279 says none).
- splitter.divider_width 4 and hover_color (row 1419: none in v0_192).
- The whole [*.expander] block (rows 1603-1612 say none). Its hover_background uses #1c1b1f / #e6e1e5, which are not this preset's on-surface (#1d1b20 / #e6e0e9).
- The whole [*.link] block (rows 1621-1626 say none).
- The [layout] gaps 6/6/10/18 (rows 1453-1456 say none). They are the shared block copied in tokyo-night, solarized, gruvbox, one-dark, nord, dracula and windows-11.

**Non-blocking.** About 60 platform-facts.md line citations in the preset comments are 1-7 lines stale, pointing at neighbouring rows. About 40 values match the facts but carry no citation comment.

Every key used exists in the registry (checked: radio_indicator_width_px :229, active_indicator_side :324, unchecked_thumb_diameter_px :435, min_diameter_px :471, arrow_area_width_px :485). ### Researcher notes

Each researcher's own notes, verbatim: coverage, method caveats and errors found outside the *differs* rows (wrong citations on ✅ rows, unpinned links). Step 7 corrects the citation errors (S4) as part of the row fixes.

<details><summary>globals</summary>

All 22 v0_192 hex values in scope confirmed against _md-ref-palette.scss. Compose 1.4.0 ColorLight/Dark/PaletteTokens give the same hexes, and these token files have identical values in 1.4.0 and 1.5.0-beta01 (Step 1 diff_s140_b01.txt lists no Color, Palette, TypeScale, Typeface, Elevation, Shape or State change).

Main findings, none of them on docs/todo.md:
(1) 1026/1030: Compose MaterialTheme's ambient text style is bodyLarge 16/24, not body-medium 14/20 (MaterialTheme.kt:107). This is a mapping decision for the maintainer.
(2) 1051/1116: Compose's outlined button uses outline-variant (and disabled outline-variant @0.1), from token set v0_11_0; material-web latest agrees. Fields, select and segmented button keep outline.
(3) 1104-1106: Compose 1.4.0 draws no focus ring; focus is a 0.1 state layer. 1.5.0-beta01 adds an opt-in inset ring (outer secondary 2dp at inset 0, inner onSecondary 3dp at inset 1), default off, and MaterialExpressiveTheme does not enable it.
(4) 1058: Compose has a text-selection colour, primary @ 0.4 (MaterialTheme.kt:218-229).
(5) 1053: Compose shadows are black at Android's platform alphas (ambient 0.039 / spot 0.19), not material-web's 0.3/0.15.
(6) 1133: 'no 16 dp icon token' is false even at v0_192: the switch icon is 16px (_md-comp-switch.scss:76, 122). Compose SwitchTokens:50, 73 agree.
(7) 1056: Expressive light on-secondary-container = #4a4458 (Secondary30). Expressive has no dark scheme (ColorScheme.kt:1166).
(8) 1060/1115: the filled-button citations differ in Compose (FilledButtonTokens v0_11_0: label on-surface-variant @0.38, container @0.1). The tonal button matches the cell values.
(9) 1055: beta01's new selectable menu items use tertiary-container or tertiary, not secondary-container.

Not modelled: Expressive shape morphing (pressed button to CornerSmall 8) and the focus-ring animation specs.

Step 1's version map holds; no pin is wrong. The whole scope (1019-1139) is covered.

</details>

<details><summary>widgets-1</summary>

Scope 2.2-2.15 (lines 1140-1400) fully covered. Every v0_192 / latest / mw-impl / MDC / pin citation in scope was opened and matches its line. Step 1's version map holds. The 1.4.0 colour roles (palette plus light/dark role map) are identical to v0_192, so all L/D hexes hold for the Compose baseline. The Expressive theme changes only 4 light on*Container roles (*30), plus motion. MaterialExpressiveTheme defaults Shapes() and Typography(), and no component reads LocalUsingExpressiveTheme (grep). So Expressive differences come from the new 1.5 composables, not from the theme. A scratch checkout is in .../scratchpad/m2-src/m2d-w2/ (mw full at cbd34a8, mdc files).

Rows where Compose 1.4.0 differs from the cell:
- 1166/1167 (outlined button only): label on-surface-variant, outline outline-variant.
- 1169: min width 58 vs 64.
- 1172: declared vertical padding 8 vs 10. Expressive gives 10.
- 1193: Compose has selection bg primary@0.4 (impl).
- 1212: checkbox drawn 20, not 18. 18 needs ComposeMaterial3Flags.isCheckboxStylingFixEnabled, which is false by default in beta01 too.
- 1228: menu divider outline-variant.
- 1235: menu item padding 12 vs 16.
- 1241: menu icon gap 12 vs 16.
- 1290/1292/1293/1294: Compose baseline slider is the 16 dp track, 4x44 bar, 4 dp ticks, secondary-container spec.
- 1302/1305: progress track secondary-container, round caps.
- 1313: tab indicator corners 3 on all four sides.
- 1315: tab divider outline-variant.
- 1317: icon+label tab 72, not 64.
- 1325: inactive tab label defaults to primary.
- 1334: drawer label bodyLarge (inferred: no text style).
- 1340: standard drawer square.
- 1341: modal drawer has no shadow.
- 1391: list vertical 8.
- Font families: Compose names no typeface (FontFamily.SansSerif).

NEW, not in todo.md: Compose 1.5.0-beta01 has a public non-experimental Modifier.nonInteractiveScrollbar. It has thumb outline@0.7, thickness 4, min thumb 24, transparent track, and fades. So "M3 has no scrollbar" (1277) is true only for 1.4.0 and material-web.

Also new in beta01: an opt-in desktop "precision pointer" density (ComposeMaterial3Flags.isPrecisionPointerComponentSizingEnabled, default false, @ExperimentalMaterial3Api). It changes button MinHeight to 36, small button vertical padding to 8, menu/list paddings to 12, and more. It may matter for a desktop theme.

The beta01 classic ListItem(headlineContent) is @Deprecated. The Expressive ListItem (10 vertical, selected secondary-container) replaces it.

Expressive menus (SegmentedMenuTokens: corner-large 16, item 44, icon 20, group SurfaceContainerLow) come only through new composables.

Not carriable by the model (notes only): button press shape morph, slider thumb gap and press width, progress track gap, stop dot and wavy variants, menu group shapes.

Already on todo.md: radio dot (todo.md:225-244, row 1220) and slider thumb colour (todo.md:787-812, row 1291).

Probe-settleable: 1148-family rows, 1212, 1325, 1334.

Scope 1401-1647 fully covered; 73 rows checked. Every material-web citation in scope was re-read at cbd34a8 and matches (line numbers right; where a cell cites a key line, the value sits on the next line, e.g. switch :135/136, card :34/35, select :82/83). Compose 1.4.0 baseline DIFFERS from the cell in 7 rows:
- 1486 dialog shadow. The token is level3 in both, but Compose's AlertDialog casts no shadow: Surface tonalElevation 0, no shadowElevation, and the window shadow has alpha 0. A probe can confirm.
- 1489 dialog min_height 140: Compose has none.
- 1490 dialog max_height 560: Compose has none; only the width is constrained.
- 1495 title family: Roboto in the cell, FontFamily.SansSerif in Compose. Both are Roboto on Android.
- 1533 spinner diameter: 48 (v0_192) in the cell, 40 in Compose (CircularProgressIndicatorTokens.Size).
- 1551 combobox min_width: 210 in material-web, 280 in Compose (OutlinedTextFieldDefaults.MinWidth).
- 1554 arrow_area_width: (none) in the cell; Compose's trailing slot is a 48 minimum-interactive box.

Expressive (1.5.0-beta01) changes for this scope:
- No component branches on the Expressive theme (LocalUsingExpressiveTheme is used only in MaterialTheme.kt). So Expressive differs only through the 4 light on*Container roles and through new opt-in components.
- 1568 segmented active_text_color light: #4a4458 (Secondary30).
- Menus: the new DropdownMenuPopup/DropdownMenuGroup use surface-container-low, a 16 standalone corner, 2 vertical padding and level2. Their group shapes morph on hover, which the model cannot carry.
- Spinner: CircularWavyProgressIndicator is 48 with a 4 stroke; its wave cannot be carried. LoadingIndicator (48/38, shape morphing) is still experimental.
- Text scale: unchanged, because MaterialExpressiveTheme defaults to Typography().
- The Expressive alternative to the segmented button is the connected ButtonGroup (ConnectedButtonGroupSmallTokens: BetweenSpace 2, height 40). SegmentedButton is not deprecated in Compose beta01.

New, not on docs/todo.md:
- beta01 adds ComposeMaterial3Flags.isPrecisionPointerComponentSizingEnabled (default false, ComposeMaterial3Flags.kt:66). It is a denser desktop/pointer sizing: dialog padding 20, title 20/26, text padding 16; menu icon-text gap 12; it also touches Button, ToggleButton and ListItem. It is not in 1.4.0, and it may matter for a desktop preset.
- In 1.4.0, TextButtonTokens.LabelColor is OnSurfaceVariant, but the impl hard-codes Primary with a TODO (Button.kt:783-784). Today's text button colour depends on that TODO.
- beta01 dialog ButtonsCrossAxisSpacing is 8 (1.4.0: 12).
- Compose VerticalDragHandle does not use the DragHandleTokens.ContainerWidth 24 token; its interactive area is 48.

No cell needs a ❓. Scratch: m2-src/m2d-s2c/ (mw clone, raw/), scripts in m2d-s2c-scripts/colors.py.

</details>

  gnome-settings-daemon writes `Xft.dpi` = 96 × `text-scaling-factor` × the X11 UI scale
  (`gsd-xsettings-manager.c:583-595`, `:665-668`, `:797-798`), the reader reported it as
  `font_dpi` and reported the factor too, and the connectors multiply by the factor: 2.25× at
  1.5. Fixed: GNOME's font DPI is 96 (gsd's `DPI_FALLBACK`; GTK on Wayland lays fonts out at 96 ×
  factor, `gdksettings-wayland.c:166-168`), in the reader and in
  `ResolutionContext::from_system()` on GNOME and Budgie. A resolve-time multiply would now be
  single on both desktops on Wayland; X11 and Xwayland clients also get the factor through the
  toolkit's `Xft.dpi` scale factor (fix round 1, below). The KDE reader's `Xft.dpi` fallback on Wayland is the display scale
  (krdb `:333-337`), for M4 with Plasma 6.8's removal of `forceFontDPI` (docs/todo.md's

### Entries

#### M3-01 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/resolve/inheritance.rs:261
**Claim:** A `color` that a preset, an app TOML overlay or the KDE reader sets under `[light.link.font]` is always thrown away: resolve() replaces it with `defaults.link_color`, so a stated link text colour never reaches the Resolved theme.
**Evidence:** inheritance.rs:261-263 runs `if let Some(ref mut font) = self.link.font { font.color = self.defaults.link_color; }` with no `is_none()` guard. Every other inheritance rule fills only a None field: the generated font fill at native-theme-derive/src/gen_inherit.rs:278-280 (`if font.color.is_none()`), and the widget-to-widget rules at inheritance.rs:288-341. The rule documents say "None sub-fields inherit independently" and give link.font.color an inheritance source (docs/inheritance-rules.toml:111-112, :145, :286-287). Nothing says it overrides a stated value, and no archive rationale records an overwrite. Overlays are merged before resolve (lib.rs:595-606), so they hit this too. The KDE reader writes `variant.link.font...color = ForegroundLink` (kde/colors.rs:247-250); the overwrite hides that write only because the reader also sets defaults.link_color from the same key (colors.rs:128). No test covers a stated value; the test at inheritance.rs:1209-1231 starts from link.font with color None. A test that fails today: `let mut v = ThemeMode::default(); v.defaults.link_color = Some(Rgba::rgb(0,0,255)); v.link.font = Some(FontSpec { color: Some(Rgba::rgb(255,0,0)), ..Default::default() }); v.resolve(); assert_eq!(v.link.font.unwrap().color, Some(Rgba::rgb(255,0,0)));`. Today the color is (0,0,255).
**Fix (reviewer):** Before `self.link.resolve_font_from_defaults(d)`, read whether link.font.color was stated, and write `defaults.link_color` only when it was None. That makes the rule a None-fill like every other rule, and it stays idempotent.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — inheritance.rs:261-263 assigns `font.color = self.defaults.link_color` unconditionally, while the generated font inherit only fills a None color (gen_inherit.rs:278-279), so a stated link.font.color is always overwritten. The rule in inheritance-rules.toml:287 describes inheritance, not an override. Impact today is narrower than S1 suggests: no bundled preset sets [*.link.font] color, and the KDE reader writes the same ForegroundLink to both fields (kde/colors.rs:128, :248-249). Only app overlays and custom TOML lose a value.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug; severity lowered from the reviewer's S1 by the session: the KDE reader fills both values from `Colors:View ForegroundLink` (kde/colors.rs:128, :248), so no shipped preset or reader shows a difference; only an overlay or preset author who states `link.font.color` loses it
**Status:** fixed in 21b87466 (T7); the KDE reader's redundant link.font.color write removed in dfb947b9 (final fix wave I1)

#### M3-02 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/model/mod.rs:267
**Claim:** An overlay TOML with no `name` key, such as the documented `[light.defaults] accent_color = "#ff6600"`, fails `Theme::from_toml` with `missing field "name"`, although `Theme::merge` throws the overlay's name away anyway.
**Evidence:** `Theme` derives `Deserialize` with no struct-level `#[serde(default)]` (mod.rs:259-260), and `pub name: Cow<'static, str>` (mod.rs:267) has no field attribute. Serde's derive therefore calls `missing_field` for a non-Option field, which is an error. `from_toml` is `toml::from_str` and nothing more (presets.rs:314-316). `Theme::merge` keeps the base name ('Keep base name (do not overwrite)', mod.rs:338), so an overlay's `name` is never read. The `from_toml` doc says 'Every field is optional -- omit any field you don't need' (mod.rs:558-559). The `SystemTheme::with_overlay` example (lib.rs:545-552) and the README's 'Apply an overlay to the OS theme at runtime' (native-theme/README.md:94-100) both parse an overlay with no `name`. Both are `no_run`, so they compile but never execute, and nothing catches the failure. A test to write: `assert!(Theme::from_toml("[light.defaults]\naccent_color = \"#ff6600\"").is_ok());` fails today.
**Fix (reviewer):** Put `#[serde(default)]` on `name`; the empty `Cow::Borrowed("")` matches `impl Default for Theme` at mod.rs:320. Then add a test that parses a nameless overlay and merges it.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — `Theme.name` (model/mod.rs:267) has no `#[serde(default)]`, there is none on the struct, and `presets::from_toml` (presets.rs:314-316) is a plain `toml::from_str`. So the name-less overlays in the docs fail at run time: lib.rs:547-552 and native-theme/README.md:96-100 are both `no_run`, so the doctests never catch it. `Theme::merge` drops the overlay's name anyway (model/mod.rs:338). No entry for it in todo.md or the ledger.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug
**Status:** fixed in ce71649f

#### M3-03 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/model/widgets/mod.rs:1028
**Claim:** `LayoutTheme` declares `check = "non_negative"` on all four fields, but that check never runs, so `[layout] widget_gap_px = -8.0` (or `nan`) reaches the connectors unvalidated.
**Evidence:** widgets/mod.rs:1030-1044 has `#[theme(check = "non_negative")]` on widget_gap, container_margin, window_margin and section_gap. The derive generates `ResolvedLayoutTheme::validate_widget` and `check_ranges` (gen_validate.rs:23-38 under `#[allow(dead_code)]`; gen_ranges.rs:20-30), but no code calls either one. rg for `ResolvedLayoutTheme`, `layout.check_ranges` and a `validate_widget` on layout finds nothing outside the generated code. `Theme::resolve_with` never reads `self.layout` (mod.rs:492-516), and `Resolved` has no layout field (resolved.rs:258-273). The pipeline passes on `merged.layout.clone()` raw (pipeline.rs:96) as `SystemTheme::layout: LayoutTheme` (lib.rs:493). Consumers then take it as it is: gpui `geometry::widget_gap` and `window_margin` return `layout.widget_gap.map(px)` (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/geometry.rs:1045-1058). Only egui sanitises it on its own side (style/base.rs:284-286). A test to write: `Theme::from_toml("name=\"x\"\n[layout]\nwidget_gap_px = -8.0")`, merged onto a preset; through `SystemTheme` or the `Theme` path no Err appears, and `layout.widget_gap == Some(-8.0)`.
**Fix (reviewer):** Treat the layout fields as soft options and run their range check wherever a theme is resolved (`Theme::resolve_with` and `run_pipeline`/`with_overlay`), returning `ResolutionInvalid` with path `layout.widget_gap`. Otherwise drop the dead attributes and the unused `ResolvedLayoutTheme`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The `non_negative` checks on `LayoutTheme` (widgets/mod.rs:1031-1043) generate a `check_ranges` that nothing calls. validate.rs:166-193 has no layout entry, and pipeline.rs:94 and lib.rs:572 copy `merged.layout` straight into `SystemTheme.layout` (lib.rs:493), so the connectors read the raw `Option<f32>`. The todo.md:874 item only describes `LayoutTheme` as public; it does not record the gap.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug; run the generated range check (the layout values are stated, never inherited), not drop the attributes
**Status:** fixed in a2515313 and 828d2d2a (layout check hand-written, public types unchanged)

#### M3-04 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/resolve/validate.rs:192
**Claim:** No range check runs on the card. A theme TOML with `[light.card.border] padding_left_px = -8` (or `nan`, or `inf`) passes validation, and the bad value reaches `ResolvedTheme.card.border.padding`.
**Evidence:** validate.rs:156 builds `card` and :228 puts it into ResolvedTheme. The range-check block at :169-194 calls check_ranges on every widget except `card`. `git log -S card.check_ranges` finds no commit, so the call was never there. The derive emits `ResolvedCardTheme::check_ranges` for every widget (native-theme-derive/src/lib.rs:83). For the card's nested `border: ResolvedWidgetBorder` (model/widgets/mod.rs:924-925), that method holds an automatic check_padding call (gen_ranges.rs:127-141), which validate_helpers.rs:461-485 implements. The padding check came with 24da5c1e. Before that commit the card had nothing to range-check, so its missing call did no harm. The same gap is in the happy-path test, which skips the card (resolve/tests.rs:2359-2387).
**Fix (reviewer):** Add `card.check_ranges("card", &mut range_errors);` between segmented_control and expander. Add a test that a negative card padding side gives ResolutionInvalid with the path `card.border.padding_left`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — validate.rs:156 builds `card`, but the check_ranges list at validate.rs:170-194 has no `card.check_ranges` call (grep finds none anywhere). The derived check_padding for card.border (gen_ranges.rs:127-139) therefore never runs, and a negative, NaN or inf card padding reaches ResolvedTheme. Also reported by R1-model (native-theme/src/resolve/validate.rs:192; CONFIRMED).
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug; with the regression test `check_ranges_happy_path_zero_errors` extended to `card` and `text_area`
**Status:** fixed in a2515313 and 828d2d2a (layout check hand-written, public types unchanged)

#### M3-05 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/model/border.rs:93
**Claim:** A widget border's own `corner_radius_px` or `line_width_px` is never range-checked, so `[light.button.border] corner_radius_px = -4.0` or `line_width_px = nan` resolves Ok and reaches `ResolvedWidgetBorder`.
**Evidence:** `WidgetBorderSpec.corner_radius` and `line_width` (border.rs:93, :95) arrive from `corner_radius_px`/`line_width_px` with no check (border.rs:160-163). For Full and Partial kinds, `validate_border` only `require`s them (validate_helpers.rs:301-327); for the None kind (menu, tab, card) it does `unwrap_or_default` (:282-284). For a nested `ResolvedWidgetBorder`, the derive emits only `check_padding` (gen_ranges.rs:127-141), never a check on corner_radius or line_width. `check_defaults_ranges` checks only `defaults.border.*` (validate_helpers.rs:670-688). So inheritance from defaults is safe, but a value stated on the widget is not. A test to write: kde-breeze light with `v.button.border.get_or_insert_default().corner_radius = Some(-4.0)` gives `into_resolved(&ResolutionContext::for_tests())` Ok and `button.border.corner_radius == -4.0`.
**Fix (reviewer):** Have gen_ranges emit `check_non_negative` for `.corner_radius` and `.line_width` of every nested `ResolvedWidgetBorder`, next to `check_padding`, with paths `{prefix}.border.corner_radius` and `{prefix}.border.line_width`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — For a nested `ResolvedWidgetBorder`, gen_ranges.rs:127-141 emits only `check_padding`. `validate_border` (validate_helpers.rs:271-343) copies `corner_radius` and `line_width` without checking them, and `check_defaults_ranges` covers only the defaults border. So an explicit `-4.0` or `nan` on a widget border resolves Ok. The same archived egui spec line (:7768) records it as a known gap, not as intended. Also reported by R2-resolution (native-theme/src/resolve/validate_helpers.rs:461; CONFIRMED). Also reported by R4-presets-derive (native-theme-derive/src/gen_ranges.rs:311; CONFIRMED).
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug
**Status:** fixed in a2515313 and 828d2d2a (layout check hand-written, public types unchanged)

#### M3-06 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/resolve/validate_helpers.rs:708
**Claim:** `defaults.focus_ring_offset_px = nan` (or `inf`) in a theme TOML passes validation, because focus_ring_offset is the one defaults f32 with no check at all. It is meant to allow negative values, but non-finite ones get through as well.
**Evidence:** validate.rs:71-76 extracts focus_ring_offset. check_defaults_ranges skips it on purpose (validate_helpers.rs:708-709), because a negative value means an inset ring. That comment justifies allowing negatives, not NaN or infinity, and every other defaults f32 is checked for finiteness (:656-759). The value reaches the public accessor `native_theme_egui::focus_ring_offset(t)` raw (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/accessors.rs:95). egui's plugin works around the gap with its own non-finite guard (plugin.rs:13-37, the test `a_zero_negative_or_non_finite_ring_is_none` at :353). That shows the core does not guarantee a finite value.
**Fix (reviewer):** Reject non-finite values only: add a `check_finite(value, prefix, field, errors)` helper (RangeViolation with min/max None) and call it for `defaults.focus_ring_offset`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — validate_helpers.rs:708-709 deliberately skips focus_ring_offset to allow negative values, and no other finiteness check covers it (is_finite appears only at :362, :382, :404, :475). TOML `nan` and `inf` deserialize into f32, so they pass. An is_finite-only check would keep the negative case. Also reported by R1-model (native-theme/src/model/defaults.rs:122; CONFIRMED).
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug; a finiteness check only, negative values stay legal as documented
**Status:** fixed in a2515313 and 828d2d2a (layout check hand-written, public types unchanged)

#### M3-07 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/model/font.rs:331
**Claim:** Merging an overlay `[light.text_scale.caption] size_px = 12.0` onto `ios` (which states `size_pt` plus `line_height_pt`) gives an entry that `to_toml` writes and `from_toml` then rejects, so a saved merged theme cannot be loaded again.
**Evidence:** `TryFrom<TextScaleEntryRaw>` rejects a table whose size and line_height use different suffixes (font.rs:331-338). `TextScaleEntry`'s merge is per field (`option { size, weight, line_height }`, font.rs:369-371; impl_merge lib.rs:53-56), and `TextScale` merges entries through `optional_nested` (font.rs:391-393; lib.rs:66-71). ios.toml:63-66 states `size_pt = 12.0`, `line_height_pt = 14.4`. After the merge the entry holds `size: Px(12.0)` and `line_height: Pt(14.4)`. `From<TextScaleEntry> for TextScaleEntryRaw` writes `size_px` and `line_height_pt` (font.rs:349-365), and parsing that output hits the error at :334-336. Validation itself converts each value on its own (validate_helpers.rs:214-223), so the mixed state renders correctly. Only the parse-time rule breaks.
**Fix (reviewer):** The model handles mixed units, so drop the same-suffix rule at font.rs:331-338. If the rule must stay, enforce it in `TextScaleEntry::merge` (an overlay size in the other unit clears or converts the base line_height), and add a test that runs to_toml then from_toml after such a merge.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — ios.toml:63-66 states `size_pt` and `line_height_pt`. `impl_merge!` (font.rs:368-370) merges per field, so the result holds `size: Px` with `line_height: Pt`. `From<TextScaleEntry>` (:343-365) writes `size_px` and `line_height_pt`, and `TryFrom` rejects that pair (:331-339), so a merged theme cannot be read back. No todo.md or ledger entry.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug
**Status:** fixed in df0f0691

#### M3-08 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/pipeline.rs:712
**Claim:** On a KDE desktop (XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=KDE) with the `kde` feature off, which is the default since native-theme has no default features, from_system returns a mixed theme: the active variant has Adwaita colours, the inactive variant is full Breeze, `preset` is "kde-breeze", `name` is "Adwaita" and the icon theme is "breeze". lib.rs:643-645 documents the adwaita preset for this case.
**Evidence:** select_reader, LinuxDesktop::Kde arm with cfg(not(feature = "kde")): `return None` (pipeline.rs:615). from_system_inner then takes the Linux fallback: `let preset = linux_preset_for_de(detect_linux_desktop()).name;` gives "kde-breeze" (pipeline.rs:712, 343), and `run_pipeline(preset_as_reader("adwaita", mode)?, preset, mode)` (pipeline.rs:713). In run_pipeline the base is full_preset = kde-breeze (pipeline.rs:35). The reader is Adwaita's active variant, merged on top (:42-43). The inactive variant comes unmerged from `full_preset.light/dark` (pipeline.rs:103/109), i.e. Breeze. The name comes from the reader, "Adwaita" (:46-50). Tier 1 of the icon theme stays kde-breeze.toml:9 "breeze", because Adwaita's variant leaves `defaults.icon_theme` None and to_theme drops Adwaita's Theme-level "Adwaita" (lib.rs:392). This is a regression from 66423ae7: before it the arm was `run_pipeline(preset_as_reader("adwaita", mode)?, "adwaita-live", mode)` (git show 66423ae7^:native-theme/src/pipeline.rs). Test to write, in the pipeline's test module: `let st = run_pipeline(preset_as_reader("adwaita", Light)?, linux_preset_for_de(LinuxDesktop::Kde).name, Light)?;` then assert st.dark equals adwaita's resolved dark variant. It fails today: st.dark is Breeze dark.
**Fix (reviewer):** Give the fallback one preset as both reader and merge base. One way is `preset_as_reader(preset, mode)` with `preset` from linux_preset_for_de (a full Breeze theme on KDE); the other is preset "adwaita" as lib.rs:643-645 documents (the behaviour before 66423ae7). Then add the test above.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — With kde off, select_reader returns None for Kde (pipeline.rs:648-649), and the fallback runs preset_as_reader("adwaita") over linux_preset_for_de(Kde)="kde-breeze" (pipeline.rs:712-713). run_pipeline then keeps the full Breeze inactive variant (:99-111), name "Adwaita" (:46-50), preset "kde-breeze" (:137), and tier-1 icon_theme "breeze" from kde-breeze.toml:9, because Adwaita states its icon theme only at the top level (adwaita.toml:5). This contradicts lib.rs:643-645. Commit a3cb768d passed "adwaita-live" here, so this is a regression from the select_reader refactor.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug
**Status:** fixed in b345f5fd and 2bb1bef3 (docs: the portal answer decides an unknown desktop either way)

#### M3-09 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/pipeline.rs:707
**Claim:** On desktops with no reader (XFCE, Cinnamon, MATE, LXQt, Sway, Hyprland, niri, COSMIC, Unknown, or KDE/GNOME built without their feature), a second from_system after the user toggles dark mode returns the old `mode`. The fallback reads the cached `system_is_dark()`, while every reader branch reads the mode fresh.
**Evidence:** Fallback branch: `let mode = if system_is_dark() {...}` (pipeline.rs:707). system_is_dark is `system().is_dark()`, cached until invalidate_caches (detect.rs:140-142). For comparison: the macOS reader fills is_dark from the uncached `detect_is_dark()` (macos.rs:602, the F5 decision), the GNOME reader from the portal color-scheme on each read (gnome/mod.rs:410), Windows from UISettings on each read (windows.rs:449). These desktops have no watcher either: watch/mod.rs:243-244 returns WatchUnavailable for them. So an app can only poll from_system or reload it by hand, and it gets the first mode for the whole process. from_system's doc says it 'reads the current theme settings' (lib.rs:626-628) and does not mention a cache. Test to write: `system().is_dark` seeded with false via the cache, the OS dark, and from_system_inner on a fallback desktop still returns Light. The pure form is a run_pipeline helper that takes the mode from detect_is_dark.
**Fix (reviewer):** Use `crate::detect::detect_is_dark()` (uncached) in the fallback, as the macOS reader does. Alternatively, document on from_system that the fallback mode is cached until `invalidate_caches()`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The fallback reads the cached system_is_dark() (pipeline.rs:707, detect.rs:140), while readers read the mode fresh, and M1-T6-01's cost check asked for uncached reads so a re-read is fresh. The impact is limited: detect.rs:121-123 documents invalidate_caches() before re-reading, and every in-tree watcher already calls it (egui watch.rs:99, all showcases). Only callers who skip that step get the old mode.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug (the verifier's note on its limited impact recorded; the fix is a fresh read in the fallback, matching the readers)
**Status:** fixed in b345f5fd and 2bb1bef3 (docs: the portal answer decides an unknown desktop either way)

#### M3-10 · bug · S2 · native-theme/src/lib.rs:613
**Claim:** `sys.with_overlay(&a)?.with_overlay(&b)?` silently drops overlay `a`: each call replays from the reader output and the preset only, and the returned SystemTheme carries the base overlay_source unchanged.
**Evidence:** with_overlay rebuilds from `self.overlay_source` (lib.rs:560-569), applies only the `overlay` argument (lib.rs:596-601), and returns `overlay_source: self.overlay_source.clone()` (lib.rs:613). OverlaySource has no field for applied overlays (lib.rs:403-420). The second call therefore starts again from reader + preset, and `a`'s fields are lost; nothing in the doc (lib.rs:534-557) says a call replaces earlier overlays. Test to write: build `st = run_pipeline(reader_from_preset("adwaita"), "adwaita", Light)?`. Overlay a = `[light.defaults] accent_color = "#ff0000"`, overlay b = `[light.defaults] background_color = "#00ff00"`. Assert `st.with_overlay(&a)?.with_overlay(&b)?.light.defaults.accent_color == Rgba::rgb(255,0,0)`. It fails: the accent is Adwaita's. This is separate from the known todo.md:339 entry (icon_theme/icon_set/layout of a single overlay).
**Fix (reviewer):** Keep the accumulated overlay in OverlaySource (an `Option<Theme>` merged with each new overlay, `Theme::merge` already supports this) and replay it before the new one. Alternatively, document that each call replaces any earlier overlay.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — with_overlay replays from self.overlay_source, which holds only the reader output and the preset (lib.rs:559-586), and copies overlay_source unchanged into the result (lib.rs:613). The second call therefore never sees overlay a. No doc says that overlays do not stack, and no test chains two overlays (merge_behavior.rs:206 chains Theme::merge only). It is not in docs/todo.md, whose :339 entry covers the icon theme only.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug; grouped with M3-41 (one replay function serves both)
**Status:** fixed in c3ed1f4f

#### M3-11 · api · api-break · native-theme/src/model/font.rs:137
**Claim:** `impl Default for FontSize` returns `Px(0.0)`, a size that validation always rejects; nothing uses it outside its own test, and the project removed `Rgba::default()` for the same reason.
**Evidence:** font.rs:137-141. rg for `FontSize::default` finds only the test at font.rs:756. `FontSpec.size` and `TextScaleEntry.size`/`line_height` are `Option<FontSize>` (font.rs:168, :290, :295), so their derived `Default` impls don't need it. A zero size fails `check_positive` (validate_helpers.rs:652, gen_ranges.rs:152). color.rs:54-59 records the G1 decision that a silent zero Default is a footgun.
**Fix (reviewer):** Delete `impl Default for FontSize` and its test (pre-1.0, so the break is acceptable).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The only caller of `FontSize::default()` is its own test (font.rs:756). The derived `Default`s hold `Option<FontSize>`, and the derive crate and validate_helpers never need it. docs/archive/v0.5.7_native-theme-api.md:2787 already named `Px(0.0)` as a cause of spurious errors. Removing it is cheap and fits 0.7.0's existing breaking changes, so it is worth doing. Also reported by API-native-theme (native-theme/src/model/font.rs:137; CONFIRMED).
**Triage:** maintainer: approved 2026-10-11 (one AskUserQuestion round, the recommended option): remove
**Status:** fixed in e60575e0 (breaking, approved); connectors adopt `Resolved.mode` in M5–M7

#### M3-12 · api · api-break · native-theme/src/presets.rs:101
**Claim:** `PresetInfo` is a public struct with all-pub fields and no `#[non_exhaustive]`. Its `light_only` field can never be true.
**Evidence:** presets.rs:101-113: `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct PresetInfo { pub key, pub display_name, pub platforms, pub light_only }`, re-exported at lib.rs:153. Every PRESET_INFOS entry sets `light_only: false` (:125-216). tests/preset_loading.rs:21-31 requires both variants in every preset, and no code reads the field (grep `light_only` in connectors and native-theme/src finds only the definition and docs at model/mod.rs:679). M1's adopted P0/P1 decisions add per-generation metadata (first and last-verified version, findings ledger :295-297), and PresetInfo is where that would go, but adding a field to it is a breaking change today. Elsewhere the workspace marks such structs `#[non_exhaustive]` (Resolved* via gen_structs.rs:30, DiagnosticEntry, IconData). `platforms` are free strings matched with `starts_with` (:308), so `"linux"` matching `"linux-kde"` is an unstated prefix rule.
**Fix (reviewer):** In 0.7.0 (already breaking): add `#[non_exhaustive]` and drop `light_only`, or give it a meaning a test checks. Optionally document the prefix rule for `platforms`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — PresetInfo has all-pub fields and no #[non_exhaustive] (presets.rs:101-113). Every entry sets light_only: false (:119-217), and all_presets_have_both_variants requires a dark variant in every preset. grep finds no reader of the field in native-theme/src or the connectors. The change pays for itself now: 0.7.0 is already a breaking release (M1), so dropping light_only and adding #[non_exhaustive] costs nothing extra, and later field additions stop being breaking.
**Triage:** maintainer: approved 2026-10-11 (one AskUserQuestion round, the recommended option): drop `light_only`, add `#[non_exhaustive]`
**Status:** fixed in e60575e0 (breaking, approved); connectors adopt `Resolved.mode` in M5–M7

#### M3-13 · api · api-break · native-theme/src/model/resolved.rs:72
**Claim:** The hand-written resolved types (`ResolvedTheme`, `ResolvedDefaults`, `ResolvedTextScale(Entry)`, `ResolvedIconSizes`, `ResolvedFontSpec`, `ResolvedDefaultsBorder`, `ResolvedWidgetBorder`, `ResolvedPadding`, `Resolved`) lack the `#[non_exhaustive]` that every generated `Resolved*Theme` carries, so adding a defaults field breaks downstream code while adding a widget field does not.
**Evidence:** gen_structs.rs:29-30 emits `#[non_exhaustive]` on each generated resolved widget struct, which is the design in docs/archive/v0.5.7_native-theme-api-2.md:718. resolved.rs:14, :36, :53, :71, :157, :257, font.rs:241 and border.rs:202, :219, :242 carry no such attribute. One downstream construction exists: egui builds a `ResolvedWidgetBorder` literal (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/style/roles.rs:338), and egui tests build `ResolvedPadding` (install_tests.rs:1563, :1602).
**Fix (reviewer):** Mark the hand-written resolved structs `#[non_exhaustive]`, with a `ResolvedWidgetBorder`/`ResolvedPadding` constructor for egui's one literal. Otherwise record in the rationale why defaults-level types are exempt.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Only gen_structs.rs:30 emits `#[non_exhaustive]`; the hand-written structs (resolved.rs:15/37/54/72/158/258, border.rs:203/220/243, font.rs:242) have none. Adding it pays off for the output-only types (`ResolvedTheme`, `ResolvedDefaults`, `ResolvedTextScale`, `ResolvedTextScaleEntry`, `ResolvedIconSizes`, `Resolved`, both border types). `ResolvedPadding` and `ResolvedFontSpec`, though, are built with struct literals outside the crate (gpui geometry.rs:329, :703; showcase-gpui app.rs:1240, :1249), so those two would need constructors first.
**Triage:** maintainer: approved 2026-10-11 (one AskUserQuestion round, the recommended option): `#[non_exhaustive]` on the output-only structs; `ResolvedWidgetBorder` and `ResolvedPadding` stay constructible (egui builds them)
**Status:** fixed in e60575e0 (breaking, approved); connectors adopt `Resolved.mode` in M5–M7

#### M3-14 · api · api-break · native-theme/src/lib.rs:246
**Claim:** AccessibilityPreferences is a public struct with all-public fields and no #[non_exhaustive]. Any accessibility flag added later (the receiver work of M1-T6-03) breaks every downstream struct literal, which the egui connector already uses.
**Evidence:** `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct AccessibilityPreferences { pub text_scaling_factor, pub reduce_motion, pub high_contrast, pub reduce_transparency }` (lib.rs:246-257). Literal construction appears at connectors/native-theme-egui/src/install_tests.rs:49, :1675, :2153, :2447 and others.

**Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE — The fact holds: lib.rs:246-257 has public fields and no #[non_exhaustive]. The payoff is weak, though. M1-T6-03's decision (findings :680) adds a method and doc receiver tables, not a field. The project makes no compatibility promise before 1.0, and 0.7.0 already breaks. Adding the attribute would forbid both struct literals and ..Default::default() downstream, so it would need a const constructor for gpui's static UNSCALED (gpui lib.rs:725) and edits to dozens of connector tests. It is worth doing only if a new flag is actually planned (high contrast is an M2 decision).
**Triage:** maintainer: approved 2026-10-11 (one AskUserQuestion round, the recommended option): `#[non_exhaustive]`, callers outside the crate use `Default` plus field assignment
**Status:** fixed in 0beec967 (breaking, approved; `AccessibilityPreferences::DEFAULT` added)

#### M3-15 · api · api-break · native-theme/src/model/resolved.rs:258
**Claim:** `Resolved` does not record which variant it holds, so a `ColorMode::Dark` request on a light-only theme returns the light variant with nothing to tell it apart, and the gpui connector infers dark/light from background lightness with a documented misfire.
**Evidence:** model/mod.rs:372-378 `pick_variant`: `ColorMode::Dark => self.dark.as_ref().or(self.light.as_ref())`; `resolve_with` :497 calls it and builds `Resolved { variant, icon_set, icon_theme, icon_theme_explicit }` at :510-515 with no mode; resolved.rs:258-273 has the four fields only. connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:380-396 `is_dark_resolved` derives the mode from `background_color` lightness, its doc: "Some presets (e.g. solarized, gruvbox) have borderline values where the auto-detected result may differ from the user's intent"; gpui `from_preset` (:291-305) hands the requested `is_dark` to `to_theme` whatever variant `into_variant` fell back to; egui ext.rs:192-196 comments that it relies on the fallback for one-variant presets. Nothing constructs `Resolved` by literal outside `resolve_with` (grep: resolved.rs:258 and mod.rs:510 only), so adding a field breaks no caller.
**Fix (reviewer):** Before: `pub struct Resolved { pub variant: ResolvedTheme, pub icon_set: IconSet, pub icon_theme: Option<Cow<'static, str>>, pub icon_theme_explicit: bool }`. After: `pub struct Resolved { pub mode: ColorMode, /* the variant actually resolved: Dark iff `self.dark` was used */ pub variant: ResolvedTheme, pub icon_set: IconSet, pub icon_theme: Option<Cow<'static, str>>, pub icon_theme_explicit: bool }`, set in `resolve_with` from which `Option` `pick_variant` took (split `pick_variant` into a `pub(crate)` helper returning `(ColorMode, &ThemeMode)`), and documented beside the cross-fallback at mod.rs:363-366.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — `Resolved` (model/resolved.rs:258-273) has no mode field, and pick_variant falls back silently (model/mod.rs:374-375). As a result gpui's `from_preset(name, true)` passes is_dark=true into to_theme with a light palette for a light-only preset (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:293-304). Callers can already check `theme.dark.is_none()` or `PresetInfo::light_only` before resolving, so the extra field mainly pays for connectors.
**Triage:** maintainer: approved 2026-10-11 (one AskUserQuestion round, the recommended option); reclassified api-add → api-break by the session: `Resolved` has public fields and no `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a new field breaks struct literals (it gets the attribute with M3-13)
**Status:** fixed in e60575e0 (breaking, approved); connectors adopt `Resolved.mode` in M5–M7 **M5:** iced in T4 (38048882, 707ba7df): `from_preset` sets `Extended::is_dark` from `Resolved.mode`, `from_system` and `to_iced_theme` from `SystemTheme::mode`; the public `to_theme` keeps iced's lightness test, a `ResolvedTheme` carrying no mode (a mode-taking public builder is a docs/todo.md item); gpui and egui in M6/M7.

**Claim:** `native_theme::theme` and `native_theme::model` are the same public namespace, so a docs.rs reader following any README path (`native_theme::theme::Theme`) lands on a `theme` page that lists no items and is sent to `model::*`, and every model type is reachable by four paths.

The built rustdoc (target/doc/native_theme/theme/index.html, built 2026-10-11 08:15, after the last change to lib.rs/prelude.rs/model/mod.rs at 25d69ceb 06:32) renders the `theme` page as two Re-exports lines, `pub use crate::presets::PresetInfo;` and `pub use crate::model::*;`, with no items, and its four docblock links point at `../model/struct.Theme.html` etc.; glob re-exports of a public module are not inlined. Usage outside the crate: 387 `native_theme::theme::` paths in connectors and tests against one `native_theme::model::` (native-theme/tests/reader_kde.rs:11). The recorded design (docs/archive/v0.5.7_native-theme-api.md:1412-1414) is one `theme` module holding the data-model types, not two.

After: `mod model;` (private) with `pub mod theme { pub use crate::model::{ColorMode, Theme, ThemeMode, ThemeDefaults, Resolved, ResolvedTheme, /* the explicit list now at model/mod.rs:59-83 */}; pub use crate::model::widgets::*; pub use crate::presets::PresetInfo; }`, the twelve sub-modules `pub(crate) mod`, so rustdoc inlines the types under `theme`. The only pub item not in the re-export list, `model::icons::detect_icon_theme` (icons.rs:588), needs a `theme` re-export or demotion (M4's icon call); update tests/reader_kde.rs:11 and the `theme` doc line.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — lib.rs:111 `pub mod model` and lib.rs:151-154 `pub mod theme { pub use crate::model::*; pub use crate::presets::PresetInfo; }`. Rustdoc does not inline a glob re-export of a public module, so the `theme` page shows only the two `pub use` lines. Types in a public submodule (for example `FontSize`, model/mod.rs:47,71) are reachable at model::FontSize, model::font::FontSize, theme::FontSize and theme::font::FontSize. Not recorded in todo.md or the ledger.

#### M3-17 · api · api-break · native-theme/src/error.rs:106
**Claim:** `Theme::from_file(path)` on a missing or unreadable file returns `Error::Io(io::Error)` with no path, displayed as "I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)".

After: `Io { path: std::path::PathBuf, source: std::io::Error }`, built in `presets::from_file` as `Error::Io { path: path.as_ref().to_path_buf(), source }`, Display "cannot read theme file `{path}`: {source}", `source()` unchanged, `kind()` unchanged, the blanket `From` removed; update the tests at error.rs:575-585 and presets.rs:493.

Adding the path is a breaking change to the variant's shape, but pre-1.0 it pays off for anyone loading user theme files.

#### M3-20 · api · api-add · native-theme/src/resolve/validate_helpers.rs:83
**Claim:** The paths that validation errors name are the model's Rust field names, not the TOML keys a theme author writes, and they carry no variant. `[dark.button] min_height_px = -1` is reported as `button.min_height`, and a missing `defaults.icon_sizes.toolbar_px` as `defaults.icon_sizes.toolbar`.
**Evidence:** Paths are built from `ident.to_string()` and stringify! (native-theme-derive/src/gen_validate.rs:27, :58-104; gen_ranges.rs:43; validate_helpers.rs:568-606; check_padding's doc at :458-460 says it names "the model's side fields"). The serialized keys carry the `_px` suffix (model/defaults.rs:118-121, model/icon_sizes.rs:15-27, border.rs:113-121). The registry is keyed by those serialized names (resolve/mod.rs:22-28). The pipeline and with_overlay return a variant's error unwrapped (pipeline.rs:115-116, lib.rs:605-606), so an overlay error does not say whether light or dark failed. Theme::resolve takes an explicit mode, so it is unaffected.
**Fix (reviewer):** Have the derive emit the serde key (it already knows the renames for WidgetFieldInfo) in missing and range paths, and prefix pipeline and with_overlay errors with `light.` or `dark.`. Or document that paths are model paths, not TOML keys.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Range paths come from the field ident (gen_ranges.rs:43, `field_name = ident.to_string()`), so `min_height` is reported where the TOML key is `min_height_px` (widgets/mod.rs:56-58). check_padding names `padding_left` (validate_helpers.rs:458-478), and RangeViolation and ResolutionIncomplete carry no light/dark (error.rs:12-14, :109-118). The change pays for itself at low cost: the derive already emits serialized TOML names into inventory (resolve/mod.rs:22-45), and resolve_with knows the mode, so prefixing the variant is a wrapper. Pre-1.0, a change in the error strings is acceptable.
**Triage:** fix — api-add: the derive emits the TOML key, pipeline and `with_overlay` errors carry `light.`/`dark.`
**Status:** fixed in d036d207 (paths name the TOML key; `light.`/`dark.` prefixes; `layout.*` and `context.font_dpi` unprefixed)

#### M3-21 · perf · S3 · native-theme/src/presets.rs:230
**Claim:** The first `Theme::preset(name)` call in a process parses all 16 bundled TOMLs (9552 lines, 247 KB), even when only one is needed. That first call is pipeline.rs:35 on `SystemTheme::from_system()`.
**Evidence:** presets.rs:230-244: `CACHE: LazyLock<HashMap<..>>` maps every PRESET_ENTRIES item through `parse(toml_str)` (:234, which is toml::from_str at :315) inside the LazyLock initialiser. preset() (:246-247) forces that initialiser on its first lookup. Production callers ask for one name: pipeline.rs:35 (`Theme::preset(preset_name)` in run_pipeline), pipeline.rs:542, lib.rs:561. `cat native-theme/src/presets/*.toml | wc -lc` gives 9552 lines and 246759 bytes, so a cold from_system parses about 16x the TOML it uses. M0's timing probe (todo_code-review-plan.md:435) takes the median of 21 warm calls, so the 1 us it reports leaves this cold cost out. The cost itself is not measured. M0's cold/warm from_system gap of 9.12 vs 3.63 ms (findings ledger :58) is an upper bound shared with the other one-time costs.
**Fix (reviewer):** Make the cache per entry: `static CACHE: [OnceLock<Parsed>; N]` indexed by the entry's position (or a `LazyLock` per entry), so `preset(name)` parses only the requested preset the first time. Add a timing assert or probe for the cold call.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — One LazyLock<HashMap> (presets.rs:230-244) parses all 16 PRESET_ENTRIES on first access, and the 16 TOMLs add up to 9552 lines and 246759 bytes (wc). docs/archive/v0.5.1_native-theme-API.md:2359 had proposed one LazyLock per preset. The ledger's warm measurement of about 1 µs (findings.md:74-75) is a cache hit and does not show the cold cost. To confirm the impact, time the first Theme::preset("kde-breeze") in a fresh process against a single from_toml of one file.
**Triage:** fix — perf, gated by a cold first-call timing in a fresh process (the M0 probe's warm medians cannot show it); dropped if the gain is below the spread
**Status:** fixed in ec377f8e (cold first `Theme::preset("kde-breeze")` median 6334.9 µs [5641–16430] → 836.5 µs [743–2911], 21 fresh release processes each)

#### M3-22 · perf · S3 · connectors/native-theme-iced/src/lib.rs:315
**Claim:** Every iced and gpui `from_preset(name, is_dark)` call runs `ResolutionContext::from_system()`. On Linux with the kde or portal feature that is the forceFontDPI file reads plus an `xrdb -query` subprocess, about 1.3-3.5 ms against 21-34 µs for resolve_with, paid on every preset or light/dark switch.
**Evidence:** iced lib.rs:315 and gpui lib.rs:303 call `variant.resolve_system()`, which calls `ResolutionContext::from_system()` (resolve/mod.rs:290-292). from_system calls detect::system_font_dpi (context.rs:77-85) on every call; it is uncached (detect.rs:963-965 calls detect_system_font_dpi :405-435 directly), with xrdb at detect.rs:256-257. The M1 F7 fix (bd12be93) moved the egui sites to one context per call (ext.rs:194) and the pipeline to the reader's DPI (pipeline.rs:61-67). iced and gpui were left on resolve_system (cited in ledger :443, not changed by decision :465). Theme::resolve also runs from_system on every call (model/mod.rs:464-466), which the showcases use for preset switches (showcase-gpui app.rs:1755, showcase-iced.rs:2066). **Fix (reviewer):** Cache the detected font DPI in DetectionContext beside the icon theme (ledger alternative B), cleared by invalidate_caches, which the watchers already call, so that from_system costs microseconds after the first call. Or give the iced and gpui from_preset a context like egui's.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — iced lib.rs:315 and gpui lib.rs:303 call `resolve_system()`, which builds `ResolutionContext::from_system()` (resolve/mod.rs:290-291) and runs the DPI chain on every call. M1-T3-01's fix covered only egui's three sites (findings.md:449-466). The ledger's Status line records the cost figures, resolve 1.28-3.50 ms against resolve_with 21-34 µs (findings.md:466). To confirm the per-call cost, add a timings.rs row for iced/gpui `from_preset` next to a from_preset variant that takes a prebuilt context. The ms cost only arises with the kde/portal feature and no forceFontDPI.
**Triage:** scheduled: M5 (iced) and M6 (gpui), connector code; gate: the connectors' `from_preset` timing added in their Step 1
**Status:** scheduled: M5 (iced), M6 (gpui); unchanged in M3. **Re-scheduled 2026-10-12 (orchestrating session; the maintainer may veto):** the core half moves to M4 (detection): cache the detected font DPI in `DetectionContext` beside the icon theme, cleared by `invalidate_caches` (the reviewer's first fix), which removes the per-call `xrdb` from `Theme::resolve` and `ThemeMode::resolve_system` for every caller; M5 and M6 only confirm it with their `from_preset` timing gate. **M4:** core half done in T11 (9ed0ca92): the cached font DPI in DetectionContext, cleared by invalidate_caches (T17 generations). **M5:** iced's `from_preset` timed at Step 8 (2026-10-14; release, three runs, load about 2.7 with another project's cargo check): medians 45.6 / 45.3 / 44.6 µs, range 35.5–49.5 µs over 16 presets × 2 modes, against the Step 1 baseline 35.5–49.2 µs: microseconds, not milliseconds, so the gate is met; gpui in M6.

#### M3-23 · perf · S3 · native-theme/src/pipeline.rs:636
**Claim:** When XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP is unset or unrecognised and the `portal` feature is on, every from_system / from_system_async call opens a new D-Bus session connection and lists activatable names to guess the desktop, though the desktop cannot change during the process. AccessibilityPreferences::from_system and every miss of the cached accessibility accessor do the same.
**Evidence:** select_reader calls the uncached `detect_linux_desktop()` (pipeline.rs:604), not the cached `system().linux_desktop()` (detect.rs:879-886). On Unknown it awaits `crate::gnome::detect_portal_backend()` (pipeline.rs:636), which runs `Connection::session().await`, `DBusProxy::new` and `list_activatable_names()` (gnome/mod.rs:555-558) and stores nothing. The reader then opens its own portal connection. reader_accessibility repeats the whole select_reader (pipeline.rs:763). Not measured. The trace shows one extra bus connect, auth and round trip per theme switch on these sessions.
**Fix (reviewer):** Cache the refined desktop (the portal answer, or the kdeglobals check) in DetectionContext next to `linux_desktop`, cleared by invalidate_caches, and have select_reader read it.
**Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE — The code path holds: for LinuxDesktop::Unknown, each select_reader call runs detect_portal_backend, which opens Connection::session() and calls list_activatable_names (gnome/mod.rs:555-558, pipeline.rs:661-662). reader_accessibility re-runs select_reader on every cache miss (pipeline.rs:762, detect.rs:806-807). The cost is unmeasured, and the selected portal reader opens its own connection anyway. To confirm, time from_system with XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP unset against XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME on a portal system, or count the Hello calls in dbus-monitor.
**Triage:** scheduled: M4 (detection), PLAUSIBLE perf: needs a measurement on a session with `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` unset
**Status:** scheduled: M4 (detection); unchanged in M3. **Dropped 2026-10-12 (M4 Step 2, measured):** warm `from_system` 4.67–7.94 ms with `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=KDE` against 5.38–7.53 ms unset (the portal probe path), at most about 0.7 ms apart, inside the readers' run-to-run spread; the backend-order correctness of the same path is M4-28.

#### M3-24 · bug · S4 · native-theme/src/model/widgets/mod.rs:12
**Claim:** On all 27 `ThemeWidget` structs, `#[serde_with::skip_serializing_none]` comes after `#[derive(Serialize)]`, so it has no effect: serialising a widget struct to a non-TOML format writes `null` for every unset field.
**Evidence:** widgets/mod.rs:11-12 (the same at :37-38, :108-109 … :1022-1025): the derive line is first and the serde_with attribute second. serde_with's own docs say 'The `#[skip_serializing_none]` attribute must be placed *before* the `#[derive]` attribute' (serde_with_macros-3.24.0/src/lib.rs:216). rustc expands item attributes in order, so serde's derive sees the fields before the attribute macro adds `skip_serializing_if`. defaults.rs:34-35, border.rs:22-23 and font.rs:178-179/:377-378 use the correct order. TOML output hides the problem because the toml serializer skips `None` struct fields. A test to write (not run, no cargo here): `assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&ButtonTheme::default()).unwrap(), "{}")`.
**Fix (reviewer):** Move `#[serde_with::skip_serializing_none]` above the `#[derive(...)]` line on each widget struct and on `LayoutTheme`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Every widget struct puts `#[serde_with::skip_serializing_none]` on the line after `#[derive(..Serialize..)]` (e.g. widgets/mod.rs:11-12, :917-918). serde_with's own docs say it must come before the derive (serde_with_macros-3.24.0/src/lib.rs:216), and every other proxy and struct in the crate does it that way (font.rs:178-179, border.rs:22-23, defaults.rs:34). TOML hides the problem because toml omits `None`; a `serde_json::to_string(&ButtonTheme::default())` test would show the `null`s.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug
**Status:** fixed in fcb14daf

#### M3-25 · bug · S4 · native-theme/src/pipeline.rs:334
**Claim:** platform_preset_name() and select_reader keep separate desktop-to-preset mappings, and they disagree for LinuxDesktop::Unknown with a KDE portal or ~/.config/kdeglobals present: platform_preset_name says "adwaita" while from_system uses "kde-breeze". The doc claims linux_preset_for_de is the 'single source of truth' for both.
**Evidence:** The doc at pipeline.rs:334-335 says linux_preset_for_de is used by from_system_inner and platform_preset_name. platform_preset_name on Linux returns `linux_preset_for_de(detect_linux_desktop())` (pipeline.rs:382), which is "adwaita" for Unknown (:344). select_reader hard-codes its own literals: "kde-breeze"/"adwaita" at pipeline.rs:608, 612, 618, 640, 645, and for Unknown with kdeglobals present it returns `(KdeReader, "kde-breeze")` (:656-657). The showcases fall back to platform_preset_name when from_system fails (gpui app.rs:1263; egui app.rs:379), so a KDE session without XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP is labelled adwaita. M1-T1-01 covers the macOS/Windows literals; this Linux divergence is not in it.
**Fix (reviewer):** Have select_reader return the preset through one mapping that both functions call (e.g. a `refined_linux_desktop()` feeding linux_preset_for_de), or correct the doc so it does not claim one source.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The doc at pipeline.rs:333-334 calls linux_preset_for_de the single source of truth, but select_reader hard-codes its own literals (:645-693). For Unknown with a KDE portal or kdeglobals it returns "kde-breeze" (:665, :683), while platform_preset_name returns adwaita (:382 via :342). M1-T1-01 (ledger, scheduled for M2a) adopts one shared mapping for both call sites, but only for macOS/Windows OS versions, so it does not cover this Linux drift.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug
**Status:** fixed in b345f5fd and 2bb1bef3 (docs: the portal answer decides an unknown desktop either way)

#### M3-27 · bug · S4 · native-theme/src/color.rs:198
**Claim:** A colour string with non-ASCII characters, e.g. `"#é0"` in a TOML file, gets a misleading error ('invalid red hex digit 'Ã'') or a byte-count length error ('#é' gives 'length 2'). The comment says such input cannot match the byte slots at all, which is wrong.
**Evidence:** `match hex.as_bytes()`: "é0" is the 3 bytes [0xC3, 0xA9, 0x30], which matches the `[r, g, b]` arm (color.rs:204). hex_nibble formats `char::from(0xC3)` = 'Ã' (color.rs:169-174). The comment at color.rs:198-201 says non-ASCII 'wouldn't match the single-byte slots'. The length message reports `other.len()`, a byte count (color.rs:242-245). The input is still rejected, so this is not a parse bug.
**Fix (reviewer):** Reject `!hex.is_ascii()` first with a message that quotes the input string, and fix the comment.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — "é0" is 3 bytes [0xC3,0xA9,'0'], so it matches the [r,g,b] arm and hex_nibble prints char::from(0xC3)='Ã' (color.rs:169-173, :203-206). "é" is 2 bytes and gives 'length 2' (:235-238). The input is still rejected, so the bug is only a misleading message, but the comment at :198-201, which says non-ASCII 'wouldn't match the single-byte slots', is wrong.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug
**Status:** fixed in 30c7b100

#### M3-28 · bug · S4 · native-theme/src/presets/documented_sizes.rs:654
**Claim:** The gate can pass for a preset it never looks at. A 17th bundled preset (e.g. the planned `macos-tahoe` or an `ios-26` rename) that is in neither `NativePreset::ALL` nor `UNSOURCED_PRESETS` goes unchecked by every test in the module.
**Evidence:** NativePreset::ALL (documented_sizes.rs:68-74) lists 5 keys and UNSOURCED_PRESETS (:654-666) lists 11, both by hand. Every test iterates one of those two lists: native_themes_state_documented_sizes :544, unsourced_presets_state_no_gated_size :674, native_themes_state_documented_fields :987, native_presets_state_no_text_scale_line_height :1104, native_themes_state_the_expanders_structure :1155/:1169. Nothing compares their union with `crate::presets::list_presets()` or PRESET_ENTRIES (grep `UNSOURCED|NativePreset::ALL` finds only uses inside this file). tests/preset_loading.rs:276-283 pins the count at 16, but adding a preset there does not touch this gate. A renamed key does fail (Theme::preset errors and the failure is pushed). An added one is silently not covered. Test to add: `let mut gated: Vec<&str> = NativePreset::ALL.iter().map(|p| p.key()).chain(UNSOURCED_PRESETS).collect(); gated.sort(); let mut all: Vec<&str> = crate::presets::list_presets().iter().map(|i| i.key).collect(); all.sort(); assert_eq!(gated, all);`
**Fix (reviewer):** Add the coverage test above, so that every bundled preset must be either a NativePreset with rows or an unsourced preset.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Every test in documented_sizes.rs iterates only NativePreset::ALL (:68-74) or UNSOURCED_PRESETS (:654-666). Nothing compares their union with list_presets() or PRESET_ENTRIES (grep for list_presets or PRESET_ in the file finds nothing), so a 17th preset in neither list goes unchecked.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug (a gate that can pass vacuously)
**Status:** fixed in c01f1c2a

#### M3-29 · bug · S4 · native-theme-derive/src/parse.rs:376
**Claim:** The derive panics instead of returning a spanned compile error when `min_max_pair = "…"`, `resolved_name = "…"` or `inherit_from = "…"` holds a string that is not an identifier path (e.g. `min_max_pair = "max width"`, `resolved_name = ""`, `inherit_from = "defaults..color"` or `"defaults.border-color"`).
**Evidence:** parse.rs:376 `Ident::new(&lit.value(), lit.span())` and parse.rs:128 (same, for resolved_name): proc-macro2 1.0.107's src/lib.rs:1010-1018 documents `Ident::new` as 'Panics if the input string is neither a keyword nor a legal variable name … use syn::parse_str::<Ident> rather than Ident::new'. gen_inherit.rs:98-106 parse_defaults_path calls `format_ident!("{}", s)` on each '.'-separated segment, which goes through Ident::new and panics on an empty or non-identifier segment. The neighbouring `font = "…"` key already does it correctly: parse.rs:225-233 uses `syn::parse_str::<Ident>` and maps the failure to `Error::new(lit.span(), …)`. These are the only panic paths in non-test derive code (grep panic!/unwrap/expect/Ident::new/format_ident!; the expects at parse.rs:488+ are in #[cfg(test)]). The last case also accepts a path without the `defaults.` prefix silently (gen_inherit.rs:99 `unwrap_or(path)`), and registers that unprefixed string as the UniformInheritanceInfo source (:66).
**Fix (reviewer):** Parse all three with `syn::parse_str::<Ident>` (for inherit_from: each segment, after requiring the `defaults.` prefix) and return `Error::new(lit.span(), …)` on failure, as the `font` key does.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — min_max_pair uses Ident::new(&lit.value(), …) (parse.rs:376), and resolved_name does the same (parse.rs:128). resolved_name is a theme_layer attribute, not a field attribute as the claim says. inherit_from's segments go through format_ident!("{}", s) (gen_inherit.rs:101-104). All three panic on an empty or non-identifier string, whereas the font attribute already uses syn::parse_str with a spanned error (parse.rs:225-233). This is a compile-time proc-macro panic only.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug: spanned `syn::Error`, never a panic in the macro
**Status:** fixed in e299f0aa (messages pinned in 9b9c6072)

#### M3-30 · bug · S4 · native-theme-derive/src/parse.rs:327
**Claim:** Some field attributes that conflict are silently dropped, depending on their order. `#[theme(category = "soft_option", nested, resolved_type = "ResolvedFontSpec")]` becomes a plain soft option: the font is replaced whole on merge instead of merged, and it gets no nested validation and no font range check. `#[theme(check = "positive", range = "0.0..=1.0")]` keeps only the last check.
**Evidence:** parse.rs:311-324: `category = …` sets `category = Some(Option|SoftOption)` unconditionally, overwriting an earlier `nested`. :325-331: `nested` is recorded only `if category.is_none()`, so a `category` written before it wins. :390-406: `resolved_type` with an Option/SoftOption category falls into `_ => {} // option/soft_option ignore resolved_type`. :347-372: `check`, `range` and `range_u16` all assign the single `range_check`, so a second one overwrites the first. parse_range_f64 :423-441 also accepts `min > max` and `NaN` (`"NaN".parse::<f64>()` succeeds), which makes check_range_f32 reject every value or none. Downstream, gen_merge.rs:148-153 whole-replaces SoftOption fields, while Nested fields are merged recursively (:155-162). gen_ranges.rs:327-351 adds the font check only for Nested. So the dropped attribute changes behaviour, with no diagnostic. No current field combines them (survey of the `#[theme(...)]` uses in native-theme/src: every nested field is `nested, resolved_type = …` alone), so the risk is in future edits.
**Fix (reviewer):** Return a spanned `Error` when `nested`/`resolved_type` meets a `category`, when a second range attribute appears, and when a range has min > max or a non-finite bound.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — With category = "soft_option" set, `nested` is skipped (parse.rs:327), and if `nested` comes first, category overwrites it (parse.rs:314). resolved_type is then dropped by the `_ => {}` arm (parse.rs:404). The field ends up SoftOption whatever the order: whole-value merge (gen_merge.rs:38-43), no nested validation and no font check (gen_ranges.rs:146). check/range is last-wins because each assignment overwrites range_check (parse.rs:350, :365). Latent: grep finds no current field with a conflicting pair.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug: a conflicting attribute pair is a spanned compile error
**Status:** fixed in e299f0aa (messages pinned in 9b9c6072)

#### M3-31 · bug · S4 · native-theme-derive/src/gen_inherit.rs:218
**Claim:** A struct marked `#[theme_layer(skip_inventory)]` that also declares `#[theme_inherit(border_kind = …)]` or `font = …` still registers BorderInheritanceInfo and FontInheritanceInfo rows. The widget and uniform registries skip it, so the drift tests would see a widget that does not exist.
**Evidence:** lib.rs:112-114 (WidgetFieldInfo) and gen_inherit.rs:54-56 (UniformInheritanceInfo) return early on `layer.skip_inventory`. gen_border_inherit (gen_inherit.rs:144-223) and gen_font_inherit (:248-320) do not receive `layer` at all (lib.rs:85-86 passes only `&inherit_meta`), and they always emit `inventory::submit!` (:218-221, :291-303).
