### Mandatory questions — the reviewers' answers

**R1-theme-palette**
- *1. (Review Focus 4) Every padding/size helper: zero, negative and unstated sides; NaN/inf from the resolved theme; float-to-iced conversions (Pixels, f32 -> u16/u32 casts).* — No problem found in the helpers. Core validation rejects non-finite or negative border padding, corner radius and line width (native-theme/src/resolve/validate_helpers.rs:523-541), and every spinner size is `check = "non_negative"` (model/widgets/mod.rs:806-815), so NaN, inf and negative values never reach these helpers through a validated theme. How each helper handles its inputs:
- padding_or (lib.rs:378-388) takes `default` per unstated side.
- stated_padding (lib.rs:399-406) gives None if any side is unstated.
- padding_inside_border (lib.rs:422-437) adds line_width only to stated sides, and zero sides pass through unchanged.
- combo_box_padding and arrow_column_margin clamp the margin to >= 0 (lib.rs:535-537).
- button_content_min_size clamps both axes to >= 0 (lib.rs:576-579).
- control_line_height (lib.rs:560-562) uses own.max(room). A negative room (padding taller than the minimum) falls back to the theme's own line box. Only a caller-supplied NaN text_size together with a negative room could produce a negative LineHeight::Absolute; that input comes from the caller, not the theme, and prefs.scaled already ignores a non-finite factor.
- Spinner: diameter goes straight into Length::Fixed (spinner.rs:142), and the arc radius is clamped to >= 0 (spinner.rs:253).
- No helper here casts f32 to u16 or u32. The one f32-to-int cast is color_to_rgb's `(c.clamp(0,1)*255).round() as u8` (icons.rs:262-268). It saturates, and NaN becomes 0, so it cannot panic.
- The int-to-float casts at icons.rs:222 and spinner.rs:180 lose precision (finding 3).
- to_iced_weight (lib.rs:1187-1200) covers every u16.
- *2. (Theme-data rule) Every ResolvedTheme field iced can receive through these files: does it reach iced, or is a constant used instead? List any resolved value this region drops.* — Every field the region writes reaches its iced slot.
- Palette (palette.rs:37-48): defaults.background_color, text_color, accent_color, success_color, warning_color, danger_color.
- Extended overrides (extended.rs:91-109): input.placeholder_color goes to secondary.base.color and strong. defaults.text_color goes to background.base.text and weak.text. defaults.surface_color goes to background.weak.color. defaults.{accent,success,danger,warning}_text_color go to the matching .base.text.
- secondary.base.text is the platform text colour after iced's `readable()`, and is iced's substitute on all bundled presets. That design is recorded at extended.rs:92-98 and counted by the contract, so I do not report it.
- Helpers: font family/size/weight, mono font, line_height, border radius and radius_lg, scrollbar groove_width, border.color, disabled_opacity, focus_ring_color, link_color, expander arrow and font colour, selection_background, info_color/info_text_color, warning_text_color, icon_sizes, combo_box.arrow_icon_size (pick_list_handle). Spinner: spinner.fill_color, diameter and stroke_width.

Constants used where no resolved field exists, each cited: the arc's sweep (SWEEP_DEGREES, from egui, spinner.rs:22) and its speed of one turn a second (spinner.rs:180), and the text-editor padding of 5 used only for unstated sides (lib.rs:479, cited to iced).

Resolved values this region drops or replaces:
- spinner.min_diameter, documented as not read (spinner.rs:45-46).
- The mode/is_dark the connector holds in from_preset/from_system never reaches iced's Extended::is_dark, which iced recomputes from luminance (finding 4; no bundled preset is affected).
- For a freedesktop symbolic indicator the spinner uses neither spinner.fill_color nor text_color: iced's renderer paints it black (finding 1).
- *3. (Review Focus 2) from_preset / from_system / to_theme on a theme switch: what is recomputed, cloned or re-read each time; is anything cached that should not be (or vice versa)?* — No new problem found.
- from_preset (lib.rs:304-318), each call: Theme::preset clones the cached parsed preset (presets.rs:93-105, per-entry OnceLock since M3-21), clones spec.name, runs into_variant, then resolve_system. That builds ResolutionContext::from_system, whose font DPI has been cached since M4 T11 (M3-22's core half). Then to_theme.
- from_system (lib.rs:332-345) runs the whole SystemTheme::from_system pipeline. It moves the chosen ResolvedTheme out instead of cloning it. The detection caches are core's; the app calls invalidate_caches on a change (M4 ruling).
- SystemThemeExt::to_iced_theme (lib.rs:357-362) clones one ResolvedTheme, which is unavoidable behind &self.
- to_theme (lib.rs:270-293) allocates the name String, converts 6 + 7 Rgba values, and runs Extended::generate once: iced's Custom::with_fn calls the closure once, at construction (iced_core theme.rs:191-200), not per frame. The closure captures only the 7 Copy colours (OverrideColors).
- The connector caches nothing, which is right because every input can change on a switch.
- Spinner::new reads the icon theme and recolours its frames once, and the doc says to build it once per theme (spinner.rs:48-51). view() clones only Arc-backed handles each frame.
- system_font_family copies face bytes on every call; that is the open todo.md:371 [1.0] entry.
- *4. Icons and spinner: every IconData variant (Svg, Rgba via RgbaData, animated frames/transform) handled; colourising; a missing icon gives None (no icon-set mixing on any fallback path); spinner frame timing from the theme.* — Variants:
- IconData (#[non_exhaustive], Svg and Rgba): to_/into_svg_handle handle Svg, to_/into_image_handle handle Rgba through RgbaData's checked width/height/data (icons.rs:31-40, :228-240). Every other variant gives None.
- AnimatedIcon: Frames are handled by animated_frames_to_svg_handles (SVG frames only; RGBA frames are dropped and the animation plays faster, finding 5) and by Spinner (both kinds; an undrawable frame means the arc, spinner.rs:194-203). Transform::Spin is handled by Spinner (spinner.rs:204-209) and by spin_rotation_radians. Any other kind gives None, which means the arc.

Colourising:
- Spinner tints only Material and Lucide (spinner.rs:109). The freedesktop symbolic case is left black (finding 1).
- custom_icon_to_svg_handle colours a system icon twice (finding 2).
- The private colorize_monochrome_svg and load_custom_via_builder are already scheduled for removal (M1-T7-01, M1-T6-06).

Missing icon:
- load_custom_via_builder tries only the requested set's loader, then the provider's own SVG for the same set, and otherwise returns None (icons.rs:113-127). No set is mixed in.
- Spinner::new with an explicit icon_theme never falls back to the system's theme (FreedesktopLoader::load_indicator(icon_theme), spinner.rs:106; tested at :302-306). A set without an indicator draws the theme-coloured arc, not another set's icon.

Timing:
- ResolvedSpinnerTheme has no timing field (model/widgets/mod.rs:801-816). Frame and spin timing come from the icon's own AnimatedIcon data (frame_duration_ms / TransformAnimation::Spin duration_ms, spinner.rs:199-207). frame_index is exact integer arithmetic (spinner.rs:215-226). The rotation and the arc lose float precision over a long elapsed time (finding 3). Under reduce_motion the spinner stays on frame 0 at angle 0 (spinner.rs:145-157, :177-181).
- *Notes:* I read all production code in lib.rs (1-1201), palette.rs, extended.rs, icons.rs and spinner.rs. I did not report items in m5-known.md or the open todo.md entries: the colouriser and loader switch, RgbaData re-validation, spinner set dispatch, from_system's tuple, Resolved.mode, system_font_family's copy, primary hover, and the Breeze current-color-scheme recolour.

Finding 2's fix must be applied together with the scheduled M1-T6-06 loader switch, or the double colouring survives that switch.

The widget helpers in lib.rs (switch, radio, at_least, tab_indicator, pick_list_handle) were in range, and I traced their size inputs for question 1. I found nothing there.

I computed the bundled presets' OKLCH background lightness with a scratch script (scratchpad/m5r1/oklch.py) to scope finding 4.

I could not verify on this machine that Adwaita ships only process-working-symbolic, because Adwaita is not installed. Finding 1 rests on platform-facts.md:1539 and on core's documented symbolic pass. On Breeze, which is installed, the plain sprite with its own stylesheet colour is used, so finding 1 does not apply there.

Per the rules, no cargo was run and nothing was edited.

**R2-styles**
- *(Review Focus 2) What each style closure/function captures and clones per call (they run per widget per frame): a ResolvedTheme clone, a Vec, a String, a colour conversion recomputed each frame?* — No problem. Each function borrows `&ResolvedTheme` only while it builds the closure. The closure captures Copy values only: iced `Color`, `f32`, `Border`, `Radius`, `Option<Color>` (checkbox_over :629, expander :1653), `Option<f32>` ratios (toggler :878-879), precomputed `(Color, Color)` tuples (toggler :865-866), and one `fn` pointer (class_button :245). There is no ResolvedTheme clone, no Vec and no String. Every to_color and composite_over runs once at construction (e.g. button :173-190, toggler :827-879). Per call there is one match, and in 15 closures one call to iced's own class to read the fields the model lacks (button::text :399, text_input::default :460, toggler::default :884, pick_list::default :979, overlay::menu::default :1036, slider::default :1092, scrollable::default :1163, rule::default :1352, class(theme,status) :266, aw menu_bar/tab_bar/sidebar/selection_list::primary aw.rs:142/:228/:312/:421). Those build stack structs from `theme.extended_palette()`, which returns a reference to a static or stored palette (iced_core theme.rs:138), so nothing allocates. The rest call `Style::default()`, which is const-like. The closures are typically rebuilt on each view() call: about 5 to 20 f32 conversions. That is not a per-draw cost.
- *(Theme-data rule) Every style function: does each colour, border width, radius, padding come from the resolved theme? List any hardcoded value where a resolved field exists, and any widget state (hovered, pressed, disabled, focused, checked, selected) that falls back to a constant or to the wrong state's value.* — No colour or size literal stands where a resolved field exists. The only literals are 0.0 radii and widths on corners or tabs the model states nothing for (segment :1599-1603, tab_bar aw.rs:225/:239, documented). Padding is builder geometry, not a Style field. State fallbacks that are wrong: (1) a hover soft option that is None over a translucent fill composites the fill over itself, so the hovered state is darker than rest (pick_list :964, toggler :830-841, checkbox_over :618-619, radio :726-727, segment :1580-1584; macos-tahoe combo_box and switch off track), see finding 1; (2) the expander's Disabled arm is the resting state, with no `defaults.disabled_opacity` fade, against inheritance-rules.toml:357-358 (:1666), finding 2; (3) the expander ignores `expander.frame_enabled` (:1656), finding 3; (4) no checked toggle-button state uses `button.checked_*`, finding 4. The other documented fallbacks match their docs: class_button Hovered/Pressed come from iced's class (:269-271), with the assumption recorded in the module doc; button_link's Pressed/Disabled fill is idle (:403-404); the selected tab/sidebar item under the pointer shows hover (an upstream limitation); slider Dragged takes its fill from iced (:1097); checkbox/radio hovered-checked equals checked; scrollable's disabled flags are ignored. All are recorded design. iced 0.14 slider, pick_list and radio have no Disabled status (slider.rs, pick_list.rs, radio.rs Status enums), so their disabled_* fields have no receiver.
- *Composite/blend helpers (composite_over and friends): alpha handling, a translucent base, out-of-range channels; consistency with core's colour model.* — composite_over (styles.rs:79-99) is straight-alpha source-over in sRGB: a = la + ba*(1-la), channels un-premultiplied by a. alpha <= 0 returns TRANSPARENT and under <= 0 returns the layer exactly. A translucent base stays translucent (the link case). Inputs from to_color (palette.rs:22-25, u8/255) are always in 0..=1. The only outside input is the consumer's `backdrop` in checkbox_over/toggler_over. There, a > 1 makes under negative, which returns the layer, and NaN propagates as NaN without a panic. faded (:107-118) clamps the opacity and treats non-finite as 1. faded_as_one (:133-138) flattens over an opaque ground and returns the colour unchanged at opacity >= 1 or NaN. This matches core's model: kde/colors.rs:28-33 `over` is the same sRGB source-over, written for an opaque bottom; egui's composite_over (convert.rs:335-337) is the premultiplied form of the same equation; the contract's independent `over` (contract.rs:852-870) agrees. Two problems: the helper is misused when a soft option is None (finding 1), and segment's local `fade` (:1591) bypasses faded's guards (finding 5). Duplication across the connectors is part of the open docs/todo.md:739 decision and is not reported again.
- *iced_aw styles: every iced_aw widget style the feature promises, matching the iced_widget-0.14 / iced_aw-0.14.1 style structs field by field (a field left default that has a resolved source).* — The module promises card, menu bar, tab bar (and Tabs::tab_bar_style), sidebar, selection list and spinner (aw.rs:5-11). Each style names every field of iced_aw 0.14.1's struct. card::Style has 11 fields, all native (aw.rs:79-91); close_color is ignored upstream, which is a known iced_aw defect. menu_bar::Style has 8 fields: bar and menu background and border are native; bar_shadow, menu_shadow and path_border come from menu_bar::primary, which is `..Default::default()`, so menu_shadow is a 10px 0.5-black blur and path_border has radius 6 (style/menu_bar.rs:28-53, :83-92). The model has no shadow geometry or row-highlight radius. `menu.border.shadow_enabled` is not consulted, but I found no preset that resolves it to false, so it is not reported. tab_bar::Style has 11 fields (style/tab_bar.rs:13-47): background, the three label colours by status, tab_label_border_color and width, and tab_border_radius are native; border_color, border_width, icon_background and icon_border_radius come from iced_aw (the model states nothing for them). sidebar::Style has 10 fields: background, border_color, border_width, label fill, text and icon are native; the label border and the icon background and radius come from iced_aw. selection_list::Style has 4 fields, all native. The spinner wraps itself in a container::Style with 5 fields, text_color native and the rest default. The fields left at iced_aw's default that have a native source are none, beyond those the module documents as having no receiver (sidebar and list corner radius hardcoded upstream at sidebar.rs:616/:992 and selection_list.rs:309; tab min_width/min_height in UNREACHABLE). ContextMenu and the picker widgets are deliberately not covered (aw.rs:24-26).
- *Notes:* I read src/styles.rs and src/styles/aw.rs line by line; neither file has a #[cfg(test)] module. I checked the code against iced_widget 0.14.2, iced_core 0.14.0 and iced_aw 0.14.1 under ~/.cargo/registry/src, the core model (native-theme/src/model/widgets/mod.rs), docs/inheritance-rules.toml, the presets, the contract tables (src/contract.rs, src/contract/rows.rs, derived.rs) and the sibling connectors. The contract's coverage test (contract.rs:1700) lists emitted iced Style fields, not native model fields, so a native field that no style reads goes unnoticed. That is how `expander.frame_enabled` and `button.checked_*` slipped through; the leaf-coverage test M1-T7-03 counts colour leaves only. Finding 1's contract rows reproduce the code's expression, so fixing it means changing styles.rs and contract/rows.rs together. I compared against egui's behaviour (states.rs:127-134). Related issues outside this region that I did not report: the showcase's own `menu_row` (examples/showcase-iced.rs:3958-3976) uses menu.border.corner_radius as the item radius, while inheritance-rules.toml:71 says the menu border belongs to the popup container; the showcase's `ghost_button` ignores `button.checked_*`. I did not run cargo; no tests were executed.

**API**
- *Can a first-time user apply a native theme to an iced app in a few lines (system theme, a preset, react to a theme change, load an icon, style a widget)?* — Preset: yes, `from_preset("dracula", true)?` (lib.rs:304). Style a widget: yes, `button(..).style(styles::button_primary(&resolved))` plus the documented builder receivers (README:123-200). System theme: one line as written, but only if the user also enables native-theme's `native` feature, which neither the connector forwards nor the README's Quick start names — as shown, `from_system()` returns the platform preset on Linux and `FeatureDisabled` on macOS/Windows (finding 1). React to a theme change: no — no recipe, no `watch` passthrough and no iced `Subscription`; the showcase's hand-written loop (`on_theme_change` → flag → `iced::time::every` → `invalidate_caches()` → re-read → `Spinner::new`) is ~40 lines (finding 2). Load an icon: only the custom-provider recipe; a role icon via core's `SystemTheme::icon(id, mode, color)` then `icons::to_svg_handle(&data, None)` is undocumented (finding 3), and the `from_system()` tuple drops the `SystemTheme`, so `Spinner::new(&resolved, icon_set, icon_theme)` and `sys.icon(..)` need the `SystemTheme::from_system()` + `to_iced_theme()` path — M1-T7-06's result struct should carry `icon_set` and `icon_theme` (or the mode-resolved theme) for these two tasks (note). Minimum sizes need `control_line_height` with the padding spelled twice per widget; per-widget wrappers would shorten it (finding 7).
- *Are names and shapes consistent with the siblings and with core after M3/M4?* — `to_theme(&resolved, name)` matches egui (gpui adds `is_dark, prefs` for its toolkit). `from_preset(name, is_dark)` without `&prefs` differs from gpui/egui — M1-T7-06 decided to keep `(theme, resolved)` and C4 records why iced takes no prefs; `from_system`'s 4-tuple and `SystemThemeExt::to_iced_theme` are M1-T7-06's (known), as are the accessor names that differ from the model's fields (`info_foreground_color`, `selection_color`, `border_radius`). egui seals `SystemThemeExt`; iced and gpui do not — fold into T7-06's reshaping. Icons: iced's `to_image_handle`/`to_svg_handle` split follows iced's `Image`/`Svg` split where gpui/egui have one `to_image_source`; `custom_icon_to_*(provider, set, Option<Color>)` matches gpui's shape (minus `size`, which iced does not rasterize); `load_custom_via_builder` and the private colouriser are M1-T6-06/M1-T7-01 (known). Spinner: `Spinner::new(resolved, set, theme)` mirrors gpui's and egui-widgets' spinners; the set dispatch is M4-15 (known), whose `SystemTheme::icon_indicator(mode)` half needs a `Spinner` constructor taking an `Option<AnimatedIcon>` (note). Core after M3/M4: `from_preset` still resolves through `into_variant().resolve_system()` rather than `Resolved.mode` / a shared `ResolutionContext` (M3-15, M3-22 known); `IconData::Rgba(RgbaData)` is consumed through `width()/height()/data()/into_data()` with no re-validation (M4-07 already satisfied); the watch contract (`invalidate_caches()` before a re-read) appears nowhere in the iced docs (finding 2). `watch` is forwarded by egui only (finding 1). Names otherwise follow the siblings: `scaled_text_size`, `font_size(resolved, prefs)`, `icon_sizes`, `line_height_multiplier`, `to_iced_weight`.
- *Which pub items does no user need?* — None worth removing. Re-exports: `DialogButtonOrder` (lib.rs:239) has no iced accessor — docs/todo.md:2952 "iced: dialog is unmapped" is the open entry; `IconRole`, `AnimatedIcon`, `TransformAnimation`, `IconProvider`, `Rgba`, `Error`, `Result`, `LinuxDesktop` match the siblings' sets. `icons::into_image_handle`/`into_svg_handle` are the copy-free twins of the borrowing forms (CHANGELOG:950, deliberate). `AnimatedSvgHandles`, `animated_frames_to_svg_handles` and `spin_rotation_radians` are the hand path `Spinner` wraps and the only way to play a custom animated icon — keep, but their examples should read the period from the data (finding 5). `Spinner::is_indicator` is a cheap query the tests and an app's layout can use. `pub mod spinner` holds only `Spinner`, re-exported at the root — harmless. `padding_or`, `stated_padding`, `padding_inside_border`, `control_line_height` are the general forms the wrappers build on and the README recipes need.
- *Are the feature flags coherent (widgets, spinner, iced_aw, icon features, system-fonts, advanced-shaping)? Can a combination fail to compile or silently do nothing?* — The set is additive and coherent: `spinner` implies `widgets` and `iced_widget`'s `svg`/`image`/`canvas`, which cargo unifies into the application's `iced_renderer`, so `Spinner::view`'s renderer bounds hold for `iced::Renderer`; `iced_aw` implies `widgets`; `default-features = false` leaves the palette and the `iced_core`-only helpers, as documented. No combination fails to compile: `advanced-shaping` with an app's `basic-shaping` picks Advanced (iced_core 0.14.0 text.rs:168-176). Silent no-ops are documented where they exist: without `material-icons`/`lucide-icons`/`system-icons` the `Spinner` draws the arc and `custom_icon_to_*` return `None`. The one incoherence is outside the forwarded set: no `native`/`linux`/`macos`/`windows` and no `watch` passthrough, with a README Quick start that names no feature, so `from_system()` silently falls back to the platform preset on Linux and errors on macOS/Windows (finding 1), and `on_theme_change` returns `WatchUnavailable` without `kde`/`portal`/`macos`/`windows` (watch/mod.rs:400-421). `all-features = true` on docs.rs covers `iced_aw` and is built by check_release.sh:771-772.
- *Do the doc examples show the real usage and would they compile? Do the README claims match the code?* — Crate and module doctests (`rust`/`rust,no_run`) compile under the three configurations check_release.sh runs (no-default, default, `iced_aw`): the Font Configuration example (lib.rs:122-150) builds a real `iced_core::Font`, `MaterialLoader::load_indicator()` exists without its feature (icons.rs:529-561 in core), `Theme::custom_with_fn` takes `impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>` so `name.to_string()` is fine. The `from_system()` 4-tuple examples (lib.rs:18, :1055) change with M1-T7-06. The README is never doctested (egui has `ReadmeDoctests`; iced's compat.rs checks only the Compatibility table), and its snippets carry: `spin_rotation_radians(elapsed, 1000)` where the data has the period (finding 5, also icons.rs:214); unscaled sizes in Minimum sizes against `control_line_height`'s own contract (finding 6); `container(Spinner::new())` that reads as this crate's three-argument `Spinner` (finding 9); `pick_list_handle` never shown with its required turbofish (finding 8). Claims: the Modules row "Icon role mapping" for `icons` is false (finding 4); "0.6" quick-start versions will be stale at 0.7.0 with no gate (finding 10); "read the OS theme at runtime" is overstated without `native` (finding 1); the Compatibility floors and Verified line are mechanically checked (compat.rs); the Features table, the four style shapes and the 25-function count match styles.rs; the T19 "first call … 3 ms" sentence (README:353-355) is the known stale one.
- *Notes:* Scope and method: read-only; read lib.rs, icons.rs, palette.rs, spinner.rs, styles.rs, styles/aw.rs, extended.rs, Cargo.toml, README.md, tests/, the showcase's watch and icon paths, the gpui/egui entry points and READMEs, core's SystemTheme/icons/detect/watch, and iced_core 0.14.0 / iced_widget 0.14.2 / iced_futures 0.14.0 sources in the registry. No cargo run. All ten findings are new against m5-known.md and docs/todo.md (grepped: no open entry on the README quick-start features, the theme-change recipe, the role-icon recipe, the `icons` row, the 1000 ms examples, the unscaled recipe sizes, the turbofish, the line-height wrappers or the version literals); M4 T19's stale README:353-355 sentence, the T7-06 tuple/accessor items, M1-T7-01's colouriser, M1-T6-06's `load_custom_via_builder`, M4-15's spinner dispatch and M3-15/M3-22's `from_preset` resolution are not re-reported.

Notes for M5's fix phase (not findings): (1) M1-T7-06's result struct, whatever its home, should carry `icon_set` and the mode's `icon_theme` (or `SystemTheme::icon_theme_for(mode)`'s value): `Spinner::new(&resolved, icon_set, icon_theme)` and `SystemTheme::icon(..)` are unusable from `from_system()`'s result today. (2) M4-15's `SystemTheme::icon_indicator(mode)` half needs a `Spinner` constructor that takes an already loaded `Option<AnimatedIcon>` plus the set (for the Material/Lucide tint rule at spinner.rs:107): e.g. `Spinner::from_indicator(resolved, icon_set, indicator: Option<&AnimatedIcon>)`, with `new` becoming a wrapper. (3) After M1-T6-06's switch to `native_theme::icons::load_custom_icon(provider, set, color)`, `custom_icon_to_svg_handle` must pass `None` to `to_svg_handle` (icons.rs:98) — core already wrote the colour into the bytes; the current double pass is idempotent only by luck of the colouriser's early returns. (4) The 0.7 README bump and the `native` feature advice apply to the gpui and egui READMEs too (M6/M7). One `implement` agent (Opus) per task, a fresh reviewer per task, `./scripts/check_release.sh --commit` before every code commit. Gates: bug → a failing test first; simplify → net deletion, tests unchanged except deleted tests of deleted code; api → the workspace compiles (`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`), every caller (connectors, showcases, doc examples, READMEs) updated, a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line.

Rulings (Step 6):

- Ruling: M1-T7-06's result struct is one per connector, not core-generic: `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct Loaded` in each connector with the same field names — `theme` (egui: `atlas`), `resolved` (the OS mode's variant), `mode: ColorMode` (not `is_dark: bool`, the model's type since M3-15), `accessibility`, `icon_set`, `icon_theme` (the mode's, `SystemTheme::icon_theme_for(mode)`, owned) — returned by `from_system` in all three and by `SystemThemeExt::to_iced_theme` / `to_gpui_theme`; egui's `to_egui_atlas` keeps returning `ThemeAtlas` (already a named result carrying both variants, the mode and the preferences; its doc records why). `from_preset` keeps `(theme, resolved)`. — why: a core `#[non_exhaustive]` struct cannot be built by a struct literal in another crate, so a generic one needs a constructor whose arguments are the field list again; the toolkit field differs per connector; `icon_set` and `icon_theme` are what `Spinner::new` and a role icon need, which `from_system`'s tuple drops today (API reviewer's note 1). — cost if wrong: one more rename of three structs before 1.0.

### Entries

#### M6-01 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:1041
**Claim:** Every `apply`, `apply_system_theme` and `apply_accessibility` resets the application's own gpui-component settings `Theme::notification`, `list`, `sheet` and `motion` to upstream's defaults. The trigger is an application that sets e.g. `Theme::global_mut(cx).sheet.margin_top = px(40.)`, `notification.placement`, or `Theme::update(cx, |t| t.motion.duration_normal = Duration::ZERO)` after init and then switches theme.
**Evidence:** `apply_inner` writes `*GpuiTheme::global_mut(cx) = theme;` (lib.rs:1041). That replaces the whole global with the value `to_theme` built through `GpuiTheme::from(&theme_color)` (lib.rs:232), and that value holds `NotificationSettings::default()`, `ListSettings::default()`, `SheetSettings::default()` and `MotionTokens::default()` (gpui-component 0.7.3 theme/mod.rs:779-787). The tripwire test calls these four fields 'left at upstream's default on purpose' (lib.rs:1287-1293; rationale v0.5.9 :361-366). That reasoning covers what `to_theme` maps. It does not cover overwriting values the application set. Upstream's own switch keeps them: `Theme::change` -> `Theme::edit` (theme/mod.rs:389-398, :298-323) -> `apply_config` (schema.rs:1064-1108) writes only the configs, highlight, fonts, radii, shadow, tokens and mode, never the four settings. gpui-component reads them at render time: `cx.theme().sheet.margin_top` (sheet.rs:144), `.notification.placement` / `.delivery` (notification.rs:420, :828), and its own dialog test edits `theme.motion` through `Theme::update` (dialog/dialog.rs:1070). Test to write: init, `Theme::global_mut(cx).sheet.margin_top = px(40.)`, `apply(from_preset("nord",true,..))`, then assert `cx.theme().sheet.margin_top == px(40.)` (fails today).
**Fix proposed:** Before the write at lib.rs:1041, copy the four fields from the installed global (`if let Some(old) = cx.try_global::<GpuiTheme>() { theme.notification = old.notification.clone(); ... }`), so `apply` replaces only what `to_theme` maps, as upstream's `apply_config` does. Add the test above.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — apply_inner (lib.rs:1040) runs `*GpuiTheme::global_mut(cx) = theme`, and to_theme builds that theme from `GpuiTheme::from(&theme_color)` (gpui-component 0.7.3 theme/mod.rs:765-790: notification/list/sheet/motion all `::default()`) without setting those four fields, while upstream's own `Theme::change` (mod.rs:388-398) edits only `mode`; nothing in apply's docs (lib.rs:836-886) tells the application its settings are reset. The motion half is already noted in docs/todo.md:2002 and the known items (:840), but only as a gap in what native-theme models, not as the application's own settings being reset.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug: `apply` must keep the application's `notification`, `list`, `sheet` and `motion` settings as upstream's own switch does (the motion half is docs/todo.md's existing entry, closed with it).
**Status:** fixed in c1208377 (M6 T5; e1e00c3b)


#### M6-02 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:1045
**Claim:** A single-variant `apply` keeps the other mode's variant stored by an earlier, different theme and installs it under the new theme's name. Trigger: `apply_system_theme(&sys)` (or `apply` of preset A dark), then `apply(from_preset("dracula", false))`, then the OS turns dark and the app calls `Theme::sync_system_appearance`. The window then shows the earlier theme's dark palette, scrollbars, base palette, tooltip delay and `geometry` values, labelled Dracula.
**Evidence:** `apply` passes `(Some(resolved), None)` for a light theme (lib.rs:896-901). `apply_inner` overwrites only `nt.light` (lib.rs:1027-1032), so `nt.dark` keeps the earlier theme's variant. lib.rs:1045-1054 then builds `other_config` from `nt.variant(!is_dark)` (that stale variant) under the new `name` and installs it as `styled.dark_theme` (:1055-1061). After `Theme::change` to dark, the observer reads the same stale variant: `repair_base_palette` (:1169), `write_base_overrides` -> `base_overrides_for` (:1091), `install_variant_tooltip_delay` (:1009), and `NativeTheme::resolved` / `native` for every `geometry` builder (:783-801). The doc says otherwise: 'A single-variant `apply` leaves the other mode's config at `ThemeConfig::default()`, so a `Theme::change` to the unstored mode shows upstream's built-in ... constants' (lib.rs:871-876). The showcase repeats that claim (examples/showcase-gpui/app.rs:1668-1669). The showcase itself installs the OS theme with both variants (app.rs:1222, :1731) and then presets with one `apply` (app.rs:1780), which is exactly this sequence. Rationale §2.22 / D34 designed the stored pair for the two modes of one theme. They do not address a theme switch.
**Fix proposed:** Have `apply` drop the other stored variant when the new theme's name differs from the installed `GpuiTheme::theme_name()` (or always, with a two-variant `apply_pair(light, dark)` for the both-modes case). Then the doc's 'upstream default for the unstored mode' holds. Add a test: `apply_system_theme`, then a one-variant `apply` of another preset, then `Theme::change` to the other mode, and assert that the palette is not the first theme's.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — apply_inner (lib.rs:1025-1031) writes only the `Some` variants into NativeTheme and never clears the other one, so a later single-variant `apply` keeps the earlier theme's `nt.dark`; `other_config` (:1045-1055) then builds the dark ThemeConfig from it under the new `name`, and base_overrides_for and install_variant_tooltip_delay read the same stale variant. This contradicts apply's own doc (:871-875: 'a single-variant apply leaves the other mode's config at ThemeConfig::default()'). Also reported by R2 (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:1027): Repeated runtime switching keeps state: a single-variant `apply` of theme B after an `apply` of theme A of the other mode (or after `apply_system_theme`) keeps A's variant as B's other mode, so a later upstream `Theme::change` / `sync_system_appearance` shows A's palette, A's base-layer scrollbar/handle values and A's geometry under B's name. Verifier: CONFIRMED — apply (lib.rs:889-902) fills only one slot, apply_inner (lib.rs:1027-1032) never clears the other, and lib.rs:1037-1053 builds the other mode's config from the stale variant under the new name. The showcase's preset switch (examples/showcase-gpui/app.rs:1780) does exactly this. Rationale §2.22 records that variants accumulate, meant for one apply per variant of the same theme, but the doc at lib.rs:877-881 ('leaves the other mode's config at ThemeConfig::default()') contradicts the code once any earlier apply stored the other mode.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED bug, found by R1 and R2 (merged): a one-variant `apply` must clear the other mode's stored variant, as the doc says.
**Status:** fixed in c1208377 (M6 T5; e1e00c3b)


#### M6-03 · perf · S3 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:623
**Claim:** The first `to_theme` / `from_preset` / `from_system` for a theme whose UI or mono family has not been seen before (feature `system-fonts`, on by default) runs one `fc-match` subprocess per new family. It runs synchronously on the calling (usually UI) thread while holding a process-wide mutex, with a 2 s timeout each. This explains the 31-105 ms first calls of the timing lead.
**Evidence:** Path: `to_theme` calls `font_family` twice (lib.rs:237, :242), and `config::to_theme_config` calls it twice more (config.rs:65, :67). Off macOS, `font_family` -> `substituted_family` (lib.rs:604). On a miss in `ASKED` that function calls `native_theme::fonts::substitute_family` (lib.rs:623) while holding the `Mutex` guard taken at :616. That function runs `stdout_with_timeout("fc-match", ...)` with `SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT` = 2 s (native-theme fonts.rs:298-312, detect.rs:20). It is asked for an installed family too (the answer is then `None`, fonts.rs:308-309), unlike egui, which asks only after `system_face` fails (native-theme-egui fonts.rs:165-171). The pattern matches the timings exactly. Preset families: kde-breeze Noto Sans/Hack, adwaita Adwaita Sans/Adwaita Mono, windows-11 Segoe UI/Cascadia Mono, macos-monterey SF Pro/SF Mono (macos-tahoe and ios-13 reuse both), material-3 Roboto/Roboto Mono, catppuccin-latte Inter/JetBrains Mono (all ten later community presets reuse both). So the six slow presets are exactly the first to bring two new families each, and the fast ones bring none. Measured here (2026-10-15, shell, not cargo): `fc-match --format=%{family[0]} <family>` takes 13.4-18.5 ms per call. Two calls give about 31-35 ms, the floor seen for adwaita, windows-11, macos-monterey, material-3 and catppuccin-latte. kde-breeze's further 30-70 ms is one-time process work on the first call: gpui-component's `DEFAULT_THEME_COLORS` LazyLock (a serde_json parse, theme/registry.rs:13-18), first reached through `HighlightTheme::default_light/dark` (lib.rs:264-266, config.rs:52-56) and `Theme::from`, plus the cold fontconfig cache of the first `fc-match`. iced's `from_preset` does no family substitution, hence 0.3-0.7 ms. No growth across switches: one answer per distinct family, kept for the process (so a family installed later stays substituted). Measurement to confirm: `strace -f -e trace=execve -c` over the timings test should count 12 `fc-match` execs, one per distinct family. Or time `font_family(&family)` cold against warm in timings.rs. Or run timings.rs without `system-fonts`: every first call except kde-breeze's should drop below 1 ms.
**Fix proposed:** Do not hold `ASKED`'s lock across the subprocess (look up, release, ask, insert), and let the application warm the cache off the UI thread: a `pub fn prefetch_font_families(&[Arc<str>])`, or `apply` spawning the stored variants' families on the background executor. State the per-new-family first-call cost (one `fc-match`, about 15 ms) in the `from_preset` / `to_theme` / `font_family` docs, beside the reduced-motion note at lib.rs:294-299.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — substituted_family (lib.rs:613-627) holds the static ASKED mutex while it calls native_theme::fonts::substitute_family, which runs `fc-match` through stdout_with_timeout with SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT = 2 s (fonts.rs:301-306, detect.rs:20), once for each family not yet cached. I measured it by putting an fc-match logging shim first on PATH (strace is not installed) and running the existing release binary target/release/deps/timings-70a7c1d576d38ab0 (no build): 12 fc-match calls of about 12.5 ms each, exactly two (UI + mono) in each of the six first calls of 31-48 ms (kde-breeze, adwaita, windows-11, macos-monterey, material-3, catppuccin-latte); every other preset's first call was 0.25-0.39 ms with no fc-match call.
**Triage:** fix — perf: the before/after first-call timing in tests/timings.rs is the gate (31–106 ms today); the subprocess must not run under the cache lock.
**Status:** fixed in 44545c55 (M6 T14): the lock half; the first-call speed half dropped by the Step 6 ruling (the cost is once per family per process, documented)


#### M6-04 · perf · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/config.rs:44
**Claim:** Each `to_theme` builds the whole 139-field `ThemeColor` twice, and each `apply_inner` builds it a third time for the other mode's config. The 127 hex strings it allocates are part of the warm per-switch cost (gpui 52-117 µs warm against iced 35-49 µs).
**Evidence:** `to_theme` computes `colors::to_theme_color(resolved, is_dark, prefs.reduce_transparency)` (lib.rs:224) and then calls `config::to_theme_config(resolved, name, mode, prefs)` (lib.rs:270). That function recomputes `to_theme_color(resolved, is_dark, prefs.reduce_transparency)` with identical arguments (config.rs:36, :44) and formats 127 `String`s through `hsla_to_hex` into `SharedString`s (config.rs:101-237). `apply_inner` adds a full `to_theme_config` for the other stored variant (lib.rs:1052): another `to_theme_color` and another 127 strings. It also adds two `font_family` calls, each a mutex lock, a HashMap lookup and a `String` clone (lib.rs:616-621), on top of the two in `to_theme`. Per-call cost not measured. To measure it, add timings.rs rows for `to_theme` alone and for `colors::to_theme_color` alone (or count allocations with a counting allocator) before and after.
**Fix proposed:** Split `to_theme_config` into a private `to_theme_config_from(&ThemeColor, resolved, name, mode, prefs)` and have `to_theme` pass the `theme_color` it already built (it is `Copy`). Pass `theme.font_family` / `mono_font_family` too, so the config takes the families `to_theme` resolved.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — to_theme computes to_theme_color at lib.rs:223, then calls config::to_theme_config (:270), which computes it again (config.rs:44) and converts 127 fields to hex SharedStrings (config.rs:45, :93-); apply_inner builds a third copy for the other mode (lib.rs:1052). How much of the warm 52 µs this costs is not measured, and the timing test calls from_preset, so the third copy (apply_inner) is not in it. A criterion bench of to_theme_color + theme_color_to_config_colors against a whole from_preset would show the share.
**Triage:** fix if measurable — build the colour table once per `to_theme`/`apply`; kept only if warm `from_preset` drops beyond the run-to-run spread, else dropped.
**Status:** dropped (M6 T13): the warm `from_preset` gain was below the before-runs' spread (numbers in the T13 report; `to_theme` alone −1–1.5 µs); the timing rows stay in tests/timings.rs


#### M6-05 · bug · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:241
**Claim:** `to_theme` hands gpui the unchecked product of `d.font.size * s`. `text_scale_factor()` only guarantees the factor is finite and positive, so an extreme factor overflows the window rem to +inf or underflows it to 0 px. Trigger: `AccessibilityPreferences { text_scaling_factor: 1e37, .. }` with a 13 px font gives inf; `1e-45` gives 0.
**Evidence:** lib.rs:241 `theme.font_size = px(d.font.size * s)` and :243 the mono size, with `s = prefs.text_scale_factor()` (:223). config.rs:66 and :68 use the same products for `Theme::change`. Core's `text_scale_factor` returns the field when `is_finite() && > 0.0` (native-theme lib.rs:393-396), and `scaled` is the plain product (:403-405). Validation bounds a font size only from below (`check_font`: finite and > 0, resolve/validate_helpers.rs:491), so neither factor nor size has an upper bound. gpui-component sets the rem to `font_size` (lib.rs:238-240), so every rem-relative length becomes inf or 0. The realistic platform ranges are far inside this (GNOME 0.5-3.0), so only an application-set or corrupt value reaches it. What gpui then does with an infinite rem is not traced here.
**Fix proposed:** Make core's `scaled()` return `size` when the product is not finite and positive (one guard that every connector and `geometry` builder inherits), and have `to_theme` / `to_theme_config` call `prefs.scaled(d.font.size)` instead of multiplying by hand.
**Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE — The mechanism holds: text_scale_factor (native-theme/src/lib.rs:393-396) checks only that the factor is finite and > 0, and lib.rs:241/:243 multiply by it unchecked. The stated triggers are wrong in f32, though: 13 * 1e37 = 1.3e38 (finite), and 13 * 1e-45 = 1.8e-44 (subnormal, not 0). Only a factor above about 2.6e37 gives inf, and what gpui does with an inf rem needs a test to show.
**Triage:** fix once reproduced — PLAUSIBLE: the fix's first step is a test giving `to_theme` a finite factor whose product overflows; a non-finite font size falls back as the text scale does.
**Status:** fixed in b2685e69, 4e2b586a (M6 T13): core `AccessibilityPreferences::scaled` keeps the size when the product is not a normal positive number; egui keeps its spec's stock-size fallback (d05d64f6)


#### M6-06 · api · api-break · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:478
**Claim:** `is_dark(resolved)` is a second public name for `is_dark_resolved(resolved)`. Both are the background-lightness guess that M3-15's ruling replaces with `Resolved.mode` / `SystemTheme::mode` in M6.
**Evidence:** lib.rs:477-480: `pub fn is_dark(resolved: &ResolvedTheme) -> bool { is_dark_resolved(resolved) }`, documented as 'Equivalent to [`is_dark_resolved()`]'. lib.rs:467-470 holds the lightness test. iced and egui export neither name (grep of connectors/*/src: only gpui). The `to_theme` docs point users at `is_dark_resolved` (lib.rs:205-206). The M3-15 ruling (docs/todo_code-review-findings.md:7367) schedules gpui's switch from that guess to `Resolved.mode` in M6. The `from_preset` mode fix itself is that known item and is not re-reported here.
**Fix proposed:** Before: `pub fn is_dark(resolved: &ResolvedTheme) -> bool` and `pub fn is_dark_resolved(resolved: &ResolvedTheme) -> bool`. After: keep only `is_dark_resolved` (or neither, once `from_preset` takes the mode from `Resolved.mode` and `to_theme` keeps its explicit `is_dark`), with the `to_theme` doc pointing at `Resolved::mode`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — is_dark (lib.rs:476-480) only delegates to is_dark_resolved (:467-469), so it is a second public name for the same function. The lightness-guess half is the known M3-15 ruling (findings ledger :7367, scheduled for M6) and not new. Note that a bare `&ResolvedTheme` carries no mode, so Resolved.mode can replace the guess in from_preset but cannot replace the helper itself (iced kept its lightness test in to_theme for the same reason, ledger M3-15 status). The only new content is removing the duplicate name. Also reported by API (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:478): `is_dark(resolved)` is a public alias of `is_dark_resolved(resolved)`: two crate-root names for one background-lightness guess that neither sibling offers and that core's `Resolved.mode` (M3-15) makes unnecessary. Verifier: CONFIRMED — is_dark (lib.rs:478-480) just forwards to is_dark_resolved (:468), and neither iced nor egui has either function. The workspace has no caller of is_dark; is_dark_resolved has an in-crate test (lib.rs:1679), a doc link (:206), scripts/check_connector_parity.py:869 and scripts/connector_parity_exceptions.toml:27 and :55 (is_dark is listed there as 'undecided'). The lightness-guess half is already scheduled for M6 by the M3-15 ruling (findings :7367), so only the alias removal is new.
**Triage:** maintainer: 2026-10-15, remove `is_dark` only; `is_dark_resolved` stays for a caller holding a bare `ResolvedTheme` (its parity exception stays, `is_dark`'s goes) → fix.
**Status:** fixed in 4c5410e8 (M6 T2): `is_dark` removed, `is_dark_resolved` kept (maintainer 2026-10-15)


#### M6-07 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/base_layer.rs:71
**Claim:** The drawn scrollbar thumb's minimum length is `min_thumb_length - (groove_width - thumb_width)`, not `scrollbar.min_thumb_length`: under kde-breeze a 7px minimum where the theme states 20, under windows-11 6px where it states 17.
**Evidence:** scrollbar_geometry passes `min_length = min_thumb_length` (:71) and `inset = (groove - thumb)/2` (:69) to every thumb state (:92-112). gpui-base 0.7.3 ThumbGeometry::new (src/scrollbar.rs:1201-1217): `logical_length = (container/content*container).max(min_length).min(track)`, `inset = inset.clamp(0, logical_length/2)`, `length: logical_length - inset * 2`, and the fill is drawn `size(thumb_width, thumb_length)` with that length (:1503-1528); resolve_thumb takes the global thumb style's inset and min_length (:993-1011). kde-breeze: groove 21, thumb 8 -> inset 6.5, drawn minimum 20 - 13 = 7px; windows-11: 17/6 -> 5.5, 17 - 11 = 6px; macos-tahoe 17/7 -> 40 - 10 = 30; adwaita 12/8 -> 40 - 4 = 36 (preset values from native-theme/src/presets/*.toml [light.scrollbar]). docs/platform-facts.md:976 defines the field as the thumb's minimum length along the scroll axis. Rationale §5.1 (todo_v0.5.8_gpui-component-0.6-rationale.md:703-711) records the inset formula and that upstream trims the thumb by inset at both ends, but not this consequence for the minimum; ScrollbarGeometry's own doc (:34-38) notes the 2 x inset subtraction without compensating.
**Fix proposed:** Write `min_length = min_thumb_length + 2 * thumb_inset` (a derivation from the two theme values and upstream's arithmetic, like the inset itself), so the drawn thumb is at least the stated length; the proportional length still loses 2 x inset at the track ends, which only a per-axis inset upstream could fix (an upstream ask beside the existing scrollbar items).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — gpui-base 0.7.3 scrollbar.rs:1211-1216 clamps the logical length to min_length and then draws length = logical - 2*inset. With inset = (groove - thumb)/2 (base_layer.rs:69), the drawn minimum is 20-13=7 on kde-breeze (21/8/20) and 17-11=6 on windows-11 (17/6/17). platform-facts.md:976 defines min_thumb_length as the thumb's length along the axis, and no rationale accepts the gap: the 0.6.4 rationale §2.6 notes the clamps but not this.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: pass the minimum length plus twice the inset so the drawn thumb is the stated minimum.
**Status:** fixed in 7369383d (M6 T6)


#### M6-08 · bug · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/geometry.rs:111
**Claim:** `defaults.line_height` reaches only the control-height builders (button, input, select, combobox, menu_item, list_item, button_label/toggle, text_area); every other text builder -- tooltip, dialog_description, dialog_title, status_bar, table, checkbox, radio, title_bar, toolbar, link -- leaves the text at gpui's default line height of 1.618, so wrapped tooltip and dialog text is spaced by gpui's metric, not the platform's (1.19 macOS, 1.21 adwaita, 1.36 KDE, 1.43 Windows).
**Evidence:** with_text (:111-114) sets size and weight only; the line height is set only in with_height_rule (:167), button_label (:240) and text_area (:338). Nothing else sets one: gpui's TextStyle::default has `line_height: phi()` (gpui-pre 0.3.9 src/style.rs:494); gpui-component's root sets the rem, family and colour only (src/root.rs:440-450); tooltip.rs and status_bar.rs set none; dialog/title.rs:44 sets relative(1.25) before the refinement. tooltip_content (:473-482) makes a tooltip's text wrap, so a three-line tooltip on windows-11 is spaced 3 x 1.618 em instead of 3 x 1.43 em. In a DataTable refined with `table` (:632-634), the Size::Size cells set no text style (sizing.rs:323-333) and clip (`overflow_hidden`, table/state.rs:1406-1412): on macos-tahoe (13px font, 24px row, Medium cell padding 4/4) a 21px phi line box sits in a 16px content box, so the text sits about 2.7px low; at the platform's 1.19 it is 15.5px and fits. docs/todo.md:2345-2359 treats the line height as carried everywhere but the Editor.
**Fix proposed:** Move `.line_height(relative(n.resolved.defaults.line_height))` into `with_text` (with_coloured_text inherits it) so every builder that sets a text size carries the platform's line height; with_height_rule, button_label and text_area then no longer need their own copy.
**Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE — Only with_height_rule (geometry.rs:166-167), button_label (:240) and text_area (:338) set defaults.line_height; with_text (:109-112) sets none. The '1.618 everywhere' part is overstated: phi is gpui-pre style.rs:494's default and holds where upstream sets nothing (tooltip.rs, status bar), but upstream sets 1.25 on the dialog title (dialog/title.rs:44) and on the checkbox and radio labels (checkbox.rs:334, radio.rs:255). Unstated-sizes rationale §5 point 3 scoped the line height to single-line control heights, so carrying it to wrapped text is an extension, and a rendered tooltip test would show the spacing.
**Triage:** fix once reproduced — PLAUSIBLE: a rendered test of wrapped tooltip text first; the unstated-sizes rationale (§5.3) limits the control-height rule to single-line controls, not the platform's line height, so applying `defaults.line_height` to text builders follows theme data.
**Status:** fixed in 15bde521 (M6 T6; reproduced first)


#### M6-09 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/geometry.rs:847
**Claim:** At a text-scaling factor above 1, `data_table_size` (and `list_header_height`) keep the row at `list.row_height` while `table` scales the cell text, so on macos-tahoe at factor 2 a 26px cell font is clipped by its 24px row -- the 'text lies inside it' rule the module applies to single-line controls (:32-45) does not reach DataTable rows.
**Evidence:** data_table_size returns Size::Size(px(row_height)) whatever the factor (:847-854); list_header_height likewise (:861-863). table() scales item_font by the factor (:633 -> :101-103). DataTable rows are `.h(row_height)` with row_height = size.table_row_height() (table/state.rs:2047, :2061; Size::Size returns it verbatim, sizing.rs:57-64), cells are `h_full().overflow_hidden()` with Medium padding 4 top and bottom (state.rs:1406-1412, sizing.rs:89-94). macos-tahoe list.row_height 24, defaults font 13pt at 72 DPI: at factor 2 the line box is 26 x 1.19 = 31px even at the platform's line height, against a 16px content box in a clipping 24px cell. Upstream's unstated fallback (Medium, 32px) is a px constant too. Rationale §5 point 3 (todo_v0.5.9_unstated-sizes-and-chrome-ux-rationale.md:104, :274-277) requires fit at scale 2 for controls; no record covers DataTable rows. A seams test would lay a one-cell DataTable out under macos-tahoe at factor 2 and assert the text probe lies inside the row.
**Fix proposed:** Above factor 1, return Size::Size(max(row_height, scaled item_font size x defaults.line_height + Medium cell padding top + bottom)) -- the same fit rule, from theme values and upstream's own padding -- and the header height likewise; or document the limit beside the builder if a fixed row is preferred.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — data_table_size (geometry.rs:847-854) returns Size::Size(list.row_height) with no text-scale branch, and DataTable rows take it verbatim as .h(row_height) (table/state.rs:2047, :2061, :2321). geometry::table scales list.item_font through with_text, so at factor 2 macos-tahoe gets a 26px font in a 24px row. Neither docs/todo.md nor the known items cover it (the 2073 item is egui's); a seams.rs case at factor 2 would show the clip.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: above text scale 1 a DataTable row and header grow with their text, as the control-height rule does for single-line controls.
**Status:** fixed in fbf5952f, 9580c240 (M6 T6)


#### M6-10 · simplify · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/geometry.rs:430
**Claim:** The defensive clamps are inconsistent: every builder clamps `corner_radius` with `.max(0.0)` and `tooltip`/`tooltip_content` clamp `line_width`, but `button`, `input`, `text_area`, `list` and `group_box_content` pass `line_width` unclamped, and no padding, height, width or gap is clamped, although the core rejects a negative or non-finite value for all of them alike.
**Evidence:** Clamped: :187, :291, :341, :428, :430, :480, :495, :541, :580, :626, :643, :654, :737 (radius), :430 and :480 (tooltip line_width); unclamped: :188, :292, :342, :624, :655 (line_width), plus every padding side, min_height, min_width, row_height, track_height, gap. Validation covers both kinds the same way: check_widget_border checks corner_radius, line_width and every stated padding side for finite and >= 0 (native-theme/src/resolve/validate_helpers.rs:517-545), and the widget fields carry `check = "non_negative"` (native-theme/src/model/widgets/mod.rs, e.g. :343-352). A hand-built or deserialised ResolvedTheme (pub fields, serde::Deserialize, resolved.rs:161-163) can bypass validation for any field, so the clamps protect radius and the tooltip edge only.
**Fix proposed:** Pick one policy: trust the validated ResolvedTheme and drop the `.max(0.0)` calls (and the same 'Issue 14' clamp in to_theme), or clamp every length through one helper used by with_padding and each builder.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — line_width is clamped only in tooltip and tooltip_content (geometry.rs:430, :480) and passed raw at :188, :292, :342, :624, :655, while corner_radius is always clamped. Core's check_widget_border (native-theme/src/resolve/validate_helpers.rs:517-545) already rejects a non-finite or negative radius, line width or stated padding side, so the clamps are inconsistent defensive code.
**Triage:** fix — drop the redundant clamps (core's validation rejects negative and non-finite lengths); deletes code.
**Status:** fixed in ee0d1701, ca5c2c58 (M6 T6)

**Claim:** custom_icon_to_image_source(provider, IconSet::Freedesktop, Some(c), _) for a full-colour freedesktop icon (Breeze's places/32/folder.svg, accent body style="fill:currentColor" under a .ColorScheme-Accent stylesheet) repaints it in c: the loader's result is coloured a second time by the monochrome colouriser. M1-T6-06's status (ledger ~:822) schedules only gpui's copy drop for M6, and docs/todo.md has no entry for the second pass, so this is new: the gpui twin of M5-05.

#### M6-12 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/icons.rs:459
**Claim:** freedesktop_name_for_gpui_icon picks a name by desktop, not by icon theme. Under Sway, Hyprland, River, Niri, Wayfire, COSMIC or an unknown desktop (all non-GTK in the matches! at :459-466), or on KDE with the adwaita preset's "Adwaita" theme, 50 of the 106 IconName variants (every split arm at :528-879) get Breeze's name, which Adwaita lacks, so they load None even though Adwaita has the icon under its GTK name.
**Evidence:** :459-466: is_gtk is true only for Gnome|Budgie|Cinnamon|Mate|Xfce; every other LinuxDesktop variant (native-theme/src/detect.rs:27-54: LxQt, Hyprland, Sway, River, Niri, Wayfire, CosmicDe, Unknown) takes the else branch. The doc (:433-435) says 'Unknown share the Breeze/KDE convention', but the name has to exist in the icon theme the caller loads from, not on the desktop. Checked against the installed /usr/share/icons/Adwaita (with and without -symbolic): every one of the 50 split arms' KDE names is missing there, and every GTK counterpart is present, e.g. Eye 'view-visible' vs 'view-reveal', Check 'dialog-ok' vs 'object-select', Close 'tab-close' vs 'window-close', ArrowDown 'go-down-skip' vs 'go-bottom'. FreedesktopLoader searches only the theme's Inherits chain, never hicolor (native-theme/src/freedesktop.rs:555-558). The gpui showcase hits it: support.rs:728-738 pairs the running desktop from XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP with the preset's or CLI's icon theme, and :805/:828 load the table's name from that theme. Test to write: for every IconName, freedesktop_name_for_gpui_icon(icon, LinuxDesktop::Sway) resolves in FreedesktopLoader::new(name).theme("Adwaita") wherever the Gnome name does. It fails for 50 icons today.
**Fix proposed:** Key the choice by the icon theme's convention instead of the desktop, for example a parameter naming the theme (Breeze-family if its Inherits chain contains breeze, else GTK). Or return both candidate names so the caller tries each in the same theme, which mixes no sets. Then add the Adwaita test above for a non-GTK desktop.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — is_gtk (:459-466) depends only on the LinuxDesktop argument, and the showcase passes the DE apart from the theme it loads from (support.rs:803-808, :826-830). A script over the 50 `if is_gtk` arms found none of the 50 Breeze-branch names in /usr/share/icons/Adwaita (e.g. go-down-skip, battery-100-charging), while every GTK-branch name is there; no rationale or todo entry records this.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: freedesktop names are chosen by the icon theme in use, not by the desktop.
**Status:** fixed in c0526654, d5d781a8, bce6dd56 (M6 T7: `freedesktop_name_candidates` and core's `FreedesktopLoader::any`)

Core's load_custom_icon (icons.rs:687) takes no size either, so the planned M1-T6-06 switch does not fix this by itself.

**Claim:** animated_frames_to_image_sources(&freedesktop_frames, Some(c), _) runs the monochrome colouriser over a freedesktop theme's frames (Breeze's animations/22/process-working.svg, fill="currentColor" under a .ColorScheme-Text { color:#232629 } stylesheet). **Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Breeze's animations/22/process-working.svg is a 22x330 strip with `.ColorScheme-Text { color:#232629 }` and fill=currentColor. parse_sprite_sheet (freedesktop.rs:482+) keeps the document, and :1179 maps each frame through to_image_source -> colorize_svg, which overrides the stated colour. #### M6-15 · bug · S1 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/icons.rs:1234
**Claim:** with_spin_animation(el, id, 0) panics in a debug build and yields a NaN rotation in release: the public u32 admits the zero that core's model forbids (TransformAnimation::Spin's duration_ms and FrameList's frame_duration_ms are NonZeroU32). AnimatedImageSources::frame_duration_ms (:56) drops the same guarantee.
**Evidence:** :1241 Animation::new(Duration::from_millis(0)).repeat(). gpui-pre 0.3.9 src/elements/animation.rs:426 computes delta = elapsed.as_secs_f32() / 0.0, which is NaN at elapsed 0 or inf after it. inf > 1.0 takes delta %= 1.0 = NaN (:438-439). :446 then hits debug_assert!(delta.is_finite(), ...), a panic in debug builds. The doc (:1221-1222) calls this 'caller's responsibility', against the no-runtime-panics rule. Every in-tree caller passes a NonZeroU32's .get() (widgets/spinner.rs:487, the showcase's duration_ms.get()). Core: native-theme/src/model/animated.rs:125, :133.
**Fix proposed:** Before: pub fn with_spin_animation(element: Svg, animation_id: impl Into<gpui::ElementId>, duration_ms: u32) -> impl IntoElement; pub frame_duration_ms: u32. After: duration_ms: NonZeroU32 (callers drop .get()); pub frame_duration_ms: NonZeroU32.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — gpui-pre 0.3.9 elements/animation.rs:426 computes elapsed/duration (0/0 = NaN, x/0 = inf, then `%= 1.0` gives NaN), and :446 debug_asserts that delta is finite. Core's Spin duration and FrameList's frame duration are NonZeroU32 (freedesktop.rs:594-595), and :1193 calls .get(), which drops that guarantee. The doc's own wording, 'a zero-duration animation' (:1222-1223), understates the result.
**Triage:** fix + maintainer: the zero-period panic is fixed without a break; maintainer 2026-10-15: `with_spin_animation`'s `duration_ms` and `AnimatedImageSources::frame_duration_ms` take `NonZeroU32` → fix.
**Status:** fixed in 8212bf00 (M6 T1: `NonZeroU32`, maintainer 2026-10-15)


#### M6-16 · perf · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/icons.rs:1311
**Claim:** Every rasterized icon and every RGBA icon copies its whole pixel buffer once more than needed, including through into_image_source, whose stated purpose is to avoid the copy (module table :12, 'avoids clone').
**Evidence:** svg_to_render_source (:1251-1254) owns the IconData::Rgba from rasterize_svg, but passes rgba.data() as a borrow; rgba_to_render_source then does rgba.to_vec() (:1311). into_image_source (:997-1002) takes ownership and delegates to to_image_source(&data, ..), so an owned RGBA icon is copied too; its doc (:987-989) reasons only about SVG. RgbaData::into_data() exists (native-theme/src/model/icons.rs:391), and iced uses it (native-theme-iced/src/icons.rs:245-248). It is 9 KiB at the default 48 px and up to 1 MiB at the 512 clamp, per icon per rebuild (a theme or colour switch re-rasterizes every cached icon).
**Fix proposed:** Make rgba_to_render_source take a RgbaData (or a Vec<u8>) and swap in place. svg_to_render_source and an owned into_image_source pass rgba.into_data(), and to_image_source's borrowed RGBA arm keeps the one copy.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Holds for rasterized SVGs and for into_image_source: rasterize_svg returns an owned RgbaData, but svg_to_render_source (:1250-1255) borrows .data() and rgba_to_render_source copies it with to_vec (:1311), and into_image_source drops the owned data and goes through the same copy, although RgbaData::into_data exists (model/icons.rs:391). For a borrowed &IconData::Rgba passed to to_image_source the one copy is needed, so 'every RGBA icon' overstates it. To confirm the cost, measure allocations and time for to_image_source at 48 and 512 px (a 9 KiB and a 1 MiB memcpy) against an owned-buffer path, for example with a dhat or criterion run.
**Triage:** fix if measurable — `into_data()` instead of a copy; a 48 px and 512 px timing before and after; dropped below the spread.
**Status:** fixed in 863594be, f8900791 (M6 T13; 512 px row 277–325 → 221 µs, above the spread)

**Claim:** The SVG branch is written twice and wrapped twice. to_image_source's Svg arm (:969-978) repeats svg_bytes_to_image_source (:1125-1137) line for line, and bundled_svg_to_image_source (:1111-1118) is a public pass-through of it. M1-T7-01's colouriser switch would have to edit both copies.
