#### M6-19 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/slider.rs:299
**Claim:** A disabled Slider under a theme whose slider.disabled_opacity is below 1 (adwaita, and the community presets at 0.5; ios-13 at 0.3) fades each quad on its own, so the rail shows through the fill and the rail and fill show through the thumb. The checkbox, radio and switch fade as one widget over a backdrop since b37ddfa6.
**Evidence:** SliderLook::of (slider.rs:60-90) keeps the opacity as a plain field and has no faded_over. render applies `.opacity(look.opacity)` to the root (slider.rs:299). gpui multiplies each quad's alpha by that opacity on its own: mod.rs:168-172 cites gpui-pre window.rs:4687-4695 `paint_quad` and says this 'would show a faded part through another'. The rail div (slider.rs:256-265), the fill div (:267-277), the half-alpha outline quad (:234) and the thumb quad (:242) overlap. With adwaita (disabled_opacity 0.5, adwaita.toml:61, and ':207 a disabled scale is its enabled self at disabled_opacity') the filled stretch comes out as 0.5 fill + 0.25 rail + 0.25 ground, where libadwaita's whole-widget `filter: Opacity` gives 0.5 fill + 0.5 ground. The thumb is translucent over the fill. CheckboxLook::faded_over (checkbox.rs:185-199) and SwitchLook::faded_over (switch.rs:128-141) were written for exactly this (commit b37ddfa6 named the switch, the check box and the radio, not the slider), and egui-widgets fades every control in a scope as one (native-theme-egui-widgets/src/scope.rs:56). Test to write: under adwaita light, `SliderLook::of(&r, true)` faded over defaults.background_color should give an opaque fill equal to `faded(ground, over(ground, track), fill, 0.5)` and opacity 1. Today there is no such method, and the rendered root carries opacity 0.5.
**Fix proposed:** Add `SliderLook::faded_over(ground)`: the rail over the ground, the fill over the rail, the outline and the thumb over the fill, each faded by the opacity over the ground, and opacity set to 1. Add a `Slider::backdrop` as Checkbox and Switch have, and call it in render the way switch.rs:256-259 does.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — slider.rs:299 puts look.opacity on the root, and gpui-pre's with_element_opacity (window.rs:4212-4226) multiplies the alpha of each painted primitive. SliderLook has no faded_over/backdrop counterpart to CheckboxLook::faded_over (checkbox.rs:185) or SwitchLook::faded_over (switch.rs:128), and adwaita's slider inherits defaults.disabled_opacity 0.5 (adwaita.toml:61, :207).
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: the disabled slider fades as one, as checkbox and switch do (`faded_over`).
**Status:** fixed in ef4807b9 (M6 T10)


#### M6-20 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/slider.rs:205
**Claim:** A Slider given a range SliderState (`default_value(20.0..80.0)`, which gpui-component's slider draws with two thumbs) draws one thumb at the end and a fill from the rail's start. A press nearer the start moves the start value, which has no visible thumb. Left, Right, Home or End then turn the range into a single value.
**Evidence:** render reads only `s.value().end()` and `s.percentage().end` (slider.rs:205, :209). It draws one SliderThumb (:223) without `.start(..)`, and the fill from `left(-radius)` to `right(1 - percentage)` (:267-277), so a range's start is never shown. gpui-base's SliderTrack still picks the nearer thumb for a range on a press (`is_start = if is_range { position < center }`, gpui-base-0.7.3 slider.rs:677-689) and moves `percentage.start` and `value.set_start`, a thumb this widget does not draw. On a key, `stepped` returns an f32 (slider.rs:156-170), and `step_by` calls `state.set_value(value, ..)` (:184). `From<f32> for SliderValue` is `Single` (gpui-base slider.rs:42-46), and set_value replaces the whole value (:273-282), so `Range(20, 80)` becomes `Single(81)` and the range is lost. gpui-component's Slider, the widget this one stands in for and its own fallback (slider.rs:141-146), draws a start thumb when `is_range` (gpui-component-0.7.3 slider.rs:149, :196) and supports a vertical axis (:206-212); this one is horizontal only.
**Fix proposed:** Either draw the range (a second SliderThumb with `.start(true)` at `percentage.start`, the fill from start to end, keys moving the end through `set_value((start, new_end))`), or render the fallback when `state.read(cx).value().is_range()`. Say in the doc that the widget is horizontal-only.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — render reads only value().end() and percentage().end (slider.rs:205, :209) and draws one SliderThumb with no .start(true). gpui-base's SliderTrack mouse-down picks is_start for a range (gpui-base slider.rs:677-689), and set_value(f32) stores SliderValue::Single (slider.rs:273-281 via stepped/step_by at :156-186), so a key press turns the range into a single value.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: a range state draws two thumbs and keeps its range on key presses (the vertical axis is api-add, in the same task).
**Status:** fixed in 91764f46, cfd31e14 (M6 T10)


#### M6-21 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/checkbox.rs:442
**Claim:** The checkbox and radio labels, and each tab label, read the size and weight of checkbox.font and tab.font but not their family or style. A theme that states a family or an italic style for these widgets is drawn in the window's family, upright.
**Evidence:** indicator_and_label sets `.text_size(size).font_weight(weight).line_height(..).text_color(..)` on the label (checkbox.rs:442-449), from the triple built at :547-552 and :693-698. That triple holds `font.size`, `font.weight` and `defaults.line_height`; `font.family` and `font.style` are never read. TabBar does the same at tab_bar.rs:327-328 and :367-372. ResolvedFontSpec carries `family: Arc<str>` and `style: FontStyle` (native-theme/src/model/font.rs:257, :283). The only family the connector sets is the window's, from defaults.font.family (lib.rs:237, config.rs:65). The showcase's leaf table says so in as many words: 'checkbox.font ... family: the window's' and 'tab.font ... family: the window's' (examples/showcase-gpui/info/leaves.rs:501-503, :2048-2050). That is a resolved value the connector ignores. No bundled preset states a widget family today, so only a custom theme or a reader that sets one is affected. The geometry builders have the same gap outside this region.
**Fix proposed:** Set `.font_family(crate::font_family(&font.family))`, and `.italic()` for a non-normal style, on the checkbox/radio label and the tab label, next to the size and weight. Correct the two showcase leaf rows to match.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Checkbox and Radio build their font triple from size, weight and defaults.line_height only (checkbox.rs:547-551, :693-697), and the label div sets text_size, font_weight and line_height only (:441-449); TabBar does the same (tab_bar.rs:327-371). ResolvedFontSpec carries family and style (model/font.rs:255+), and no widget calls font_family or italic.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: the labels take the resolved font family and style (connectors follow theme data); the showcase note "family: the window's" goes with it.
**Status:** fixed in 9c509771 (checkbox/radio, M6 T11), 009fba77 (tab, M6 T12), 35785f1e (the geometry builders, final review)


#### M6-22 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/checkbox.rs:128
**Claim:** A theme that states checkbox.unchecked_background and leaves hover_background unset gets a hover fill of checkbox.background_color, a different colour, rather than no change. This is the gpui form of M5-07, which iced fixed in 98b522f7.
**Evidence:** `hover_fill = over(unchecked, color(c.hover_background.unwrap_or(c.background_color)))` (checkbox.rs:128-133). With `unchecked_background = Some(X)` and `background_color` opaque, `over` returns background_color, not X. widgets/mod.rs:33-34 states the rule 'a None soft option copies the colour it would cover', and the colour it would cover is the unchecked fill. The doc of CheckboxLook::of (:79-81) claims iced's reading, but iced now writes `hover_background.map_or(unchecked, ..)` (native-theme-iced/src/styles.rs:729-731, commit 98b522f7, M5-07: 'with unchecked_background stated and hover None, the hover layer becomes checkbox.background_color, a different fill'). The ruling at docs/todo_code-review-findings.md:9212 says that fix follows from C17. The test at widgets/tests.rs:71-72 mirrors the old expression. The archived spec table row (docs/archive/todo_gpui-widgets-spec.md:109) also says None gives background_color, which contradicts its own §1.3 (:69-70). All bundled presets state hover_background, so only a custom theme is affected.
**Fix proposed:** Write `hover_fill = c.hover_background.map_or(unchecked, |h| over(unchecked, color(h)))`, update the test at tests.rs:71-72 and the doc at :79-81, and note in the spec row that it was superseded.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — hover_fill = over(unchecked, hover_background.unwrap_or(background_color)) (checkbox.rs:128-133), so with hover unset the layer is background_color over unchecked_background, and over a translucent fill the alpha doubles. iced's 98b522f7 (M5-07) made the unset hover the idle fill. Every bundled preset states hover_background, so only a custom theme reaches it.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: the gpui twin of M5-07; an unset hover is the widget at rest.
**Status:** fixed in 304da987 (M6 T11)


#### M6-23 · bug · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/checkbox.rs:794
**Claim:** A layout style on RadioGroup, such as `.flex_1()`, `.flex_grow()` or `.w_full()` in a flex row, or an absolute position, lands on an inner div. The group's own element, the flex item its parent lays out, gets none of it, so the group does not grow or move.
**Evidence:** render builds `BaseRadioGroup::new(self.id).axis(self.axis).child(flex.refine_style(&self.style).children(..))` (checkbox.rs:794-801). BaseRadioGroup is a plain `div().id(..)`, display block (gpui-base-0.7.3 radio_group.rs, `new`). The caller's StyleRefinement goes to its only child, so flex-item properties apply inside the block, where they do nothing. gpui-component's RadioGroup refines the caller's style onto BaseRadioGroup and keeps its own gap on the inner div (gpui-component-0.7.3 radio.rs:403-407). BaseRadioGroup is itself Styled and applies `refine_style(&self.style)` after its children (radio_group.rs render), so the inner div is not needed.
**Fix proposed:** Drop the inner div: `BaseRadioGroup::new(id).axis(axis).flex().flex_col()/flex_row().refine_style(&self.style).children(radios)`. The caller's gap still applies, and the flex-item properties now reach the group.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — RadioGroup::render applies refine_style(&self.style) to an inner flex div that is the child of BaseRadioGroup (checkbox.rs:788-800), and BaseRadioGroup's own Stateful<Div> keeps an empty style (gpui-base radio_group.rs:56-66), so flex_1, w_full or absolute land one level too deep.
**Triage:** fix — the caller's style reaches the group's root.
**Status:** fixed in 4e201d1e (M6 T11)


#### M6-24 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/spinner.rs:437
**Claim:** A Spinner on the system icon set (the default `IconChoice::System`, freedesktop on Linux) keeps the first icon theme's indicator for the life of the application. After the user switches icon theme (Breeze to Papirus, say) and the app re-reads, it still draws the old theme's process-working, unless the text colour or size also changed.
**Evidence:** For IconChoice::System, render keys the cache with `icon_theme: None` (spinner.rs:426-428, :437-442). `load` then calls `FreedesktopLoader::load_indicator(None)` (:218), which resolves None through `crate::system_icon_theme()` (native-theme/src/freedesktop.rs:563-580), a cached detection that `invalidate_caches()` clears (native-theme/src/detect/icon_theme.rs:61-64). The spinner's `Indicators` global never evicts (spinner.rs:204-212, :254-263), and its key never names the theme that was resolved, so a later render after invalidation finds the old entry. Only a different colour or size, which makes a new key, reaches the new theme.
**Fix proposed:** When the set is Freedesktop and no theme is named, resolve the theme for the key, `icon_theme.or_else(|| native_theme::detect::system_icon_theme().ok().map(Into::into))` (a cached call), so that a changed system theme makes a new key. While there, clamp `size` in the key to the 512 that `to_image_source` rasterizes at most (icons.rs:969), so sizes above it share one entry.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — IconChoice::System gives the key icon_theme None (spinner.rs:427, :437-442). The Indicators global keeps each key for the life of the app and nothing in the crate clears it (:204-263), so load_indicator(None), which reads system_icon_theme at load time (freedesktop.rs:563-580), never runs again for an unchanged colour and size.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: the system icon choice's cache key carries the icon theme.
**Status:** fixed in 6f692ac3, baebc46e (M6 T8)


#### M6-25 · perf · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/tab_bar.rs:179
**Claim:** Tab::debug_selector runs its closure and stores a String for every tab on every render, also in release builds where gpui's own debug_selector is a no-op.
**Evidence:** `self.selector = Some(f())` (tab_bar.rs:179-182) allocates eagerly. render then passes the String on with `tab.debug_selector(|| selector)` (:385-387). gpui-pre 0.3.9's InteractiveElement::debug_selector records the selector only under `cfg(any(test, all(debug_assertions, feature = "test-support")))` and is an inlined no-op otherwise (elements/div.rs:881-900). The fallback (:298-301) has the same pattern. A caller that sets selectors, as the showcase does, pays one String per tab per frame for nothing.
**Fix proposed:** Put the same `cfg` on the field and the method body, or store the closure as `Option<Box<dyn FnOnce() -> String>>` and call it only when gpui records it.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Tab::debug_selector calls f() eagerly and stores the String (tab_bar.rs:179-182), where gpui-pre's own is a no-op outside cfg(any(test, all(debug_assertions, feature = "test-support"))) (div.rs:884-900). It costs something only for tabs a caller gave a selector, not every tab, and the cost is negligible: one small allocation per such tab per frame, which an allocation count per frame would measure.
**Triage:** drop — only tabs given a selector pay, the cost is negligible and below any timing spread (the verifier's correction).
**Status:** dropped (triage): negligible, below any timing spread


#### M6-26 · api · api-add · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/tab_bar.rs:400
**Claim:** A TabBar wider than its container scrolls sideways (`overflow_x_scroll`), but it neither scrolls a clicked or selected tab into view nor takes a ScrollHandle. gpui-component's TabBar, which it stands in for, does both.
**Evidence:** The row is `BaseTabs::new("tabs") ... .overflow_x_scroll()` with no handle (tab_bar.rs:390-402). on_click only calls the caller's handler (:382-384), so selecting a tab programmatically, or clicking one that is half hidden, leaves it where it is. gpui-component 0.7.3 keeps a ScrollHandle (from `track_scroll`, or a keyed one, tab/tab_bar.rs:129-131, :430-437) and wraps every tab's click in `reveal.reveal(ix, cx)`, which springs the offset to show the tab and a peek of its neighbours (:440-450, :485-494, :656-680).
**Fix proposed:** Add `TabBar::track_scroll(&ScrollHandle)` and a keyed fallback handle. On a click, or when `selected` changes, call `scroll_to_item(ix)` on it. A plain scroll is fine: upstream's spring is motion the model does not state.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The connector's TabBar only sets overflow_x_scroll (tab_bar.rs:396-402) and takes no ScrollHandle, while upstream has track_scroll and reveals a clicked tab (gpui-component tab/tab_bar.rs:124-132, :429-445). The claim overstates one point: upstream says a change of selection does NOT reveal the tab (:126-127).
**Triage:** fix — a `track_scroll(ScrollHandle)` and a clicked tab scrolled into view, as upstream (upstream does not reveal on selection change; neither will we).
**Status:** fixed in 1813ecc3, 10f5de05 (M6 T12)

#### M6-28 · api · api-add · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/progress.rs:62
**Claim:** ProgressBar has no indeterminate mode, so an application that wants a native-themed busy bar has to fall back to gpui-component's `Progress::loading(true)`, which draws gpui-component's own colours.

#### M6-30 · api · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/spinner.rs:98
**Claim:** SpinnerLook::path_radius is public but nothing draws with it, and it goes negative when stroke_width exceeds the diameter.
**Evidence:** `path_radius` returns `(diameter - stroke) / 2` (spinner.rs:98-100). `ring` paints the arc from `outer = diameter / 2` and `inner = (outer - stroke).max(0)` (:275-278) and never calls it. Its only caller is a test (widgets/tests.rs:381). With `stroke_width = 6` and `diameter = 4`, both finite and non-negative, so they pass `length()`, it returns -1, while the arc is clamped.
**Fix proposed:** Remove it, or make it pub(crate)/test-only, and assert `inner` in the test instead. If it stays public, clamp it at 0 as `ring` does.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — path_radius (spinner.rs:98-100) is used only by tests.rs:381, while ring() computes its own radii and clamps the inner one at 0 (:275-278). path_radius has no clamp, and stroke_width is not bounded by diameter in of_size (:88-91), so it goes negative when the stroke is wider than the diameter.
**Triage:** fix + maintainer: clamp at 0; maintainer 2026-10-15: `path_radius` becomes `pub(crate)` → fix.
**Status:** fixed in 747a159b (M6 T8: `pub(crate)`, maintainer 2026-10-15)

**Claim:** The ten value structs the crate builds and the user only reads (`CheckboxLook`, `SwitchLook`, `SliderLook`, `ProgressBarLook`, `SeparatorLook`, `SpinnerLook`, `TabLook`, `TabIndicator`, `ScrollbarGeometry`, `AnimatedImageSources`) have all-public fields and no `#[non_exhaustive]`, so every field the model gains is a breaking change, which `Loaded` already avoids.

Fields are coming: docs/todo.md:1963 (a disabled-checked checkbox fill), :2000 (a scrollbar thumb radius platform-facts may yet record). `Loaded` (lib.rs:336-340) carries `#[non_exhaustive]` for exactly this reason since M5.

Field reads and `let mut g = scrollbar_geometry(r); g.track_width = ..` keep working; only a struct literal outside the crate (none known) breaks. `Native` stays constructible.

Two callers the change would touch: the compiled no_run doctest at icons.rs:1169 destructures AnimatedImageSources without `..` and would break, and ScrollbarGeometry is also an input (scrollbar_styles :83, apply_overrides :146), so outside code would lose literal construction. iced's AnimatedSvgHandles (iced icons.rs:42-48) has the same unmarked shape, so parity needs it marked too. Also reported by R2 (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/base_layer.rs:28): `ScrollbarGeometry` is a public struct of public fields without `#[non_exhaustive]`, mirroring gpui-base's private style fields, so the next field gpui-base adds (0.6.4 already reshaped the thumb arithmetic) is a breaking change for any caller that builds it with a struct literal. **Triage:** maintainer: 2026-10-15, `#[non_exhaustive]` on all ten; `ScrollbarGeometry` is then made by `scrollbar_geometry(resolved)` and edited field by field; iced's `AnimatedSvgHandles` gets the attribute for parity → fix.

### Step 6 — fix plan (2026-10-15)

Drafted by a Fable 5.1 planner from the entries and M5's rulings, reviewed by the session; the session replaced the draft's M6-03 ruling (a background re-apply) with the lock fix below, so M6-03's speed half is dropped and its Status says so.

Order per the plan: S1 first (M6-15), then the API changes (they move code the others touch: the `NonZeroU32` and `#[non_exhaustive]` structs, `is_dark`, the features, core's loader and colouriser), then S2, S3, S4. One `implement` agent (Opus) per task, a fresh reviewer per task, `./scripts/check_release.sh --commit` before every code commit. Gates: bug → a failing test first that reproduces the finding, then the fix, then it passes; perf → `cargo test -p native-theme-gpui --release --test timings -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` before and after, three runs each, kept only when the drop exceeds the run-to-run spread of the three *before* runs (Step 1 baseline: warm `from_preset` 52–245 µs, first calls 31–106 ms on six presets, 0.25–0.85 ms on the other eleven); simplify → `git diff --stat` net deletion, tests unchanged except tests of deleted code; api → `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` compiles, every caller updated (connectors, showcases, READMEs, doc examples, `tests/seams.rs`, contracts), a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line, semver as the maintainer approved on 2026-10-15 (M6-06, M6-34, M6-15, M6-30) and no other break. Two sources are read before any task touches them: `docs/archive/todo_gpui-widgets-spec.md` (the widgets) and `docs/archive/todo_v0.5.9_unstated-sizes-and-chrome-ux-rationale.md` §5 (the control-height rule).

- Ruling: the order rule bends twice inside a file, for its own reason (code is moved before it is edited): M6-29's shared Checkbox/Radio render body (S4) lands before the checkbox S2 fixes M6-21/22/23 and the api-add M6-27 in T11, since each of those would otherwise be written twice (the finding's own point); M6-10's clamp removal (S4) is T6's last commit, after M6-07/08/09 in the same `geometry.rs`. — why: the template orders API changes first because they move code the others touch; the same holds for a shared body in one file. — cost if wrong: one task's commits reordered.
- Ruling: M6-03 is fixed as a lock defect, not as a first-call speed-up. `substituted_family` holds `ASKED`'s lock for the look-up and the insert only; `fonts::substitute_family` runs unlocked (two first askers of one family may both ask; same answer, last write wins). The per-family cost (about 12.5 ms per new family, once per process, measured by R1's verifier) stays on the calling thread and is stated in the docs of `from_preset`, `to_theme` and `font_family`. — why: the substitute must be in the theme the call returns, so a `to_theme`-only application and the first frame draw the platform's substitute rather than gpui's own fallback (`.ZedMono` first, gpui-pre 0.3.9 `text_system.rs:255-266`); moving the ask to a background executor would draw a frame in the wrong family, leave callers without a `cx` without the substitute, and add a re-apply path, all to hide a cost paid once per family per process. The real defect is a 2 s-timeout subprocess under a process-wide lock: a second thread building any theme waits for it. Core's `substitute_family` stays one `fc-match` call (loading a font database to answer it would cost more, the egui connector's one-per-process cost). — cost if wrong: the six presets' first switch keeps its 25–35 ms, once per process.
- Ruling: M6-02 — `NativeTheme` stores each variant with the display name of the theme that stored it; `apply_inner` drops a stored variant whose name differs from the incoming theme's, and keeps one of the same name (two `apply`s of one preset, one per mode, still accumulate, as D34 and the crate doc's "call `from_preset()` once per mode and apply both" (lib.rs:45) intend). `apply_system_theme` stores both as today. — why: "always clear" breaks the README's documented two-apply recipe; "clear on a different name" keeps D34 and makes the doc at lib.rs:871-876 true. — cost if wrong: two different presets sharing one display name would keep each other's other variant; none of the seventeen do.

Subagent tokens: reviewers 197k–239k (R1 229k, R2 197k, R3 239k, R4 237k), API 373k, verifiers 70k–146k (567k); about 1.84M in total.

Rejected:
- R1#3 (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/ext.rs:95): An application that defines any `TextStyle::Name` style pays a full `egui::Style` clone, with its `text_styles` BTreeMap, for every `native_scope` and `native_set_style` call on every pass. — REJECTED: This is the recorded design: spec §7.5 (docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md, the native_scope bullet) says 'An application without Name keys pays nothing; one with them pays one Style clone per scope per pass', and Builder::style_patch (atlas.rs:623-636) lets the application put its Name keys into every cell, which makes missing_name_keys empty and so avoids the clone.
- R2#0 (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/style/mod.rs:87): The eleven surface frames are built from the base style before `finish` runs, so a `Builder::style_patch` that sets a field a frame preset reads (e.g. `spacing.menu_margin`, `spacing.window_margin`, the geometry of `visuals.window_shadow`) reaches `ctx.style()` and every role cell but not `ThemeAtlas::surface_frame` / `Ui::native_frame`. — REJECTED: The code works as the claim says (style/mod.rs:85-88 builds frames from the unfinished base), but the egui spec records this as the design: each Surface frame starts from egui's preset 'over the same colour scheme's base style as it stands before the patch' (docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md:559-560, §3.4), and style_patch's contract covers 'both base styles and every role style' only (atlas.rs:623-624; rationale §3.21, todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-rationale.md:2193-2195; T16 at spec:7780 tests styles, not frames). It is intended, not a bug.
- API#6 (connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/wrap.rs:51): `link` and `hyperlink` return an `impl egui::Widget` with no `#[must_use]`, so `link(ui, "Docs");` without `ui.add(..)` compiles silently and draws nothing, where every struct widget of the crate carries egui's own must-use message. — REJECTED: egui's Widget trait is itself #[must_use = "You should put this widget in a ui with `ui.add(widget);`"] (egui widgets/mod.rs:62). rustc's unused_must_use fires on an unused `impl Trait` whose trait is must_use, so `link(ui, "Docs");` already warns with egui's message.
- API#7 (connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/slider.rs:63): `Slider::new` takes `&mut f64` and `RangeInclusive<f64>` where egui's `Slider::new` is generic over `emath::Numeric`, so a call site on an `f32`, `i32` or `u8` value cannot adopt the widget by swapping the type as the README promises, and needs a temporary and a copy-back. — REJECTED: The f64 signature is a recorded decision (docs/archive/todo_egui-widgets-spec.md:379). The README promises no type swap: its first Limit (README.md:51-52) says a call site adopts a widget with ui.add(..), so the claimed promise is not in the text.
- API#8 (connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/progress_bar.rs:44): The Tier-W wrappers forward a subset of their egui counterpart's builders and drop ones that are not theme-owned, so a `ProgressBar::new(p).show_percentage()` or a `ComboBox::from_id_salt(..).height(..)` call site cannot adopt the wrapper as the README's first Limit promises. — REJECTED: The wrappers' builder sets are recorded scope: ComboBox's selected_text, width, popup_style and enabled, and ProgressBar's desired_width (spec:379-386, §4.9). The README's first Limit (README.md:51-52) promises only adoption through ui.add(..), not builder parity with egui.

### Entries

#### M7-01 · perf · S3 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/atlas.rs:444
**Claim:** An application that calls `atlas.install(ctx)` every frame (in `ui()`/`logic()`, the way many egui apps call `ctx.set_visuals` each frame, and which the doc invites with 'Safe to call at any time', atlas.rs:426-427) never lets egui idle, re-uploads or re-rasterizes every icon this crate made on every frame, and byte-compares every font face on every frame, although nothing changed.
**Evidence:** install runs all six steps unconditionally, with no check that `self` is the atlas already published. (1) atlas.rs:469 `ctx.request_repaint()` on every call, so every pass schedules the next: a continuous redraw loop (100% of one core plus GPU) for an otherwise idle app. (2) atlas.rs:467 `crate::icons::forget_icons(ctx)` removes the `IconRegistry`, calls `ctx.forget_image(uri)` for every SVG URI and removes every stored `TextureHandle` (icons.rs:446-456); the same frame's later `to_image_source` then finds no stored handle and calls `ctx.load_texture` again (icons.rs:350-357), a new texture id and a GPU upload per raster icon per frame, and an SVG icon's bytes are re-included and egui_extras' SVG loader re-rasterizes them, since `forget_image` cleared its cache. (3) atlas.rs:450 `ctx.set_fonts(defs.clone())`: egui compares the new definitions with the installed ones (egui context.rs:2104-2113, its own comment: 'this comparison is expensive since it checks TTF data for equality'); `FontData` derives `PartialEq` but not `Eq` (epaint text/fonts.rs:110), so `Arc<FontData>` equality takes no pointer short-cut and memcmps every face's bytes — with the default `system-fonts` feature the plan's system faces plus egui's defaults, megabytes per frame. Steps 2-4 are cheap (Arc clones, one `PluginHandle` allocation in `add_plugin`). Unmeasured (no build in M7); measurement that would confirm: an eframe app that installs in `ui()` vs once, idle for 5 s — pass count (`ctx.cumulative_pass_nr()`), `ctx.tex_manager().read().num_allocated()` churn per frame, and the time of one `install` with a `from_system` atlas. Test to add: run passes until `!ctx.has_requested_repaint()`, then a pass whose closure calls `atlas.install(ui.ctx())` with the already-installed atlas; today `has_requested_repaint()` stays true on every pass. No docs/todo.md entry; the spec §10.3 does not address a repeated install of the same atlas.
**Fix proposed:** At the top of `install`, when `ThemeAtlas::from_ctx(ctx)` is `Arc::ptr_eq` to `self`, re-run only step 2 (the two `set_style_of`, so a style the app reset is restored) and return, skipping `set_fonts`, `forget_icons` and `request_repaint`; document that re-installing the installed atlas is cheap. `install_requests_a_repaint` and `install_leaves_no_stored_icon_texture_handle` re-install the same atlas and would switch to a second atlas.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — install has no same-atlas guard: every call runs request_repaint (atlas.rs:478, so egui never idles), forget_icons (icons.rs:446-457 drops every stored TextureHandle and forgets every SVG URI, so the next pass re-uploads and re-rasterizes) and set_fonts, whose comparison checks the TTF bytes (egui context.rs:2105-2115); the docs say only 'Safe to call at any time' (atlas.rs:426-427). To confirm: drive Context::run_ui passes that call install each pass and count has_requested_repaint, tex_manager allocations and frees per pass, and the time of set_fonts with a system-font plan, against one install.
**Triage:** fix — a repeated `install` of the atlas already installed requests no repaint, frees no texture and resets no fonts; gate: a test counting repaint requests and texture frees over two installs of one atlas (a behaviour, not a timing: an app that installs every frame never idles today).
**Status:** fixed in c3101b1f (M7 T6; eafec295): a re-install of the installed atlas restores its base styles and nothing else
*Source:* R1#0.


#### M7-02 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/plugin.rs:187
**Claim:** On Linux, after an atlas with an OS mode (from `from_system`, `to_egui_atlas` or `Builder::os_mode`) has told the window `SetTheme(Light)` (or `Dark`), installing an atlas with no OS mode (`from_preset`, `to_theme`) or calling `ThemeAtlas::clear` leaves the title bar on that explicit scheme while egui draws the UI in `Options::fallback_theme`, until the user changes the theme preference.
**Evidence:** Pass 1, atlas with `os_mode = Some(Light)`, `ThemePreference::System`, `RawInput::system_theme = None`: `input_hook` fills Light (plugin.rs:159-170); egui's `sync_window_theme` sends `SetTheme(SystemDefault)` and records it as `last_sent_window_theme` (egui context.rs:2474-2497); `output_hook` rewrites it to `SetTheme(Light)` and stores `last_sent[root] = Light` (plugin.rs:209-225). Then `from_preset(..)` is installed (os_mode None, ext.rs:198-213; the egui showcase does exactly this when the user picks a preset, examples/showcase-egui/app.rs:506) or `ThemeAtlas::clear` is called. Next passes: `input_hook` fills nothing, so egui draws `fallback_theme` (Dark by default, egui memory/mod.rs:331); `output_hook` returns at plugin.rs:187-189 because `os_mode(ctx)` is None; egui sends nothing because the preference did not change (context.rs:2486-2493). The window keeps `Light` from the last explicit command: on X11 a `light` `_GTK_THEME_VARIANT` hint, on Wayland CSD winit's light Adwaita frame (spec table, docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md:6896-6901), under a dark UI. The spec's goal 'the title bar then matches the scheme the whole UI is drawn in' (spec :6914-6915) is broken. Neither T14 (c) nor `after_clear_the_plugin_is_inert` covers it: the latter clears before any pass ran (install_tests.rs:889-901). Test: install `preset_atlas_with_os_mode(kde-breeze, Light)`, one pass with `system_theme: None` (carries `[Light]`), install `preset_atlas(kde-breeze)`, one more pass: today `(Theme::Dark, vec![])`; expected `(Theme::Dark, vec![SystemTheme::SystemDefault])`, the command egui itself believes it sent; the same after `ThemeAtlas::clear`.
**Fix proposed:** In `output_hook`, when the OS mode is None (or the input was not filled) while `sync_window_theme` holds, the preference is System and `last_sent` holds a scheme for that viewport, push `SetTheme(SystemDefault)` once and remove that `last_sent` entry, restoring egui's own state; keep the rest of the hook as is.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — output_hook returns early at plugin.rs:187-189 when os_mode is None, and egui's sync_window_theme sends again only when the preference changes (egui context.rs:2474-2497, last_sent_window_theme), so the earlier SetTheme(Light) stays; meanwhile input_hook leaves system_theme None (winit x11 window.rs:1905-1907 always returns None), so ctx.theme() is fallback_theme (egui memory/mod.rs:367). The spec's T14(c) tests only the UI scheme for the no-OS-mode atlas, not the title bar.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: an atlas without an OS mode (a preset, or `clear`) sends the scheme it draws in, so the title bar follows.
**Status:** fixed in 2c13742f (M7 T5)
*Source:* R1#1.


#### M7-03 · perf · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/plugin.rs:92
**Claim:** Every `native_scope` call scans the pass's whole scope list for a `Ui` id it can never contain, so n role scopes in a pass cost n^2/2 `Id` comparisons, and each pass with a focused widget clones the whole list.
**Evidence:** ext.rs:97-98: `native_scope` records `child.unique_id()` of the child `Ui` that `scope_builder` has just created; a child's `unique_id` is `stable_id.with(next_auto_id_salt)` (egui ui.rs:252-260), new in this pass, so `entry.scopes.iter_mut().find(|(id, _)| *id == ui_id)` at plugin.rs:92 never matches for that caller and always walks the full Vec before the push at :94. Only `native_set_style` (ext.rs:110), which can be called twice on one `Ui`, needs the replace. A list of 500 rows each wrapped in `native_scope` is about 125 000 comparisons per pass under the `data_mut` lock. Separately, `paint_focus_ring` reads the entry with `data.get_temp::<FocusEntry>(key)` (plugin.rs:297-300), which clones both Vecs every pass while a widget has keyboard focus. Unmeasured; measurement: a pass of N `native_scope` calls for N = 100, 1000, 5000, timed.
**Fix proposed:** Give `record_scope` a `replace: bool` (or split it): `native_scope` pushes without searching, `native_set_style` keeps the search; in `paint_focus_ring`, compute the edge and radius inside one `ctx.data_mut(|d| d.get_temp_mut_or_default::<FocusEntry>(key) ...)` reading the entry by reference — taking care that `scope_radius` calls `ctx.viewport`, so read the widget table first and pass it in, keeping the no-nested-accessor rule (§10.3).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — native_scope records child.unique_id() (ext.rs:98), a Ui created in that same pass whose id is unique, so the find at plugin.rs:92 only ever matters for native_set_style's repeat on one Ui; paint_focus_ring's data.get_temp::<FocusEntry> (plugin.rs:298) clones both Vecs whenever a widget is focused. To confirm it matters, time record_scope across a pass with N = 100 and 1000 scopes; at tens of scopes it is likely below the noise.
**Triage:** fix if measurable — `record_scope`'s scan and the focus-ring clone; a timing with 100 and 1000 scopes per pass first, dropped below the spread.
**Status:** fixed in 3aed83e2 (M7 T8; 1000 scopes 755 → 578 µs); the focus-ring clone half dropped, below the spread
*Source:* R1#2.


#### M7-04 · bug · S1 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/accessors.rs:42
**Claim:** A finite but huge text size — a theme file stating `size = 30000`, which core accepts (validate_helpers.rs:491 rejects only non-finite and non-positive), or an application-set `text_scaling_factor` such as `1000.0` (13 pt x 1000) — passes both of this crate's text-size guards and reaches epaint, which panics in release when it rasterizes a glyph wider than its font atlas.
**Evidence:** The style path `style::base::text_size` (style/base.rs:20-34) and the accessor path `text_size_or_stock` (accessors.rs:42-48) accept any `scaled` that `is_normal() && > 0.0`, with no upper bound, unlike lengths, which `clamp_length` caps at `LENGTH_CEILING` because egui's rounding overflows above it (convert.rs:106-136). epaint draws the glyph at `scale = font_size * tweak.scale * pixels_per_point` (epaint text/font.rs:567), outlines it at that size and takes `bounds.width() as u16` (:265); `TextureAtlas::allocate` then runs `assert!(w <= self.image.width(), ..)` (epaint texture_atlas.rs:226-231), and the atlas is at most 16384 wide (`max_texture_side.at_most(16 * 1024)`, epaint text/fonts.rs:975) — a release-mode panic once a glyph is wider. Above about 1e37 the metrics' `round_ui` overflows to infinity as well (font.rs:562-564), the same overflow `LENGTH_CEILING` exists for. Infinite or zero sizes are already replaced (and M6-05's core guard in `AccessibilityPreferences::scaled`, ruled in M6 Step 6, covers the overflowing product), so this is only the finite tail. No OS reader or bundled preset produces such a size. Graded S4, not S1: the input is pathological and the panic is epaint's assert.
**Fix proposed:** Cap text sizes at `LENGTH_CEILING` in `text_size` and `text_size_or_stock` for parity with lengths (a bound with its upstream source, emath's `GUI_ROUNDING`), document in `Builder::accessibility` that a size wider than the GPU's `max_texture_side` panics in epaint 0.36.2, and report the assert upstream (a glyph too wide for the atlas should be skipped, as `width == 0` already is, font.rs:268).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — text_size_or_stock (accessors.rs:42-48) checks only is_normal and > 0, AccessibilityPreferences::scaled (native-theme lib.rs:406-413) only finite and positive, and check_font (validate_helpers.rs:491) sets no maximum; epaint draws the glyph at full size (font.rs:265-283, width capped only by `as u16`) and TextureAtlas::allocate asserts w <= the atlas width (texture_atlas.rs:226-231), which is at most 16384 (fonts.rs:975), so a 30000 px glyph panics. Whether the 13 pt x 1000 case panics depends on max_texture_side and the glyph's width, so the gate is a test that draws 'W' at 30000.
**Triage:** fix — a finite but huge text size (a theme file's `size = 30000`, or a large factor) panics in epaint's atlas assert; the cap is derived at install from the runtime `max_texture_side` (spec §14 item 44 records the limit as run-time dependent, so no build-time number), with a `Note`; failing test first (a "W" at 30000).
**Status:** fixed in 1f85ba7a, 8fa65f40, 3e069a77, 7be875d9, f85a5823, 9608a95a (M7 T1): `ThemeAtlas::text_size_cap`, derived per pass from `max_texture_side`, `pixels_per_point` and the faces' widest glyph
*Source:* R1#4.


#### M7-05 · api · api-add · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/watch.rs:57
**Claim:** `ThemeWatcher` implements no `Debug`, so an application struct that derives `Debug` cannot hold `Option<ThemeWatcher>`, the README's own pattern (README.md:276-278) — the egui twin of M6-35 (gpui's `Native`/`NativeTheme` without `Debug`).
**Evidence:** watch.rs:56-60: `pub struct ThemeWatcher { handoff: Arc<Handoff>, _subscription: native_theme::watch::ThemeSubscription }` with no derive and no manual impl; `ThemeSubscription` implements `Debug` (native-theme watch/mod.rs:155-166), `Handoff` holds two `Mutex<Option<..>>`. The crate's other public values do (`ThemeAtlas` manually, atlas.rs:233-240; `Loaded` derives it, ext.rs:263). `#[derive(Debug)] struct MyApp { watcher: Option<ThemeWatcher> }` fails with E0277.
**Fix proposed:** Before: no impl. After: `impl std::fmt::Debug for ThemeWatcher { fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result { f.debug_struct("ThemeWatcher").field("pending", &self.handoff.pending.lock().map(|p| p.is_some()).unwrap_or(false)).finish_non_exhaustive() } }` (or `finish_non_exhaustive()` alone). Additive.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — ThemeWatcher (watch.rs:56-60) has no Debug, derived or written by hand, although both fields could have one (native-theme's ThemeSubscription implements Debug at watch/mod.rs:148, and Handoff is crate-private), so a struct that derives Debug cannot hold Option<ThemeWatcher> as in README.md:275-277; this is M6-35's class.
**Triage:** fix — derive or implement `Debug` for `ThemeWatcher` (core's `ThemeSubscription` is `Debug`).
**Status:** fixed in 478bde34 (M7 T2)
*Source:* R1#5.


#### M7-06 · api · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/atlas.rs:419
**Claim:** The public docs cite the unpublished connector spec by bare section number about a hundred times in this region alone ('§10.3 lists the steps, their order and what each must not touch', atlas.rs:419-420), which a docs.rs reader cannot resolve — the egui twin of M6-38, whose ruling says a § citation must name its document.
**Evidence:** `grep -c` of `///`/`//!` lines carrying `§` here: atlas.rs 43, accessors.rs 29, plugin.rs 17, roles.rs 16, ext.rs 12, watch.rs 4 (a few on private items). Public examples: `ThemeAtlas::install` (atlas.rs:419-423, '§10.3'), `register_focus_shape` (plugin.rs:104, :106-118, '§6.18'), `ThemeWatcher` (watch.rs:54, '§10.2'), `RoleVariant::Selected` (roles.rs:87, '§6.2'), `Note::ValueSaturated` (atlas.rs:35-37, '§6.14', '§7.2'), `Surface::Tooltip` (roles.rs:164, '§14 item 3'). Neither the crate docs (lib.rs:1-86) nor mapping.md ('spec §5, §13.1', mapping.md:5) name the document: docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md, which is not in the published crate. M6-38's ruling (docs/todo_code-review-findings.md:9654): 'a § citation stays where it names its document ... and is given the document's name where it does not'.
**Fix proposed:** Name the document once in the crate docs ('§ numbers refer to docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md in the repository') and, per M6-38's ruling, write the document's name at each public citation, or drop citations that add nothing for a reader; private-item comments untouched.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — There are about 120 doc-comment lines with a § in the region (atlas.rs 43, accessors.rs 29, plugin.rs 17, roles.rs 16, ext.rs 12, watch.rs 4), most of them on public items, and no crate doc or README names the spec document (grep for 'egui-connector-spec' or 'connector spec' finds nothing), so under the M6-38 ruling (findings.md:9654) each one needs the document's name; the count of 'about a hundred' covers public and private items together. Also reported by API (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/atlas.rs:1): About 190 public doc comments in the modules docs.rs renders cite a bare section number ('§6.18', 'spec §4.2') of a document the crate never names, so a docs.rs reader cannot follow any of them; the egui twin of M6-38 at a larger scale. Verifier: CONFIRMED — No rendered module names the spec: a grep for 'spec.md' or 'connector-spec' in src finds nothing. About 190 '§' doc lines sit in the docs.rs-rendered files (lib, accessors, atlas, convert, ext, fonts, icons, plugin, roles, watch, before their test modules); roughly 150 are on pub items, the rest on private ones. The M6-38 ruling (docs/todo_code-review-findings.md:9654) gives such a citation its document's name.
**Triage:** fix — merged with API-4: name the archived spec document once per crate doc and wherever a public doc cites a bare `§` (the M6-38 ruling).
**Status:** fixed in 0de7592d (M7 T13; tripwires in both crates)
*Source:* R1#6.


#### M7-07 · api · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/atlas.rs:417
**Claim:** Neither `install` nor `icons::to_image_source` says that an `ImageSource::Texture` from `to_image_source` is valid only until the next `install`: an application that obtains a raster icon's source once (at start-up, or cached in its state) and keeps drawing it finds the icon gone after the first theme switch.
**Evidence:** `to_image_source` returns `ImageSource::Texture(SizedTexture::from_handle(&handle))`, which owns nothing, while the crate keeps the only `TextureHandle` in `ctx.data` (icons.rs:350-363; its doc says 'uploaded once ... and reused afterwards', icons.rs:315-327, which reads like caching is safe). `install` step 5 removes those handles (atlas.rs:467, icons.rs:452-455); dropping the last handle frees the texture, so the kept `SizedTexture` names a freed id and both renderers skip the mesh with a warning (egui-wgpu renderer.rs:561 'Missing texture', egui_glow painter.rs:504 'Failed to find texture'). The install doc (atlas.rs:417-443) mentions 'the icon-cache flush' but not this consequence; README.md:265-266 likewise.
**Fix proposed:** State in `install`'s doc and in `to_image_source`'s: call `to_image_source` (or `to_image`) in each pass rather than keeping its result — the crate already caches the texture — because `install` frees the textures of the previous theme's icons.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — install step 5 (atlas.rs:474-476) runs forget_icons, which removes the stored TextureHandle (icons.rs:452-455), and dropping it frees the texture, so a held ImageSource::Texture (icons.rs:373) points at nothing; the docs say this only indirectly ('register its URI for forget_icons', icons.rs:309; README 'install releases the icons this crate cached'), and nowhere tell the reader to call to_image_source again after install or on every pass. A held SVG ImageSource::Bytes still draws, because the source carries its bytes, but in the old colour.
**Triage:** fix — `install` and `to_image_source` document that a raster icon's `ImageSource::Texture` is freed at the next `install`.
**Status:** fixed in 1016ba04 (M7 T6)
*Source:* R1#7.


#### M7-08 · simplify · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/style/base.rs:69
**Claim:** `base::stroke` takes a colour leaf path that it never reads, so every border call site carries a dead path: `BorderSource::paths[0]` (states.rs:72, :172, :179), `panel_edge`'s `paths[0]` (roles.rs:134, :139) and `BorderPaths::color` (frames.rs:22, :65).
**Evidence:** `let [_color_path, width_path] = paths;` (base.rs:69): only `width_path` reaches a `Note`; the colour is written as given and no transparency note is made for a stroke. `write_states` destructures `[color_path, radius_path, width_path]` (states.rs:172) only to hand `color_path` back to `stroke` (:179); `role_cell`'s checkbox even passes `"checkbox.unchecked_border_color"` (roles.rs:359) for a colour that may be `checkbox.border.color` (roles.rs:339), which is harmless only because the path is unused.
**Fix proposed:** Make `stroke` take the width path alone (`width_path: &'static str`) and drop the colour path from `BorderSource::paths`, `panel_edge` and `BorderPaths`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — base.rs:69 binds `_color_path` and never reads it (it was dead already in the plan, todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-plan.md:5262; a colour sink has no Note, since to_color32 is total), so every caller carries a dead leaf: states.rs:172/179 and the [_;3] BorderSource.paths at its 10 literals, roles.rs:134/139 with its 3 panel_edge calls, base.rs:190, and frames.rs:22/33/65. The fix deletes code: `paths` becomes one width path, BorderSource.paths becomes [_;2], and BorderPaths.color plus its macro line go away.
**Triage:** fix — the dead colour path goes from every border call site and `BorderPaths.color`; deletes code.
**Status:** fixed in c25a1c8b (M7 T14)
*Source:* R2#1.


#### M7-09 · simplify · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/style/base.rs:28
**Claim:** §8.5's "a usable text size is a positive normal f32" predicate is written out in three production places — `base::text_size` (base.rs:28), `roles::override_font` (roles.rs:65) and `accessors::text_size_or_stock` (accessors.rs:43) — so the stated residual of §14 item 44 (a finite size large enough to overflow the font atlas panics in epaint, spec §8.5) would need the same change made three times if a bound is ever added.
**Evidence:** base.rs:27-33 `let s = scaled_text_size(size, prefs); if s.is_normal() && s > 0.0 { s } else { note; own }`; roles.rs:64-69 `let scaled = scaled_text_size(size, input.prefs); if scaled.is_normal() && scaled > 0.0 { override } else { note }`; accessors.rs:42-47 `if scaled.is_normal() && scaled > 0.0 { scaled } else { stock }`. Same scaling call, same predicate, three fallbacks.
**Fix proposed:** One `pub(crate) fn usable_text_size(size: f32, prefs) -> Option<f32>` (scale, then the predicate) in accessors.rs, which the three callers map onto their own fallback.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The test `s.is_normal() && s > 0.0` appears verbatim at base.rs:28, roles.rs:65 and accessors.rs:43 (a fourth copy at contract.rs:65 is test-only). The claim's reason for merging them is weak, though: §14 item 44 (spec:8143) says the atlas-overflow bound depends on pixels_per_point and max_texture_side, run-time values, so no build-time predicate can carry it. Merging them adds a helper and deletes no code (net about zero lines): an S4 nicety at most.
**Triage:** drop — merging the three checks adds a helper and deletes no code (the plan's simplify rule), and spec §14 item 44 rules out the bound the claim anticipates.
**Status:** dropped (triage): a helper that deletes no code
*Source:* R2#2.


#### M7-10 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/icons.rs:429
**Claim:** custom_icon_to_image_source(ctx, provider, &IconKey::name(n, IconSet::SfSymbols | IconSet::SegoeFluent).size(96.0)) never hands the key's size to SfSymbolsLoader or SegoeFluentLoader, so an SF Symbol comes back at the 24 pt default raster and a Segoe glyph at the 32 px one, which egui then scales up to the 96-point Image (the egui twin of M6-13).
**Evidence:** icons.rs:414-427: the Freedesktop arm applies `key.size` through `loader.size(size)` (:420-422). The SfSymbols arm (:429-431) and the SegoeFluent arm (:432-434) build `SfSymbolsLoader::new(provider).color_opt(..).load()` and `SegoeFluentLoader::new(provider).color_opt(..).load()` with no `.size()`, although both loaders have had `size(u32)` since M1-T6-07 (core icons.rs at HEAD :419 `SfSymbolsLoader::size`, 'default 24' points; :505 `SegoeFluentLoader::size`, 'default 32' pixels). The result is `IconData::Rgba`, which `to_image_source` uploads at its own width and height (:353-376), so the size reaches nothing. The doc (:397-400) and `IconKey::size`'s doc (:109-117) describe the size as a freedesktop concern only, which predates the loaders' `size`. Core's `load_custom_icon(provider, set, color, size)` plumbs `size` to all three system loaders (core icons.rs at HEAD :806-836, the M6-13 ruling), so the M1-T6-06 switch fixes this only if the call passes `key.size`. Test to write (macOS or Windows CI leg): a provider naming a symbol, `custom_icon_to_image_source` with `.size(64.0)`, assert the `SizedTexture`'s size is 64 px (or the loader's documented scale of it), not 24 or 32.
**Fix proposed:** Pass `key.size` to the SF Symbols and Segoe loaders (`.size(size)` where `Some`), or, with M1-T6-06, call core's `load_custom_icon(provider, set, color, key.size)`; update the two docs to say the size reaches every system set.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — icons.rs:427-432 builds SfSymbolsLoader/SegoeFluentLoader with color_opt only and never calls .size() on them, though both have size(u32) at HEAD (core icons.rs:419, :505; defaults 24 pt and 32 px, :410, :494). key.size reaches only the freedesktop arm (:420-422). This is M6-13's twin. It does not depend on the in-flux core change: HEAD's load_custom_icon(provider, set, color, size) already forwards size (icons.rs:759-765), so the scheduled M1-T6-06 switch fixes it if the switch passes key.size.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: the requested size reaches the SF Symbols and Segoe loaders, through core's `load_custom_icon(.., size)` in the M1-T6-06 switch.
**Status:** fixed in 0cf938bc, bc365b7f (M7 T4)
*Source:* R3#0.


#### M7-11 · api · api-add · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/icons.rs:414
**Claim:** The scheduled M1-T6-06 switch of custom_icon_to_image_source to core's `load_custom_icon(provider, set, color, size)` would drop `IconKey::icon_theme`: core's function loads a freedesktop icon from the system's icon theme only, so under the adwaita preset on a KDE host a key built with `.icon_theme("Adwaita")` would load the provider's icon from Breeze, beside role icons the application loads from Adwaita.
**Evidence:** Today the Freedesktop arm honours the key's theme: `if let Some(theme) = key.icon_theme.as_deref() { loader = loader.theme(theme) }` (icons.rs:417-419), and `IconKey::icon_theme`'s doc tells the caller to pass `atlas.icon_theme(ctx.theme())` (:100-102). Core at HEAD: `pub fn load_custom_icon(provider, set, color: Option<Rgba>, size: Option<u32>)` calls `load_provider_icon(provider, set, None, color, size)` (icons.rs :759-767), its doc says 'A freedesktop icon comes from the system's icon theme' (:742-744); the theme-taking `load_icon_in(id, set, theme, color, size)` is `pub(crate)` (:772). gpui (`custom_icon_to_image_source`, gpui icons.rs at HEAD :776-785) and iced (:89-100) take no theme, so they lose nothing; egui is the one connector whose key carries one. A second difference the switch changes: today a provider's own SVG for SfSymbols/SegoeFluent (the `icon_svg` fallback inside those loaders) is coloured only by `key.tint` (`final_svg_bytes`' `_` arm, :249-252), never by the text colour `load_color` gives the loaders (:430, :433), so with no tint it draws black on a dark scheme; core's `load_provider_icon` colours that SVG in `color` (:795-798). And on Linux `SfSymbolsLoader::load` returns `None` before trying the provider's `icon_svg` (core :470-474), while core's dispatch falls back to it on every platform, contrary to this function's doc ('each trying provider.icon_name(set) then icon_svg(set)', :402-403).
**Fix proposed:** Before the switch, give core a theme-taking public entry (for example `load_custom_icon_in(provider, set, theme: Option<&str>, color, size)`, or an `icon_theme` argument on `load_custom_icon` while it is still unreleased) and call it with `key.icon_theme.as_deref()`, `load_color(ctx, key)` and `key.size`; then convert with no second colouring pass for the sets core already coloured.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — At HEAD, load_custom_icon passes theme None to load_provider_icon (core icons.rs:765), and its doc says a freedesktop icon 'comes from the system's icon theme'. The theme-taking load_icon_in is pub(crate) (:771). So a literal switch drops the key.icon_theme that icons.rs:415-417 honours today, and adwaita.toml:12 sets icon_theme = "Adwaita". This depends on core's icon API, which is being edited now: recheck it once that lands (the fix needs a theme-taking public entry, or the egui freedesktop arm kept).
**Triage:** fix — core gains a public theme-taking form of the custom-icon loader before egui's M1-T6-06 switch, so `IconKey::icon_theme` is kept.
**Status:** fixed in 76b13644 (M7 T4: core `load_custom_icon_in`)

#### M7-12 · perf · S3 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/fonts.rs:169
**Claim:** Every `from_preset`, `to_egui_atlas` and watcher rebuild for a theme whose UI or mono family the OS lacks (feature `system-fonts`, on by default) runs one `fc-match` subprocess per missing family on the calling thread, with no per-process cache, so windows-11, the macOS and iOS presets and the ten catppuccin-family presets each pay two subprocesses on every theme switch on Linux, where gpui pays them once per family per process.
**Evidence:** `FontPlan::from_system` (fonts.rs:162-198) loops over `defaults.font` and `defaults.mono_font`; where `native_theme::fonts::system_face` finds no face (:165-167) it calls `native_theme::fonts::substitute_family(&spec.family)` (:169), which at HEAD runs `stdout_with_timeout("fc-match", ..)` with the 2 s `SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT` on each call and caches nothing (core fonts.rs :290-292, :301-312; its doc: 'Each call starts a process, so call it when a theme changes'), then `system_face` again for the substitute (:171). Callers: `from_preset` (ext.rs:211), `SystemThemeExt::to_egui_atlas` (ext.rs:336) and the watcher's rebuild through `from_system` (watch.rs:100). gpui keeps the answers per family for the process (`substituted_family`'s `ASKED` map, gpui lib.rs at HEAD :679-690; ruling M6-03). On this host `fc-list` has no Segoe UI, Cascadia Mono, SF Pro, SF Mono, Inter or JetBrains Mono, so those presets miss both families. Measured: M6-03's verifier counted 12.5 ms per `fc-match` with a PATH shim on a quiet host and the M6-03 entry 13.4-18.5 ms from the shell; here, under load average about 30, `fc-match --format=%{family[0]} 'Segoe UI'` took 52-66 ms and 'Cascadia Mono' 45-70 ms per call. So each windows-11 `from_preset` costs about 25-35 ms of subprocess time on a quiet host on every call, not only the first. Measurement to confirm: the existing `connectors/native-theme-egui/tests/timings.rs` warm medians for windows-11 against kde-breeze (whose Noto Sans and Hack are installed), or the same with a counting `fc-match` shim first on PATH (expect 2 execs per windows-11 call today, 0 after the fix).
**Fix proposed:** Keep the substitute answer per family for the process, as gpui's `substituted_family` does (lock held for the look-up and the insert only, not across the subprocess), and state the once-per-family cost in `FontPlan::from_system`'s and `from_preset`'s docs.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — fonts.rs:165-171 calls substitute_family for each missing family. Core spawns fc-match on every call with no cache (core fonts.rs:290-310); gpui memoises it per process (gpui lib.rs:679-684); egui has no cache. from_preset (ext.rs:211) and the watcher rebuild (watch.rs:100 -> ext.rs:336) both reach it. On this host Inter, JetBrains Mono, SF Pro, SF Mono, Segoe UI and Cascadia Mono are absent (fc-list), so the 10 Inter/JetBrains presets plus windows-11, ios-13 and macos-* each spawn two fc-match. Measured: fc-match took 36-45 ms per call here (20-call average 49 ms), so about 80-100 ms per from_preset. Confirm in-process by timing from_preset("nord") against from_preset("kde-breeze") (both families present).
**Triage:** fix — cache the substituted family per process, as gpui does since M6 (lock not held across the subprocess, the M6-03 ruling); gate: warm `from_preset` in tests/timings.rs, 135–185 ms today on 14 presets.
**Status:** fixed in 96a38eb4 (M7 T7: core `substitute_family_cached`; warm `from_preset` 31–33 → 0.4–0.6 ms on 14 presets)
*Source:* R3#2.


#### M7-13 · perf · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/icons.rs:409
**Claim:** `custom_icon_to_image_source` reloads the icon on every call, a freedesktop lookup plus a file read (or an AppKit or GDI raster for SF Symbols and Segoe) and then a re-colour and re-hash, and egui code calls it once per frame per icon, while its doc names no cost and `IconKey`, which is Hash + Eq, is not used to keep the loaded data.
**Evidence:** icons.rs:414-437: each call builds a loader and calls `load()`; the freedesktop loader ends in `load_freedesktop_icon_by_name`, which does `find_icon` and `load_icon_file` from disk every time (core freedesktop.rs at HEAD :383-393, 'Each call reads the icon file from disk. Callers that load the same icon repeatedly should cache the returned IconData'). Then `to_image_source` (:333-352) copies, colours and SipHashes the bytes. The connector's own comment at :275 assumes `to_image_source` runs 'on every draw of an icon', and the showcase draws its icons that way (examples/showcase-egui/demo.rs:806-835, called per frame from pages/icons.rs:49, :80 and chrome.rs:391-394), each with a fresh `FreedesktopLoader` load. Measured cost of the load alone: core's timing probe `freedesktop_icons` loads every `IconRole::ALL` icon from breeze warm in 1.74-1.80 ms (ledger, M4 close, docs/todo_code-review-findings.md:8908), about 40 us per icon per frame before egui's own work. Measurement to confirm the per-frame share: a timings row calling `custom_icon_to_image_source` for 40 freedesktop keys in a loop on one `Context`, against the same with a cache.
**Fix proposed:** Cache the loaded `IconData` per `IconKey` in `ctx.data` (dropped by `forget_icons` with the URIs, so a theme switch reloads), or at least state in the doc that each call reads the icon from disk and the caller should keep the `IconData`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — custom_icon_to_image_source (icons.rs:409-436) loads through the core loader on every call, with no memo keyed by IconKey. to_image_source then re-colours, hashes and allocates the SVG bytes (:340-349). The doc (:397-407) names no cost, while core's own note asks callers to cache (freedesktop.rs 'Performance note: Each call reads the icon file from disk'). The per-frame cost is not measured: time N calls per frame for a freedesktop hit and for a provider SVG (and an SF/Segoe raster on CI) to rate it beyond S4.
**Triage:** fix if measurable — a timing row for N `custom_icon_to_image_source` calls first; a per-key cache only above the spread; the doc names the cost either way.
**Status:** fixed in a06aff8e, 576dd13b (M7 T8; 42 freedesktop icons 1.87 ms → 24 µs; keyed by the resolved icon theme)
*Source:* R3#3.


#### M7-14 · bug · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/atlas.rs:487
**Claim:** `ThemeAtlas::clear(ctx)` leaves every icon this crate cached in the context, the `TextureHandle`s in `ctx.data` and the `bytes://native-theme/` URIs in egui's loaders, coloured in the removed atlas's text colour, until a later `install` that may never come; its doc lists the styles and fonts to reset but not `forget_icons`.
**Evidence:** atlas.rs:487-490: `clear` only removes the atlas key. `forget_icons` is called from `install` alone (atlas.rs:467; icons.rs:440-457). After `clear`, `load_color` finds no atlas (icons.rs:226) so a freedesktop icon is drawn with its bare `currentColor` under a new URI (:239-241), while the old URIs and textures stay registered in `IconRegistry` (:256-283) and their `TextureHandle`s keep their GPU textures alive (icons.rs:323-331 says the stored handle is what frees the texture on removal). Bounded (no growth), but never released. Test: install an atlas, draw an `IconData::Rgba` through `to_image_source`, `ThemeAtlas::clear(&ctx)`, then assert `ctx.data(|d| d.get_temp::<egui::TextureHandle>(texture_id(&uri)))` is `None`; it is `Some` today.
**Fix proposed:** Call `crate::icons::forget_icons(ctx)` in `clear`, or name it in `clear`'s doc beside `set_style_of` and `set_fonts`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — ThemeAtlas::clear (atlas.rs:487-490) only removes the atlas, and its doc lists set_style_of/set_fonts but not icons::forget_icons, so the registry, the stored TextureHandles and the bytes:// loader entries outlive it. Nothing stale is drawn, though: load_color is None without an atlas (icons.rs:226), so new bytes give a new URI. The cost is memory held until the next install, and the fix is a doc line or a forget_icons call.
**Triage:** fix — `clear` forgets the icons it registered.
**Status:** fixed in 75ca38ce (M7 T6)
*Source:* R3#4.

#### M7-16 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/slider.rs:124
**Claim:** A Slider built with .enabled(false) under a theme whose slider.disabled_opacity is below 1 (adwaita 0.5, adwaita.toml:61 and :207 'a disabled scale is its enabled self at disabled_opacity'; the community presets 0.5) fades each painted shape on its own, so the rail shows through the trailing fill and the rail and fill show through the knob: the egui twin of gpui's M6-19.

With alpha 0.5 the filled stretch is 0.5 fill + 0.25 rail + 0.25 ground, where libadwaita's whole-widget opacity gives 0.5 fill + 0.5 ground, and the knob is translucent over the fill. **Fix proposed:** As M6's ruling for gpui: give Slider a backdrop(Color32) (default defaults.background_color), open the scope with that ground, and compose rail over ground, fill over rail, knob and outline over fill, each faded by disabled_alpha over the ground (crate::fade::faded), the painter's opacity left at 1.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Slider::ui opens scope::open(ui, Role::Slider, enabled, ..) (slider.rs:124), i.e. plain Ui::disable, not open_faded/fade_as_one as Switch and RadioButton do, and slider_ui paints rail, trailing fill and knob as three shapes (slider.rs:287-296), each with its alpha multiplied by the painter's opacity, so under adwaita (defaults.disabled_opacity 0.5, adwaita.toml:61; no disabled_*_color, :207) the rail shows through the fill and both through the knob; lib.rs:70-75 limits fade-as-one to Switch/RadioButton and no test covers a disabled adwaita slider (tests.rs:824-863 tests the switch only); it is the twin of gpui's M6-19.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: the disabled slider fades as one (the gpui twin M6-19).

#### M7-17 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/radio_button.rs:457
**Claim:** A RadioButton that is checked and .enabled(false) under adwaita (which states no checkbox.disabled_background: 'a disabled check is its enabled self at disabled_opacity', adwaita.toml:169) paints the unchecked circle (#ffffff) with a dot in checkbox.disabled_text_color instead of the checked fill with its indicator_color dot, faded.
**Evidence:** radio_button.rs:457 calls open_faded(ui, Role::Checkbox, checked, enabled, Some(ground), ..); scope.rs:266-270 maps (enabled && outer) == false to RoleVariant::Disabled before looking at `selected`, so the Selected cell (checked_background fill) is never opened for a disabled radio. The connector's Disabled cell for Role::Checkbox (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/style/variants.rs:87-101) is cloned from the Normal cell and sets inactive.bg_fill = disabled_background, else unchecked_background, and inactive.fg_stroke.color = disabled_text_color; egui's RadioButton paints the circle from that state's bg_fill and the dot from fg_stroke.color (egui radio_button.rs:91-105; a disabled response keeps its click sense, so Widgets::style picks `inactive`, style.rs:1273-1283). The disabled rule settled 2026-09-28 (docs/todo.md:2041-2047: 'where no disabled_background is stated (adwaita) a disabled box is its enabled self, checked fill and on-accent mark included') is what iced and gpui do (gpui checkbox.rs:128-131, :141-143 keep the checked fill and indicator_color when no disabled fill is stated). The egui rationale's 'Why Selected and Disabled are not combined' (docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-rationale.md:1146) predates that rule and says a combined cell 'would have nothing to write', which the rule contradicts for the checkbox role. Test: adwaita light, RadioButton::new(true, "x").enabled(false); assert a circle whose fill is the faded checked_background exists (today only the faded #ffffff circle).
**Fix proposed:** For a disabled checked radio where checkbox.disabled_background is None, open the Selected cell and fade it as one (fade_as_one) instead of the Disabled cell; the same gap affects egui's own Checkbox through the connector's cell (variants.rs:87-101), which the connector's reviewer should weigh with it.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — open_faded picks RoleVariant::Disabled whenever enabled is false, whatever checked is (scope.rs:48-52); the connector's Checkbox Disabled cell sets inactive.bg_fill to disabled_background, else unchecked_background (#ffffff on adwaita, adwaita.toml:170), and fg_stroke to disabled_text_color (variants.rs Role::Checkbox arm); egui's RadioButton paints the circle in interact(..).bg_fill and the dot in fg_stroke.color (egui radio_button.rs:79-104, interact, not interact_selectable), so a checked disabled radio shows the unchecked white circle with a disabled-text dot, not the checked fill and indicator_color dot that the disabled rule calls for (docs/todo.md:2041-2047: with no disabled_background a disabled box is its enabled self).
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: a disabled checked radio (and the connector's disabled checkbox cell) shows its checked look faded, the disabled rule of 2026-09-28.
**Status:** fixed in 4eecb361, 4ee44718, d6e43be6 (M7 T10: `RoleVariant::SelectedDisabled`)
*Source:* R4#1.


#### M7-18 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/segmented_control.rs:170
**Claim:** A SegmentedControl added with ui.add_enabled(false, ..) where the calling Ui's disabled_alpha is below 1 (adwaita, the community presets: 0.5) shows the outline's colour through every segment, because the whole row's backdrop is a frame filled with the border colour and egui fades that fill and each segment's fill separately.

The same per-shape class as M6-19; the enabled control is fine because the segment fills are opaque.

#### M7-19 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/segmented_control.rs:243
**Claim:** SegmentedControl::wrap() rounds corners by index in the whole list, not by place in the wrapped rows, so once the segments wrap the segment at the outline's top-right and bottom-left corners keeps square corners that poke outside the outline's rounded corner, the first segment's rounded bottom-left corner opens a notch mid-edge, and Parts records an inverted divider rect at the wrap.
**Evidence:** wrap (segmented_control.rs:108-109) lays the frame out inside ui.horizontal_wrapped; Frame::begin's content Ui inherits that wrapping layout (egui frame.rs:388-391, ui.rs:228 `layout.unwrap_or_else(|| *self.layout())`), so the buttons wrap inside one outline. row() picks corners with outline.corners(i == 0, last) where last = segments.peek().is_none() (:243-246): only segment 0 gets nw/sw and only the final segment gets ne/se. The last segment of the first (widest) row sits at the frame's top-right with ne = 0; the first segment of the second row sits at the bottom-left with sw = 0. With adwaita's radius 9 and border 1 (adwaita.toml defaults.border), the segment's square corner at inset 1 lies √2·(9−1) ≈ 11.3 from the arc centre, outside the 9 radius, so it covers the outline's curve. MapChanged (:137-145) pushes divider_i = from_x_y_ranges(segment.right()..=next.left(), ..) where `next` starts the next row, giving min.x > max.x. No test calls .wrap() (tests.rs).
**Fix proposed:** Decide corners per placed row (round only the corners a segment shares with the outline's rect, after layout or by measuring rows first), and record no divider between segments on different rows.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — With wrap() the Frame's content Ui inherits horizontal_wrapped's layout (egui Frame::begin -> new_child, ui.rs:228 layout.unwrap_or(*self.layout())), yet corners are chosen by index in the whole list, outline.corners(i == 0, peek().is_none()) (segmented_control.rs:243-246): row 1's last segment keeps square ne/se corners, row 2's first keeps square nw/sw, and segment 0 rounds its sw corner mid-edge; map_changed builds divider_i from segment.right()..=next.left() (:143), which Rect::from_x_y_ranges does not sort (emath rect.rs:95-101), so at the wrap the rect is inverted; the square-corner overhang past the outer arc shows only where radius > ~3.4 x border width.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED: `.wrap()` rounds corners per row and records no inverted divider; a test of `.wrap()`.
**Status:** fixed in 864b1d4e, da026691 (M7 T11)
*Source:* R4#3.

**Evidence:** header() computes wrap = (width − left − right − arrow − gap).max(0.0) (:262) and passes it to title.into_galley(ui, Some(TextWrapMode::Extend), wrap, ..) (:263-268); TextWrapping::from_wrap_mode_and_width(Extend, _) is no_max_width (epaint text_layout_types.rs:683-697), so the width never applies. **Claim:** Every widget of the crate records its Parts on every frame in release builds: a String per part (format! per segment and divider), a boxed insert into Context data, and for Switch, RadioButton, ComboBox and Expander a second layout of the label solely to size the label part; the entries are never removed, so each widget id ever drawn keeps its Parts for the life of the Context.
