**Evidence:** Parts::push allocates name.into() (parts.rs:50-52); store calls ctx.data_mut(insert_temp) (:55-57), which boxes the value (egui id_type_map.rs:425-433). Call sites run unconditionally per frame: switch.rs:319-331, slider.rs:262-269 (before the is_rect_visible check), radio_button.rs:489, progress_bar.rs:259-264, segmented_control.rs:134-147 (format!("segment_{i}"), format!("divider_{i}")), combo_box.rs:196-210, expander.rs:148-167 and :295-298, :231. The label re-layouts used only for Parts: switch.rs:208-217, radio_button.rs:479-487, combo_box.rs:159-167 (also used for `grow`), expander.rs:130-138. egui's IdTypeMap has no GC for temp values (only persisted ones are generation-collected at save, id_type_map.rs:700-770; Memory::end_pass does not touch `data`, memory/mod.rs:806-819), so a widget whose id changes (auto ids in a dynamic list, rows that come and go) leaves a Parts behind each time. Readers: the showcase (pages/basic.rs:358, :978, :1310) and tests. Unmeasured: a timing would compare a frame of N switches with and without the store.
**Fix proposed:** Record Parts only on request (a Context flag the showcase and tests set, or a cargo feature), and name parts with a &'static str plus an index instead of a String; the extra label layouts then run only when recording.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Every widget calls Parts::store, which runs insert_temp under id.with(..) (parts.rs:51-53) with no cfg gate and no removal, and egui's IdTypeMap has no GC for temp values (id_type_map.rs:375 'cleared when egui is shut down'; max_bytes_per_type applies only to persisted entries, :708-738), so an entry stays for every widget id ever drawn; the growth is bounded by distinct ids and matters only where ids churn, and the second label layout (radio_button.rs:146-154, expander.rs:130-138, switch.rs:210, combo_box.rs:161) is a galley-cache hit after the first frame. Confirm by counting temp_keys() after N frames of widgets with changing ids, plus an allocation count per frame.
**Triage:** fix — `Parts` stop accumulating in egui temp data for every widget id ever drawn (record only where read, or clear per pass); the leak is the gate (a temp-key count over frames), the speed half is measured.
**Status:** fixed in 8392f1e6, 9b1ecafe, c4cfea24 (M7 T9: a two-generation store per viewport)
*Source:* R4#6.


#### M7-23 · perf · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/wrap.rs:401
**Claim:** Each hyperlink, on every frame, clones the whole visited set (a BTreeSet<String> of every URL the Context has seen clicked) just to test one URL, so N hyperlinks with V visited URLs cost N·V String allocations per frame.
**Evidence:** themed() calls ui.ctx().data(|d| d.get_temp::<Visited>(visited_key()).is_some_and(|v| v.0.contains(url))) (wrap.rs:400-405); IdTypeMap::get_temp returns `.cloned()` of the stored value and documents 'The call clones the value (if found), so make sure it is cheap to clone!' (egui id_type_map.rs:446-450). Visited derives Clone over BTreeSet<String> (wrap.rs:341-342). Unmeasured.
**Fix proposed:** Store Arc<BTreeSet<String>> (cheap clone, copy-on-write on insert), or test membership inside data_mut with get_temp_mut_or_default, which borrows instead of cloning.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — themed() reads d.get_temp::<Visited>(visited_key()) (wrap.rs:97-101), and IdTypeMap::get_temp returns .cloned() (egui id_type_map.rs:448-450), so each link deep-clones the whole BTreeSet<String> every frame to test one URL (a borrow via data_mut/get_temp_mut_or_default or an Arc<BTreeSet> avoids it); the cost is small in practice since V is the set of clicked URLs; measure with an allocation count per frame over N hyperlinks and V visited URLs.
**Triage:** fix if measurable — the hyperlink reads the visited set without cloning it.
**Status:** fixed in 073ead86 (M7 T9; 100 links × 100 visited 600 → 188 µs)
*Source:* R4#7.


#### M7-24 · perf · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/expander.rs:91
**Claim:** Expander::show clones the entire ResolvedTheme (every widget's resolved struct with all their font-family Strings) on every frame for every expander, only to read t.expander and pass &t to expander_icon.
**Evidence:** expander.rs:91-92: ThemeAtlas::from_ctx(ui.ctx()).map(|atlas| atlas.resolved_for(ui.ctx().theme()).clone()). ThemeAtlas is an Arc wrapper (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/atlas.rs:231) and resolved_for returns &ResolvedTheme borrowed from it (:280-285), so keeping the atlas alive in a local gives the same &ResolvedTheme with no clone. own() needs only &ResolvedTheme for expander_icon (accessors.rs:456) and painted() only &ResolvedExpanderTheme. Smaller instance: wrap.rs:350 clones ResolvedLinkTheme (its font family String) per link per frame; holding the ThemeAtlas in the returned closure avoids it. Unmeasured.
**Fix proposed:** let atlas = ThemeAtlas::from_ctx(ui.ctx()); let t = atlas.as_ref().map(|a| a.resolved_for(ui.ctx().theme())); and pass the borrow; in wrap.rs move the cloned ThemeAtlas into the closure instead of the cloned link theme.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Expander::show does ThemeAtlas::from_ctx(..).map(|atlas| atlas.resolved_for(..).clone()) (expander.rs:91-92), deep-copying the ResolvedTheme (with its font-family Strings) each frame for each expander, where ThemeAtlas is an Arc (atlas.rs:231) whose resolved_for returns a borrow (:280-285), so keeping the atlas in a local avoids the copy; the gain is likely below timing noise (one struct clone per expander per frame); measure with a per-frame allocation count.
**Triage:** fix if measurable — the expander keeps the atlas `Arc` instead of a `ResolvedTheme` clone per frame.
**Status:** fixed in a4647e0e (M7 T9; 100 expanders 306 → 250 µs); the link half dropped, within the spread
*Source:* R4#8.


#### M7-25 · perf · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/spinner.rs:145
**Claim:** A Spinner drawing the icon set's animated indicator rebuilds the frame's ImageSource on every frame it animates (it requests continuous repaints): the SVG bytes are copied or recoloured, hashed and given a new formatted URI each time, though the frame list, colour and size are fixed.
**Evidence:** paint_indicator calls icons::to_image_source(ctx, &key, frame) every frame (spinner.rs:142-147). For IconData::Svg that runs final_svg_bytes (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/icons.rs:345, :236-254: bytes.to_vec(), or colorize_monochrome_svg for Material/Lucide, or a currentColor scan and replace for freedesktop), hashed_uri (:188-202: hashes all bytes, format! a String) and remember_uri (:273-283, a data_mut lock); egui's bytes loader then ignores the duplicate (bytes_loader.rs:15-26). The indicator itself is cached per Context (spinner.rs:108-124), but its image sources are not. Unmeasured: time a frame with one Material spinner before and after.
**Fix proposed:** Cache the per-frame ImageSources beside the AnimatedIcon in the spinner's Context entry, keyed by set, icon theme, colour and diameter, and reuse them by frame index.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — paint_indicator calls icons::to_image_source(ctx, &key, frame) every frame (spinner.rs:145), and for SVG data that runs final_svg_bytes (a to_vec, replace or colorize_monochrome_svg copy, native-theme-egui icons.rs:236-253), hashed_uri (hash plus format!, :188-201) and remember_uri (:273-282) each time; egui's loader caches by URI, so only the copy, hash and format repeat, and for a few-KB indicator that is small (the M6-16 twin, kept only if measurable); confirm with a timing of to_image_source for the indicator frame against a cached ImageSource.
**Triage:** fix if measurable — the animated spinner's SVG URI is not rebuilt per frame.
**Status:** fixed in 580aa40e, 032fc513 (M7 T9; 5.8 → 4.3 µs per spinner pass)
*Source:* R4#9.


#### M7-26 · api · api-add · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/progress_bar.rs:211
**Claim:** ProgressBar exposes only new(progress) and desired_width, so an application that wants egui's busy animation (animate), a label (text, show_percentage) or a height (desired_height) has to leave the themed wrapper for egui's own bar, losing the stated outline and radius; the egui twin of M6-28.
**Evidence:** progress_bar.rs:211-230 has two fields; egui::ProgressBar takes text, fill, animate, desired_height and corner_radius (egui progress_bar.rs:100-109), and the wrapper already builds one egui::ProgressBar (:238), so forwarding is a builder per option. The stated outline (:265-271) is independent of them.
**Fix proposed:** Before: pub fn desired_width(self, width: f32) -> Self only. After: add pub fn animate(self, bool) -> Self, pub fn text(self, impl Into<WidgetText>) -> Self and pub fn show_percentage(self) -> Self, forwarded to egui::ProgressBar (fill and corner_radius stay the theme's).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — egui::ProgressBar has desired_height, fill, text, show_percentage and animate (egui progress_bar.rs:41-95), and the wrapper exposes only new and desired_width (progress_bar.rs:36-47), as the spec scoped it (todo_egui-widgets-spec.md:384, :770-777) without a recorded decision against the rest; corrections: egui skips the animate arc under a custom corner_radius, which the wrapper always sets (egui :78-80, :163), so animate would give only the pulse, and desired_height or fill would override the theme's track_height and fill_color.
**Triage:** fix, narrowed — `animate` (the indeterminate bar, parity with gpui's M6-28) only; `text`/`show_percentage` stay out by the recorded wrapper scope (spec §4.9, the rejected API-8).
**Status:** fixed in 2d0236e2 (M7 T11: `ProgressBar::animate`)
*Source:* R4#10.

#### M7-28 · api · api-add · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/ext.rs:26
**Claim:** `NativeThemeUiExt` gives a `Ui` form to two of the three delivery seams (`native_scope`/`native_set_style` for the role scope, `native_frame` for `surface_frame`) but none to `ThemeAtlas::role_modifier`, so every popup, menu and combo-box call site spells `ThemeAtlas::from_ctx(ui.ctx()).map(|a| a.role_modifier(ui.ctx().theme(), role, variant))` and the showcase wrote its own helper for it.
**Evidence:** ext.rs:26-82 declares exactly three methods; `native_frame` (:114-119) is the `Ui` sugar for `surface_frame(theme, surface)` (atlas.rs:406-408), while `role_modifier(theme, role, variant)` (atlas.rs:379-393) has no counterpart. The showcase defines `fn role_modifier(ui, role, variant) -> Option<StyleModifier>` (examples/showcase-egui/demo.rs:307-313) and calls it at :455, :573, :597 and :619. The trait's invariant 'degrades to egui's own behaviour; none returns an Option' (:14-15) holds for an identity modifier: egui 0.36.2's `StyleModifier` derives `Default` as `None` and `apply` does nothing then (egui/src/style.rs:193, :226-230). Neither `egui::Ui` nor `egui::Context` has a method named `native_role_modifier`, so the name rule of :17-25 holds.
**Fix proposed:** Before: `pub trait NativeThemeUiExt { fn native_scope(..); fn native_set_style(..); fn native_frame(&self, surface: Surface) -> egui::Frame; }`. After: the same plus `#[must_use] fn native_role_modifier(&self, role: Role, variant: RoleVariant) -> egui::style::StyleModifier;` returning `atlas.role_modifier(self.ctx().theme(), role, variant)` or `StyleModifier::default()` with no atlas; the showcase's helper and its four call sites use it. Additive (the trait is sealed).
**Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE — The gap is real: the showcase wrote its own Option-returning helper (examples/showcase-egui/demo.rs:307-314, used at :455, :573, :597, :619, with one direct call at :331), and widgets combo_box.rs:143 already holds the atlas. But a Ui form cannot fall back to StyleModifier::default() with no atlas, because MenuConfig's default is menu_style (egui menu.rs:83, :226) and a default modifier would drop it. So the method would have to return an Option or a role-dependent fallback, which breaks the trait's 'none returns an Option' contract (ext.rs:15).
**Triage:** defer (docs/todo.md) — PLAUSIBLE: a `Ui` form needs an `Option` with no atlas, against the trait's documented contract (ext.rs:15); the showcase helper stands until M8's cross-connector API batch.
**Status:** deferred (docs/todo.md, M8 API batch)
*Source:* API#0.

**Claim:** An application on the OS theme that has fonts of its own, or a `style_patch`, cannot add them to what `to_egui_atlas` builds; the doc tells it to re-spell the seven-call builder chain by hand, although a `Builder` borrowing the `SystemTheme` is exactly what `to_egui_atlas` constructs before `.build()`.
**Evidence:** ext.rs:305-316: 'Equivalent to — and the chain to spell out when adding `Builder::style_patch` or a plan of the application's own — `ThemeAtlas::builder(&self.name, &self.light, &self.dark).layout(..).accessibility(..).os_mode(..).icon_set(..).icon_theme(..).icon_theme(..).fonts(plan).build()`'. README.md:225-231 says to pass own fonts as `FontPlan::from_system(&light).with_base(its_definitions)` into `Builder::fonts` without showing that chain. `Builder<'a>` (atlas.rs:515-526) borrows only a `&'a str`, two `&'a ResolvedTheme`, `&'a LayoutTheme`, `&'a AccessibilityPreferences` and two `&'a str` icon-theme names, every one of which `&SystemTheme` provides (`name`, `light`, `dark`, `layout`, `accessibility`, `icon_theme_for(mode)` as `to_egui_atlas` reads them, :323-333), so `fn to_egui_builder(&self) -> Builder<'_>` is the body of :323-337 without `.build()`. No caller in the workspace needs it today (the showcase at app.rs:499 uses to_egui_atlas plain), so the addition touches 0 call sites.

*Source:* API#1.


#### M7-30 · api · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/lib.rs:30
**Claim:** The crate-level and README 'from a bundled preset' examples build the atlas with `is_dark = true` and install it, but never pick egui's colour scheme, so a reader copying them sees the OS scheme on macOS and Windows and egui's `fallback_theme` (Dark) on Linux rather than the variant they asked for.
**Evidence:** lib.rs:26-34 and README.md:160-169: `from_preset("catppuccin-mocha", true, ..)?; atlas.install(ctx);` and nothing else, while the README prose at :156-158 says 'egui's own `set_theme` picks the scheme on screen'. `from_preset`'s doc (ext.rs:172-174) states `is_dark` 'does not pin egui's colour scheme — that is egui's `ctx.set_theme(..)`', and `install` never touches `Options::theme_preference` (atlas.rs:429-438); a preset atlas carries no `os_mode` (ext.rs:168-170), so on Linux egui falls back to `Options::fallback_theme`, default `Theme::Dark` (atlas.rs:440-441). The OS-theme Quick start does set `ThemePreference::System` (lib.rs:19).
**Fix proposed:** Add the one line both snippets lack: `ctx.set_theme(egui::ThemePreference::Dark);` (or `if is_dark { Dark } else { Light }` where the bool is a variable), with the sentence that a preset pins the scheme while `from_system` follows the OS. No signature change.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — lib.rs:30-31 and README.md:165-166 install a from_preset atlas without ctx.set_theme. from_preset's own doc (ext.rs:172-173) says is_dark does not pin egui's scheme, and catppuccin-mocha has a light variant (presets/catppuccin-mocha.toml:9), so on a light-scheme macOS or Windows the example shows Latte-derived colours. On Linux it happens to match, since fallback_theme is Dark and is_dark is true.
**Triage:** fix — the preset Quick start (lib.rs, README) calls `set_theme` for the variant `is_dark` named.
**Status:** fixed in a829f6ff (M7 T3)
*Source:* API#2.


#### M7-31 · api · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/README.md:246
**Claim:** The README's only icon recipe hard-codes `IconSet::Lucide`, loads through `load_icon` (the bundled sets only) and passes no icon theme, so copied as is it ignores the installed theme's `icon_set` and `icon_theme`; the general one-call path, `icons::custom_icon_to_image_source`, is hidden behind 'custom'/'application-supplied `IconProvider`' wording although `IconRole` is an `IconProvider`.
**Evidence:** README.md:242-258: `let set = IconSet::Lucide;` then `native_theme::icons::load_icon(IconRole::DialogWarning, set)` and `to_image`. The atlas doc says icon code 'follows the theme with no second input' through `ThemeAtlas::icon_set` and `icon_theme(ctx.theme())` (atlas.rs:315-342). `custom_icon_to_image_source(ctx, provider, key)` (icons.rs:409-437) already dispatches per set with the key's icon theme and size and the colour `to_image_source` uses, and core has `impl IconProvider for IconRole` (native-theme/src/icons.rs:547), so `custom_icon_to_image_source(ctx, &role, &IconKey::role(role, set)..)` is the role path; its doc (:397-407) names only 'an application-supplied IconProvider'. The colour it loads a freedesktop icon in comes from the private `load_color` (:222-229), which a caller following the `to_image_source` doc's 'load a freedesktop icon for it with `FreedesktopLoader::color` in the same colour' (:316-317) cannot read. The showcase re-implements that dispatch in `role_image` (examples/showcase-egui/demo.rs:801-836, 35 lines) and again in `named_image` (:898-922).
**Fix proposed:** Rewrite the README recipe from the installed atlas (`let atlas = ThemeAtlas::from_ctx(ui.ctx())?; let set = atlas.icon_set(); let mut key = IconKey::role(role, set).size(side); if let Some(t) = atlas.icon_theme(ui.ctx().theme()) { key = key.icon_theme(t) } custom_icon_to_image_source(ui.ctx(), &role, &key)`), say in `custom_icon_to_image_source`'s doc that an `IconRole` is a provider, and optionally add `custom_icon_to_image(ctx, provider, key) -> Option<egui::Image<'static>>` beside `to_image` so the role path also gets the alt text (api-add, additive); the showcase's two helpers then shrink to it.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — README.md:247-249 hard-codes IconSet::Lucide and never consults atlas.icon_set or icon_theme. One correction: core's load_icon (native-theme/src/icons.rs:692-700) reaches all five sets, not just the bundled ones, though with no theme, size or colour. custom_icon_to_image_source (icons.rs:397-438) is the loading path that takes theme, size and tint, and IconRole implements IconProvider (model/icons.rs:547).
**Triage:** fix — the icon recipe goes through `custom_icon_to_image_source` for an `IconRole`, with the icon theme.
**Status:** fixed in b61475db, 28f4727d (M7 T12: `icons::custom_icon_to_image`)
*Source:* API#3.

**Claim:** `ExpanderResponse<R>`, a value struct the crate builds and the user only reads, has two public fields and no `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the fields egui's own `CollapsingResponse` also carries (`body_response`, `openness`) cannot be added later without a breaking change — the class M6-34 fixed for gpui's ten value structs.

M6-34 (ledger) put `#[non_exhaustive]` on every such struct.

After: `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct ExpanderResponse<R> { pub header_response: egui::Response, pub body_returned: Option<R> }`; field reads keep working, only an outside struct literal or exhaustive pattern (none known) breaks, and `body_response`/`openness` can follow additively.

None constructs or destructures the struct, so adding it touches 0 call sites.

*Source:* API#5.

The crate's only version statement is lib.rs:4 'Target: egui 0.36.2' and Cargo.toml:8 `rust-version = "1.95"`. A published crate's README is rendered from its own package, where `../native-theme-egui/README.md` does not exist; the connector's README links its own sibling by URL (`https://crates.io/crates/native-theme`, :10).
**Fix proposed:** Add a Quick start `toml` block (`eframe`, `native-theme-egui`, `native-theme-egui-widgets` at the workspace minor), one Compatibility sentence (egui 0.36.2, rust-version 1.95, as the connector's) and the connector's crates.io or docs.rs URL in place of the relative path; when M5-20's README version check lands in the connector (M7), cover this README's block too.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Partly confirmed. The widgets README has no [dependencies] block and no egui version (a grep for 0.36, MSRV, dependencies and toml finds nothing), while the connector README has one (README.md:124). The link part does not hold: crates.io resolves relative README links through path_in_vcs, and the maintainer prefers relative links. MSRV is shown from Cargo.toml:8 on crates.io. The version check itself is the known M5-20 item.
**Triage:** fix — the widgets README gains a `[dependencies]` block and the egui version (relative links stay: the maintainer's rule).
**Status:** fixed in 36620c8e, 08bd7b04 (M7 T3; the README compiled as a doctest in T13)
*Source:* API#10.


#### M7-35 · bug · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/watch.rs:29
**Claim:** A failed watcher rebuild stores its message in `last_error` but requests no repaint, so an idle egui application does not run `logic` and the error is seen only when some unrelated event repaints — the documented 'reports its message through `last_error`' is reachable but never signalled.
**Evidence:** watch.rs:20-35: the `Ok` arm stores the atlas and calls `ctx.request_repaint()` (:27); the `Err` arm (:29-34) only writes `last_error`. The README's recipe (:288-293) reads the watcher in `App::logic`, which eframe runs once per frame, and egui repaints only when asked or on input. The sibling shapes avoid the gap by design: gpui's `on_theme_change` runs the application's closure on the foreground (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/watch.rs:7-12) and iced's `theme_changes` delivers a message, so a re-read's error surfaces at once.
**Fix proposed:** Call `ctx.request_repaint()` in the `Err` arm too, and say in `start`'s and `last_error`'s docs that the UI is woken either way. No signature change.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — watch.rs:29-34, the Err arm, stores last_error with no ctx.request_repaint(), while the Ok arm calls it (:27). The spec's §10.2 (spec:6715-6716) records no reason for skipping it, and test T15(b) (watch.rs:172-191) does not count repaints; a test with set_request_repaint_callback counting 1 after a failing rebuild would show it.
**Triage:** fix — a failed watcher rebuild requests a repaint, as a successful one does.
**Status:** fixed in 61090f39 (M7 T5)
*Source:* API#11.


#### M7-36 · api · api-break · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/convert.rs:186
**Claim:** `convert::to_color32_with_opacity` is a public function with no caller in the connector, the widgets crate or the showcase; its only use is its own test, so it is dead code exported as API.
**Evidence:** A grep of `to_color32_with_opacity` over connectors/native-theme-egui/src, connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src and connectors/native-theme-egui/examples finds the definition (convert.rs:186) and the test at :572-581 only; the style modules apply opacity through `unit_interval` directly (style/variants.rs:325, :432). The spec lists it (docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md:2009) but no rationale names a consumer, and its own doc warns the result must never reach `bg_fill` (:181-183).
**Fix proposed:** Delete it with its test (a `Color32::gamma_multiply` is the egui-side spelling an application would use), or make it `pub(crate)` if a sink is about to need it.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The only references in the repository are its definition (convert.rs:186), its own tests (:572-581) and a doc link (:48); its doc (:176-179) says it is not for borders, the use the spec first gave it (spec:1878). Note that removing it is an api-break, not S4.
**Triage:** maintainer: 2026-10-15, remove `to_color32_with_opacity` → fix.
**Status:** fixed in 8524b36a (M7 T2, maintainer 2026-10-15)
*Source:* API#12.


#### M7-37 · api · api-break · connectors/native-theme-egui-widgets/src/lib.rs:97
**Claim:** The public module `wrap` names the implementation tier ('Tier W: wrapped'), not what it holds, and in the same crate and in egui 'wrap' means line-wrapping (`SegmentedControl::wrap`, `ComboBox::wrap`, `TextWrapMode`), so `native_theme_egui_widgets::wrap::link` reads as a wrapping link.
**Evidence:** lib.rs:97 `pub mod wrap; // Tier W: \`link\`, \`hyperlink\``; wrap.rs:1 '**Tier W**: egui's `Link` and `Hyperlink` in `link.*`'s state and visited colours'. segmented_control.rs:77 `pub fn wrap(mut self) -> Self` 'Wraps the segments onto a further line'; egui 0.36.2 `ComboBox::wrap`/`wrap_mode` (egui/src/containers/combo_box.rs:166-173). The tier names are a documentation taxonomy (lib.rs:50-56) that no other public path carries. One consumer: examples/showcase-egui/pages/basic.rs:1078. The widgets spec names the module (docs/archive/todo_egui-widgets-spec.md:325, :613) and the rationale gives no reason for the name.
**Fix proposed:** Before: `pub mod wrap;` with `wrap::link`, `wrap::hyperlink`. After: `pub mod links;` with `links::link`, `links::hyperlink` (the module doc keeps the tier note); one showcase import changes.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The name is recorded in spec:324 with no stated reason, every other module is named for its widget, and SegmentedControl::wrap (segmented_control.rs:77) and egui's ComboBox::wrap (combo_box.rs:173) do use 'wrap' for line-wrapping. A rename touches widgets lib.rs:27 and :97, README.md:16, tests.rs:28, :238, :246, :319, :323, :612, and the showcase's pages/basic.rs:27 and :1078.
**Triage:** maintainer: 2026-10-15, rename the module `wrap` to `links` → fix.
**Status:** fixed in 7e4787b8 (M7 T2, maintainer 2026-10-15)
*Source:* API#13.

### Step 6 — fix plan (2026-10-15)

Drafted by a Fable 5.1 planner from the entries, the maintainer's three answers, M5's and M6's rulings and what M6's fix phase built (`git log 1e60e1c9..HEAD`), reviewed by the session.

Order per the plan: S1 first (M7-04), then the API changes (they move code the others touch: the three approved breaks, the features, core's theme-taking loader and its per-process family memo, the connector's new `RoleVariant`), then S2, S3, S4. One `implement` agent (Opus) per task, a fresh reviewer per task, `./scripts/check_release.sh --commit` once per task on its last commit (maintainer). Gates: bug → a failing test first that reproduces the finding, then the fix, then it passes; perf → `cargo test -p native-theme-egui --release --all-features --test timings -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` three runs *before* (taken at the task's start, not Step 1's baseline, which ran at load 15–21) and three *after*, kept only when every after median lies below the three before runs' minimum by more than their spread (max − min); a widgets-crate row lives in the same file, the widgets crate being the connector's dev-dependency (`connectors/native-theme-egui/Cargo.toml`, `native-theme-egui-widgets = { path = .. }`); simplify → `git diff --stat` net deletion, tests unchanged except tests of deleted code; api → `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`, the egui crates in every gate configuration (`--no-default-features`, default, `--all-features`, `scripts/check_features.sh`'s each-feature run), every caller updated (the widgets crate, the showcase, the README, doc examples, `contract.rs`, `install_tests.rs`), a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line, semver as the maintainer approved on 2026-10-15 (M7-32, M7-36, M7-37) and no other break. Two sources are read before any task touches them: `docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md` (§3.4 cells, §6.18 the focus ring, §8.5 text sizes, §9.2 icon colouring, §10.2–§10.3 the watcher and the install sequence, §14 the ledger) and `docs/archive/todo_egui-widgets-spec.md` (the widgets' tiers and recorded scope). The lint hints of Step 1 (90 production hits) go to each task's implementer for its files, never as findings.

Rulings (Step 6):

- Ruling: the order rule bends once inside a file, for its own reason (code is moved before it is edited): M7-08's dead colour path (S4 simplify in `style/base.rs`, `states.rs`, `roles.rs`, `frames.rs`) is T14's last commit, after the `extreme_bg_color` fix in the same `base.rs`; and T10 carries an api-add (the connector's `RoleVariant::SelectedDisabled`) inside a bug task, because the widgets' fix cannot be written without the cell it opens. — why: the template orders API changes first because they move code the others touch; the same holds inside one file. — cost if wrong: one task's commits reordered.
- Ruling: M7-04 (S1) — the cap is owned by the install plugin and derived, never stated. `Builder::build` records in `AtlasInner` the widest glyph of the faces the atlas installs, in em: for each face of the `FontDefinitions` `font_definitions(plan)` makes (or `egui::FontDefinitions::default()`'s faces for an atlas built with no plan, said in `Builder::fonts`'s doc), skrifa's `Metrics::bounds` (`skrifa-0.44.0/src/metrics.rs:72-102`, the font's own `head` bounding box, which every glyph's box lies inside) gives `(x_max − x_min) / units_per_em × tweak.scale`, the maximum kept; the parse is the one `fonts.rs:394-406` already makes for the row height. `NativeThemePlugin::input_hook` (`plugin.rs`, before egui's `begin_pass` builds the pass's root `Ui`) reads `input.max_texture_side` (`egui/src/data/input/raw_input.rs:45`, `Option<usize>`; `ctx.input(|i| i.max_texture_side)` where `None`) and the pass's `pixels_per_point` (`input.viewport().native_pixels_per_point` × `ctx.zoom_factor()`, egui's own product), and whenever that pair or the published atlas changed since the last pass derives `cap_pt = floor((min(max_texture_side, 16 × 1024) − 2) / (pixels_per_point × widest_em))` — the atlas width epaint allocates (`epaint/src/text/fonts.rs:975`), less the two pixels `control_box().expand()` can add (`epaint/src/text/font.rs:265-266`), over the widest glyph's width at one point — stores it in the atlas (`AtomicU32`, f32 bits, `f32::INFINITY` until derived; `ThemeAtlas::text_size_cap(&self) -> Option<f32>`, public, api-add), and clamps every `text_styles` size above it in both installed base styles (`ctx.style_of` → `ctx.set_style_of`, written only when a size exceeds the cap, so the common pass writes nothing). `native_scope`, `native_set_style` and `role_modifier` clamp a cell's `override_font_id` the same way beside `carry_name_keys` (a `Style` clone in the pathological case only). The accessors keep no cap (they take no `Context`); each `FontId` accessor's doc names `text_size_cap` as the bound an application clamps a size it hands egui with. `Builder::accessibility`'s and `scaled_text_size`'s docs say what is capped and why (epaint's `assert!` at `texture_atlas.rs:226-231`); a `docs/todo.md` entry records the upstream ask (an oversize glyph skipped as a `width == 0` one is, `font.rs:268`). Gate: a kittest pass drawing `"W"` under a theme file stating `defaults.font.size = 30000` (core accepts it, `validate_helpers.rs:491`) panics today in epaint and completes after; a unit test of the derivation; a pass whose `native_pixels_per_point` doubles re-derives (the cap halves). — why: spec §14 item 44 records the limit as run-time dependent (`max_texture_side`, `pixels_per_point`), so no build-time number is honest; the faces' own bounding boxes are the one upstream-sourced width a glyph cannot exceed, and the plugin is the one place that sees both run-time values before every pass; a clamp at install alone would break on the next monitor change. — cost if wrong: the largest task of the phase for the rarest input; a glyph wider than its font's `head` box (a CFF face whose control box exceeds it by more than the floor's slack) is the stated residual, narrower than today's by the whole box; if the implementer finds the root `Ui` cloned before `input_hook` runs, the fallback is the same clamp in `install` plus the plugin re-clamping with one pass of lag, stated.
- Ruling: M7-01 — `install` of the atlas already published (`ThemeAtlas::from_ctx(ctx)` `Arc::ptr_eq` to `self`) re-runs step 2 only (both base styles through `carry_name_keys`, so a style the application reset is restored, which "safe to call at any time" promises) and returns: no `set_fonts` (egui compares TTF bytes, `egui/src/context.rs:2109-2115`), no `forget_icons`, no `request_repaint`; `ThemeAtlas::clear(ctx)` then `install` runs the whole sequence, and the doc says so. `add_plugin` already ignores a second plugin of the type (`context.rs:2047-2055`, `plugin.rs:203-215`), so the plugin's state persists either way. Gate: a test counting repaint requests (`set_request_repaint_callback`) and stored-texture removals over two installs of one atlas — today both happen twice; `install_requests_a_repaint` and `install_leaves_no_stored_icon_texture_handle` install a second atlas. — why: a repeated install of what is installed is a no-op by the doc's own promise; the three skipped steps are the ones that cost per frame (an idle app never idles, every raster icon re-uploads). — cost if wrong: an application that called `set_fonts` itself and re-installs the same atlas to get the atlas's fonts back now needs `clear` first — documented.
- Ruling: M7-02 — `output_hook` gains the inverse of its rewrite: when `os_mode(ctx)` is `None` (a preset atlas, or after `clear`), `sync_window_theme` holds, the preference is `System` and `last_sent` holds a scheme for the viewport, it pushes `SetTheme(SystemTheme::SystemDefault)` once and removes the entry — the command egui believes it sent (`context.rs:2474-2497`) and will not send again, so the window and egui agree and the plugin is inert, as `after_clear_the_plugin_is_inert` requires. Not `SetTheme(ctx.theme())`: a preset atlas pins its scheme through `ctx.set_theme(Dark|Light)` (M7-30's recipe), which egui syncs itself; asserting `fallback_theme` would make the plugin track a value egui owns. Gate: the entry's sequence — `preset_atlas_with_os_mode(kde-breeze, Light)`, one pass with `system_theme: None`, then `preset_atlas(kde-breeze)` and one pass: `(Theme::Dark, vec![SystemDefault])`, today `vec![]`; the same after `ThemeAtlas::clear`. — why: spec §10.3's title-bar goal and its table (spec:6896-6901); restoring egui's own state is the smallest true fix. — cost if wrong: on X11 `SystemDefault` writes `_GTK_THEME_VARIANT = "dark"` whatever the desktop (winit, the spec's table), egui's own behaviour under a preset, not ours.
- Ruling: M7-12 — the per-process family memo moves into core, and both connectors use it: `native_theme::fonts::substitute_family_cached(family: &str) -> Option<String>` (api-add) is gpui's `asked_once` (`connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:714-732`: the lock held for the look-up and the insert only, never across the `fc-match` subprocess; two first askers may both ask, the last answer is kept) over a `static` map, with gpui's `a_family_ask_in_flight_blocks_no_other_look_up` (`lib.rs:1486`) moved to core's `fonts` tests; gpui's `substituted_family` becomes one call and its map and helper are deleted; egui's `FontPlan::from_system` (`fonts.rs:165-171`) asks it in place of `substitute_family`. `substitute_family` keeps its uncached contract ("each call starts a process"). The once-per-family cost is stated in `FontPlan::from_system`'s and `from_preset`'s docs, as M6-03 stated gpui's. — why: a memo of a subprocess answer is toolkit-free (M1-T7-01's rule) and M8 R1 would otherwise find it written twice; M6-03's ruling kept *core's `substitute_family`* one call, which stays true. — cost if wrong: a family installed after the first ask stays substituted for the process (gpui's accepted rule, now egui's too); one more `pub fn` in core.
- Ruling: M7-13 (if measurable) — `custom_icon_to_image_source` keeps the loaded `IconData` per `(IconKey, the colour it was loaded in)` in `Context` data as an `Arc<IconData>`, dropped by `forget_icons` with the URIs (so an install, and the same-atlas install's doc, say when it reloads); the colour is in the key because `load_color` follows `ctx.theme()`, which flips without an install. Gate: a timings row first — `IconRole::ALL` as providers, 40 freedesktop keys loaded per pass, 21 passes — three runs before and after; the cache stays only above the spread; the doc names the per-call cost (a disk read; core's own note, `freedesktop.rs`) either way. — why: the triage's rule. — cost if wrong: a bounded cache (one entry per distinct key per install) nobody measured a need for.
- Ruling: M7-03 (if measurable) — `record_scope` gains `replace: bool`: `native_scope` pushes without the scan (its `child.unique_id()` is new every pass, `egui/src/ui.rs:252-260`), `native_set_style` keeps the replace; `paint_focus_ring` reads the entry by reference inside one `data_mut` after the widget table and viewport are read outside it (the §10.3 lock rule). Gate: timings rows of 100 and 1000 `native_scope`s per pass and one focused widget; kept above the spread. — why: the triage. — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: M7-22 — the leak is fixed by one store, not a flag: every widget's `Parts` go into one `PartsStore` under one key, two generations (`current`, `previous`) swapped when the pass number advances, so entries live two passes and `Parts::of` reads `current` then `previous`; the public shape and "as the pass that drew it last painted them" stay (a widget not drawn for two passes answers `None`, which a reader of stale rectangles should get). Gate (bug): `IdTypeMap::len()` (`egui/src/util/id_type_map.rs:620`) stays flat over 200 passes of widgets with churning ids and the store holds at most two passes' widgets — today the map grows by one key per widget per pass (`count::<Parts>()`, `:646`, shows it). The speed half (the `String` per part, the second label layout, a galley-cache hit after the first pass) is measured by a row of 200 `Switch`es per pass; static names and index pairs follow only above the spread. — why: `Parts` are public and read by the showcase's Widget Info and the tests in the pass that drew the widget; an opt-in flag would make `Parts::of` `None` for every application by default, a behaviour change the leak does not need. — cost if wrong: one `HashMap` swap per pass.
- Ruling: M7-23, M7-24, M7-25 (each if measurable) — `Visited(Arc<BTreeSet<String>>)`, clone-on-write on a click (`get_temp` clones the `Arc`, `egui/src/util/id_type_map.rs:448-450`); `Expander::show` and `wrap::link_theme` keep the `ThemeAtlas` (an `Arc`, `atlas.rs:231`) and borrow `resolved_for` instead of cloning a `ResolvedTheme`/`ResolvedLinkTheme`; the widgets' `Spinner` keeps the indicator's per-frame `ImageSource`s beside the `AnimatedIcon` in its `Context` entry, keyed by set, icon theme, colour and diameter, so `to_image_source`'s copy, hash and `format!` run once per frame index. Gates: rows of 100 hyperlinks with 100 visited URLs, 100 expanders, and one Material spinner frame's `to_image_source`; each kept above the spread, else dropped with its numbers in the ledger. — why: the triage rules; a gain below the spread is noise. — cost if wrong: three small refactors kept for no measured gain.
- Ruling: M7-16, M7-17, M7-18 — the disabled rule of 2026-09-28 (docs/todo.md:2041-2047; iced's `styles::checkbox`, gpui's `checkbox.rs:128-143`) in egui: (1) the connector gains `RoleVariant::SelectedDisabled` (api-add; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, `roles.rs:81`): for `Role::Checkbox` its cell is the `Selected` cell's colours (the checked fill, the indicator mark) with the role's `disabled_alpha` where `checkbox.disabled_background` is `None`, and the `Disabled` cell where it is stated (a platform that dims by colour draws its stated disabled fill, the open [1.0] question at docs/todo.md:2038 untouched); for every other role it is the `Disabled` cell (an `Arc` clone, no new style). `RoleVariant`'s doc names it beside `Selected`. (2) The widgets' `open_faded` (`scope.rs:36-62`) maps `(disabled, selected)` to it, so a checked disabled `RadioButton` opens the checked look and `fade_as_one` fades it over its backdrop. (3) `Slider` gets `backdrop(Color32)` (default `defaults.background_color`) and composes rail over ground, fill over rail, knob and outline over fill, each `fade::faded` by `disabled_alpha` over the ground, the painter's opacity left at 1 (gpui's M6-19 shape: `SliderLook::faded_over`). (4) `SegmentedControl` under a disabled calling `Ui` with `disabled_alpha < 1` composes each segment's fill over the outline's fill and fades both over the backdrop (`fade_as_one` over the scope's cells, the outline fill included), as `Switch` does. `lib.rs`'s *Disabled* paragraph names the four. Gates: adwaita light — a disabled slider's fill shape equals `faded(ground, over(ground, rail), fill, 0.5)` at opacity 1; a disabled segmented control's unselected segment equals `faded(ground, segment, 0.5)`, no border colour in it; `RadioButton::new(true, ..).enabled(false)` paints a circle filled with the faded checked fill — each fails today. — why: the widgets fade as one where the platform fades the whole widget (libadwaita's `filter: Opacity`); a cell the connector owns keeps the data test out of applications; the egui rationale's "Why Selected and Disabled are not combined" predates the rule. — cost if wrong: one more `RoleVariant` nobody opens for a role other than the checkbox.
- Ruling: M7-19 — `.wrap()` takes its corners from the rows, egui's own way: the previous pass's segment rectangles (kept in the control's `Parts`, read by the control's id before layout) tell which segment corner coincides with the outline's rectangle corner (nw/sw for the first row's first and the last row's first, ne/se for the first row's last and the last row's last, within a point), and only those are rounded; a divider is recorded only between two segments of one row (`next.left() >= segment.right()` and equal `y_range`); with no previous rectangles (the first pass, a changed segment list) the index rule stands and `ctx.request_discard("segmented control wrap")` (`egui/src/context.rs:1992`, egui's mechanism for a sizing guess, `Options::max_passes` default 2) re-runs the pass with them known. Gate: a `.wrap()` control in a `Ui` narrower than its segments — the first row's last segment keeps square `ne`/`se`, the second row's first keeps square `nw`/`sw`, segment 0's `sw` is square, no `divider_n` has `min.x > max.x`; today all four fail. — why: egui lays the segments out one by one, so a segment's place in its row is known only after the pass, which is what `request_discard` exists for; the control already keeps the rectangles. — cost if wrong: one discarded pass when the control first wraps or its segments change.
- Ruling: M7-20 — the painted header lays its title out with `TextWrapMode::Wrap` at the computed `wrap` width (the height already follows the galley) and allocates `max(ui.available_width(), galley.width + left + right + arrow + gap)`, so a title that cannot wrap (one long word) still lies inside the header, as `CollapsingHeader` allocates at least its text (`egui/src/containers/collapsing_header.rs:516-532`). M7-21 — with no `desired_width`, the wrapper passes `desired_width(ui.available_size_before_wrap().x.max(clamp_length(progress_bar.min_width)))` where `min_width` is finite: egui's own formula (`progress_bar.rs:113-114`) with the theme's floor in place of 96. Gates: a long title under a 120-point `Ui` wraps inside the header rectangle and never under a trailing arrow; a bar in a 50-point column is 100 wide under macos-monterey and 50 under kde-breeze (min 6) — today 96 and 96. — why: connectors follow theme data; the values' own sources stay docs/todo.md's [1.0] item (the triage). — cost if wrong: a title wrapped where libadwaita would ellipsize (it wraps by default, `title-lines = 0`).
- Ruling: M7-26 (narrowed) — `ProgressBar::animate(bool)` forwards egui's own `animate`; under a stated radius egui draws its pulse and skips the arc (`egui/src/widgets/progress_bar.rs:78-80`, its own rule), and the wrapper passes `false` under `atlas.accessibility().reduce_motion`, as the widgets' `Spinner` stills itself; the doc says both. `text`/`show_percentage` stay out (the recorded wrapper scope, the rejected API-8). M7-27 — `Expander::open(Option<bool>)` (`CollapsingHeader::open` in `own()`, `state.set_open` plus `mark_changed` in `painted()`, egui's `show_dyn:635-637`) and `enabled(bool)` through `scope::open`. — why: the motion is egui's and the model states none (M1-T7-02). — cost if wrong: a pulse without an arc, which is what egui draws for itself under a radius.
- Ruling: M1-T6-06, M7-10, M7-11, M5-04's egui half, M1-T7-01 — core gains `icons::load_custom_icon_in(provider, set, icon_theme: Option<&str>, color, size)` (api-add; `load_custom_icon` becomes `_in(.., None, ..)`, keeping iced's and gpui's unreleased call shape; `_in` is core's existing name for the theme-taking form, `load_icon_in`, `icons.rs:772`), and `custom_icon_to_image_source` loads every set through it with `key.icon_theme.as_deref()`, `key.size` and the colour per set — `load_color(ctx, key)` (tint, else the atlas's text colour) for Freedesktop, SF Symbols and Segoe, `key.tint_rgba()` alone for Material and Lucide (an untinted bundled icon stays as it is, `IconKey::tint`'s rule) — then hashes and registers the bytes with no second colouring pass (a private path shared with `to_image_source`, which keeps colouring the bytes an application loaded itself). `final_svg_bytes`'s freedesktop arm and `sets_color` go for core's `fill_current_color` (`icons.rs:1006`, the same rule: `currentColor` filled where the document sets no `color`), its tests moved where core's lack the case; the bundled arm already calls core's `colorize_monochrome_svg`, so M1-T7-01 is closed for egui by inspection (docs/todo.md:436 says so). Two behaviours the switch changes are kept and documented: a provider's own SVG for a system set is coloured in `color` (core's `load_provider_icon`), and SF Symbols fall back to `icon_svg` on every platform, which the function's doc already claims. ### Steps 7–8 — fix phase closed (2026-10-16)

- Tasks T1–T14, one `implement` agent (Opus 5.5) per task, with a fresh reviewer per task: Opus, or Sonnet for the mechanical ones. Fix rounds followed 12 of the 14 reviews. `check_release.sh --commit` ran once per task (the maintainer's rule of 2026-10-15). The commits and rulings are in the SDD ledger (`.superpowers/sdd/todo_code-review-plan/progress.md`, "## M7 fix phase"), and each entry's Status names its commits.
- Rulings made during execution, beyond the fix plan:
  - M7-04's cap: a variable or CFF face takes its own glyph boxes at the drawn weight, in a checksum-keyed process cache; at most 2.6 ms once per process for the default plans.
  - `install` lowers sizes only with a real pass's inputs, and a per-pass viewport stack keeps each viewport's cap.
  - The custom-icon cache is keyed by everything core's named load depends on, including the resolved system icon theme (M7-13).
  - The checkbox's `SelectedDisabled` cell is the Selected cell with the disabled fill and the disabled text colour, and a translucent slider knob fades over the backdrop (M7-16, M7-17).
  - The segmented control re-lays out, discarding a pass, whenever its rows change, bounded by egui's `max_passes` (M7-19).
  - The showcase panel toggle's alt text is descriptive.
- Final whole-phase review (Fable 5.1, `c5ff9271..c25a1c8b`): Ready, nothing Critical or Important. Its two Minors were fixed in `0c831ad4`.
- Full `./scripts/check_release.sh` at `f9d00612`: 115 checks · 106 ✅ · 7 ⚠️ · 2 ❌, 33 min 52 s.
  - The warnings are the existing tag v0.6.1 and soft semver ×6. The semver items are approved breaks only: for egui, M5's accessor renames and `to_color32_with_opacity`; for egui-widgets, the `wrap` → `links` rename and `ExpanderResponse` becoming `#[non_exhaustive]`; for gpui, iced, core and build, the earlier milestones' approved breaks.
  - The two ❌ are expected: the visual assets and the compatibility stamps, which the release asset run refreshes.

That leaves 89 entries: 1 api S4, 2 api api-add, 4 api api-break, 9 bug S2, 27 bug S4, 4 bugs S2, 24 bugs S4, 2 docs S4, 1 preset S4, 1 scripts S4, 6 simplification S4, 8 simplify S4.

During the review, CI run 38915441812 on the push of `c1f91449` passed all 36 jobs. The macOS and Windows tests of M5–M7 now ran there for the first time.

Rejected:
- R1#10 (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:948): (c) `Native<'a>` is the one public value struct of the connectors' entry layer without `#[non_exhaustive]` (the three `Loaded`s, `AnimatedSvgHandles`, `AnimatedImageSources` carry it; egui's `IconKey` has private fields), so an application that builds it as `Native { resolved, accessibility }` breaks when a third input joins, which the attribute would turn into a non-event — at the cost of a constructor the struct lacks. — REJECTED: M6-34's ruling (ledger :9583, maintainer 2026-10-15) applied #[non_exhaustive] to the ten built-only structs and states '`Native` stays constructible' because it is meant to be built; the claim's evidence is also wrong, since tests/seams.rs builds `Native { .. }` 11 times and the README (:210) presents the literal shape.
- R3#7 (scripts/generate_assets_release.sh:190): The release asset run accepts a partial CI download: an artifact that is missing or holds no PNG is skipped, so the previous release's macOS or Windows screenshots stay in docs/assets and the provenance stamp then declares them captured from HEAD. — REJECTED: The skip path at :191/:201 exists, but the script downloads only from a run whose conclusion is success (:142-169). In screenshots.yml every matrix job's capture loop runs under bash -e (macOS default shell; Windows `shell: bash`), --screenshot exits non-zero on a bad capture, and fail-fast:false still makes a failed job fail the run, so a successful run carries all six artifacts with their PNGs. Only an edit that dropped a matrix leg or a theme could leave old files, which would be hardening, not the claimed partial download.
- R3#9 (scripts/update_provenance.sh:39): docs/showcase-elements.toml feeds all three showcases but is not a stamped source, so an edit to it leaves stale screenshots stamped as captured from HEAD's sources; scripts/README.md:199-200 and CONTRIBUTING.md:223 say docs-only changes need no recapture. — REJECTED: The showcases do include_str! docs/showcase-elements.toml, but only for Widget Info's titles and rows and for --dump-layout. The capture scripts and screenshots.yml hover nothing, and the captures show only the 'Hover any widget...' placeholder (e.g. gpui linux-kde-breeze-light.png), so an edit to the list does not change a pixel and the screenshots are not stale. (The header phrase 'every path that feeds the showcases' at update_provenance.sh:20 is loose, at most.)
- R4a#2 (connectors/native-theme-gpui/README.md:197): The gpui README's `from_preset` bullet, and `from_preset`'s rustdoc (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:364-366), say that the first `detect::accessibility_preferences()` call after a system read may still run the reduced-motion detection (about 3 ms). Since 107ab86d it cannot: a system read stores the reader's whole block, and the call returns it. — REJECTED: With a reader, the block is stored (pipeline.rs:1143-1145). But the Linux readerless SystemTheme (linux_fallback, pipeline.rs:1099-1104), which a gpui default build gets now that `native` is off, stores nothing, so the next accessibility_preferences() runs readerless_accessibility -> detect_reduced_motion (pipeline.rs:1250-1254). So 'may still run the reduced-motion detection' still holds there.

#### M8-01 · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-iced/src/lib.rs:1189
**Claim:** (b) defect to align, gpui/egui are right: a theme font family the system lacks (windows-11's `Segoe UI`, the macOS presets' `SF Pro`, the Inter/JetBrains Mono presets, all on Linux) is handed to iced under its stated name and drawn in cosmic-text's own fallback, while gpui and egui draw fontconfig's substitute for it, the family every native application of the system gets.
**Evidence:** `system_font_family(spec)` (lib.rs:1187-1195, feature `system-fonts`) calls `native_theme::fonts::system_face(&spec.family, spec.weight, spec.style)` and on `None` returns `spec.family.clone()`; nothing in connectors/native-theme-iced/src calls `substitute_family` or `substitute_family_cached` (grep: no hit). gpui's `font_family` (connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:706-717) falls through `substituted_family` -> `native_theme::fonts::substitute_family_cached` (:729-732); egui's `FontPlan::from_system` (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/fonts.rs:144-153) on a `system_face` miss asks `substitute_family_cached(&spec.family)` and then `system_face(&substitute, spec.weight, spec.style)`. Core's `substitute_family` doc (native-theme/src/fonts.rs:270-279) states the answer is `fc-match`'s best match, 'which is the font every native application of the system gets for that family'. CHANGELOG.md:363-365 (0.6.0) gave the substitute to core, egui and gpui in one release and :334 describes iced's `system_font_family` without it; no rationale (docs/archive, ledger M5) records why iced was left out, and the iced README (:249-251) states only the macOS `.SF NS` case. Test: with `system-fonts` on a host whose `fc-list` has no `Segoe UI`, `system_font_family(&Theme::preset("windows-11")?.resolve(ColorMode::Light)?.variant.defaults.font)` returns `"Segoe UI"` today; after the fix it returns `system_face(&substitute_family_cached("Segoe UI").unwrap(), 400, FontStyle::Normal).unwrap().family` (the match's own first family name).
**Fix proposed:** In `system_font_family`, on a `system_face` miss ask `native_theme::fonts::substitute_family_cached(&spec.family)` and `system_face(&substitute, spec.weight, spec.style)` before falling back to the stated family, as egui's `FontPlan::from_system` does; state the once-per-family `fc-match` cost in its doc and the README's `system-fonts` sentence as gpui's `font_family` and egui's `from_preset` do.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — iced lib.rs:1189-1194 falls back to the stated family on a system_face miss and nothing in iced calls substitute_family(_cached), while gpui (lib.rs:731) and egui (fonts.rs:172) ask fontconfig's substitute; no parity exception, ledger ruling or rationale records iced's omission (ledger :9303 only notes as a timing fact that iced does no substitution; docs/todo.md:3590 is the per-widget family item, a different gap).
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T7 (2fcc26fb..29531be4)
*Source:* R1#0.


#### M8-02 · api · api-break · connectors/native-theme-iced/src/icons.rs:89
**Claim:** (b) defect to align, egui is right: `custom_icon_to_image_handle(provider, icon_set, color)` and `custom_icon_to_svg_handle(provider, icon_set, color)` take neither an icon theme nor a size, so under a pinned preset whose variant states an icon theme other than the system's (adwaita's `Adwaita`, native-theme/src/presets/adwaita.toml:12, on a KDE desktop whose detection says `breeze`) a provider's freedesktop icon is loaded from the system's theme while `Spinner::new(.., loaded.icon_theme)` draws the preset's — two icon themes in one window, which `Loaded::icon_theme` (lib.rs:421-423, 'for a freedesktop icon or spinner') exists to prevent — and every system-set icon comes at its loader's default size.
**Evidence:** icons.rs:89-99 `custom_icon_to_image_handle` and :112-120 `custom_icon_to_svg_handle` call `load_custom_icon(provider, icon_set, color.map(to_rgba), None)`; core's `load_custom_icon` (native-theme/src/icons.rs:741-749) is `load_custom_icon_in(provider, set, None, color, size)`, so the icon theme is `None` (the detected system theme, `detect::system_icon_theme`) and the size `None` (freedesktop 24 px, SF Symbols 24 pt, Segoe 32 px, the `IconKey::size` doc in egui icons.rs:111-131). The M6-13 ruling (docs/todo_code-review-findings.md:9641) records only that 'iced's `custom_icon_to_svg_handle` passes `None`' for the size; docs/todo.md:1203-1216 records core's `SystemTheme::icon` lacking a size, not these helpers; no entry records the missing theme. egui's `custom_icon_to_image_source(ctx, provider, &IconKey)` (connectors/native-theme-egui/src/icons.rs:508-531) passes `key.icon_theme` and `key.size` through `load_custom_icon_in` (:530), with its doc (:106-109) naming `atlas.icon_theme(..)` as the source. The known M8 entry docs/todo.md:3605 (clamp 1.. vs 1..=512) presumes iced has a size; it has none. Test: a fixture theme `Fixture` holding `places/16/folder.svg` (as the connector's own `icon_fixture` makes one) with the child's `kdeglobals` naming another installed theme; a provider naming `folder` on `IconSet::Freedesktop` loaded with `icon_theme = Some("Fixture")` must return the fixture's bytes — impossible to express with today's signature.
**Fix proposed:** Give both helpers the loader's inputs, matching egui: `custom_icon_to_svg_handle(provider: &(impl IconProvider + ?Sized), icon_set: IconSet, icon_theme: Option<&str>, color: Option<iced_core::Color>, size: Option<u32>) -> Option<svg::Handle>` and the same for `custom_icon_to_image_handle`, each calling `load_custom_icon_in(provider, icon_set, icon_theme, color.map(to_rgba), size)`; or, with no break, `_in` siblings of that shape and the old two documented as 'the system's icon theme at the loaders' default size'. The README's spinner recipe then passes `loaded.icon_theme.as_deref()` to the custom-icon helper too.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Both helpers (icons.rs:89-99, :112-120) call load_custom_icon(.., None) = load_custom_icon_in(provider, set, None, color, None), so a freedesktop icon comes from the detected system theme at the loader default while Loaded::icon_theme (lib.rs:421-423) carries the variant's; the M7 T4 ruling (ledger :10127) only kept 'iced's and gpui's unreleased call shape' and M5's note (ledger :9194) excused the size alone ('iced does not rasterize'), not the theme; api-break touches 14 call lines in iced src/icons.rs (tests) and 3 in its README, no showcase.
**Triage:** maintainer: 2026-10-16, iced `custom_icon_to_image_handle`/`custom_icon_to_svg_handle` gain `icon_theme: Option<&str>` and `size: Option<u32>`, through core's `load_custom_icon_in` → fix.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T4 (a45a32a6..1dd5eecd)
*Source:* R1#1.

#### M8-04 · api · api-add · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:569
**Claim:** (c) design question: gpui and egui each export four one-field readers of `SystemTheme::accessibility` — `is_reduced_motion(sys)`, `is_high_contrast(sys)`, `is_reduced_transparency(sys)`, `text_scaling_factor(sys)` — and iced exports none, a sibling difference no exception records because scripts/check_connector_parity.py holds only `ResolvedTheme` one-field accessors to its rules.
**Evidence:** gpui lib.rs:568-582 (`is_reduced_motion` :569, `is_high_contrast` :575, `is_reduced_transparency` :581) and :616-619 (`text_scaling_factor`), each `sys.accessibility.<field>`; egui accessors.rs:609, :614, :619, :634, the same four bodies, with the comment at :600-604 explaining only why they take `&SystemTheme`; iced's crate root has no function taking a `&SystemTheme` (the `pub fn` list of connectors/native-theme-iced/src/lib.rs:329-1359) and its crate docs route the application to the field instead (lib.rs:120-126, 'the application forwards' `prefs.reduce_motion` to `Spinner::view`). The parity script classifies a `&SystemTheme` reader as `outside` (scripts/check_connector_parity.py:69-70) and 'Only one-field accessors are held to the two rules' (:81-82), so the absence needs no `absent` entry in scripts/connector_parity_exceptions.toml and none exists. M1-T7-06's decision (docs/todo_code-review-findings.md:1049, 'every one-field accessor takes the model field's name') would name these `accessibility_reduce_motion` etc., which is longer than the field read `sys.accessibility.reduce_motion` (or `loaded.accessibility.reduce_motion`, the `Loaded` field all three connectors carry).
**Fix proposed:** Either remove the eight (before: `pub fn is_reduced_motion(sys: &SystemTheme) -> bool` in gpui and egui; after: none, the README and crate docs naming `loaded.accessibility.reduce_motion`), the direction M1-T7-06's rule points to since each is a public field read under a name unlike the field's; or add iced's four (api-add) and record the deviation from the naming rule as a `name` exception. Either way, extend the script's sibling rule to `&SystemTheme` one-field readers (the next finding) so the choice is gated.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — gpui lib.rs:569-619 and egui accessors.rs:609-634 export the four &SystemTheme readers, iced exports none, and the parity script classes them `outside` (check_connector_parity.py:69-70, :81-82) so no exception exists; egui's spec copies gpui's names (archived egui spec :1959) but nothing records iced's absence; removal would touch one gpui test (lib.rs:1922-1925) and egui's re-export (lib.rs:165) only.
**Triage:** fix — iced gains the four `&SystemTheme` accessibility readers gpui and egui export (the additive side of the parity; removal would be a break nothing asks for).
**Status:** fixed — M8 T4 (a45a32a6..1dd5eecd)
*Source:* R1#3.


#### M8-05 · simplify · S4 · scripts/check_connector_parity.py:81
**Claim:** (b) the parity gate's sibling rule compares only `one-field` `ResolvedTheme` accessors, so a function the script classes `outside`, `group` or `inputs` can exist in one or two connectors and be absent from a sibling with no exception and no failure — which is how the four `&SystemTheme` readers (gpui+egui, not iced), the group accessors (`icon_sizes` in iced and gpui, `text_scale` in gpui alone, neither in egui, whose `icon_size(theme, IconContext)` is `inputs`) and the public composites (`layer_over` in gpui, `composite_over` in egui, none in iced) reached M8 unreported.
**Evidence:** Docstring :67-77 defines the six classes; :81-82 'Only one-field accessors are held to the two rules'; `CLASSES` :126; `outside` functions are appended with empty leaf sets (:436) and the sibling comparison runs over one-field accessors only. Concrete escapes, each verified in the sources: gpui lib.rs:569-581/:617 and egui accessors.rs:609-634 (`&SystemTheme` readers, none in iced); gpui lib.rs:627 `icon_sizes` and :635 `text_scale`, iced lib.rs:1319 `icon_sizes`, egui accessors.rs none and icons.rs:42 `icon_size(theme, IconContext)` (an enum whose five variants are `ResolvedIconSizes`' five fields); gpui lib.rs:665 `pub fn layer_over(base, layer)`, egui convert.rs:319 `pub fn composite_over(layer, idle)`, iced styles.rs:85 `pub(crate) fn composite_over(layer, base)`. The exceptions file has entries for none of them because the rules do not reach them. The script's own `--self-test` fixtures (:783 `to_weight: outside`, :815) exercise `outside` as 'skipped', so the gap is by construction, not by accident; the docstring does not say that a sibling difference among these classes is unchecked.
**Fix proposed:** Hold `group` functions and `&SystemTheme` one-field readers to the sibling rule with the existing `absent`/`unlike` exception kinds (a group accessor's name is its group path, `icon_sizes`, `text_scale`), and print the `outside`/`inputs` names per connector in a 'not compared' section so a reviewer sees them; then add the exception entries the maintainer's answers to the previous finding and the composites' names need.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The script's docstring (:67-82) holds only one-field accessors to the sibling rules, and the cited escapes exist (gpui icon_sizes :627 and text_scale :635, iced icon_sizes :1319, egui none; gpui layer_over :665, egui composite_over convert.rs:319, iced's pub(crate)); the scope is documented, not accidental, so this is a coverage extension rather than a defect.
**Triage:** fix — the parity gate also compares the `outside`, `group` and `inputs` functions across connectors, with exceptions for recorded differences.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T9 (9246c7de..2fe70354)
*Source:* R1#4.


#### M8-06 · simplify · S4 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/colors.rs:41
**Claim:** (b) for the body, (c) for the public name: straight-alpha sRGB source-over is written twice in f32 with the same formula and opposite argument orders — gpui `over(base, layer)` (public as `layer_over(base, layer)`) and iced `composite_over(layer, base)` — while egui's public `composite_over(layer, idle)` is deliberately ecolor's premultiplied `u8` blend; the toolkit-free f32 formula belongs in core once, and the two public helpers name one concept two ways with reversed parameters.
**Evidence:** gpui colors.rs:41-59: `if layer.a >= 1.0 { return layer }`, `if layer.a <= 0.0 { return base }`, then `under = b.a * (1 - l.a)`, `a = l.a + under`, `mix = (below*under + above*l.a)/a` per channel, exported at lib.rs:665 as `layer_over(base: Hsla, layer: Hsla)`. iced styles.rs:85-107: `under = base.a * (1 - layer.a)`, `alpha = layer.a + under`, `alpha <= 0 -> TRANSPARENT`, `under <= 0 -> layer`, `blend = (layered*layer.a + beneath*under)/alpha` — the same arithmetic, `pub(crate)`, layer first. egui convert.rs:306-321: `to_color32(idle).blend(to_color32(layer))`, documented as differing in rounding from iced's f32 composite (:313-315), the egui spec's choice (§6.1), so it stays. Both f32 copies exist for the same reason (C17, docs/todo.md:822-879: the platform layers where the toolkit replaces) and M1-T7-01's rule (docs/todo_code-review-findings.md:9215, the M5-04 ruling: 'toolkit-free helpers written three times move into core') was applied to the icon colouring and the font-substitute memo (M7-12) but not here. docs/todo.md:879 records that gpui exports the composite; nothing records iced's lack of a public one or the two names. The core `Rgba` type is 8-bit (native-theme/src/color.rs:43-70), so the shared function must be over `[f32; 4]` to keep iced's contract rows exact (styles.rs:91-96: 'a contract row compares exactly').
**Fix proposed:** One `native_theme::color::over_straight_alpha(layer: [f32; 4], base: [f32; 4]) -> [f32; 4]` (name the maintainer's) with gpui's early-outs and iced's zero-alpha case, called by gpui's `over` and iced's `composite_over` through their colour conversions, with iced's and gpui's unit tests moved to core; then one public name and parameter order for the two exported helpers (layer first, as iced and egui have it: `layer_over(layer, base)` or `composite_over(layer, base)` — an api-break of gpui's `layer_over(base, layer)` or egui's `composite_over` the maintainer decides), and an iced public twin so an application composites a stated hover as the connector does (docs/todo.md:879's reason for gpui's).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — gpui colors.rs:41-59 `over(base, layer)` and iced styles.rs:85-107 `composite_over(layer, base)` share the interior straight-alpha f32 formula with reversed argument order, but their early-outs differ (a zero-alpha layer: gpui returns base exactly, iced TRANSPARENT when base is also transparent and a recomputed base otherwise; a transparent base: iced returns layer exactly, gpui divides), and M1-T7-01 ruled 'composites stay per toolkit; no Rgba::over' (ledger :928) on the premise that gpui used Hsla::blend, which M6 T9 has since replaced, so the core move reopens a recorded ruling and the naming/parameter-order split is unrecorded.
**Triage:** fix — one straight-alpha source-over in core (`[f32; 4]`), the connectors convert; M1-T7-01's "composites stay per toolkit" assumed gpui still used `Hsla::blend`, which M6 T9 replaced; gpui's public `layer_over` and iced's private helper call it.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T3 (072855bc..04bac38d)
*Source:* R1#5.


#### M8-07 · simplify · S4 · connectors/native-theme-iced/src/lib.rs:543
**Claim:** (b) the padding-inside-the-border step — each stated side of `ResolvedWidgetBorder::padding` plus `line_width`, an unstated side left to the toolkit — is written in iced (`padding_inside_border`) and egui (`padding_with_border`) as the same toolkit-free arithmetic on core's types, with only the toolkit default and egui's spec-required sanitising differing; gpui needs no copy because its box model lays padding inside the border already.
**Evidence:** iced lib.rs:543-557: `side(stated, default) = match stated { Some(v) => v + border.line_width, None => default }` over the four sides, documented at :530-541 (iced paints the border inside the bounds over the padding, so a stated side reaches iced as side + width). egui convert.rs:256-271: `width = clamp_length(finite_or(line_width, 0.0))`, `side(stated) = stated.filter(finite).map(|v| (v + width).min(f32::MAX))`, returning a `ResolvedPadding` whose `None` sides 'every consumer resolves to egui's own value' (:252-253); `to_button_padding` (:293-307) and `to_margin` then supply egui's defaults. gpui geometry.rs:171-190 `with_padding` sets a stated side as `pt/pr/pb/pl` and leaves an unstated one to the widget, adding nothing. Core's `ResolvedWidgetBorder` (native-theme/src/model/border.rs:244-252) and `ResolvedPadding` (:203-212) have no method for it. Core's validation already rejects non-finite and negative lengths (the M6 T6 ruling, ledger :9664: 'core's validation rejects negative and non-finite lengths'), so on a resolved theme the two bodies agree side for side; egui's filter is its spec §7 rule for a value a `style_patch` could not reach anyway and can stay as a one-line wrapper. Test: for every preset and widget border, `padding_or(&border.padding_plus_line_width(), default)` equals today's `padding_inside_border(&border, default)` in iced, and egui's `padding_with_border(&border)` equals the core result.
**Fix proposed:** A core method `ResolvedWidgetBorder::padding_plus_line_width(&self) -> ResolvedPadding` (name the maintainer's) adding `line_width` to each stated side; iced's `padding_inside_border` becomes `padding_or(&border.padding_plus_line_width(), default)` and egui's `padding_with_border` the core call behind its finite filter, with the two unit tests (iced lib.rs:1625-1700's and egui convert.rs:506) kept where they are.
**Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE — iced lib.rs:543-557 and egui convert.rs:256-271 compute the same per-side sum on a validated theme (core rejects non-finite and negative lengths), but egui also clamps the width to LENGTH_CEILING (~1.06e37) and saturates, and M1-T7-01 already recorded this core method as optional `padding_outside()` (ledger :924, :928), so it is that open option rather than a new finding.
**Triage:** fix once confirmed — PLAUSIBLE: a core `padding_outside()` on `ResolvedWidgetBorder` (M1-T7-01 recorded it) replaces iced's and egui's sums where they agree; egui keeps its width clamp.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T3 (072855bc..04bac38d)
*Source:* R1#6.


#### M8-08 · api · api-break · connectors/native-theme-iced/src/icons.rs:216
**Claim:** (b) what docs/todo.md:3587 misses: beside `AnimatedSvgHandles::frame_duration_ms: u32`, iced's `spin_rotation_radians(elapsed, duration_ms: u32)` takes the spin period as a `u32` with a `duration_ms == 0` guard, while the model states it as `TransformAnimation::Spin { duration_ms: NonZeroU32 }` and gpui's `with_spin_animation(element, id, duration_ms: NonZeroU32)` takes the model's type, so the iced caller must `.get()` the model's value to hand it back and the function admits a period the model cannot produce.
**Evidence:** icons.rs:216-229: `pub fn spin_rotation_radians(elapsed: Duration, duration_ms: u32) -> Radians { if duration_ms == 0 { return Radians(0.0); } ... }`; its doc example :201-212 reads `TransformAnimation::Spin { duration_ms }` and passes `duration_ms.get()`. native-theme/src/model/animated.rs:123-125: `Spin { duration_ms: NonZeroU32 }`, 'guaranteed non-zero'. gpui icons.rs:1079-1083: `duration_ms: NonZeroU32`, `Duration::from_millis(u64::from(duration_ms.get()))`, no guard. egui icons.rs:676-688 `spin_angle(ctx, icon, reduced_motion)` reads the period from the `AnimatedIcon` itself through `duration_ms.get()` into `u128`. The known entry names only `AnimatedSvgHandles::frame_duration_ms` (iced icons.rs:48; gpui's `AnimatedImageSources::frame_duration_ms: NonZeroU32` at gpui icons.rs:100). Test: `spin_rotation_radians(Duration::from_millis(500), NonZeroU32::new(1000).unwrap())` is `Radians(PI)`; the zero case no longer exists to test.
**Fix proposed:** `pub fn spin_rotation_radians(elapsed: Duration, duration_ms: NonZeroU32) -> Radians`, the guard and the example's `.get()` removed, in the same commit that makes `AnimatedSvgHandles::frame_duration_ms` a `NonZeroU32` (docs/todo.md:3587); the README's spin recipe follows.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — spin_rotation_radians (icons.rs:216) takes `u32` with a zero guard while the model's Spin period is NonZeroU32 and gpui's with_spin_animation takes NonZeroU32; the archived rationale for the u32 (v0.5.1_iced-connector-API.md §17, Option C) was 'match the source type, Spin stores u32', whose premise is now NonZeroU32; callers are the doctest, the showcase (showcase-iced.rs:11708) and seven unit-test lines, and docs/todo.md:3587 names only frame_duration_ms.
**Triage:** maintainer: 2026-10-16, iced `spin_rotation_radians` takes `NonZeroU32` → fix.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T4 (a45a32a6..1dd5eecd)
*Source:* R1#7.


#### M8-09 · api · S4 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/accessors.rs:39
**Claim:** (c) what docs/todo.md:3589 misses: the three connectors export a `scaled_text_size(size: f32, prefs: &AccessibilityPreferences) -> f32` of one name and signature, and egui's returns the raw product (`+inf` or `0.0` for a finite factor that overflows or underflows it) where iced's and gpui's return the unscaled size through `AccessibilityPreferences::scaled`; the entry describes the atlas path (egui's stock size with a `Note::ValueSanitised`), not this public accessor, which keeps neither the theme's size nor egui's.
**Evidence:** egui accessors.rs:38-41 `size * prefs.text_scale_factor()`, with its doc :17-25 stating 'The product is returned as it is, even where it is not a positive normal f32' and naming the siblings' different contract; its own test :652-662 covers the non-finite-factor case only. iced lib.rs:1229-1231 and gpui lib.rs:649-651 `prefs.scaled(size)`; core lib.rs:407-414 returns `size` where the product is not normal and positive. The egui doc :26-35 then tells the application to clamp what it hands egui to `ThemeAtlas::text_size_cap`, which the sibling accessors need not, and epaint's atlas assert (M7-04, ledger :9763) is what an unclamped `+inf` `FontId` would reach. Test: `scaled_text_size(10.0, &prefs(f32::MAX))` is `10.0` in iced and gpui and `+inf` in egui today.
**Fix proposed:** When docs/todo.md:3589 is decided, decide this function with it: either egui's `scaled_text_size` goes through `prefs.scaled(size)` too (the atlas path keeps `text_size_or_stock` for the sizes it writes, as the spec prescribes) and its doc drops the 'returned as it is' clause, or the three functions get different names, since one name with two contracts is the inconsistency the parity script was written to catch.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — egui accessors.rs:38-41 returns the raw product (+inf for an overflowing finite factor) while iced lib.rs:1229 and gpui lib.rs:649 go through AccessibilityPreferences::scaled; the egui doc states the difference and docs/todo.md:3589 cites d05d64f6, the commit that made this accessor the plain product, so it is a refinement of that known entry (its wording describes only the atlas outcome) rather than a separate item; the archived egui spec (:1922-1925) promised 'same semantics as' iced's and gpui's.
**Triage:** fix — egui's `scaled_text_size` doc states it returns the plain product (`+inf` on overflow) by its spec §8.6, and why the siblings differ.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T6 (66053837..db16676e)
*Source:* R1#8.


#### M8-10 · api · api-break · connectors/native-theme-iced/src/lib.rs:457
**Claim:** (c) `SystemThemeExt` is a sealed trait in egui (spec §4.5) and an open one in iced and gpui, so a downstream crate can implement `to_iced_theme`/`to_gpui_theme` for its own types and the trait cannot later gain a method without breaking it, while egui's can.
**Evidence:** iced lib.rs:457-470 `pub trait SystemThemeExt { fn to_iced_theme(&self) -> Loaded; }` with one impl for `native_theme::SystemTheme` (:469); gpui lib.rs:514-523 the same shape, impl at :525; egui ext.rs:6-10 `mod sealed { pub trait Sealed {} impl Sealed for native_theme::SystemTheme {} }` and :305 `pub trait SystemThemeExt: sealed::Sealed`, documented 'Sealed, like the extension trait of spec §4.5' (:304). M1-T7-06 (ledger :1049) kept each `SystemThemeExt`'s return shape per toolkit but says nothing about sealing. Adding a private supertrait is a breaking change for any downstream impl (cargo-semver-checks `trait_added_supertrait`), which 0.7.0 can carry.
**Fix proposed:** Seal iced's and gpui's as egui's: a private `sealed::Sealed` implemented for `SystemTheme` as the supertrait, one sentence in each trait doc; or record in the two crates' docs that the trait is open on purpose.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — egui's SystemThemeExt is sealed (ext.rs:6-10, :305) while iced's (lib.rs:457) and gpui's (lib.rs:514) are open; the M5 iced review already noted it ('fold into T7-06's reshaping', ledger :9194) but no ruling, todo entry or exception carried it, and sealing is technically a break for a downstream impl.
**Triage:** maintainer: 2026-10-16, seal iced's and gpui's `SystemThemeExt` with a private supertrait, as egui's → fix.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T4 (a45a32a6..1dd5eecd); M8 T5 (d7146ce9..ed3e559b)
*Source:* R1#9.


#### M8-11 · simplify · S4 · connectors/native-theme-iced/src/icon_fixture.rs:31

#### M8-12 · bugs · S2 · native-theme/src/resolve/tests.rs:1921
**Claim:** 19 validation tests pass when validate() returns the wrong error variant: each matches the variant with `let crate::Error::<Variant> { .. } = result.unwrap_err() else { return; };`, so the BUG-01 regression test `validate_missing_field_short_circuits_before_range_checks` (:1911) passes if a missing field plus an out-of-range weight comes back as ResolutionInvalid again, the very bug it guards.
**Evidence:** The let-else `return` sits at resolve/tests.rs :1321-1323, :1343, :1362, :1383, :1430 (ResolutionIncomplete), :1661, :1680, :1699, :1733, :1764, :1804, :1821, :1840, :1859, :1878, :1896, :1939 (ResolutionInvalid), :1921 (ResolutionIncomplete), and tests/resolve_and_validate.rs:80-82 (UnknownPreset). Before it each test asserts only `result.is_err()`. Trace for :1911: accent_color = None and font.weight = Some(0); if validate() ran check_ranges before the missing-field short-circuit it would return Err(ResolutionInvalid{..}); `is_err()` holds, the let-else pattern ResolutionIncomplete does not match, the else block returns, and the test passes. The same holds for :1931 (`validate_range_only_errors_produce_resolution_invalid`, BUG-02) with the variants swapped, and for every range test (a range error reported as Incomplete passes). The comment at :1322 ('validate() always returns ResolutionIncomplete for missing fields') states the assumption the code should assert. A scan of every crate (let-else with a non-Option/Result pattern whose else returns) finds no other test with this shape; the connector hits return Err, which fails the test.
**Fix proposed:** Make the wrong variant fail: `let missing = match result { Err(crate::Error::ResolutionIncomplete { missing }) => missing, other => panic!("expected ResolutionIncomplete, got {other:?}") };` (ResolutionInvalid and UnknownPreset alike) in all 19 tests; the preceding `assert!(result.is_err())` then goes.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — resolve/tests.rs:1921-1923 returns early on any variant other than ResolutionIncomplete, after only checking is_err() at :1920, so a regression to ResolutionInvalid passes. The count is off by one: resolve/tests.rs has 18 such let-else-return matches (:1321 to :1939), and the 19th is tests/resolve_and_validate.rs:80 (UnknownPreset), the same shape M3-32 fixed only in presets.rs.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED.
**Status:** fixed — M8 T13 (e6031bc2..1088da03)
*Source:* R2#0.
