#### M9-131 · M9x · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:2652
**Claim:** In the iced showcase, hover a widget on any page but Basic (one that is not in the element list), then switch theme or mode without moving the pointer: from the command palette (Ctrl+K), or by an OS change under --features watch. Widget Info and its Copy button keep showing the previous theme's values. gpui and egui rebuild the shown info on the next frame.
**Evidence:** state.widget_info is a String captured in view at hover time and set only by Message::WidgetHovered from mouse_area::on_enter (hoverable :6610-6616, update :2652-2655). WidgetUnhovered keeps it (:2659-2661). install_in_mode (:2035-2068) never rebuilds or clears it, and the inspector prints it (:6147-6164). gpui replaces the hovered and shown info from each frame's rebuilt targets ('a theme switch -- reaches the inspector; hover events alone would miss it', info/registry.rs:87-104). egui marks screen_changed on install (app.rs:535) and re-chooses in end_pass (demo.rs:167-173). No known item records it.
**Fix proposed:** Keep the hovered target's identity, not its text, and rebuild the info string from state in view, as ElementInfo::of already does for listed elements (:5418). Or rebuild widget_info in install_in_mode.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — iced's Widget Info is a String built in view and stored on mouse_area on_enter (showcase-iced.rs:6610-6615, :2652-2653). install_in_mode (:2035-2065) never refreshes it, and on_enter fires only on a hover change (iced_widget-0.14.2 mouse_area.rs:342-346), so an OS change under watch leaves stale values. gpui marks screen_changed on every install (app.rs:1809, registry.rs) and egui rebuilds per frame. The palette path probably does not hold, though. The open palette is `stack![window, opaque(..)]` (:2840), which levitates the cursor for the window (stack.rs:266-273, an Idle interaction), and closing it changes the root's widget, so the next redraw fires on_enter again with the new info. (verifier: The watch path holds; drop or test the palette path. Related to docs/todo.md:2950 (iced per-instance Widget Info), which does not name the stale info.)
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED.
**Status:** open
*Source:* X#8.
**Status (M9b close, 2026-10-23):** fixed — 916522f9 (M9b T7): a page widget's hover carries its identity, so an install reaches the shown info and its Copy text.

**Claim:** The three showcases do not accept the same flags, and they exit differently. `--screenshot` on Linux keeps gpui running (exit 0 when closed, no file), makes iced write a frame-less content capture, and makes egui exit 1. `--icon-theme` exists only in gpui. `--icon-set default` works only in egui. `--tab text-inputs` works in gpui and iced but not egui, and `--tab inputs` in gpui and egui but not iced. #### M9-137 · M9x · bug · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/examples/showcase-gpui/main.rs:1501
**Claim:** On macOS or Windows, `--dump-layout F --screenshot P` without `--capture` makes gpui and iced write F and exit 0 before the screenshot is taken, so P is silently missing. egui keeps running until both are written.
**Evidence:** gpui passes `quit = !cli_args.capture` to dump_layout (main.rs:1495-1503). The dump is written after DUMP_SETTLED_READINGS 4 readings DUMP_POLL 250 ms apart (:789-794, :836-850) and then calls app::quit, about 1 s in. The capture waits 200+1300 ms on macOS and 1500 ms on Windows (:1544-1556, :1571). iced exits at LayoutScaled `if !cli.capture { return iced::exit(); }` (:2606-2608), after LAYOUT_SETTLES_AFTER 1 s (:587), while the screenshot countdown is 60 x 50 ms = 3 s (:2019). egui sets `keep_running: cli.capturing()`, which counts --screenshot (app.rs:431-435, main.rs:207-209).
**Fix proposed:** In gpui and iced, quit after the dump only when neither `--capture` nor `--screenshot` was given, as egui's `capturing()` does.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — gpui passes quit = !capture to dump_layout (main.rs:1495-1502), which writes and quits after 4 equal 250 ms readings, at about 1 s. The screenshot fires after 1.5 s (main.rs:1541-1554 macOS, :1564-1567 Windows). iced writes after LAYOUT_SETTLES_AFTER 1 s and exits unless --capture (showcase-iced.rs:587, :2602-2609), and its screenshot countdown is 3 s (:2019). egui keeps running when capturing(), which includes --screenshot (app.rs:431-435; main.rs:201-203). For iced this holds on Linux as well.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED.
**Status:** open — gpui half fixed: M9a T3 (83b9c27c, b66091f7 cli::Outputs, 275814b0 the bounded dump); iced half M9b T2; egui keeps running until both are written
*Source:* X#14.
**Status (M9b close, 2026-10-23):** fixed — 843620f3 (M9b T2): `--dump-layout F --screenshot P` without `--capture` writes both before it exits; with M9a's gpui half the entry is whole (egui already waited for both).

#### M9-138 · M9x · perf · S3 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/examples/showcase-gpui/app.rs:1859
**Claim:** A colour-mode switch under the `default` theme (the Mode picker, Theme > Light/Dark, the palette) re-reads the whole OS theme in gpui and iced, and reloads every icon from its source. egui does nothing but egui's own set_theme. The rebuild cost on a mode switch is uneven, and egui is the cheap one.
**Evidence:** gpui: set_color_mode (app.rs:1859-1863) calls install_in_mode (:1867-1879), which calls apply_theme_by_name (:1803-1838): SystemTheme::from_system() for `default` (:1813), then reload_icons always (:1834-1836; load_all_icons and load_gpui_icons, :942-967). iced: ColorModeSelected (:2648-2651) calls install_in_mode (:2035-2068), which calls load_theme. load_theme calls read_system_theme for OsTheme (:2081-2096) although SystemTheme holds both variants (`system.pick(mode)`, :2088), then reload_icons (:2139-2170: icons, chrome icons, animation caches, Spinner). egui: set_mode (app.rs:545-551) only calls ctx.set_theme, because the atlas holds both schemes. Measured costs (ledger Baseline Timings): from_system warm 3.6–9.7 ms; a freedesktop icon reload warm 1.8–2.9 ms, cold about 40 ms. For presets, gpui's first from_preset per preset is the slowest step at 31–106 ms, already known (M6 Step 1 timings).
**Fix proposed:** In gpui and iced, keep the SystemTheme read at install and re-pick its variant on a mode switch. Re-read only on Reload System Theme and watcher events. Reload icons only when the effective set or theme changed, and otherwise recolour the loaded ones.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — gpui's set_color_mode goes to install_in_mode, then apply_theme_by_name, which under `default` calls SystemTheme::from_system() and reload_icons (app.rs:1810-1833, :1859-1880, :942-967). iced's install_in_mode calls load_theme, whose OsTheme branch re-runs read_system_theme, then reload_icons (showcase-iced.rs:2035-2065, :2086-2099). egui's set_mode is only ctx.set_theme (app.rs:546-551), since the atlas holds both variants.
**Triage:** fix — the per-frame/per-switch work moves to once per install; a before/after count or timing in the test.
**Status:** open — gpui half fixed: M9a T10 (00ca6bfb..210c7269); iced half M9b T6 (the OS read) and T13 (the icon reload)
*Source:* X#15.
**Status (M9b close, 2026-10-23):** fixed — fb0d3ef5 (M9b T6: the OS read kept, not re-read on a mode switch) and f374fbd7 (M9b T13: the comment states why every install reloads the icons, a colour-mode switch needing the mode's own); with M9a's gpui half the entry is whole.

#### M9-139 · M9x · perf · S3 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:5211
**Claim:** While Widget Info shows a listed element, iced converts the whole ResolvedTheme to a toml::Value on every view call. gpui converts it to a serde_json::Value on every Widget-tab render, even when nothing listed is shown. egui serialises once per install and caches it. Unmeasured, but traced on a per-frame path.
**Evidence:** iced element_info_view (:5406, from :6141) calls ElementInfo::of (:5418), which does `toml::Value::try_from(&state.current_resolved)` (:5211-5212). view runs after every update, including the 50 ms AnimationTick while the Basic spinner animates (:12752). gpui widget_tab (inspector.rs:107-111) builds PanelLook::of before testing `listed`, and PanelLook::of does `serde_json::to_value(r)` (:461). egui's JsonCache keeps one Value per scheme (info.rs:239-245), reset only in apply (app.rs:533).
**Fix proposed:** Cache the serialised theme per install, as egui's JsonCache does: in iced next to current_resolved (rebuilt in install_in_mode), in gpui in the Showcase (rebuilt where the theme is installed). Build PanelLook only for a listed element.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — iced's ElementInfo::of runs toml::Value::try_from(&state.current_resolved) (showcase-iced.rs:5214-5215) from element_info_view in view (:5418). gpui's widget_tab builds PanelLook::of on every render (inspector.rs:111), and that runs serde_json::to_value(r) (:461) before the listed check, so it runs for the hint and unlisted info too. egui caches theme_json per scheme in JsonCache's OnceCells (info.rs:243-259).
**Triage:** fix — the per-frame/per-switch work moves to once per install; a before/after count or timing in the test.
**Status:** open
*Source:* X#16.
**Status (M9b close, 2026-10-23):** fixed — bd474004 (M9b T15): the serialised theme is built once per install.

#### M9-140 · M9x · ux · S4 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:1040
**Claim:** Only the ends of the three page lists correspond: Basic and Buttons first, Icons and Theme Map last. In between, pages with the same content have different names and a different order, and nothing records how the pages correspond. The `--tab` keys differ with them.
**Evidence:** gpui main.rs:116-128: Basic, Buttons, Inputs, Data, Feedback, Typography, Layout, Overlays, Charts, Icons, Theme Map. iced :1040-1053: Basic, Buttons, Text Inputs, Selection, Range, Display, Layout, Graphics, [Extra], Icons, Theme Map. egui app.rs:30-43: Basic, Buttons, Selection, Inputs, Range, Text, Colour, Containers, Data, Overlays, Icons, Theme Map. iced and egui order Selection and Inputs oppositely. gpui puts Data before its text page and Overlays after Layout; egui puts Data after Containers. The inputs page is 'Text Inputs'/`text-inputs` in iced and 'Inputs'/`inputs` in the others. Recorded reasons: per-toolkit page sets follow each toolkit's widget catalogue (M1-T8-01); egui's set is in its spec's palette table (docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md §10.4). Nothing records the order or the naming of corresponding pages, in docs/showcase-elements.toml or elsewhere.
**Fix proposed:** Record one counterpart order in docs/showcase-elements.toml's header (Basic, Buttons, Inputs, Selection, Range, Text, Data, Layout/Containers, Overlays, Graphics/Charts, toolkit-only pages, Icons, Theme Map) and order the three lists by it. Give corresponding pages one label and key (iced's 'Text Inputs' becomes 'Inputs'/`inputs`).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The page lists are gpui main.rs:170-183 (Basic, Buttons, Inputs, Data, Feedback, Typography, Layout, Overlays, Charts, Icons, Theme Map), iced showcase-iced.rs:1040-1052 (Basic, Buttons, TextInputs, Selection, Range, Display, Layout, Graphics, [Extra], Icons, ThemeMap) and egui app.rs:30-58 (Basic, Buttons, Selection, Inputs, Range, Text, Colour, Containers, Data, Overlays, Icons, Theme Map). docs/showcase-elements.toml:165 covers shared elements only. The egui spec's page table (archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md:7235ff) lists egui's own pages, not how they correspond.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED.
**Status:** open
*Source:* X#17.
**Status (M9b close, 2026-10-23):** fixed — 91423451 (M9b T19) and 1d57e42d (the key): the three showcases list their pages in gpui's order, recorded in `docs/showcase-elements.toml`'s header; iced's "Text Inputs" is "Inputs".

#### M9-141 · M9x · ux · S4 · .github/workflows/screenshots.yml:55
**Claim:** The release captures build the three showcases with three feature rules: gpui with its defaults, iced with defaults plus iced_aw, egui with --all-features. egui's release screenshots therefore come from a build that differs from the one its README tells users to run. It adds svg-rasterize, which egui does not enable by default, and the connector's watch feature, which starts the OS watcher during Linux `--capture` runs; gpui and iced run no watcher there.
**Evidence:** screenshots.yml:37/:46 (iced `--features iced_aw`), :41/:50 (gpui ""), :55/:59 (egui `--all-features`). The same split is in generate_screenshots_iced.sh:47, generate_screenshots_gpui.sh:51 and generate_screenshots_egui.sh:51. egui defaults are material, lucide, system icons and system fonts (Cargo.toml:29), without svg-rasterize (:33) or watch (:40). The egui README's run line has no features (README.md:443; root README.md:54). egui starts its watcher unless --screenshot (app.rs:474-477), so `--capture` with watch runs it. M8-40 (T12) merges the scripts' loops and lists the feature difference as a fact; it does not unify the features.
**Fix proposed:** Build each capture with the features its README's showcase command names (defaults, plus iced_aw for iced as its README already says), in the workflow and the shared capture function T12 introduces. Alternatively, state the egui feature set in the egui README's showcase section.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — screenshots.yml builds gpui with no features (:38-41, :47-50), iced with --features iced_aw (:33-37, :42-46) and egui with --all-features (:51-59). The egui README runs a plain `cargo run` (README.md:443), and egui's default leaves out svg-rasterize and watch (Cargo.toml:29). With watch on, the watcher starts unless --screenshot is given (app.rs:474-477), so it runs in the Linux spectacle --capture runs (scripts/generate_screenshots_egui.sh:12-18, :51). The --all-features choice itself is recorded in archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md:7496-7502, to build its cfg-gated sections. Not recorded: the README difference and the watcher in captures. (verifier: Partly a recorded decision. Weigh the README mismatch and the watcher in captures, not the --all-features choice itself.)
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED.
**Status:** open
*Source:* X#18.
**Status (M9c close, 2026-10-24):** fixed — 9a862594 (M9c T17): the egui README's Showcase section says that the release screenshots and `scripts/generate_screenshots_egui.sh` build with `--all-features`, which adds `svg-rasterize`, `native` and `watch` over the defaults, and that a captured or dumped window does not follow the OS theme, by `CliArgs::follows_os` (fc2fa811, M8 T12; the crate's since c3abfa8f); the `--all-features` build stands, as the Step 6 ruling decided.

#### M9-144 · M9b · info-truth · S4 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:6177
**Claim:** Hovering the open Theme menu, Widget Info's "Not themeable" section says "shadows: iced_aw's own" under every theme, while `menu_bar_style` draws no menu shadow where `popover.border.shadow_enabled` is false.
**Evidence:** `iced_not_themeable`'s "Menu" arm is unconditional (:6172-6178 at 6a8f5986). `menu_bar_style` keeps iced_aw's `menu_shadow` only where `popover.border.shadow_enabled` is true, and `iced::Shadow::default()` otherwise (:4622-4636). Every bundled preset resolves the flag to true through `defaults.border.shadow_enabled`, so only an OS or user theme that states false shows the false line.

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the M9b T5 review (Minor 1); `iced_not_themeable` already takes the state since T5.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED.
**Status:** fixed — 89dd2ea4 (M9b T5 fix round 1; `the_menus_panel_lines_name_what_pads_and_shadows_it`).
*Source:* m9b-T5-review.md, Minor 1.

#### M9-145 · M9b · info-truth · S4 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:5339
**Claim:** Widget Info routes each listed tab as if it were in the state the element list names. Basic's tab One is always the open one, Two always closed, the page tab Basic open and Buttons closed. After a click opens the other tab, or on another page, the lines claim the open tab's fill, frame and line on the closed tab, and the closed tab's colours on the open one. Under macos-tahoe, which states no `tab.hover_background`, the line "tab_style: a tab's background under the pointer" names a leaf that is not drawn.
**Evidence:**
- In the iced_aw build, `drawing` fixes `basic.tabs.one` to the open tab's statuses and `.two` to a closed tab's (:5339-5350 at 6a8f5986), although `basic_tab` chooses the open one. iced_aw asks `Active` of the open tab and `Disabled` of another (iced_aw 0.14.1 `src/widget/tab_bar.rs:589-595`).
- The hand routes (:5922-5940) do not depend on which tab is open, and neither does `drawing`'s `tab.active_indicator_color` arm (:5354). Meanwhile `tab_style(resolved, open)`, `tab_indicator` and `styles::aw::tab_bar` (frame width 0 except on `Active`) draw by it.
- `tab_style` takes `tab.hover_background.unwrap_or(tab.background_color)`, and macos-tahoe's `[light.tab]` and `[dark.tab]` state no `hover_background`.
**Fix proposed:** Route a tab by which one is open in the state shown: `basic_tab`, the page shown and the inspector tab. A closed tab is neither framed nor marked. Where `tab_style` draws it, a tab has its own state's colours. iced_aw's statuses come from `basic_tab`. An unstated `tab.hover_background` reads not drawn.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the M9b T5 review (Minor 6 (b), the iced_aw half). The default build's tabs, the page tabs and the inspector's are the same class, and the T5 fix round's table test found macos-tahoe's hover fill.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED.
**Status:** fixed — 89dd2ea4 (M9b T5 fix round 1; `a_route_names_a_widget_only_where_the_state_draws_it`, tabs held to `tab_style` by splicing, iced_aw's statuses to `basic_tab`).
*Source:* m9b-T5-review.md, Minor 6 (b).

**Claim:** The iced connector says the focus ring is drawn where it is inset, "`defaults.focus_ring_offset` minus its width". That is unclear about the condition, and it says nothing of a ring inset with a gap, which is not drawn. The condition is `focus_ring_offset == -focus_ring_width`.

#### M9-142 · M9b · theme-data · S2 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:4536
**Claim:** The iced side panel ignores `sidebar.border.padding`. Under adwaita, windows-11 and material-3, which state it since M9a T17, the panel itself is not padded and its theme settings and inspector content are padded by `layout.container_margin`, where the gpui and egui side panels pad the whole panel by the stated sides and leave its content unpadded.
**Evidence:** At `fa90c6c0` (the parent of the fix) no line of `showcase-iced.rs` reads `sidebar.border`. `side_panel` (:4536) pads the settings by `gap.container` (:4597-4598) and the inspector's content by the same (:4613), and its doc says so ("padded by `layout.container_margin`", :4527-4528). gpui reads the stated sides through `sidebar_padding` and `side_panel_content_margin` (`showcase-gpui/demo.rs:1545`, `:1556`), egui through its `side_panel` (`showcase-egui/chrome.rs:757-759`). The three presets state `[light.sidebar.border]` and `[dark.sidebar.border]` paddings (adwaita.toml:311, :743; windows-11.toml:411, :1008; material-3.toml:360, :879), the only bundled presets with a `sidebar.border` section.
**Fix proposed:** Pad the whole side panel where `sidebar.border.padding` states any side, each unstated side by `layout.container_margin` (none where that is unstated), with no line width, and then pad the settings, the inspector's tab row and its content by nothing, as gpui and egui do; where no side is stated, keep `container_margin` on those three.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the M8 T16 review (the amendment of 2026-10-17, 7767fbbe: "iced's side panel reads `sidebar.border.padding` as gpui's and egui's do"); the id is the one m9b-rulings.md's Addendum A (S9) reserved.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (M9b T8).
**Status:** fixed — 127d2ed5 (M9b T8; `the_side_panel_is_padded_as_gpuis`, over every bundled preset in both modes and kde-breeze with a spliced partial padding).
*Source:* M8 T16's review amendment (7767fbbe); m9b-rulings.md, Addendum A, S9.

#### M9-143 · M9b · theme-data · S2 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:12872
**Claim:** The `iced_aw` Extra-page Card pads its head, body and foot by `card.border.padding` without `card.border.line_width`, so where a preset states both its text sits a line width closer to the border than the Basic and Display cards', which pad inside the border.
**Evidence:** At `b73dd1c6` (the parent of the fix) the Card takes `Card::padding(stated_padding(&card_t.border.padding))` where every side is stated (:12872), which sets the three sections alike (iced_aw 0.14.1 `src/widget/card.rs:216-221`). The Card paints its border over its whole bounds and lays its sections inside them with no inset (`:604-633`). The Basic and Display cards pad by `padding_inside_border(&card.border, Padding::ZERO)` (:11374, f6d73eb7, M8 T16). Under kde-breeze, the head's title is 7 px from the card's left and top and the body's caption 7 px from its left, where padding and line width give 8 (M9b T10's red run).
**Fix proposed:** Where `card.border.padding` states every side, pad each section by the stated sides, a side that meets the card's edge (the head's top, every section's left and right, the foot's bottom) adding `card.border.line_width`, a side between two sections the stated side alone; where any side is unstated, keep iced_aw's own padding, which it keeps private (`card.rs:21`).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the M8 T16 review (the amendment of 2026-10-17, 7767fbbe: "the iced_aw Extra-page Card pads inside its border as the Basic and Display cards do"); the id is the one m9b-rulings.md's Addendum A (S9) reserved.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (M9b T10).
**Status:** fixed — 0b9bb16b (M9b T10; `aw_card_padding`, gated by `the_extra_card_pads_inside_its_border` under kde-breeze and adwaita).
*Source:* M8 T16's review amendment (7767fbbe); m9b-rulings.md, Addendum A, S9.

#### M9-149 · G3 · bug · S4 · native-theme/src/pipeline.rs:1043
**Claim:** native-theme built without its Linux readers (no `kde`, no `portal`: the features the gpui connector enables by default) warns `unused variable: reader` at the MSRV, and no gate denies it.
**Evidence:** `cargo +1.95.0 check -p native-theme-gpui --locked` at `0b9bb16b` warns at `pipeline.rs:1043`: `linux_reader` binds `reader` to a `match` over `LinuxReader`, which has no variant in that build, so the code after it is unreachable (an `allow(unreachable_code)` kept that quiet) and the binding unused. Stable (1.99.1) does not warn, so `scripts/check_features.sh`, which builds every feature combination on stable, cannot see it; CI's MSRV job checks that configuration at 1.95.0 without `-Dwarnings`. Seen in G3 Task 1's MSRV log (the Task 1 fix round's re-review).
**Fix proposed:** Give the build without a reader a `linux_reader` of its own, the empty `match` alone, and deny warnings in the MSRV job's three gpui connector checks.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the G3 Task 1 fix round's re-review; reproduced at `0b9bb16b`.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (G3 Task 3b, the controller's carry).
**Status:** fixed — the commit that files this entry (G3 T3b): `linux_reader` is two functions by `cfg`; the MSRV job's gpui step runs its three checks with `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings`, which fails on the old code (`error: unused variable: reader`) and passes on the new. G3 T3b fix round 1: `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings` is the whole MSRV job's, and the job also checks native-theme without its readers (its default features) at its own MSRV, 1.88.0; every check in it passes so.
*Source:* g3/g3-T1-rereview.md; g3/g3-T3b-carry.md.

#### M9-150 · M9b · theme-data · S2 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:9156
**Claim:** Above an OS text scale of 1 the iced showcase's Basic list keeps a stated `list.row_height` and the window's menu rows a stated `menu.row_height`, so the scaled label and its padding run past the row, where gpui's list and menu rows grow.
**Evidence:** at `c6db5a7a` the Basic list's rows are `Length::Fixed(list_t.row_height.unwrap_or(..))` (`showcase-iced.rs:9156`, `:9166`) and a menu row is `entry.height(Length::Fixed(h))` for `menu.row_height` (`:4366-4369`); gpui's `geometry::list_item` and `geometry::menu_item` (`connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/geometry.rs:427`, `:406`) take `with_height_rule` (`:204-213`): the stated height at a factor of 1 or less, a minimum with an automatic height above it. Under macos-monterey at 1.5 a list row stays 24 px and a menu row 22, where their text and padding need 39 and 37.
**Fix proposed:** Grow both above a factor of 1 through the shared crate's `rows::scaled_height`, the rule M9b T11 gave the tables, with each row's own padding and no rule.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the M9b T11 review (`m9b-T11-review.md`, the ⚠️ on the controller's question 2).
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (M9b T11 fix round 1, the controller's ruling).
**Status:** fixed — the commit that files this entry (M9b T11 fix round 1): the Basic list's rows and the window's menu rows take `rows::scaled_height(stated, prefs, font size, defaults.line_height, padding, 0)`; `stated_list_and_menu_rows_hold_their_text_at_every_text_scale` fails on the old code (macos-tahoe and macos-monterey list rows 24 tall, want 41 and 39; macos-monterey's menu row 22, want 37) and passes on the new. The Extra page's `iced_aw` menu rows and `SelectionList` are not changed.
*Source:* m9b-T11-review.md; m9b-T11-fix1-brief.md.
**Status (M9b T12, 2026-10-22):** the Extra page's `iced_aw` menu rows are covered (77484992): a row of a stated `menu.row_height` grows above a text scale of 1 through `rows::scaled_height`, and the menus' titles, rows and context entries draw at `defaults.line_height`, where they took iced's 1.3; `the_extra_menus_hold_their_text_at_every_text_scale` fails on the old code (macos-monterey's row 22 tall at 1.5, want 37; each title and context entry at iced's line height) and passes on the new. The `SelectionList` is not changed.

**Evidence:** at `2e7dffcd` the table's header and body cells are containers padded by `LAYOUT_CELL_PAD` (`showcase-iced.rs:12529-12534`, built of `SP.xs` and `SP.s`), and `layout_header_height` adds its `y()` to a stated `list.header_height`; the Basic table pads its cells by `padding_or(&l.border.padding, ..)` (`fn basic_table`). Under kde-breeze (`list.border.padding` 2 px across, 1 above and below) the first header cell is 176 px wide where its 160 px text and the list's padding make 164.
**Fix proposed:** Pad each cell by `list.border.padding`, `LAYOUT_CELL_PAD` named as the showcase's own on a side the theme leaves unstated, the header height holding that padding, and print the padding's values in the Table info.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the M9b final review (`m9b-final-review.md`, Important 3, which the T11 review's Minor 3 had named).

**Status:** fixed — the commit that files this entry (M9b final fix): `layout_cell_padding` is `padding_or(&list.border.padding, LAYOUT_CELL_PAD)`, the cells, the column widths and `layout_header_height` take it, and the Table info prints it; `the_layout_table_pads_its_cells_by_the_lists_padding`, over every bundled preset in both modes, fails on the old code (kde-breeze: the first header cell 176 px wide, want 164) and passes on the new. The table draws no `list.border` line round its cells, only iced's separators, so no line width is added (the Basic table's cells likewise take the padding alone, its frame the line).
*Source:* m9b-final-review.md; m9b-final-fix-brief.md.

The connector's button styles set colours, borders and shadows only, so nothing else applies the minimum; `button_content_min_size` (`src/lib.rs:766-773`) and `at_least` (`:1198-1217`) are the connector's per-call helpers. The gpui showcase's Buttons page sends every button but its size row (`demo::sized_button`, `showcase-gpui/demo.rs:3165-3188`) through `geometry::button`, where `button.min_width` arrives (`native-theme-gpui/src/geometry.rs:220-227`). `button_info` lists `("min-height", "hardcoded by iced")` under Not themeable (`:11364`). **Claim:** The iced showcase's Basic expander headers take a stated `expander.header_height` as a floor, so at a text scale of 1 or less a title and padding taller than the stated height grow the header, above 1 the title's line box is not rounded up, and the title wraps; the one rule every stated row height takes (M9-150) gives the stated height verbatim at 1 or less, the title on one line, and above 1 at least the line box at `defaults.line_height`, rounded up, and the padding. #### M9-157 · M9c · theme-data · S2 · connectors/native-theme-egui/src/fonts.rs:1
**Claim:** The egui connector draws every theme font but `defaults.mono_font` in the face of the light variant's `defaults.font`, so a widget font that states a family of its own is drawn in the body's family. The KDE and Windows readers state such fonts from the desktop's own settings. A user whose menu or toolbar font is another family sees it in egui's menus and toolbars in the body's family, where gpui and iced draw the stated one.
**Evidence:** at `7efe6294`:
- The font plan registers at most two faces, `defaults.font` at the head of `FontFamily::Proportional` and `defaults.mono_font` at the head of `Monospace`, from the light variant (`connectors/native-theme-egui/src/fonts.rs:1-4`; `FontPlan::from_system`, `:165-201`; `ext.rs:274`). Every `FontId` the connector installs or hands out names one of those two families (`style/roles.rs:66`, `:1327`, `:1553`, `:2243`, `:2338`; `accessors.rs:269`, `:504`).
- The 19 per-widget `*.font.family` leaves are UNMAPPABLE `egui-limited` (`mapping.toml`, e.g. `menu.font.family`: "a TextStyle key naming a FontFamily::Name (declined, §5.8 item 7)").
- Readers that state them: KDE's `populate_fonts` sets `menu.font` from `menuFont` and `toolbar.font` from `toolBarFont` (`native-theme/src/kde/fonts.rs:190-201`). Windows sets `window.title_bar_font`, `menu.font`, `tooltip.font` and `status_bar.font` from `NONCLIENTMETRICS` (`native-theme/src/windows.rs:530-535`).
- A route would emit a `FontFamily::Name` per stated family. The archived spec forbids that as structural, not stylistic (`docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md` §8.1, "The never-`Name` invariant"). A `Name` in a `Style` that the loaded `FontDefinitions` does not bind panics at the first text that names it, in release too (`epaint/src/text/fonts.rs:1021-1033`, `FontsImpl::font`). `Context::set_style_of` takes effect at once (`egui/src/context.rs:2250`), while `set_fonts` waits for the next pass (`:2106`). So an install, an application's own `set_fonts`, or a dropped face could leave a style naming an unbound family.
- The spec records the loss as an upstream limit (§14 item 8, "A typeface by name only for the two default fonts", which needs "a `FontId` that can name a family without a registered `Name` key").
- Found by the M9c T10 review (Important 1): the showcase's Widget Info named such a font's own family as drawn. M9c T10 fix round 1 makes the showcase name the face drawn instead (`demo::DrawnFamilies::drawn_at`, the shared crate's `status::DrawnFamily::OtherFont`).
**Fix proposed:** None in the connector while the invariant stands. Taking it means an epaint hook or a `FontId` that names a family with no registered key (the spec's §14 item 8). A connector route through `FontFamily::Name` would need an ordering guarantee across `set_style_of` and `set_fonts` that egui does not give, and a face per stated (family, weight, style).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by M9c T10 fix round 1 at `7efe6294`: the never-`Name` invariant and the readers' per-widget fonts, as cited.
**Triage:** known — the archived spec's §14 item 8 carries it as an upstream limit. The egui showcase states the face drawn (M9c T10 fix round 1).
**Status:** open (upstream).
*Source:* m9c-T10-review.md, Important 1.
**Correction (M9c T10 round 2, 2026-10-24):** the triage "known" names no docs/todo.md entry that carries the item, as the file's "known" entries do, and "open (upstream)" is no status form of the file. docs/todo.md now carries it: *native-theme-egui connector*, "A widget font's own family is drawn in the body's face", `[upstream]`. The triage reads "defer — docs/todo.md, that entry (the spec's §14 item 8 limit)", and the status reads "open".

#### M9-158 · M9c · ux · S2 · connectors/native-theme-iced/examples/showcase-iced.rs:10947
**Claim:** On every preset whose list frame is rounded inside its line (adwaita, macos-tahoe, kde-breeze and windows-11 among them), the iced showcase's Basic table header fill and its selected last row, and the Basic list's selected or hovered rows where they meet the frame, are square rectangles drawn over the frame's corner arcs and past them. This is the iced counterpart of M9-110.
**Evidence:** at `496009e8`:
- The table's header container (`showcase-iced.rs:10947-10950`) and its row containers (`:10972-10975`) set a background and iced's default `Border`, radius 0. The frame container is rounded by `list.border.corner_radius` (`:10979-10983`) and padded by `list.border.line_width` (`:10987`), so the fills start at the line's inner edge.
- The list's rows are buttons in `list_row` (`:4729-4753`, the default border, radius 0), in a scrollable in a container padded by the line's width (`:10553-10559`) and framed by `list_frame` (`:4758-4771`).
- iced draws a container's content after its own quad (iced_widget 0.14.2 `src/container.rs:351-370`). Nothing clips a child to a rounded shape: a container's clip is its rectangle (`:365-366`), the scrollable's layer is its shown rectangle (`src/scrollable.rs:1152`, `:1187`), and iced_graphics 0.14.0 keeps a layer's clip as given (`src/layer.rs:85-98`).
- The line's inner edge is rounded by the radius less the width about the arcs' centres (iced_wgpu 0.14.0 `src/shader/quad/solid.wgsl:78-83`; iced_tiny_skia 0.14.1 `src/engine.rs:204-234`). A square corner at the inside lies (r − w)·√2 from that centre, past the outer arc where that exceeds r: adwaita (9, 1) 11.3, kde-breeze (5, 1) 5.7.
- Found by M9c T9's report, concern 1 (`m9c-T9-report.md`).
**Fix proposed:** Round the header's top corners and the selected last row's bottom corners by the frame's inner radius, `(list.border.corner_radius − list.border.line_width).max(0.0)`, through the containers' `border.radius`. Paint a list row's fill on the part of the row the list shows, rounded where that meets the frame's inside, as egui's T9 does: a row's button paints no fill, and a draw hook under it paints `list_row`'s.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by M9c T9b at `496009e8`, as cited. The test below reproduces it: with the rounding held at 0, the table's header is `Radius { 0, 0, 0, 0 }` where adwaita wants `{ 8, 8, 0, 0 }`, and the list's first row is square where adwaita wants its top corners at 8.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (M9c T9b, added by the controller).
**Status:** fixed — the commit that files this entry (M9c T9b):
- `table_row_style`, which `basic_table` styles its rows with, rounds the header's top corners and the last row's bottom corners by `inner_radius`.
- The list's rows are `Underlay`s. The scrollable's `Underlay` records its bounds and shown part (`ListView`), and each row's paints `list_row`'s background (`list_row_fill`) on the shown part of the row (`shown_fill`), rounded at a corner where that meets the frame's inside. The button's own style keeps `list_row`'s text colours and drops its background.
- An edge meets the frame's within half a pixel: the scrollable rounds its translation to whole pixels (iced_widget 0.14.2 `src/scrollable.rs:1876-1903`). Scrolled to the end, adwaita's last row ends 0.27 px short of the frame's inside and kde-breeze's 0.33. At rest iced lays the rows out unrounded from the inside, a 0.5 px line's included.
- `the_basic_list_and_table_fills_keep_inside_the_frames_corners`, under adwaita, kde-breeze and macos-tahoe light, checks the table's container radii and the list's drawn fills: at rest, half a row down and at the end. It fails with the rounding held at 0 (on all three presets, the header, the selected last row and every list case but the square middle row) and with an exact edge match (adwaita's and kde-breeze's end cases), and passes on the new code.
*Source:* m9c-T9-report.md, concern 1; m9c-T9b-brief.md.
**Status (M9c T9b round 1, 2026-10-24):** the Basic list's scrollbar keeps inside the frame's rounded inside too, at the controller's ruling on the review's Minor 3 (`m9c-T9b-review.md`, Check 4: iced lays the rail flush with the inside, the list's full height, rounded 2, so on 13 of 17 presets it painted `scrollbar.track_color` over the line's arc at the right-hand corners, and the scroller crossed the outer edge at rest on adwaita, material-3 and ios-13):
- `list_bar` gives `styles::scrollbar` an iced margin, `list_bar_margin`: a floating bar is held the inner radius off the frame's right-hand edge, clear of the corners the rows round into, so their rounded right-hand corners show beside it (adwaita 8, ios-13 9.5); a bar beside the rows only as far as the inner radius is more than half its wider part (material-3 5, every other bundled preset 0). The stated widths are kept.
- `list_bar_style` rounds the rail's and the scroller's right-hand corners by the inner radius less their inset, at most half their width, so each touches the inside's arcs from within (kde-breeze's rail 4, the radius-8 presets' rail 7 and thumb 4); iced's own 2 where that is more.

#### M9-159 · M9c · ux · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/examples/showcase-gpui/demo.rs:8817
**Claim:** On gpui-pre, on every preset whose list frame is rounded inside its line (adwaita, macos-tahoe, kde-breeze and windows-11 among them), the gpui showcase's Basic table header fill and its last row's, and a List row's selected or hovered fill where it meets the frame, are square rectangles drawn past the frame's corner arcs. This is the gpui counterpart of M9-110 (egui) and M9-158 (iced).
**Evidence:** at `bcbd1365`:
- `demo::files_table` fills the header and each body row with a plain `.bg(..)` and no radius (`demo.rs:8872-8879`); the frame is rounded by `list.border.corner_radius` and `overflow_hidden` (`:8946-8951`).
- A List row is a `ListItem` refined by `geometry::list_item`, which sets no radius (`native-theme-gpui/src/geometry.rs:427-431`); gpui-component paints its selected fill (`list_active`) and its hover fill (`list_hover`) on the row's own root (gpui-component 0.8.0 `src/list/list_item.rs:227-233`, `:257-264`), inside `geometry::list`'s rounded, clipping box (`geometry.rs`, `pub fn list`).
- gpui-pre clips the children of a rounded box to its rectangle: its content mask is bounds only (gpui-pre 0.3.9 `src/window.rs:2226-2234`, "only rectangular content masks are supported"). GPUI Fast clips them to the box's curved padding edge (gpui-fast 0.1.10 `src/fast/rounded_clip.rs:68-104`), so there the fills already follow the curve (docs/todo.md, *File the gpui-kit issue: gpui-pre clips a rounded box's children to a rectangle*).
- The routes M9c T14 wrote (`info/leaves.rs`, a60d4541) said so: "not applied — the header's fill is square". The connector's doc on `geometry::list` said the clip keeps a square fill from showing through the corners, true on GPUI Fast and false on gpui-pre; `demo_frame`'s doc (`support.rs`) and the connector README's `list` row said the same.
- Found by M9c T14's report, concern 2 (`m9c-T14-report.md`), and the M9c final review part 2a, I1.
**Fix proposed:** Round the header's top corners and the last row's bottom corners by the frame's inner radius, `(list.border.corner_radius − list.border.line_width).max(0.0)`, and a List's first row's top corners and its last row's bottom corners, as egui and iced do; the fills are then the same on both cores. Word the routes and the core-dependent docs true for each core.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by M9c B1 at `bcbd1365`: the test below finds the three fills' quads with all four radii 0.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (M9c B1 item 11, added by the controller's rulings of 2026-10-24).
**Status:** fixed — the commit that files this entry (M9c B1 item 11):
- `files_table` rounds the header's top corners and the last row's bottom corners by the inner radius (`rounded_tl`/`tr`, `rounded_bl`/`br`); the hover fill takes the row's radii.
- `ListRow::at_edges` marks the List's first and last rows, which `SampleListDelegate` sets; their fills take the inner radius on the top and the bottom corners. The List does not tell a row where its view is scrolled to, so a row cut by the view's edge mid-scroll keeps square corners on gpui-pre (egui and iced round the shown part of such a row); at rest and scrolled to either end the rows that meet the frame are rounded.
- The five routes name the inner radius; `geometry::list`'s doc, `demo_frame`'s and the connector README's `list` row say what each core's clip does.
- `the_row_fills_are_rounded_where_they_meet_the_frame`, under adwaita on either core, reads the painted quads: it fails at `bcbd1365` (header, last table row and the hovered first List row all `[0, 0, 0, 0]`, where adwaita wants 8 on the corners that meet the frame) and passes on the new code; `the_row_fill_corner_routes_say_the_fills_are_rounded` replaces T14's square-fill route test.
*Source:* m9c-T14-report.md, concern 2; m9c-final-review-part2a.md, I1.
**Status (M9c B1 fix round 1, 2026-10-24):** fixed, unchanged — the B1 review's follow-ups: e99191d3 (m6) makes the inner radius one helper, `demo::list_inner_radius`, which both fills and the test read; d3624407 (m10) names both cores' clips in `files_table`'s comment; 4f72a45d (m8) says in `geometry::list`'s doc and the connector README's `list` row that the application rounds the fill and `geometry::list_item` sets no radius; 4292064b (part 2b, m3) joins the CHANGELOG's gpui line with the egui and iced one.

**Claim:** The egui showcase's Data and Theme Map tables draw each cell's text at the top of its row, so a stated `list.header_height` or `list.row_height` taller than the line leaves a blank band under the text: under material-3 the 56 px headers, under windows-11 the 40 px headers and rows. The Theme Map's colour cell (`info::swatch_cell`) lays its swatch and value in the cell's whole height, centred, where `ui.horizontal` laid them in a row `interact_size.y` tall, which at a text scale of 1.5 is taller than the row (catppuccin-mocha and macos-monterey: its centre 1.75 to 2 px below the row's).

At `1b5a19a7` it fails on the six `TableBuilder` cases (material-3 header text 18 px above the row's centre, windows-11 10 px) and the Basic case passes; it passes on the new code. `the_tables_headers_take_the_themes_header_height`, `the_data_and_theme_map_rows_are_the_themes_row_height` and `the_tables_keep_their_columns_at_the_largest_text_scale` measure the cells by their centres, which no longer share their row's top.
*Source:* m9c-step8-fix-brief.md, item 1.

### Step 6 — controller's rulings on the three drafts (2026-10-17)

The three plans below were drafted in parallel by Fable 5.1 planners from the entries, Step 4's rulings and the M8 Step 6 format, while M8's fix phase ran; reviewed and reconciled by the session. These rulings settle every "Needs a ruling" item and bind over the drafts.

- Ruling (M9a and M9c, M9-117: the macOS menus): both showcases present the same list — the application menu (About <showcase>, Preferences… ⌘, , Services, Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Quit, with the HIG's separators), View, Theme (without Preferences…, which moves to the app menu), Window (Minimize, Zoom, Bring All to Front); no File, no Help (Apple HIG, *The menu bar*: the app menu and the Window menu are expected even with one window). M9a takes gpui's half now, M9c egui's, and each macOS runner check reads back the item titles, not only the menu count. — why: the two showcases must match, and the gpui half is gpui code — cost if wrong: one list in two files.
- Ruling (M9a T3, the safe capture rewrite): verified by one `screenshots.yml` run at M9a's Step 8, before M9b moves iced onto the crate. Dispatching it needs a push of the branch: an outward action the maintainer approves at that point (asked then, with the commit list). — why: T3 deletes the only capture code macOS and Windows had — cost if wrong: one CI run.
- Ruling (M9b T19, M9-140: the page lists): M9b's T19 reorders the three page lists in one commit, with `docs/showcase-elements.toml`'s counterpart table; M9c does not touch page order. — why: one commit makes the correspondence one change — cost if wrong: a commit spanning two showcases.
- Ruling (M9b, page names): iced keeps "Display" (its content is not gpui's Typography page), "Text Inputs" becomes "Inputs"; the counterpart table records Display's correspondence. — cost if wrong: one label.
- Ruling (M9b T18, M9-135): the Theme row alone becomes searchable, as gpui's preset Combobox is and its icon-theme Select is not. — cost if wrong: two more combo boxes.
- Ruling (M9c, M9-111: the grid line width): `separator.line_width_px` joins the shared list's `basic.table.frame`/`basic.table.header` leaves once M9c's task reviewer confirms the gpui and iced Basic tables draw their grid at that width; a showcase that does not gets the fix in the same task. — cost if wrong: one leaf row.
- Ruling (M9c T2): `native_theme_egui::from_preset_with(key, is_dark, prefs, configure: impl FnOnce(Builder) -> Builder)` is accepted as an api-add (Step 4's "no public API change" meant no break): the System-mode bug it fixes (M9-1xx, C2#0: a preset atlas has no OS mode, so egui falls back to Dark on Linux) is an application's bug too, and an application needs the same `Builder::os_mode` hook the showcase does; CHANGELOG Added; the parity exception names egui's `Builder` as the reason the siblings have none. — cost if wrong: one function folded at 1.0.
- Ruling (all three, the shared crate): M9a's plan defines `native-theme-showcase-support` at `tools/showcase-support` (modules `cli`, `capture`, `dump`, `elements`, `values`, `info`, `rows`, `status`, plus `Kind`, `WINDOW_SIZE_PX`, `INFO_SETTLE`); M9b's T1 and M9c's T1 are written against "the crate M9a's plan defines" and take its names as M9a's T2 lands them — each later milestone's T1 brief quotes the crate's API as committed, not as drafted. — cost if wrong: a rename in two briefs.

### Step 6 — fix plan, M9a (2026-10-17)

Drafted by a Fable 5.1 planner from the 64 M9a entries, the M9x entries the dispatch assigns to M9a (M9-123, M9-124, M9-125, M9-126, M9-128, M9-136 whole; the gpui halves of M9-127, M9-137 and M9-138), the three carry-overs M8's fix phase recorded for M9a (progress ledger: `demo::group_box`/`demo::card` record `geometry("container_margin")` where `card.border.padding` states all four sides; `info/layout.rs`'s `content_padding` has no test against `pad_unstated_sides`; the inspector's Theme tab names the stated `font_family`, docs/todo.md:3499's gpui half), the Step 4 rulings (binding), M6's and M8's rulings on the connector and the shared code, and the maintainer's whole-repo standard of 2026-10-16. Nothing is deferred for being S4; what leaves M9a does so with a reason beyond priority (the last ruling). Order per the plan: S1 first (T1), then the structural move that relocates code the others touch — the shared `publish = false` showcase-support crate (T2) and gpui's move onto it (T3, T4) — then S2 (T5–T15), S3 (T16), S4 (T17–T19). One `implement` agent (Opus) per task, a fresh reviewer per task, `./scripts/check_release.sh --commit` once per task on its last commit, the full run at Step 8. Gates by kind, each mechanical: bug → a failing test first that reproduces the finding, then the fix, then it passes; info-truth → a test that builds the info under the preset the entry names and reads the claim or the note, failing on today's text, or the class gate named in the ruling that catches the whole family; theme-data → a test reading the built element's style (`gpui::Styled::style()` gives a `Div`'s `StyleRefinement` back, gpui-pre 0.3.9 `src/styled.rs:24`, `elements/div.rs:1872`) or the painted frame (`Window::painted_quads` and `painted_underlines`, gpui-pre 0.3.9 `src/window.rs:2881-2887`, under `test-support`, which the showcase's `painted_fill`/`painted_edge` helpers already read), and, where the look changes, a size-checked before/after `--capture` of the page under the same theme through `scripts/capture_window.sh`, compared by eye, plus a `--dump-layout` diff before and after on the three captured presets whose differences the task lists against the entry's claim; perf → a `#[cfg(test)]` counter on the path, a before/after count in a windowed test, and the switch timed on this host in release, recorded in the task's close; simplify → `git diff --stat` net deletion, tests unchanged except tests of deleted code; ux → the text or the behaviour derived from the data it describes and a test that the derivation holds. The gpui showcase's harness (`examples/showcase-gpui/tests.rs`: `open`, `draw`, `read`, `click`, `settle_on`, `apply_cli`, `use_preset`, `list_icon_themes`, `painted_fill`, `painted_edge`) and the connector's source gates (`src/showcase.rs`: `every_colour_claim_is_read_at_the_line_it_cites`, `every_prose_citation_still_exists`, `every_geometry_builder_has_a_note`, `the_omission_report`; every gate reads `SHOWCASE_FILES`, which `the_gates_read_every_showcase_file` holds to the directory) are what the gates build on; a gate added to `src/showcase.rs` is test code of the connector and changes no public API. Sources read before a task touches them: docs/showcase-elements.toml's header (the list's reader, the Widget Info format, the layout dump), docs/archive/todo_v0.5.9_unstated-sizes-and-chrome-ux-rationale.md §3.1 (a named showcase constant only where the theme states nothing, with its comment and its info saying so) and §5 (the two-path rule), docs/archive/todo_v0.5.9_showcase-app-spec.md §3–§5 (WidgetInfo, the registry, the inspector), docs/archive/todo_gpui-widgets-spec.md (the Looks), the M8 T5 ruling (group_box_content pads the stated sides; the showcase fills unstated sides with `layout.container_margin`), the M8 T12 ruling (the dump at rest) and the M8 T2 ruling (the fixture crate's shape, which T2 copies).

Rulings (Step 6):

- Ruling: the order bends once, for its own reason. The shared crate (T2) and gpui's move onto it (T3, T4) come before every S2 task: they relocate the command line, the capture, the dump, the element list, the leaf values and the status bar, which T5–T19's tests and infos sit on, so a later task edited first would be edited twice. Inside the S2 block T7 (the claim helpers) comes before T8, T14 and T15 (they claim edges and optional colours through them), and T12 (the one text helper) before T13 (the HOW lines name it). — why: the template orders structural moves first because they move code the others touch. — cost if wrong: two tasks reordered.
- Ruling: the shared crate — the Step 4 ruling's one `publish = false` workspace crate — is `native-theme-showcase-support` at `tools/showcase-support` (version 0.0.0, `edition`, `license`, `rust-version` and `repository` from the workspace, `publish = false`, as `tools/test-fixtures`), a path-only dev-dependency of each connector (`native-theme-showcase-support = { path = "../../tools/showcase-support" }`; cargo strips a path-only dev-dependency when packaging, so the published crates are unchanged; M9a adds gpui's line, M9b and M9c theirs), with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used)]` and `#![deny(clippy::expect_used)]` in its root and `scripts/check_strict_panic.sh -p native-theme-showcase-support --lib` beside the fixture crate's line in check_release.sh (`:665-668`) and ci.yml (`:74`), `cargo test -p native-theme-showcase-support` beside ci.yml's `:194`, and `tools/showcase-support/src` in check_release.sh's panic-pattern directories (`:372`) unless M8 T10 has made that list come from `cargo metadata`. It depends on `native-theme` (workspace; no feature named — the items it uses are feature-free, which its own `cargo check -p native-theme-showcase-support` proves; where one is not, the crate names that feature, which the connectors' dev-dependencies turn on anyway), `serde_json = "1.0.151"` and `toml = { workspace = true }` (the versions Cargo.lock holds), and under `cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "windows"))` on `xcap = { version = "0.9.8", default-features = false }` and `image = { version = "0.25.10", default-features = false, features = ["png"] }` (the egui showcase's capture dependencies, Cargo.lock's versions). a theme or icon-theme name keeps its case; an unknown flag ignored); `CliArgs::capturing(&self) -> bool` (`capture || screenshot.is_some()`); `CliArgs::shields_pointer(&self) -> bool` (`capturing() && pointer.is_none()`);   What each showcase keeps: its toolkit's window, pages, menus, chrome drawing and tests that drive a window; its page-key table (`Page::ALL`), its menu titles and any toolkit-only row (gpui's built-in icons); where its elements were drawn (the rectangles the dump takes); the panel's drawing; the HOW lines (gpui's `info/leaves.rs`, iced's `iced_route`, egui's `mapping.toml` route) — the toolkit's "how" is the one part of Widget Info the list's header lets differ. How the command lines become the same: one parser, one flag set — `--theme`, `--variant`, `--tab`, `--icon-set` (with `default`), `--screenshot`, `--capture`, `--pointer`, `--press`, `--dump-layout`, `--open-menu` — one validator per flag with one error text, and one exit rule: a bad `--pointer` exits 1 before the window; `--screenshot` exits 1 before the window where the showcase cannot capture its frame (`screenshot_support`); a value a picker does not offer is reported and ignored, `--open-menu` included; a layout dump quits only when nothing captures (`quits_after_dump`); a failed `--screenshot`, dump write or window open exits 1. — why: the Step 4 ruling; the M8 T2 precedent; five copies of a parser that already disagree (M9-136). — cost if wrong: one dev-only crate; a toolkit that needs a flag of its own adds it in its own `main` after the shared parse (the parser ignores what it does not know).
- Ruling: M9-126's row list and name parser go into the shared crate, not core: `rows::icon_rows` and `cli::icon_set_choice` above. — why: Step 4 recorded that no M9 entry changes a crate's public API, and the showcases are the only callers; a core `IconSetChoice::from_name` would be an api-add with a CHANGELOG line, a semver report and a doc, for three dev-only callers. — cost if wrong: an application that wants the parser later gets it moved into core as an api-add, one function.
- Ruling: M9-128's gpui half needs no connector API: the showcase prints a gpui colour through `native_theme::color::Rgba::from_f32(r, g, b, a)` of `gpui::Rgba::from(hsla)` (core `color.rs:114`) and `Rgba`'s `Display` (`:188-199`, which decides on the rounded byte), and `info::hsla_to_hex` (`info/mod.rs:422-432`) goes with `a_translucent_colour_prints_its_alpha` rewritten over the conversion; the six call sites follow. iced's `color_to_hex` is M9b's (the same conversion through `native_theme_iced::palette`'s private `to_color` is iced's to open or avoid). — why: the entry's "make each connector's conversion public" is a api-add nothing but the showcase needs; `from_f32` is already public. — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: M9-127's gpui half — the window capture goes through the crate's `FrameCapture` (xcap, safe): `main.rs:1050-1349`'s `get_main_window_ptr`, `cg_types`, `screencapture_own_window`, `capture_own_window_macos`, `bitblt_own_window`, `capture_own_window_windows` and `checked_capture` go, with the `windows` dev-dependency (`Cargo.toml:116-122`) and the raw `objc2::msg_send!` use; `main` calls `run_finder` before `gpui_kit::application()` so the Windows finder run never opens a window. The Retina nudge (`nudge_content_size`, `:1133-1146`) stays, on objc2-app-kit 0.3.2's safe generated calls (`NSApplication::sharedApplication(mtm)`, `mainWindow`/`keyWindow`/`windows`, `NSWindow::contentView`, `NSView::frame`, `NSWindow::setContentSize`, with `objc2::MainThreadMarker::new()`), the Step 4 ruling's second safe route; `objc2-app-kit` joins the macOS dev-dependencies with the features those items need and `objc2` stays for the marker. Whether gpui-pre 0.3.9's Metal path still needs the nudge is unverifiable on Linux: a docs/todo.md `[1.0]` line asks the next asset run to try a capture without it (the frame check fails if it is still needed). The remaining differences the verifier listed (no `CAPTUREBLT`, a window across two monitors clipped, the finder process) go into the crate's `capture` module doc. — why: the no-unsafe rule and the Step 4 ruling; egui's capture is the traced-equal safe route. — cost if wrong: the next macOS or Windows capture run fails its size check and the task's author reads the run.
- Ruling: `--icon-theme` goes (M9-136). gpui's own `--icon-set <installed theme>` already selects that theme (`main.rs:986-988`: `IconSetChoice::Freedesktop(theme)`, which `choose_icon_row` keeps across theme switches as a user's pick), so the override state goes with the flag: `Showcase::icon_theme_override`, `set_icon_theme_override`, the `cli_override` parameter of `load_all_icons` and `load_gpui_icons` and their `cli_override.or(default_theme)` precedence (`support.rs:466`, `:728-731`, `app.rs:714-718`), the three tests of the override (`the_icon_theme_override_reloads_the_icons`, `the_icon_theme_select_shows_the_icon_theme_override`, `picking_an_icon_theme_ends_the_icon_theme_override`), the `--icon-theme` half of `the_icon_flags_say_when_no_icon_theme_is_installed`; `scripts/generate_screenshots_gpui.sh`'s four-field `THEMES` entries become the iced and egui scripts' three-field ones and the run passes `--icon-set "${icon_theme:-$icon_set}"` as `generate_gifs_theme_switching.sh:70-73` does for iced (the GIF script's gpui loop, `:109-111`, `:149-152`, the same); `scripts/README.md:74`'s sentence and the gpui README's flags line (`README.md:833-841`) follow; a CHANGELOG *Changed* line. With the override gone, `load_all_icons`' two `cfg` arms differ by nothing (M9-027): one match per loader with only the `Freedesktop` arm under `cfg(target_os = "linux")`, `FreedesktopLoader::new(role).theme(t)` for `t = default_theme` (the loader looks the role's name up itself, native-theme `icons.rs:343-350`), the comment at `support.rs:467-468` gone. `--icon-set default` on gpui is the icon-theme Select's `default` row where the installed theme names an available icon theme, `system` otherwise, as the Select's rows are (`icon_theme_rows`): `IconPick::FollowTheme` sets `icon_choice_follows_preset` and `show_icon_choice` re-derives the choice. — why: the entry's own equivalence; one flag set in three showcases. — cost if wrong: a script of the maintainer's that passed `--icon-theme` passes `--icon-set` instead, one word.
- Ruling: the exit rules, gpui side. `--screenshot` on Linux exits 1 before the window with the crate's text (M9-018: `main.rs:1586-1594` goes); a failed `open_window` exits 1 after its message (M9-019: `main.rs:1487-1491`, through `cli::refuse`); `dump_layout`'s `quit` is `cli_args.quits_after_dump()` (M9-137: `main.rs:1495-1503` passes `!capture` today, so `--dump-layout F --screenshot P` quit before P was written). - Ruling: the install path (M9-028, M9-016, M9-138's gpui half) — one `Showcase::install_system(system, window, cx)` used by `new` and `install_system_theme` (the constructor's copy already lacks the user's overrides, `app.rs:1730-1731`), the `(default)` placeholder spec one `const fn`; the showcase keeps the `SystemTheme` it installed (`system: Option<SystemTheme>`, both variants in it) so a colour-mode switch under `default` re-picks the variant (`system.pick(mode)`, `apply_system_theme`, `Theme::change`) and re-reads the OS only on Reload System Theme and a watcher event; `reload_icons` runs only where the effective set or theme changed since the last load, else `rebuild_icon_caches` recolours the loaded icons with the new foreground; the icon tint handed to the system loaders is `None` where no native theme is installed (M9-016: the placeholder's `TRANSPARENT` reached `color_opt`, which keeps r, g, b, so every recoloured system icon drew black) through one pure `fn icon_tint(native_installed: bool, font_colour: Rgba) -> Option<Rgba>`. Gate: `#[cfg(test)]` counters on the system read and on `load_all_icons` — a test under `default` switches the mode three times: reads +0 (today +3), loads +0 (today +3), `is_dark` follows each; Reload System Theme: reads +1; a preset switch from a bundled set to a freedesktop one: loads +1; `icon_tint(false, Rgba::TRANSPARENT) == None`; the mode switch timed on this host in release before and after (the ledger's Baseline numbers: `from_system` warm 3.6–9.7 ms, a freedesktop icon reload warm 1.8–2.9 ms, cold about 40 ms), recorded in the task's close. — why: the entries; M8-44's rule that a switch does once what it needs once. — cost if wrong: one field on the Showcase.
- Ruling: the per-frame work (M9-020, M9-021; M9-139's gpui half is M9-020's fix, the entry stays M9b's for iced) — `PanelLook` is built once per install and kept on the Showcase (rebuilt in `apply_theme_by_name` and `demo::change_preferences`), the inspector borrowing it; `widget_tab` builds nothing before the listed check and clones no `Theme` (`inspector.rs:107-111`, `:433-439`, `:461`, `:675-680`); the animation timer steps and notifies only while `active_page == Page::Icons` (the page shows `frames.get(index)`, so a paused index is harmless; `show_page` into Icons restarts it). Gate: `#[cfg(test)]` counters — serialisations over ten drawn frames on the Basic page: 1 (today 10); timer ticks that notified after the executor clock advanced ten frame durations on the Basic page under Material (24 frames at 42 ms, the bundled indicator): 0 (today 10), on the Icons page: > 0. — why: the entries' traces; the Basic page's Spinner draws every frame. — cost if wrong: a stale panel until the next install, which the rebuild sites rule out.
- Ruling: the keyboard listeners (M9-017) — the seven listeners (`inputs.rs:29-40`, `buttons.rs:88-93`, `basic.rs:292-294`) call `cx.notify()`, as the page's other listeners do. Class gate: a source gate in `tests.rs` over `pages/*.rs` and `demo.rs` — every `cx.listener(` closure whose body assigns `this.<field> =` calls `cx.notify()` (the gate prints the offenders). Behaviour gate: a windowed test tabs to the Inputs page's first checkbox, presses Space, and reads the next frame drawn without `refresh()`; on `--features gpui-fast` a frame reuses the subtrees no view notified (`tests.rs:9-12`, docs/todo.md:1682), so the un-notified control keeps its old frame and the test fails today; on gpui-pre it passes trivially and its comment says so; the task runs it once under gpui-fast (`cargo test -p native-theme-gpui --features gpui-fast --example showcase-gpui`, the configuration CI builds). — why: gpui-component documents the value as controlled (`checkbox.rs:104-108`), and the mouse path masked the omission. — cost if wrong: seven `cx.notify()` calls.
- Ruling: captures and dumps where the look changes. A task whose fix changes what a page draws (T5: the Inputs page's textarea gains the surface; T6: the chrome menu rows take `geometry::menu_item`; T8: the expander's and the number field's chevrons come from the chosen set; T11: the pages; T18: the Tree's rows) takes a size-checked before/after `--capture` of that page under kde-breeze with Breeze (and material-3 with Material for T8) through `scripts/capture_window.sh`, compared by eye in the review, and a `--dump-layout` diff before and after on kde-breeze, material-3 and catppuccin-mocha in the rest and menu runs with every difference listed in the task's report against the entry's claim — the shared chrome is compared by `scripts/check_showcase_parity.py` at the next asset run (M8 T12's step), whose `[parity]` exceptions already record the menu rows' per-toolkit geometry (docs/showcase-exceptions.toml:135-165); a difference T6 or T8 makes to a listed element that the exceptions explain by the old drawing gets its reason re-read. — why: the maintainer's rule (showcases verified side by side with screenshots under the same theme); the dump is the deterministic half. — cost if wrong: one capture per task.
- Ruling: the unstated sides (M9-010, M9-011, M9-048, the two M8 T5 carry-overs) — one helper, `padded(el, &padding, x, y: Option<impl Into<DefiniteLength> + Copy>)` (`demo.rs:319-343` generalised from `Option<Rems>`), called by `card` and `group_box` (`padded(content_style, &card.border.padding, margin, Some(margin))`, since `geometry::group_box_content` already set the stated sides), `segmented` (`padded(.., SEGMENT_PADDING, None)`), `tool_box_of` (stated sides only: `padded` with no fallback, or its `side` closure kept as the one stated-sides-only shape, which the verifier distinguished) and `side_panel`; `pad_unstated_sides` (`:6134-6160`) goes; the `geometry("container_margin")` line is recorded only where `container_margin` is `Some` and a side is unstated — the toolbar's rule (`:941-946`) — in `group_box`, `card` (carry-over 1) and `side_panel` (M9-011), whose "padding" instance line (`info/chrome.rs`, side_panel) then says which sides the margin pads; `info/layout.rs:716`'s segmented line says 12 px on an unstated left or right and none on an unstated top or bottom (M9-048). Gate: a unit test over every bundled preset in both modes that `padded(div(), &p, x, Some(y)).style()` equals what `pad_unstated_sides` produced on `group_box_content`'s refinement, run before the deletion and deleted with it; windows-11 (all four `card.border.padding` sides stated): the card's and the GroupBox's info hold no `container_margin` line, kde-breeze: they do; `content_padding`'s text names `card.border's` for exactly the stated sides and `layout.container_margin` for the rest, over every preset (carry-over 2); a custom theme stating all four `sidebar.border.padding` sides: the side panel's info holds no `container_margin` line and its padding line names the stated sides; material-3 (`padding_horizontal` only): the segmented line as above. — why: the entries and the carry-overs; five implementations of one rule. — cost if wrong: net deletion reverted.
- Ruling: what leaves M9a, each with its reason beyond priority. (1) M9-117's gpui half (the macOS app menu: `chrome::menus()` starts with File, so AppKit shows Quit under the app's name) — the entry is M9c's and names both showcases; its only verification is a capture on the macOS runner, which M9a cannot take from Linux; the question of who takes it is under *Needs a ruling*. (2) M9-139's gpui half — M9-020's fix (T16); the entry stays M9b's for iced. (3) M9-130's gpui half (the status bar's environment copy) — T4's adoption of `status::environment`; the entry stays M9b's. (4) docs/todo.md:3654 ("For M9a: the egui showcase's `named_image`…") — the egui showcase is M9c's; the label is M8 T21's to correct, and M9a takes nothing from it. (5) docs/todo.md:2723 (`EmptyMedia`'s 2 rem frame outgrown by the large icon) — T15 fixes only the literal text (M9-058); the frame's sizing is the design question the entry holds, not an S4 deferral. (8) docs/todo.md:3094's windows-11 `widget_gap = 6` provenance — D3, M2's domain; T11 applies the §3.1 rule the entry asks for. (9) The dump's at-rest behaviour (M8-44, docs/todo.md:2195) — M8 T12's; T3 keeps it under the shared writer. Nothing is deferred for being S4.
