### Step 6 — fix plan, M9b (2026-10-17)

Drafted by a Fable 5.1 planner from the 37 M9b entries, the nine M9x entries the dispatch assigned (M9-129, M9-130, M9-131, M9-132, M9-133, M9-134, M9-135, M9-139, M9-140) and the iced halves of M9-127, M9-137 and M9-138, the Step 4 rulings (binding), the known items of `m9-known-items.md` that name the iced showcase (docs/todo.md:433, :2950, :3493, :3496, :3499, :3505, :3508, :3625's "the showcase's own leak is M9b's to shrink", the M8 T7 carry), M1-T7-07's ledger entry (:1080-1100) and the maintainer's whole-repo standard of 2026-10-16. Nothing is deferred for being S4; the four items that leave M9b each carry a reason beyond priority (the last ruling). The plan is written against *the support crate*, the `publish = false` crate under `tools/` that M9a's plan defines for what the three showcases copy (the Step 4 ruling: the command-line parser and validators, `check_frame_capture`, the layout-dump writer, the icon-set and preset rows, the hex formatter, the status bar's environment text; M9-124 adds the element-list reader, the leaf walk and value text, the panel model and its Copy text; M9-127 egui's capture); the controller reconciles the names when merging the plans. M9b's fix phase runs after M9a's, so the crate exists when T1 starts.

Order per the plan: no S1; the structural moves first (T1 the support crate, T2 the capture, T3 the contract export — they relocate the code every route, info and perf task edits), then S2 (T4–T12, T14's M9-068, T17), then S3 (T13, T15, T16), then S4 (T18, T19). One `implement` agent (Opus) per task, a fresh reviewer per task, `./scripts/check_release.sh --commit` once per task on its last commit, the full run at Step 8. Gates by kind, mechanical, in the showcase's own `#[cfg(test)]` module unless said otherwise (the `iced_test` `Simulator` harness: `interface`, `probe_bounds`, `drive`, `texts`, `drawn_layout`/`surveyed_layout`, the `State::starting_with(read)` injection, the source scanner `strip_comments_and_strings`/`call_sites`/`is_dressed`): bug → a failing test first that reproduces the finding, then the fix, then it passes; info-truth → a test that the claim equals what is drawn (the named function exists on the build's path, the hex equals the style closure's output at the row's status, a widget is claimed only where the state draws it), written first and failing on the text as it is, over every bundled preset in both modes where the claim depends on the theme; theme-data → a splice test (the leaf spliced in a resolved theme moves what the page draws, the method of the connector's `every_colour_leaf_reaches_a_row_or_is_named`) or a probe-bounds measurement, failing first, plus a size-checked before/after capture (`scripts/capture_window.sh`, `--capture`, `--tab`, `--pointer` where the change shows under the pointer) compared by eye where the change is visible on a Linux preset; perf → a before/after count in the test (a `#[cfg(test)]` counter on the function the finding names: the showcase has no timing test, Step 1–2's note, and a count is deterministic where a timing is noise); simplify → `git diff --stat` net deletion, tests unchanged except tests of deleted code; ux → a headless test of the behaviour where `iced_test` can drive it, else a size-checked capture compared by eye, and where only another OS can see it (T17) the cross-target check plus the next CI screenshot run. Every value a task writes cites its source (a gpui constant by file and line, a preset value by its TOML line); no value is invented. Sources read before a task touches them: `docs/showcase-elements.toml`'s header (section B, the value format, the layout dump); `docs/archive/todo_v0.5.9_widget-info-rationale.md` §2 (why hand-written panels are gated); `connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:1129-1145` and spec v0.5.9 §5 (reduce motion); `connectors/native-theme-egui/src/mapping_doc.rs:1-20`, `:355-360` (the generated-file pattern T3 copies); `connectors/native-theme-egui/examples/showcase-egui/capture.rs:1-10` (the safe capture T2 adopts); `connectors/native-theme-gpui/examples/showcase-gpui/info/registry.rs:13-27` (the settle T7 copies); `docs/todo.md:433` (why the showcase's font memo exists) and `:3505` (why `register_weight` stays).

Rulings (Step 6):

- Ruling: M1-T7-07, the form of the export (the Step 4 ruling's choice) — a checked-in data file, not an `include!`-shared table: `connectors/native-theme-iced/contract-leaves.toml` at the crate root beside `README.md` (where egui keeps `mapping.toml`), written by `#[ignore] regenerate_contract_leaves` (`cargo test -p native-theme-iced --all-features --lib -- --ignored regenerate_contract_leaves`) and held current by `every_colour_leaf_reaches_a_row_or_is_named` (`contract.rs:4830-4997`), which already computes the map and now also compares it with the file and fails naming the regenerate command, as `mapping_md_is_current` does (`mapping_doc.rs:3-4`, `:351`); the showcase reads it with `include_str!("../contract-leaves.toml")` and the `toml` crate (a dev-dependency since the element list), the connector's public surface unchanged (no `pub` item, no feature: the file is data). The file ships in the package as egui's `mapping.toml` does (a few KB; excluding it would break `cargo test` of the packaged crate). *What it holds:* per colour leaf of `ResolvedTheme`, the rows it moves — a style row as `styles::<fn>.<field>` with the statuses it moved under (the `Reading::style` strings are per status, `contract.rs:4554-4572`, so the regenerator records the status), a palette slot, an accessor row, a `Spinner` Look read (`SPINNER_READS`, `contract.rs:4781`) — or the `UNREAD_COLOURS`/`UNREACHABLE` entry that names it with its reason; and per row the converse, the leaves that move it, with the `DERIVED` entry's name where the row's native side is a derivation (`derived.rs`); a row behind `iced_aw` (`styles::aw::*`) is marked so, since the showcase's default build draws those widgets otherwise (M9-073). *What the generated rows cover:* every colour row of Widget Info — a listed element's colour leaves (`iced_route`'s colour arms, T3) and a page widget's colour section (the `widget_tooltip` colour triples, T4) — so a colour claim names a row the contract proves. *What stays hand-written:* the non-colour leaves (`*_px`, `*_ms`, `font`, `shadow_enabled`, `icon_set`, `icon_theme`, `layout.*`, `text_scale.*`, `line_height`, `*_side`), each route a short string as today; the routes of what the showcase draws itself with no connector row (`ghost_button`, `menu_row`/`menu_title`, `surface`, `list_row`, `tab_style`, `CheckMark`, the icon colours, `copy_button`, the Widget Info chrome), gated by T3's showcase splice test; the "Not themeable" lines; and a per-row prose table in the showcase keyed by the export's row names for a derivation's sentence (iced's `Primary::generate(..).strong`), every key held to the export by a test. — why: the map is computed by splicing, not kept by hand, so a file a test writes and checks is its only truthful form; an `include!`-shared `.rs` table would be either hand-kept (the drift M9-084 names) or test-written Rust source, and egui already proves the data-file pattern. — cost if wrong: one file format.
- Ruling: the per-widget colour sections (T4) show the *drawn* value: for a style row the showcase calls the connector's closure itself, `styles::button_primary(resolved)(&state.current_theme, button::Status::Hovered).background` (M9-085's own fix), through a small per-field extractor set of its own (background, text_color, border colour, the checkbox's `icon_color`, the toggler's `background`/`foreground`, the progress bar's `bar`/`background`/`border`, the text input's four, the pick list's and slider's) — a handful of lines per `Style` type, not a copy of the contract's `*_style_fields` walk — and labels it with the export's leaf or derivation; the `DERIVED` sentence from the prose table. A `*.border.color` row whose sibling `line_width` leaf is 0 reads "not drawn (`<table>.border.line_width` 0)" with no swatch, the common rule "a zero-width edge is not drawn in its colour", applied in the renderer for every border row at once (M9-088's class). A status the page shows (the switch off, M9-087) gets its status's rows; a disabled class keeps its own pair faded by `disabled_opacity` as `class_button` draws it (M9-086), which the closure's output already is. — why: the finding's class is a hex that is not on screen; the closure is what is on screen. — cost if wrong: one extractor per style type.
- Ruling: M9-067 follows the Step 4 reduce-motion ruling, not the entry's proposed fix: the OS's request still stops the animations whatever the Preferences switch shows ("off" is no request, `native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:1129-1145`, spec v0.5.9 §5), so `motion_reduced()` stays an OR, but of the OS's preference the showcase already holds (`system.accessibility.reduce_motion`, T6's kept `SystemTheme`) and the shown one — the second read of the same OS setting, `State::reduced_motion` re-read by `prefers_reduced_motion()` at every icon reload (`:1503`, `:2163`), goes — and the Reduce motion row (`:6549`) says "an OS request keeps them stopped whatever the switch shows". — why: the ruling; one OS read, not two of the same setting. — cost if wrong: one condition.
- Ruling: M9-066, M9-065, M9-079, M9-138 (the OS read) and docs/todo.md:3493 — one shape for `load_theme`'s OS arm, gpui's: `State` keeps the last OS read (`system: Option<SystemTheme>`, read at startup, on `ReloadSystemTheme` and on a watcher event, through the injectable `read_system_theme`) and a mode switch under `default` picks `system.pick(mode)` with no read; the user's Preferences live apart in `PreferenceOverrides` (one `Option` per field, set by the dialog) laid over the OS's `accessibility` on every install, as gpui's `install_preferences` does (`showcase-gpui/demo.rs:2497-2537`), and the startup fallback's preferences are `native_theme::detect::accessibility_preferences()`, not `default()`; the OS arm takes `system.icon_theme_for(mode)` (`native-theme/src/lib.rs:667-680`, the connector's own choice at `lib.rs:482`, `:542`) and builds the theme through `to_theme_in(&r, name, mode)` (M8 T4's public builder) at the three sites, `starting_with` through `system.to_iced_theme()`'s `Loaded` for the picked mode instead of assembling it by hand (`:1739-1753`). The startup fallback's preset off Linux is the platform's own (the preset core's `from_system` names for the host where it falls back to one, else the first platform preset of `Theme::list_presets_for_platform()`), adwaita staying the Linux answer where no desktop is known: the never-another-platform's-preset rule is symmetric, and the entry's own text names this answer. — why: the entries' fixes agree on one struct; iced is the outlier among the three on each of the four. — cost if wrong: one `SystemTheme` kept in `State`; one preset name off Linux.
- Ruling: M9-131 and M9-132 — a page widget's hover carries its identity, not its text: `hoverable` takes a key (`UnlistedKey`, one variant per `widget_tooltip*` site, 30 `hoverable(` call sites) and `State` keeps `hovered: Option<Hovered>` (`Listed(&'static str)` or `Unlisted(UnlistedKey)`); the text is built in `view` from the key through one `unlisted_info(state, key) -> String` match whose arms are the existing builders moved out of the page functions, so every install rebuilds it on the next frame, as gpui's registry (`info/registry.rs:87-104`) and egui's `end_pass` do; and a new choice replaces what is shown only after it has stood `INFO_SETTLE` 250 ms (gpui's constant, `info/registry.rs:16`, egui's `main.rs:46`), held as `pending: Option<(Hovered, Instant)>` and promoted on the next tick (the 50 ms `AnimationTick` where it runs, else a settle tick the subscription adds while `pending` is `Some`). The listed elements' path (`ElementHovered`, `hovered_element`) folds into the same field. — why: a string captured at hover time is a value, and a value cannot follow a theme switch; the settle is the shared chrome's behaviour in two of three. — cost if wrong: one enum of 31 keys.

Only macos-tahoe states no `container_margin` and no `section_gap` (every other bundled preset states all four: `grep -l` over `native-theme/src/presets`), so nothing changes on a Linux preset and no Linux capture can show it; the gate is headless under macos-tahoe. — why: the maintainer's rule, the shared chrome looks like gpui's; the page's own column count already assumed no gap, which is M9-074's 3 px. — cost if wrong: two constants and a label.
- Ruling: M9-083 and M9-089 — the showcase builds every tooltip through one `showcase_tooltip(state, content, tip, position)` (today `chrome_tooltip`'s recipe: `tooltip.font` through `.themed`, the tip in a container at `tooltip.max_width`, `tooltip_padding` where iced can carry it, `styles::tooltip`, `.show_delay(resolved)`), the Display page's four and the Basic page's one included; the gap to the control is one rule for all six, the gpui showcase's for the compared Basic tooltip (the implementer reads gpui-component's tooltip offset through `demo::built_tooltip_button` and cites it; `layout.widget_gap` is what the chrome's used, `:4158`, and is kept only if gpui's is the same), and the Tooltip's "Not themeable" line names the rule and its value; "max width" moves from Not themeable to the Theme section (`tooltip.max_width`, `:9929`). — why: the model states no gap (`docs/property-registry.toml:259-264`: `background_color`, `font`, `max_width_px`, `show_delay_ms`, `border`), so the showcase's own value must be one value, and the compared one gpui's. — cost if wrong: one number in one builder.
- Ruling: M9-077, M9-094, M9-138 (the icon reload) — `IconSource::Fallback`, the Material preload and the "fallback" count go (no loader substitutes a set: the never-mix rule, `freedesktop.rs:820`); `LoadedIcon` keeps, beside the `IconData` as loaded, the handle the page draws (`svg::Handle` or `image::Handle`, built once in `load_all_icons` with the theme's text colour through the connector's per-set colouring: `to_svg_handle(data, Some(fg))` for Material and Lucide, `to_svg_handle(data, None)` for a system set, whose loader coloured it at load) and `build_icon_cell` takes the cached handle; `reload_icons` splits into a reload (the effective set, the freedesktop theme or the text colour changed: the loaders run) and nothing otherwise — a mode switch under a preset whose icon theme and `defaults.text_color` are the same in both modes loads nothing — the rule written where `install_in_mode` calls it, with the three inputs compared. A recolour without a reload is not attempted: a freedesktop icon is coloured by its loader at load (`FreedesktopLoader::color_opt`, core's symbolic colouring, which no public step applies to bytes afterwards), and a colour change is the common case of a mode switch, so the gain would be the rare case at the cost of a second colouring path. — why: the entries' fixes, less the half that needs core to grow a function. — cost if wrong: a reload on a mode switch that changes only the text colour, as today.

### Step 6 — fix plan, M9c (2026-10-17)

Drafted by a Fable 5.1 planner from the 21 M9c entries (M9-102–M9-122), the cross-showcase entry M9-141, the Step 4 rulings (Reduce motion, the shared showcase-support crate, the docs/todo.md:3499 extension rule), the open docs/todo.md items that name the egui showcase (`:3585`, the `For M7` table-row item nobody took; `:3654`'s egui half, labelled `For M9a` though it is this showcase's `named_image`; `:3499`'s egui sites; `:433`'s new caller), the M9x entries whose egui halves the shared crate takes (M9-124, M9-125, M9-126, M9-127, M9-130, M9-136), and the maintainer's whole-repo standard of 2026-10-16. Nothing is deferred for being S4; what leaves M9c carries a reason beyond priority (the last ruling). The showcase's own harness is the gate wherever it can see the defect: `tests.rs` drives the real `eframe::App` headlessly through egui_kittest (`open`, `cli`, `hover_and_settle`, `centre_of`, the registry's `records()` and `places()`, `harness.output().shapes` for painted fills and galleys, AccessKit nodes for labels and toggles), so a layout, a painted colour or radius, a font id, a Widget Info seam or row, a key press and a menu click are all testable without a display; a look the harness cannot judge gets a size-checked Linux capture (`scripts/capture_window.sh`, `--capture`, 1280×720) compared by eye with the gpui showcase's under the same preset.

Order per the plan: no S1; the structural move first (T1: the showcase onto the shared crate M9a's plan defines, which relocates the parser, the validators, the rows and the formatters the later tasks would otherwise edit in place), then S2 (T2–T12), S3 (T13), S4 (T14–T17), docs last (T18). M9c's fix phase runs after M9a's and M9b's, so the crate exists before T1 starts; the controller reconciles its names. One `implement` agent (Opus) per task, a fresh reviewer per task, `./scripts/check_release.sh --commit` once per task on its last commit (it runs the showcase's tests under `--no-default-features` and `--all-features`, `check_release.sh:766-769`, and the macOS cross-target check that compiles the system-menu module, `:549-550`), the full run at Step 8. Gates by kind: bug → a failing kittest first that reproduces the finding, then the fix, then it passes; theme-data and info-truth → a kittest that reads the painted shape, the galley's `FontId`, the record's rect or the shown info's seams and rows against the resolved value, failing on the code as it is; perf → a `#[cfg(test)]` counter of the loads the test reads before and after (a count, not a timing: the paths are disk reads and SVG recolours whose number is the claim); simplify → `git diff --stat` net deletion in `examples/showcase-egui/`, tests unchanged except tests of deleted code; ux → a kittest where the harness can drive it (keys, clicks, the open palette, the Preferences switches), else the capture pair; api-add (the one connector change, T2) → `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`, the crate in every gate configuration, a unit test, a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` *Added* line, `cargo semver-checks` at Step 8 reporting only the add; docs → each claim checked against the code by the reviewer, the CHANGELOG lines read against `git log`. Sources read before a task touches them: `docs/archive/todo_v0.6.0_egui-connector-spec.md` §10.4 (the showcase's rules: the atlas as the one theme field, the icon rule, the per-call leaves, Widget Info's registration rule), its lines 7206-7208 (the Widget Info text R11 superseded, T14) and 7496-7502 (the `--all-features` capture decision, T17); `connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:1129-1145` (gpui's reduce-motion design, T4); Apple's HIG "The menu bar" as M9-117 cites it (T5); `docs/showcase-elements.toml`'s header (the list the three showcases share, T1, T14).

Rulings (Step 6):

- Ruling: the order bends once. T1 (the shared crate) goes before every fix because it moves `CliArgs` and its parser (main.rs:176-266), the three validators (app.rs:144-198), `check_frame_capture` and `capture_app_id` (main.rs:115-170), `layout_json` (app.rs:241-266), the icon rows (chrome.rs:937-951) and preset rows (app.rs:564-580), the element-list reader (elements.rs), the value formatters (info.rs:303-400) and the status bar's environment text with `desktop()` and the two inline defined-size formatters (chrome.rs:698-752, info.rs:1123-1127) out of the files T2–T17 edit; a fix landed in a copy the next task deletes is work done twice. — why: the template's rule for structural moves. — cost if wrong: one task reordered.
- Ruling: T1 is written against the crate M9a's plan defines (the Step 4 ruling: one `publish = false` workspace crate, a path-only dev-dependency as `tools/test-fixtures` is since M8 T2). egui hands over what the toolkit does not force and keeps what it does: `Page` and its keys stay the showcase's (its page set is its spec's §10.4 palette table), but the keys of the pages that correspond across the three come from the crate's one page-key table (M9-136: `inputs`, not `text-inputs`); the crate's one flag set and exit rule hold (`--icon-set default` accepted, as egui already does; `--screenshot` exits 1 where the frame cannot be captured, egui's rule, main.rs:303-306; an unknown `--open-menu` reported and ignored, egui's rule, app.rs:444-452); `FrameCapture` (capture.rs, xcap) moves to the crate under M9a's unsafe-replacement ruling (M9-127) and egui takes it back from there with `check_frame_capture`; the family label the crate formats (M9-130's family half, T10) takes the drawn family as an argument, since each toolkit learns it differently (egui from the atlas's `Note::FontFamilyUnavailable`). The dump's JSON stays byte-identical to today's (`check_showcase_parity.py` reads it; M8 T12's two-dumps gate re-run). egui has no local hex formatter (M9-128: it prints core's `Rgba` `Display` through the JSON string), so M9-128 has no egui half. — why: the Step 4 ruling and M9x's "the first that touches a shared one"; M9a owns the crate, M9c is the last adopter. — cost if wrong: names the controller renames once.
- Ruling: Reduce motion, egui's half of the Step 4 ruling — in the egui showcase the switch "off" becomes no request. `rebuild_atlas` (app.rs:488-509) composes the preferences it installs from the OS's reading and the user's overrides through one pure function, `effective_preferences(os: &AccessibilityPreferences, overrides: Option<&AccessibilityPreferences>) -> AccessibilityPreferences`: every field the override's where one is set, except `reduce_motion`, which is `override || os` — the OS's reading is `sys.accessibility` under `default` (today replaced wholesale at app.rs:495-497) and `detect::accessibility_preferences()` under a preset (today the override alone, app.rs:502-506), both after the `invalidate_caches()` the path already runs. The Preferences switch shows the user's request (`settings.prefs`, chrome.rs:1693-1697); the status bar's flag and the Theme tab's `reduce_motion` row show the atlas's value, the effective one, because the atlas is the one field the connector's styles read (spec §10.4's third rule: `animation_time` 0 and the scroll animation off come from `atlas.accessibility()`), so an OS request must reach it; the row's description (chrome.rs:1787) says "off is no request: an OS request still stops the animations". — why: the Step 4 ruling (gpui's `forward_reduce_motion(false)` undoes only its own switch and re-reads the system, `lib.rs:1129-1145`; iced's `motion_reduced()` is `self.reduced_motion || self.accessibility.reduce_motion`, `showcase-iced.rs:2182-2184`); the high-contrast and reduce-transparency switches keep their override semantics, since the atlas builds no differently for them (their own descriptions, chrome.rs:1793, :1799). — cost if wrong: one `||`.
- Ruling: M9-113 — the egui connector gains `pub fn from_preset_with(name, is_dark, prefs, configure: impl FnOnce(Builder<'_>) -> Builder<'_>) -> Result<(ThemeAtlas, ResolvedTheme)>` (api-add), `from_preset` becoming `from_preset_with(.., |b| b)`; the showcase's preset arm passes `|b| b.os_mode(mode)` with `mode` from `native_theme::detect::system_is_dark()` (cached; cleared by the `invalidate_caches()` the watcher's closure and `ReloadTheme` already run, app.rs:640, :710), so Mode = System under a preset follows the desktop on Linux as under `default` (`to_egui_builder` sets `.os_mode(self.mode)`, ext.rs:379-383). The closure form, not a returned builder: `Builder<'a>` borrows the two resolved variants, the layout and the preferences (atlas.rs:263-283), which a preset has no owner for outside the function, where `SystemTheme` owns them for `to_egui_builder`; the closure also gives an application its `style_patch` and fonts under a preset, which today needs a copy of `from_preset`'s body. The install plugin fills `RawInput::system_theme` only where the integration reports none (plugin.rs:415-427), so macOS and Windows keep winit's live report. `from_preset`'s doc paragraph on the OS mode (ext.rs:206-208) points at the new function; one CHANGELOG *Added* line. — why: the entry's own route (M7-29's shape); the alternative, the showcase copying `from_preset`'s 25 lines, is the duplication M1-T7-01 forbids. — cost if wrong: one additive function.
- Ruling: M9-114 and M9-115 — the watcher's hand-off goes through one helper `install_atlas(&mut self, ctx, atlas)` that `install` (app.rs:513-529) and `logic`'s watcher arm (app.rs:793-801) both call: it installs, registers the faces, resets the JSON cache and `last_scheme`, marks `screen_changed` and clears `theme_error` (today the arm repeats `apply` minus the clear). The selection the watcher reads carries a generation (`selection: Arc<RwLock<Settings>>` becomes a selection with an `AtomicU64` bumped by `publish_selection`, app.rs:621-627); the closure records the generation it built for in an `Arc<AtomicU64>` before it returns the atlas (the store precedes `Handoff::on_change`'s store of the pending atlas under its mutex, watch.rs:20-27, and `take()` locks that mutex, so the UI thread reads the matching generation), and `logic` installs a hand-off whose generation is the current one and drops a stale one, then calls `self.install(ctx)` — the current selection rebuilt, which also re-reads the OS the event announced. `ThemeWatcher::last_error()` (watch.rs:139-150) is shown in the banner as `theme watcher: …` until a later rebuild succeeds or an install; the watcher's start error (app.rs:645) goes to its own `watcher_error: Option<String>`, shown as a note ("OS theme changes are not followed: …") that no install clears. — why: the entries' own fixes; the generation is the stamp the entry proposed, kept in the showcase because the connector's hand-off carries an atlas alone. — cost if wrong: one atomic.

The list, from Apple's HIG *The menu bar* (read 2026-10-17 through developer.apple.com's JSON for the page): the app menu — About <name> first with a separator after it ("Display the About menu item first. Include a separator after the About menu item"), Settings… ⌘, (the HIG's name for the item, replacing "Preferences…" in the macOS menu), Services where the toolkit offers it (muda's `PredefinedMenuItem::services`; gpui-pre 0.3.9 has no OS-submenu item, so gpui's app menu has none, recorded as a toolkit limit in `scripts/connector_parity_exceptions.toml`'s showcase section or the module doc), Hide <name> ⌘H, Hide Others ⌥⌘H, Show All, Quit <name> ⌘Q; a File menu holding Close ⌘W ("to close a window, people choose Close in the File menu"; "If your app doesn't handle any types of files, you can rename or eliminate this menu" — the showcases handle none, so File keeps Close alone); View; Theme (less Settings…); a Window menu ("Provide a Window menu even if your app has only one window. (f) is chosen: it fixes the default for every application with no new API; `from_preset` already reads the system (`ResolutionContext::from_system()`, `ext.rs:233`), the read is cached and invalidated with the others, and the mode reaches egui only where the integration reports none (`plugin.rs:415-427`: Linux), where `ThemePreference::System` means "follow the OS". An application that wants a fixed scheme sets egui's preference, as it does today; one that wants no OS mode at all builds through `ThemeAtlas::builder` (the documented manual route). It supersedes the archived spec's clause that a preset atlas has no OS mode (T18 (g); the tests at `install_tests.rs:77`, `:2319`, `:2346` change to `Some(<system_is_dark()'s mode>)`), recorded in the spec's *As built* list and a CHANGELOG *Changed* line under the egui connector; `to_theme(resolved, name)`, which reads nothing from the system, keeps `None`. #### M9-163 · M9x · ux · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/examples/showcase-gpui/app.rs:979
**Claim:** Under `system (sf-symbols)` and `system (segoe-fluent)` the gpui showcase draws no icon of the set: the Basic page's icon Buttons show "Copy Paste Delete" (on macos-tahoe "Delete" wraps to a second line) and its folder icons are missing, the toolbar shows "Preferences" where iced and egui draw a gear, and the Expander's chevrons and the Number input's steppers are missing, on every macOS and Windows capture.
**Evidence:** at d661a11a:
- `App::role_chrome_icon` (`app.rs:979-998`) and `ChromeIcon::of` (`support.rs:798-808`) take a set's icon only as `IconData::Svg`; anything else is `ChromeIcon::Missing` ("or only pixels, which an `Icon` cannot draw", `support.rs:784-787`). The SF Symbols and Segoe Fluent loaders give pixels only, `IconData::Rgba` (docs/todo.md, *Segoe Fluent icons as SVG outlines*).
- gpui-component 0.8.0's `Icon` draws a path or SVG bytes alone (`src/icon.rs:78-81`, `IconSource`); the showcase's Icons page draws the same sets' pixels with `gpui::img` from the decoded sources it keeps (`Showcase::rebuild_icon_caches`, `demo::icon_cell`).
- The captures `screenshots-gpui-macos/macos-macos-{monterey,tahoe}-{light,dark}.png` and `screenshots-gpui-windows/windows-windows-11-{light,dark}.png` of the run.
**Fix proposed:** A raster `ChromeIcon` that carries the Icons page's decoded image, drawn with `gpui::img` at the size the SVG's builder gives, wherever the widget takes any element; where the widget takes an `Icon` alone, the label fallback stays and its info says so; upstream's limit in docs/todo.md.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the RED run of the tests below at d661a11a.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (the M9x CI brief, item 1).
**Status:** fixed — the commit that files this entry:
- `ChromeIcon::Raster` holds the set's decoded image (`Showcase::gpui_icon_sources`, `loaded_icon_sources`; `ChromeIcon::of` and `role_chrome_icon` take it); `demo::Glyph` draws an SVG as an `Icon` and pixels as `gpui::img`, sized as an `Icon` of the same `Size` is. The pixels keep the colour their loader drew them in (`defaults.font.color` through `icon_tint`, the colouring `load_custom_icon_in` applies), which the sites' Widget Info says in place of the text-colour claims an SVG takes.
- The sites that take any element draw it: the Basic page's icon Buttons and folder icons, the toolbar's and the status bar's buttons, the page row's menu, the Expander's arrows (pixels do not turn, so an open item shows the set's ChevronDown under a leading arrow and ChevronUp under a trailing one), the Number input's steppers, the Buttons page's Toolbar, the Icons page's sizes, the Inputs page's search addon, the Data page's Attachment, the Feedback page's Empty state and Plain Marker, the Overlays page's menu rows, Dialog and AlertDialog.
- Upstream's `Icon`-only widgets keep their fallback through `ChromeIcon::svg_only`, their info naming no icon: `Toggle`, `Button::icon` (a `ButtonIcon`), `CommandItem`, `Alert`, `StepperItem` and `SidebarMenuItem`; docs/todo.md, *native-theme-gpui connector*, "PR: an `Icon` that draws an image".
- `a_raster_sets_icons_are_drawn_as_images_on_the_basic_page`, `a_raster_sets_chevrons_are_the_expanders_arrows_and_the_steppers`, `a_raster_sets_icons_are_drawn_as_images_in_the_chrome`, `a_raster_sets_icons_on_the_other_pages` and `the_dialog_samples_draw_a_raster_sets_icon` give the loaded entries pixels (`IconData::rgba`) and decode them as an install does; each fails at d661a11a (the icon Buttons' icon records absent, the Expander's arrows absent, the toolbar's icon record absent, no image in the Inputs page's group or the Dialog) and passes on the new code.

#### M9-164 · M9x · ux · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/examples/showcase-gpui/app.rs:1843
**Claim:** In every dark variant on macOS (both presets) and on Windows (windows-11) the gpui showcase's window title bar stays light (pixel 255 at about 640,15 on macOS, 243 on Windows), where iced and egui make it dark (30 and 32).
**Evidence:** at d661a11a:
- Nothing in the showcase or the connector asks gpui for a window appearance: no call of `App::set_window_appearance` (`grep`), which on macOS sets `NSApplication.appearance` and with it the title bar (gpui-pre-macos 0.3.9 `src/platform.rs:808-829`; gpui-fast-macos 0.1.10 the same lines). The window then takes the system's appearance, light on the runners.
- iced sets the window's theme through winit's `Window::set_theme` from the theme's mode (iced_winit 0.14.0 `src/window/state.rs:231`, `:255`, `src/lib.rs:670`); egui sends `ViewportCommand::SetTheme`, which egui-winit 0.36.2 turns into `Window::set_theme` (`src/lib.rs:1911`), and the egui connector's plugin sends the installed scheme (`native-theme-egui/src/plugin.rs:484-560`).
- On Windows gpui's `set_window_appearance` is the trait's no-op (gpui-pre 0.3.9 `src/platform.rs:433`, gpui-fast 0.1.10 `:434`): gpui-pre-windows sets the title bar's `DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE` from the system's appearance alone, when the window opens and when the system's changes (gpui-pre-windows 0.3.9 `src/window.rs:574`, `src/events.rs:1229-1240`, `src/util.rs:134-148`; gpui-fast-windows 0.1.10 `src/window.rs:575`, `src/events.rs:1240`).
**Fix proposed:** Ask gpui for the installed theme's mode on every install and at startup; record Windows' limit as `[upstream]`.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED: the test below, with the showcase's request taken out, finds none asked.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (the M9x CI brief, item 2); Windows' half deferred upstream.
**Status:** macOS half fixed, Windows half deferred upstream — the commit that files this entry: `Showcase::show_window_appearance` asks `cx.set_window_appearance(Some(Dark or Light))` from the mode the installed theme is drawn in, from `Showcase::new` and from `apply_theme_by_name`, which every install, mode switch, reload and the theme watcher's reinstall run through. The system's own dark-mode reading is not affected: `native_theme::detect::system_is_dark` reads the global `AppleInterfaceStyle` default (`native-theme/src/detect.rs:211`, `:817-832`). Windows' half is docs/todo.md, *native-theme-gpui connector*, "PR: let an application set the window's appearance on Windows", and the function's doc. `the_window_frame_takes_the_installed_themes_mode` reads what the showcase asked (gpui's test platform records no appearance) when it opens and after kde-breeze dark and light, windows-11 dark and macos-tahoe light are installed; with the two calls taken out it fails ("the window opened without the theme's mode", left `None`, right `Some(Dark)`), and passes with them. What the next macOS capture should show: a dark title bar in the monterey and tahoe dark captures; the Windows dark capture keeps its light one.
Part A's review (part B item 13(f)): the test can only check that the showcase asks gpui for the mode, through the `#[cfg(test)]` field that holds what it asked; gpui's test platform keeps no record of an appearance, so whether the title bar takes it is the next macOS capture's to show.

#### M9-165 · M9x · theme-data · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/widgets/separator.rs:88
**Claim:** On macOS (macos-monterey and macos-tahoe, both variants) the gpui showcase draws nothing under the Basic page's "Separator" heading: no pixel differs from the ground at about x 1000-1010, y 286-345, where iced and egui draw the line; on windows-11 gpui draws it. The page row's rule under the tabs is missing there too.
**Evidence:** at d661a11a:
- The Basic Separator is the connector's `widgets::Separator` (`demo::separator`), painted with `separator.line_color` and laid out as a box `separator.line_width` high (`src/widgets/separator.rs:88-91`, `.h(look.width)` with `.bg`). The macOS presets state no separator width, so it inherits `defaults.border.line_width`, 0.5 (macos-tahoe.toml and macos-monterey.toml `[light.defaults.border] line_width_px`, and the dark ones), and its colour `defaults.border.color`, `#00000019` light; windows-11's is 1.
- gpui rounds a box's stated size to the device-pixel grid half toward zero (gpui-pre 0.3.9 `src/taffy.rs:522-526`, `AbsoluteLength::to_taffy` through `round_to_device_pixel`, `src/util.rs:130-142`): 0.5 at a scale of 1, the macOS runners' 1280 × 752 captures, is 0, so the line takes no room and paints nothing. A border is rounded as a stroke, at least one device pixel (`src/taffy.rs:416-426`, `src/util.rs:145-151`), which is why the same presets' 0.5 px frames show. The page row's rule is a box of the same height (`demo::native_tab_bar`).
- iced and egui paint a 0.5-point line, which their renderers antialias into the pixel it crosses.
- On gpui's test platform at a scale of 1 under macos-tahoe the Separator's bounds are 170 × 0 and the rule's 979 × 0 (the test below).
**Fix proposed:** Draw the line as a border, as gpui draws the preset's frames: one device pixel where the stated width is under one, the stated width elsewhere.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the RED runs of the tests below at d661a11a's code.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (the M9x CI brief, item 3). The theme states the width; nothing in the theme makes it invisible.
**Status:** fixed — the commit that files this entry: `widgets::Separator` draws its line as a top (horizontal) or left (vertical) border `separator.line_width` wide in `separator.line_color`; the page row's rule is a `widgets::Separator`. At a scale of 2 and on every preset whose width is a whole pixel nothing moves. `a_separator_thinner_than_a_device_pixel_is_one_device_pixel` (the connector) and `a_hairline_separator_is_drawn_at_scale_one` (the showcase, the Basic Separator and the page row's rule under macos-tahoe at scale 1) fail at d661a11a's code (`(200px, 0px)`; `basic.separator.line` 0px) and pass on the new; Widget Info's "drawn by" line and the rule's routes say one device pixel at least. What the next macOS capture should show: a 1 px line under "Separator", `#00000019` over the ground (light) and the dark variant's colour, and the rule under the page tabs.
Reopened (controller, 2026-10-25, part B item 11): the Screenshots run 40218601365 on f8506510 still shows no line under "Separator" on macos-tahoe dark (x 900-1040, y 296-319, no row off the ground `#1e1e1e`, where iced's capture has a 140 px row at y 313), and none on windows-11 light either (read by eye from `screenshots-gpui-windows/windows-windows-11-light.png` beside iced's), where gpui drew it before e7095bbb. Cause: the line, a top border one device pixel wide on a box one device pixel tall (the border is rounded to at least a device pixel and the box takes its size from it), is a border-only quad of one row, and every gpui renderer's quad shader takes a pixel's border by the half of the quad its centre lies in, `center_to_point.y < 0.0 ? top : bottom` (gpui-pre-apple 0.3.9 `src/shaders.metal:133-137`; gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.9 `src/shaders.wgsl:603-611`; gpui-pre-windows 0.3.9 `src/shaders.hlsl:590-593`): the one row's centre lies on the quad's middle, `center_to_point.y` 0, so it takes the zero bottom border and is shaded as the transparent background. gpui's test platform runs no shader, so the layout tests passed. The colour's alpha is not the cause: iced draws the same `#ffffff19` at y 313.
Fixed, part B: `widgets::Separator` draws a box filled in `separator.line_color`, `max(separator.line_width, one device pixel)` thick (`1 / window.scale_factor()`), which every renderer draws through its fill path; the Basic table's two grid lines (`demo::files_table`, boxes `separator.line_width` thick that rounded to 0, part A's review, item 13(b)) are `widgets::Separator`s recoloured `list.grid_color`. No Linux test runs a gpui shader, so the gates come as near as the test platform allows: `a_separator_is_painted_as_a_filled_line_at_scale_one` (the connector, gpui-pre: under macos-tahoe and windows-11 at scale 1 the separator is a filled quad of its colour over its whole box) fails on f8506510's border ("is not painted as a filled quad") and passes; `the_hairlines_are_filled_quads_at_scale_one` (the showcase, macos-tahoe at scale 1: the Separator, the page row's rule and the table's grid lines are filled quads one device pixel thick at least) fails without the table change ("the table's grid lines: 0 filled quads") and passes. The next Screenshots run is the runtime check: a 1 px line under "Separator" and under the page tabs, and the table's header and column lines, on macOS and Windows.
Part B's review (item 14(c), (g)): the in-window menu's separators were boxes `separator.line_width` tall too (`demo.rs`, `MenuRow::Separator`, `MenuLook::separator_width`), 0 at scale 1 under the macOS presets; they are `widgets::Separator`s in `menu.separator_color`. `the_hairlines_are_filled_quads_at_scale_one` opens the Theme menu under macos-tahoe at scale 1 and finds `chrome.menu.theme.separator_1` a filled quad of that colour; without the change it is `217px × 0px` with none. No other box in the three showcases is sized by a `separator_width` or `line_width` (grep): the segmented control's dividers are its segments' borders on boxes far wider than a pixel, and iced and egui draw their lines as antialiased shapes. `a_hairline_separator_is_its_stated_thickness_at_scale_two` holds the 0.5 px line at 0.5 logical px, one device pixel, at scale 2.

#### M9-166 · M9x · ux · S3 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/examples/showcase-gpui/demo.rs:2275
**Claim:** Under macos-monterey, both variants, the gpui showcase's Basic Segmented control wraps "Month" onto a second row (about 710-875, 403-452). Under macos-tahoe and windows-11 it keeps one row, and iced and egui keep one row on every preset.
**Evidence:** at d661a11a:
- The control's segments sit in a wrapping row, by design: "The segments wrap onto a further line where the control's column is too narrow for them, as the Basic page's other rows do" (`demo::segmented`, `demo.rs:2275-2278`). iced's and egui's controls wrap the same way (`showcase-iced.rs`, `row(segments).spacing(..).wrap()`; `showcase-egui/pages/basic.rs`, `SegmentedControl::wrap`).
- The column is the shared count's (`pages/basic.rs:228`, `basic_column_count`, as iced's and egui's count): five columns where each holds the widest fixed-width control the theme states (`combo_box.min_width`, the two tabs, `BASIC_WIDE` 170, `BASIC_WIDTH` 140). Under macos-monterey that is exactly 170 wide, its `layout.section_gap_px` 20 four times between them; macos-tahoe states no section gap, so its columns are 186 wide. The segmented control's own width is not in the count.

#### M9-167 · M9x · theme-data · S2 · connectors/native-theme-gpui/src/lib.rs:752
**Claim:** On macOS (every preset) the gpui showcase draws the Basic page's Monospace sample (about 898,267) in a proportional face, where iced and egui draw a monospace one; on Windows all three do.
**Evidence:** at d661a11a:
- The macOS presets state `defaults.mono_font.family` "SF Mono" (macos-tahoe.toml and macos-monterey.toml `[light.defaults.mono_font] family`, and the dark ones), whose name as a family is an open question (docs/platform-facts.md §1.1.1, `+monospacedSystemFontOfSize:weight:`: the face is `.AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced`, "whether its family is \"SF Mono\" stays ❓"). No fallback chain is stated.
- The connector asks gpui for "SF Mono" as stated: `font_family` aliases only the system UI family on macOS (`ui_font_family`, `src/lib.rs:728-734`), and its substitute lookup is fontconfig's, which macOS has none of (`src/lib.rs:736-761`, `native_theme::fonts::substitute_family_cached`).
- On the runner gpui's font names do not hold it: the run's log prints `font-names: stated mono family "SF Mono" in gpui's font names: false` on each macOS capture (`showcase-gpui/main.rs`, the `--screenshot` arm). gpui's macOS text system then finds no family (gpui-pre-apple 0.3.9 `src/text_system.rs:284-297`), and `TextSystem::resolve_font` takes the first face of its fallback stack it finds, `.ZedMono` (Lilex), `.ZedSans` (IBM Plex Sans), then Helvetica (gpui-pre 0.3.9 `src/text_system.rs:255-266`, `:370-379`): neither Zed font is on a stock macOS, so the sample is drawn in a proportional sans face, Helvetica by that order.
- iced's and egui's font databases lack it too: `SF Mono: stated "SF Mono", system_font_family gives "SF Mono", in iced's font database: false`; `system_faces_resolve: macos-tahoe Light: mono family "SF Mono" resolves: false`, and `.AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced` neither (the same run's runner checks). They draw their toolkit's own monospace there, a generic monospace family, where gpui's stack starts monospace only with fonts gpui ships and the showcase does not register.
- The showcase's Theme tab (`mono_font_family`) and Widget Info's `defaults.mono_font` row on the sample already say it: "SF Mono (gpui finds no face of it; drawn in the first family of gpui's fallback stack it finds, ...)" (`inspector::DrawnFamilies`); neither is in a capture, which shows the Widget tab's hint.
**Fix proposed:** The cause is the connector's, not the showcase's, so this round does not change `src/` and the controller chooses: (a) on macOS `font_family` aliases Apple's system mono family as it aliases the system UI family, to the name gpui's Core Text loader takes for the face `+monospacedSystemFontOfSize:weight:` returns, which only a macOS run can confirm (font-kit's `select_family_by_name` with `.AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced`); (b) where gpui's font names hold no face of a monospace role's family, the connector asks for a monospace family the platform has, which needs a sourced family per platform (docs/platform-facts.md states none); (c) leave it, the Theme tab and Widget Info naming the face drawn. The showcase's `--screenshot` log line now also names the family gpui draws the stated one in, so the next run's log says which face it is.
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED from the run's log and the sources above; the face's name (Helvetica by the stack's order) is read in the next run's log.
**Triage:** needs a ruling (the M9x CI brief, item 5: "If the cause is in the gpui connector rather than the showcase, say so in the report before changing src/").
**Status:** open — the cause found; the commit that files this entry adds the drawn family to the macOS `--screenshot` log line (`font-names: ... ; drawn: <label>`), compiled on Linux with its `cfg` widened for the check and restored.
Ruled (controller, 2026-10-25, m9c-rulings.md's last line, part B item 10): (a). Fixed, part B: `native_theme::fonts::is_macos_system_mono_family` ("SF Mono" caselessly, docs/platform-facts.md:65) beside `is_macos_system_ui_family`, and on macOS the connector's `ui_font_family`, which `font_family` and so every theme font goes through, passes it as the face's name, `.AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced`, the twin of the `.SystemUIFont` alias: gpui's macOS text system looks the name up as it does `.AppleSystemUIFont`, font-kit's `select_family_by_name`, memory fonts first, then the system source (gpui-pre-apple 0.3.9 `src/text_system.rs:290-297`). Every other family, and every family elsewhere, is passed as stated. `the_macos_system_mono_font_is_its_face_only_on_macos` (the connector, the platform a parameter) fails before the change (`left: "SF Mono"`, right `.AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced`) and passes after it; the shared crate's family label names the face ("SF Mono (drawn as the system monospaced font, .AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced)"), where it would have called it the platform's substitute. What the next Screenshots run's macOS log should print: `font-names: stated mono family "SF Mono" in gpui's font names: false; drawn: SF Mono (drawn as the system monospaced font, .AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced)` where gpui finds the face, or, where it does not, `drawn: SF Mono (gpui finds no face of the system monospaced font, .AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced; drawn in the first family of gpui's fallback stack it finds, …)`; the capture's Monospace sample shows which.

#### M9-172 · M9x · theme-data · S2 · connectors/native-theme-iced/src/styles.rs:546
**Claim:** The iced showcase's focused field does not draw the theme's focus ring on macOS or Windows: under macos-tahoe it shows its 0.5 px rest line and no ring, under macos-monterey a 0.5 px `#007aff` line, under windows-11 a 1 px `#0067c0` line, where the theme states a 3 px ring at -1 (tahoe, monterey) and a 2 px ring at +1 (windows-11), and egui draws them.
**Evidence:** at f8506510:
- `InputColors::new` draws the ring only where `focus_ring_offset` is minus `focus_ring_width`, as the field's border; elsewhere the focused field recolours its rest line in `input.focus_border_color` (`styles.rs:546-555`), recorded as the contract's `UNREACHABLE` `defaults.focus_ring_offset` (`contract/derived.rs:954-985`): a `text_input::Style` has one border and no outline (iced_widget 0.14.2 `src/text_input.rs:1713-1726`), and a quad's border lies inside its bounds (iced_wgpu 0.14.0 `src/shader/quad/solid.wgsl:78-83`).
- The ring's values: macos-tahoe and macos-monterey `defaults.focus_ring_width_px` 3, `focus_ring_offset_px` -1; windows-11 2 and 1 (the presets' `[light.defaults]` and `[dark.defaults]`). The egui connector strokes the ring outside the field grown by the offset (`native-theme-egui/src/plugin.rs`, `paint_focus_ring`).
- The test below at f8506510: the pixel in the ring's band left of the field is the ground (tahoe light `#ffffff`, windows-11 light `#f3f3f3`).
**Fix proposed:** A connector widget, as `tab_flares` draws outside its child: the field, then while it holds the focus a quad round it, its bounds the field's grown by `offset + width`, its border `width` in `focus_ring_color`, its radius the field's grown as much; the focus learnt by iced's `Focusable` operation, never `tree::State::downcast_ref` (which panics on a wrong type, iced_core 0.14.0 `src/widget/tree.rs:231-241`).
**Verdict:** CONFIRMED by the RED run below.
**Triage:** fix — CONFIRMED (the M9x CI brief part B, I4).
**Status:** fixed — the commit that files this entry: `native_theme_iced::focus_ring(&resolved, corner_radius, field)` (`src/focus_ring.rs`) wraps a field with its own tree state, the content's tree its one child; it runs a `Focusable` probe over the field when the tree is laid out, updated and operated on, reads its state through `tree::State`'s variant (no panicking downcast) and draws the ring after the field where the theme states one not inset at the edge (inset, adwaita, stays `styles::text_input`'s border). The showcase wraps the Basic page's four fields, its text area and its number input, the Inputs page's two fields and its editor and the command palette's query; a `ComboBox` cannot be ringed, as iced_widget 0.14.2's implements no `operate`, so no operation reaches its field (the README says so). The contract's `UNREACHABLE` entry is gone, its doc naming the ring as the consumer's widget beside the builder-method values; the routes of the ring's width, offset and colour name `focus_ring` where it draws the ring; `scripts/connector_parity_exceptions.toml` excepts `focus_ring` for gpui (gpui-component's own ring) and egui (the install plugin's). `the_focused_field_draws_the_themes_ring_round_it` (macos-tahoe and windows-11, both modes, the field clicked into: a whole pixel of the band left of the field is the ring over the ground to 3 per channel) fails at f8506510 ("macos-tahoe Light: at x 532 the band is [255, 255, 255, 255], the ring over the ground [128, 179, 250, 255]"; windows-11 Light `[243, 243, 243, 255]` for `[26, 26, 26, 255]`) and passes on the new code; the connector's `a_focused_field_is_ringed_by_the_themes_ring` checks the quad's bounds, width, colour and radius under both presets and modes, and `no_ring_is_drawn_where_the_border_is_the_ring_or_none_is_stated` adwaita's inset ring and unstated or non-finite rings.
Part B's review (item 14(a), (b), (d), (e), (g)): `focus_ring`'s doc no longer offers a `ComboBox` (iced_widget 0.14.2 `src/combo_box.rs` implements no `operate`); the wrapper keeps the window's focus beside the field's and draws no ring while iced reports `window::Event::Unfocused`, where iced's text input keeps its own focus (`src/text_input.rs:1313-1317`, `:1501-1503`) and the egui connector draws none; it asks the field again only after a mouse button, a key, a touch or a window event, so a pointer move no longer has iced_aw's `NumberInput` rebuild its step elements (iced_aw 0.14.1 `src/widget/number_input.rs:604-640`). `the_ring_follows_the_focus_through_update` (a press focuses, a pointer move changes nothing, `Unfocused` hides the ring, `Focused` shows it) fails with the window's focus not tracked ("the window lost the focus", left 1, right 0); `a_replaced_field_is_asked_again` holds a field replaced in the view. The CHANGELOG's two older iced focus-ring lines and `register_focus_shape`'s exception reason say what `focus_ring` draws.
The controller's Linux parity run on d12398a8 (item 16(a)): iced's layout dump under material-3 light put the Basic page's four text fields, its text area and its number input, each wrapped by `focus_ring`, at (0, 0) at their own sizes, their text parts at (16, 16.56), in the other five runs at their places; the capture drew them right, so the record was wrong, not the drawing, and the 15 differences the run left unexcepted were the column's keys measured from them. The cause is I4's (8b7a7576): `FocusRing::layout` ran its focus probe over the content with the content's node as `layout` returns it, before the parent places it, and the showcase's `Tagged` records its rectangle into the dump's survey on every operation, an operation handing each widget its placed layout. The dump surveys the tree and then writes after the scale-factor task, so where iced laid the view out again in between, the wrapper's probe recorded the fields at the origin over the survey's places; whether it did is the frames' timing, one run in six. Fixed at the root, the commit that adds this line: the wrapper asks its content nothing while it is laid out; it learns the focus when the tree is operated on, as iced's focus operations are, and after the events that can move it, and where the view puts a widget of another kind in the content's place (`diff`, the child's tag changed) it takes the focus as lost, the new widget's state holding none. `the_layout_dump_has_the_ring_wrapped_fields_where_they_are` (the showcase: every bundled preset in both modes, the page surveyed and then laid out five times more, each wrapped field where the survey found it, at its heading's x) fails at d12398a8 ("kde-breeze (dark: false), layout 0: basic.text_inputs.placeholder at Rectangle { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, .. }, surveyed at Rectangle { x: 530.4, y: 141.89333, .. }") and passes on the new code; the connector's `laying_the_ring_out_asks_its_field_nothing` holds the field unoperated through three layouts, and `a_replaced_field_loses_the_ring` the replaced field.
Round 2-3 review item 15(4), ruled (a) (item 16(c)): `Focus.window` starts true. iced keeps it in each wrapper's tree state and sends `window::Event::Focused` only when the window's focus changes, so a wrapper built after the window gained the focus (a field on a page opened later, the command palette's query) would never learn the window held it, as starting it false showed (three connector tests and the showcase's ring test fail with it, each focusing a field with no `Focused` first); egui-winit starts its one per-window state unfocused (egui-winit 0.36.2 `src/lib.rs:149`). The corner case: a window opened without the OS's focus shows a focused field's ring until its first focus change. `Focus::default`'s doc says so (the commit that adds this line).
Round 5 review, item 18 M4: `focus_ring` returned the field unwrapped where the theme draws no ring (inset, adwaita), so switching presets between adwaita and a ringing one changed the slot's tag, iced rebuilt the tree, and a focused field lost its focus (the showcase focuses its Focused field at boot alone). It always returns the wrapper now, its look an `Option` that draws nothing where `None`, so the tree's shape does not depend on the theme. `the_focus_survives_a_theme_that_draws_no_ring` (a field focused under windows-11, then adwaita, then windows-11, and the other way round) fails before the change ("the field focused under the first theme lost its focus through the second") and passes after it.

### Rulings made while executing G1 and G2

Copied from the plan's execution ledger, which was deleted at the close. Each reads
"what was decided — why — what it costs if wrong". R-G2-1 to R-G2-5 came from G2's pre-flight
scan of the plan.

G1:
- Task 0 (registering G1/G2 in the review plan and ledger, committing the three documents) is done by the controller — it is bookkeeping, no code — cost if wrong: none (a docs commit).
- the pushes and the probe dispatch (T1, T8) are done by the controller, as the plan says — approved by the maintainer — cost if wrong: none beyond CI minutes.
- fix both Minors before the probe dispatch — the run is the evidence the macOS header-height presets cite, and a stale window-less reading would be undetectable without another CI run — cost if wrong: one short fix round.
- the two Windows failures are fixed as Task 5b (native-theme code, debug + fix, own review, validated by a CI push), after Task 5 makes the branch green — not now, because Task 2's implementer is working in the shared tree and Tasks 2–5 leave gates red — cost if wrong: Windows stays red a few tasks longer; G1 cannot close until it is green.
- a range is renumbered when the whole old block occurs exactly once in the new file, even where its first line alone repeats (14 ranges) — a unique whole block is stronger evidence than a unique first line — cost if wrong: 14 citations move to Task 4's hand-read list.
- TooltipDefaults cited as GB/tooltip.rs:58-108 (the impl block closes at 108), not the spec's 58-107 — the spec's range was one line short — cost if wrong: none.
- the stale SC/support.rs:236-237 `App::drop_image, gpui-pre src/app.rs:3044-3054` (wrong since 0.3.8; drop_image is at 3103-3113) is fixed inside Task 5, which edits support.rs — cost if wrong: one extra line in Task 5's diff.
- Diff — turn on its hover highlight (a themed state worth showing; claim list_hover at its line); the add-annotation button and the conflict side get `.instance` notes (the panel API's existing form for "not in this instance", info/layout.rs:699) naming the fields they would read, with lines; line fills cite :1576/:1578. DataTable — make one column sortable so 0.7.3's labelled sort button is painted and claimed; the right-clicked cell outline gets an `.instance` note (turning on cell_selectable would change the row-selection panels). — the spec asks for claims of what the panel's widget paints; claiming unpainted colours would be false, and the new 0.7.3 sort button should be shown — cost if wrong: two notes that could have been shown elements.
- the spec's claim that unicode-properties is also used on core's svg-rasterize path is wrong (the implementer measured: only gpui-pre and gpui-component use it); the docs/todo.md entry states the measured users — measurement over the design-time reading — cost if wrong: none.
- Task 6's Minors 1–4 (README sentence contradicting its bullets; stale scripts/README.md gpui family/gates/check_features lines and CONTRIBUTING.md --commit list; ci.yml strict-panic block hiding the gpui-fast run — split into two soft steps; stale gpui-pre dev-dependency comment) are fixed in Task 8, the documents task — cost if wrong: they stay stale two more tasks.
- the 10 theme-switch tests under gpui-fast count as the live-switch evidence (they switch themes within a window on GPUI Fast's test platform); a hand check by the maintainer is optional — cost if wrong: a runtime-only switch bug on GPUI Fast surfaces later.
- the G1 ledger section stays where Task 7 appended it (end of file), to keep the edit append-only — cost if wrong: section order only.

G2:
- R-G2-1: the parity sibling rule is kept green in every commit — a task that adds an accessor before its siblings have it adds `kind = "absent"` exceptions for those siblings whose reason names the G2 task that adds them, and that task removes them (stale exceptions fail the script). Permanent gaps (dialog_entrance in egui/iced; anything the script cannot see in gpui's geometry.rs) get exceptions in the file's existing style, with the real reason — cost if wrong: a few exception lines that a later task deletes.
- R-G2-2: if a gate keyed on the model's leaf set goes red at a commit only because the leaf's consumer lands in a later task, the implementer brings the consumer's minimal true part forward into that commit (the later task then finds it done) — never a placeholder or a false text — and reports it — cost if wrong: a later task's diff is smaller than its brief.
- R-G2-3: the spec's line numbers predate M4/M5's changes (df86348c); implementers locate each cited site by its quoted text or symbol; a cited site that no longer exists is reported, not guessed — cost if wrong: none.
- R-G2-4: M5 landed colour-leaf coverage for iced only (b5's message); G2's three fields are not colours, so per spec §0.2 iced's new receivers are held by their own tests and the coverage table, not contract rows — cost if wrong: a later M6 leaf-coverage task adds the rows.

- Material's §8.2 cell is `scale_fade` from material-components-android 1.14.0 (MDC pin: fade 0→1 with scale 0.8→1, 400 ms); Compose's AlertDialog.kt states none. So per spec §8.1 DialogEntranceStyle is {ScaleFade, FadeRise} (no SlideDown) and per §8.3 material-3 = scale_fade — the spec's own conditional, resolved by the source — cost if wrong: one enum variant added later.
- the macOS header-height cells are tagged (API), not the spec's (measured) — the facts file defines (measured) as pixel-measured and tags the probe's rowHeight reading (API); the file's convention wins over the spec's word — cost if wrong: a tag.
- Kirigami Dialog.qml cited at src/dialogs/ (the true path at the KIRI pin), not the spec's src/controls/ — cost if wrong: none.
- evidence directory dated 2026-10-14 (local date of a run started 2026-10-13 22:31 UTC; README states both) — cost if wrong: a directory name.
- the Task 9 fixes are applied by the controller (five one-line edits, no judgment beyond the reviewer's) — cost if wrong: a re-review catches it.
- the spec text is not edited for the §8.2 results (append-only design documents; Task 15 writes the *As built* note at archiving): this ledger and Task 10's dispatch carry them — cost if wrong: the spec reads stale until Task 15.

- egui mapping rows are keyed by the resolved field names (tooltip.show_delay, dialog.entrance, list.header_height), not spec §7.4's `tooltip.show_delay_ms` — the mapping file's key convention; Task 12 uses them — cost if wrong: none.
- egui's dialog-entrance row says egui has no scaling or rising entrance (egui's windows/modals do fade, area.rs:347-354), not the spec's "no dialog animation" — the true statement — cost if wrong: none.
- the ios-13 comment "UIToolTipInteraction, iOS 15+, states no delay" verified by the controller against Apple's documentation JSON (introducedAt 15.0; no delay/interval/duration on the page) — cost if wrong: a comment.
- the four pre-existing material-3 citation errors are fixed in Task 10's fix round (they sit beside the new fields, and a wrong citation is a defect wherever found) — cost if wrong: four comment lines.
- material-3's broader citation drift (~60 lines per variant, 1–4 lines off; found by a controller scan of all presets — the other native presets' mismatches are deliberate cross-row citations) is not fixed in G2: M2d re-cites material-3 against its pinned Compose release; recorded as a docs/todo.md entry (54f8e316) with the method and a gate suggestion — cost if wrong: wrong line numbers (not values) stay until M2d.
- SC/info/feedback.rs:768's "500ms … the showcase installs no defaults" is made false by 0ae7be3c (apply installs the theme's delay) — the plan's rule "in the same commit, the panel texts this makes false" puts it in Task 11, not Task 14: fixed in Task 11's fix round (Task 14 keeps registry.rs and whatever stays true-but-incomplete) — cost if wrong: a text moves between two tasks.
- the connector tells its own TooltipDefaults write from the application's by value (an app delay equal to the connector's last write reads as the connector's); documented in rustdoc and README — the spec §7.4 algorithm as designed — cost if wrong: such an app's delay is replaced by the next theme's.

**Problem:** gpui-component 0.8.0's charts derive `IntoPlot`; two of them, `RadarChart` and

(`demo::radar_chart`, `demo::sankey_chart`, ids `CHARTS_RADAR_CHART`, `CHARTS_SANKEY_CHART`),
coloured as the page colours the others, through the charts' setters from the theme's chart
palette: the radar's two series `chart_1` and `chart_2`, each over a fill of itself at the
showcase's `RADAR_FILL_OPACITY`; the sankey's five nodes `chart_1` to `chart_5` through
`SankeyChart::node_color`. Their Widget Info (`info::charts::radar_chart`, `sankey_chart`)
claims the upstream-read colours at their lines (radar labels `muted_foreground`
`radar_chart.rs:563`, grid `chart_grid` `:507`, hovered vertices' ring `background` `:656`;
sankey node labels `muted_foreground` `sankey_chart.rs:391`) and notes the literals (series
2px, rings and spokes 1px, label text 10px, the link opacity, `HOVER_DIM`).
`every_chart_shows_its_own_info` hovers all seven. The coverage script's half is C-07a.
**Status:** done, b1b8f095.

#### C-07a · check_widget_coverage.py learns `IntoPlot`
**Problem:** `check_widget_coverage.py` read only `impl RenderOnce/IntoElement` and
`#[derive(IntoElement)]`, so gpui-component's seven charts, which derive `IntoPlot`, were
never discovered and two went unshown unnoticed.
**Fix:** `IntoPlot` joins the derives it reads (the derive writes the charts'
`impl IntoElement`, gpui-component-macros 0.8.0 `derive_into_plot.rs:20`), with a self-test
case; gpui discovered 158, missing 0.
**Status:** done, d2d4a3af (W2).

**Problem:** iced paints an application's background from its base style, which `Base::base`
takes from the palette's background (`iced_core-0.14.0/src/theme.rs:222-230`, `:291-293`,
`:328-336`), `defaults.background_color` under this connector; nothing read

(`iced-0.14.0/src/application.rs:394-399`): `background_color` is
`window.background_color`, `text_color` the base style's (`defaults.text_color`), each with a

`UNREAD_COLOURS` entry is gone and `contract-leaves.toml` regenerated (the leaf moves
`styles::application.background_color`). The iced showcase installs it. The README's style
table has an application shape and the crate docs' *Theme Field Coverage* counts 29
functions. No bundled preset differs in the two leaves, so nothing drawn changes there.

  and the radar's hover test read the hover dots and halos from the frame (`hover_marks`); by
  mutation, a changed area line, radar line or radar fill each turns a test red. M4:
  `ROADMAP.md` counts 29 iced style functions, `application` among the 21 that replace
  iced's own. Commit 3a0da4a3.
